544288|2026-06.headline: BlackBuck Q1 FY27: total income up ~38% YoY, adjusted EBITDA up 16% to ₹55 crore, with reported PAT at ₹42 crore after a deferred-tax effect.
544288|2026-06.overview: Management said the business recovered through late May and June after a weak April caused by macro logistics headwinds. Revenue from operations grew ~42% YoY and ~10% QoQ, while net revenue grew 25% YoY and contribution margin held at ~93%. Adjusted EBITDA rose from ₹47 crore to ₹55 crore, and reported PAT of ₹42 crore fell sequentially from ₹66 crore because of a deferred tax item recognised in Q4 FY26. Growth businesses (Super Loads and vehicle finance) grew ~44% QoQ after ~20% QoQ last quarter.

segments.name: Core businesses (payments/tolling, telematics)
segments.commentary: Core revenue grew ~21% YoY and delivered a record quarter for profitability and cash flow. Telematics recorded its highest-ever quarterly new device sales, across AI, non-AI and specialised devices.

segments.name: Super Loads and vehicle finance (growth businesses)
segments.commentary: Growth businesses revenue is up ~2.5x YoY and grew ~44% QoQ, up from ~20% QoQ last quarter. Super Loads now operates in 14 cities. Vehicle finance is expected to reach profitability by end of FY27.

guidance_outlook: Tolling demand has normalised after April; management says it is back to its normal modelling framework (road growth, toll fare inflation, truck growth).
Fuel business is still uncertain. Management gave no timeline for full recovery in fuel loyalty margins.
Super Loads will keep investing aggressively; investment is stepping up each quarter.
Vehicle finance expected to converge to profitability by end of FY27 (reaffirmed).
Effective tax: for the next two quarters, deferred tax is expected to offset current tax; the loss-utilisation view will be reassessed in Q4.
Super Loads segment-level disclosure expected in about three to four quarters, once the business is large enough.
capex_capacity: Super Loads present in 14 cities (4 initial cities plus 10 launched by March/April 2026); live in under 5% of India's industrial hubs.

First Super Loads hub is close to the ~250 loads/day (about 5,000/month) milestone; management says it is about 60-70% there on playbook building, and 70-80% of newer cities are growing faster than the first four.
Telematics device depreciation is front-loaded over two years, which raised depreciation this quarter.
About 40-50% of Super Loads loads are AI-enabled on a given day.
demand_pricing: Tolling GTV grew 16% YoY, which management says is only a low single-digit rise at NETC level and a higher single-digit rise against the CV market.

Renewal rates for telematics: first renewal around 80% for GPS products (early 70s by some accounts), stabilising in the 80s for second and third renewals; higher-end products run 5-10 percentage points better.
Fuelling is a small share of revenue. Management said loyalty margin spend is discretionary and fuel recovery is only partial.
On Delhivery's possible entry into tolling, fuelling and vehicle finance, management sees it as positive for the industry and does not expect near-term threat.

qa_highlights.question: Gaurav Malhotra (Axis Capital): Which hubs is Super Loads present in, daily load volumes, and outlook for the next 1-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Present in 14 cities; the first four are Bangalore, Hyderabad, Mumbai and Chennai. Super Loads sequential growth was ~50%, up from ~23-24% a quarter earlier. Detailed volume disclosure is limited.

qa_highlights.question: Atul Borse (JM Financial): Will the macro headwinds in tolling and fuelling taper in Q2 and FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Tolling caution has gone away and BAU is restored after a sharp April contraction in normalised swipe metrics. Fuel is only partially recovered, and management gave no timeline for a full recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Atul Borse: Is Delhivery's entry into tolling, fuelling and vehicle finance a medium-term threat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees it as a positive for the industry since there is little qualified competition. It sees no near-term threat and will watch market share closely.

qa_highlights.question: Abhisek Banerjee (ICICI Securities): What drives the 13% growth in transacting users, and what share of users use Super Loads?
qa_highlights.answer: User growth is driven by tolling, telematics and marketplace acquisition, which have been secular for 10-12 quarters. Super Loads is a low-frequency use case and too early to move usage minutes (under 5% of hubs covered).

qa_highlights.question: Monica Joshi: What learnings from earlier cities are being applied to new ones, and how are Bangalore like-for-like numbers trending?
qa_highlights.answer: New cities are layered and run with several parallel experiments; AI-first, less people-dependent workflows are used. Management declined to give like-for-like Bangalore numbers until the segment is large enough to report separately.

qa_highlights.question: Gaurav Malhotra: What is the effective tax rate this year and next?
qa_highlights.answer: For the next two quarters, deferred tax is expected to offset current tax. The loss-utilisation position will be reassessed at the end of the year (Q4).

qa_highlights.question: Lokesh Manik (Vallum Capital): Why did depreciation rise, and why did GTV fall from ₹6,800 crore to ₹6,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Telematics devices are depreciated over two years, so depreciation is front-loaded with the device investment. GTV now reports tolling only, with fuelling removed because of fuel price uncertainty.

risks_watch: Fuel business recovery: no timeline given, and fuel loyalty spend is discretionary.
Tolling volume: tolling transactions fell 3% QoQ, and tolling GTV growth (16%) lags NETC and the CV market.
Super Loads investment: spending rises each quarter, and segment-level disclosure is not expected for 3-4 quarters.
Reported PAT volatility from deferred tax; the Q4 loss-utilisation reassessment could move reported earnings.
Potential competition from Delhivery in tolling, fuelling and vehicle finance.
544288|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on telematics, tolling recovery and Super Loads momentum, but cautious on fuel recovery, with no timeline given. Management deflected granular Super Loads metrics and unit economics, citing limited disclosure.

financial_highlights.change: +25% YoY; down from ₹66 crore in Q4 FY26 due to deferred tax

key_quotes: Despite a very tough April month from a movement perspective, I think there was a decent recovery through end of May and June, which has enabled the business to deliver strong results and something which has helped us get back on track and do well from a BAU perspective.
So, core businesses have again delivered a record quarter from a profitability and cash flows perspective despite the macro headwinds.
We are reaching close to 900,000 transacting customers, and the usage continues to be the same, hovering around 45 minutes daily.
But I don't have a full hold on or let's say to give you a guidance on when will the full recovery sort of you know set in.
So, for the next two quarters, broadly, this trend should continue with deferred tax offsets the tax that is there.

rows.why: Management reaffirmed that vehicle finance converges to profitability by end FY27, and growth-business revenue is up ~2.5x YoY and ~44% QoQ.

544290|2026-03.headline: Enviro Infra FY26 revenue rose 7.5% to INR11,456 mn, missing 35% guidance; FY27 guided to ~INR2,000 crore revenue with 13.5-14% PAT margin.
544290|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR4,273 mn (+8.8% YoY), EBITDA INR799 mn (18.7% margin) and PAT INR543 mn (12.4% margin), with margin pressure attributed to renewable IPP mix, higher employee cost, ECL provision and depreciation. Management said FY26 revenue partly missed guidance because awarded projects stayed in design and bid evaluations were delayed, and it cut FY27 EBITDA guidance to 21-22% from 22-24% citing commodity cost pressure. Working capital stretched to 166 days (unbilled revenue days at 195) because AMRUT state-scheme funds were delayed. The renewable segment (BESS, wind EPC via Suyog Urja) is now a major part of the order book.

financial_highlights.value: INR422 crore (LT INR250 crore, ST INR175 crore)

segments.name: Water & wastewater
segments.commentary: Execution order book about INR2,733 crore plus O&M order book about INR951 crore; FY27 water/wastewater revenue expected about INR1,350 crore. Recent wins: INR348 crore BUIDCO (Bihar) project and two Swachh Bharat sanitation projects in Pune and Nashik worth INR824 crore in Q4.

segments.name: Renewable energy
segments.commentary: Execution order book about INR2,051 crore plus O&M/IPP about INR1,079 crore; renewable revenue was about INR129 crore in FY26 (INR117 crore in Q4, mostly IPP with near-zero margin). FY27 renewable revenue target about INR650 crore; BESS EPC PAT margin guided about 10%, renewables blended PAT 10-12%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of about INR2,000 crore, with PAT of INR270-280 crore (13.5-14% PAT margin).
FY27 EBITDA margin cut to 21-22% from earlier 22-24%, with a possible further 1-2 percentage point dip from commodity and geopolitical cost pressure.
FY27 order inflow target of at least INR2,500 crore; bid pipeline submitted about INR1,200 crore plus about INR5,000 crore under evaluation.
Working capital cycle targeted to fall to about 90 days; debt-to-equity to be capped at 1:1 on consolidated basis.
Capex for FY27 expected at about INR20-30 crore; Q1 FY27 revenue said to be well above Q1 FY26 (about INR250 crore), without a number.
FY28 indicative revenue from existing order book about INR2,500-2,800 crore; management reiterated 35-40% long-term topline growth ambition.
capex_capacity: Total execution order book about INR4,800 crore, said to give visibility over FY27 and FY28 (execution period 18-24 months for renewable projects).
BESS: 4 NTPC EPC projects totalling 930 MWh worth about INR1,070 crore (UP, Assam, Karnataka, Telangana) plus acquired 150 MWh Bihar BESS project.
Lithium-ion cell procurement deferred due to price rises; BOS works (civil, transformers, HT lines) already started.
Renewable team above 250 professionals; business heads appointed for each division.
Asset monetisation possible if leverage rises; Suyog Urja (wind EPC) acquired during FY26.
demand_pricing: Most contracts carry a price variation clause, which offsets only part of the cost increase; management says guidance was lowered for this gap.
Water project cost benchmarks: STP INR1-1.5 crore per MLD; water treatment INR30-50 lakh per MLD; CETP highly variable (INR2-15 crore per MLD).
Design component is 2-5% of turnkey water project value; STPs and CETPs are the most technology-intensive.

Revenue shortfall attributed to slow evaluations and re-bidding of an MIDC CETP/ZLD project and two Bangalore projects stuck in design, plus delayed AMRUT funds in Chhattisgarh, MP, Rajasthan, Haryana and Punjab.
Renewable receivables de-risked via NTPC and A-to-AAA rated private clients for Suyog's wind EPC work.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 revenue guidance (about 35% growth) missed and is execution delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ongoing projects have no delays, but the order book of about INR1,200 crore at 1 April 2025 converted to about INR1,145 crore (about 95%) with timing slipping; some projects stayed in design and a re-bid hit timelines. Renewables were about INR100 crore below the INR200 crore guidance and wastewater about INR100 crore below as well.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 margins fall and what is the underlying margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited mix: about INR100-120 crore of zero-margin IPP revenue, employee cost up to about 6% of revenue, other expenses 3.5%, ECL provision INR10 crore and depreciation up about INR25 crore. Manufacturing cost fell about 1 percentage point; FY26 EBITDA stayed above 24%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of renewable revenue in FY26 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Renewable revenue was about INR129 crore for FY26, with about INR12 crore up to December and INR117 crore in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook and drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Net working capital cycle was 166 days, with UBR days at 195 because AMRUT funds were not released; receivable days fell to 53. Management expects funds from Chhattisgarh and a path for Rajasthan, Haryana and MP, targeting about 90 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 EBITDA guidance be cut further and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cut EBITDA guidance to 21-22% from 22-24% due to commodity and geopolitical cost pressure; a further 1-2 point dip is possible, depending on whether the situation stabilises.

qa_highlights.question: What are the BESS and renewable margins and how is the FY27 revenue split?
qa_highlights.answer: BESS EPC PAT margin is about 10%; renewable blended PAT target is 10-12%. FY27 revenue split is about INR1,350 crore water/wastewater and INR650 crore renewables, against the INR2,000 crore total; about 42% of the INR4,800 crore order book.

qa_highlights.question: What is the operating cash flow position?
qa_highlights.answer: Adjusted pre-tax OCF is roughly balanced (about INR4 lakh positive) in FY26; post-tax OCF is negative INR63 crore, mainly due to service concession receivables recognised in OCF under audit policy.

risks_watch: Delayed central and state fund release (AMRUT, Jal Jeevan) could keep UBR days near 195 and working capital above 166 days.
Lithium-ion cell cost increases and geopolitical commodity pressure could cut EBITDA by a further 1-2 percentage points.
Revenue execution slippage: FY26 missed guidance; FY27 guidance of about INR2,000 crore depends on converting only about 42% of the INR4,800 crore order book.
Renewable IPP projects carry near-zero margin; segment profitability disclosure is promised separately going forward.
Debt rising toward the stated 1:1 debt-to-equity ceiling as renewable development projects are funded.
544290|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on order book visibility and FY27 targets, but defensive on the FY26 miss and margin compression; management repeatedly described guidance as deliberately conservative and admitted the revenue guidance was not met.
key_quotes: So we are just projecting a topline of INR2,000-odd crores, which will replicate into a conversion of somewhere around 42%. So we are trying ourselves to be just too conservative this time so that there is no fallback at all.
We will delay the procurement of lithium-ion battery to a certain extent so the prices get settled down, and at that point of time, we'll go for the procurement.
So as such, I can confirm with respect to the execution, the delay was not there.
The present debt level is 0.34.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance cut to 21-22% from 22-24%, with a possible further 1-2 pt dip from commodity pressure, and Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin was 18.7% against FY26's 24.2%, driven by zero-margin IPP mix (INR100-120 crore) and BESS EPC PAT margin only ~10%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 4 NTPC BESS EPC projects totalling 930 MWh (~INR1,070 crore) plus acquired 150 MWh Bihar BESS project are under construction, and the INR4,800 crore order book gives visibility over FY27-FY28; no timing given for the BESS capacity itself.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided to ~INR2,000 crore vs FY26 INR1,146 crore (~17.5% growth), with renewables target ~INR650 crore vs FY26 ~INR129 crore and water/wastewater ~INR1,350 crore, though FY26 missed guidance by ~35%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex guided only at INR20-30 crore, debt is INR422 crore with D/E 0.34 against a 1:1 ceiling, and lithium-ion cell procurement was deferred; utilisation is not disclosed as a capacity constraint.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY26 revenue missed the ~35% growth guidance (+7.5% actual) and FY27 EBITDA margin was cut to 21-22%, so there is no sign of an upward revision.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged a possible further 1-2 pt EBITDA margin dip from commodity and geopolitical cost pressure, and FY27 revenue depends on converting only ~42% of the INR4,800 crore order book, after FY26 execution slipped (order book ~INR1,200 crore converted to ~INR1,145 crore with timing slipping).

rows.label: Working capital cycle to ~90 days
rows.why: Cycle is 166 days (UBR 195 days) vs ~90-100 target, and it depends on AMRUT and state fund releases from Chhattisgarh, Rajasthan, Haryana and MP that have been delayed.

rows.label: FY27 order inflow of at least INR2,500 crore
rows.why: Bid pipeline is ~INR1,200 crore submitted plus ~INR5,000 crore under evaluation, and Q4 wins of INR824 crore show momentum, but evaluations have been slow and a MIDC CETP project was re-bid.

rows.label: Debt-to-equity capped at 1:1
rows.why: Total debt is INR422 crore at D/E 0.34, with renewable development projects funded by debt, and management says asset monetisation is possible if leverage rises.

tone.note: Management was confident on the INR4,800 crore order book, FY27 PAT of INR270-280 crore and working capital easing to ~90 days, but defensive about the FY26 revenue miss and Q4 margin compression; analysts pressed on the margin cut and execution slippage.

544290|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 49% YoY to INR359.2 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 21.07% from 26.65%, and FY27 guidance was trimmed to 21-22%.
544290|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR359.2 crore (+49% YoY) with EBITDA of INR75.7 crore (+17.9% YoY) and PAT of INR45.2 crore (+6.5% YoY). Management attributed the margin compression to higher raw material costs, a renewables mix, and a step-up in employee cost (about 7% of revenue vs 3-3.5% earlier). Total order book is about INR6,721 crore, split INR3,694 crore water/wastewater and INR3,027 crore renewables and BESS. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR2,000 crore and PAT of INR260-270 crore, while lowering the EBITDA margin guidance to 21-22% from 22-24%, and later described a blended 19-20% margin.

financial_highlights.change: vs 26.65% in Q1 FY26 and 18.7% in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Wind segment revenue (Suyog Urja, per Q&A)

segments.name: Water and wastewater treatment
segments.commentary: Order book INR3,694 crore (INR2,696 crore execution, INR998 crore O&M). Q1 revenue approx INR255 crore; management guides EBITDA margin 21-22% and FY27 topline INR1,300 crore from this order book at about 50% conversion.

segments.name: Renewable energy and BESS
segments.commentary: Order book INR3,027 crore (INR1,948 crore execution, INR1,079 crore IPP and O&M). Q1 revenue approx INR104 crore; guided EBITDA margin 15-18%, with execution over 12-18 months.

segments.name: Suyog Urja (wind EPC)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue INR80 crore; FY27 revenue expectation INR400-450 crore; wind EPC pipeline INR800 crore with a further INR500-600 crore expected; EBITDA margin 15-16%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance maintained at INR2,000 crore; PAT guidance INR260-270 crore (per analyst recap, confirmed by management).
EBITDA margin guidance lowered to 21-22% from the earlier 22-24%; later framed as blended 19-20% (water 21-22%, renewables 15-18%).
Employee cost expected to normalise to 5-5.5% of revenue and finance cost to 3-3.5% during FY27.
FY27 order inflow expected at about INR2,500 crore (about 20% strike rate); INR256 crore won so far.
Quarterly revenue split expected as roughly 20%/20%/20% for Q1-Q3 and about 40% in Q4; BESS NTPC (930 MWh) procurement to start in Q3.
Management stated a bare-minimum growth target of 25-30% a year going forward while maintaining margins.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the gross margin decline YoY, and was it raw material costs or industry competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher raw material costs, the renewables mix, and employee cost rising to about 7% of Q1 revenue from 3-3.5% earlier (team grew from about 900 at IPO to about 2,300); employee cost to normalise to 5-5.5% and finance cost to 3-3.5% in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Execution timelines for the order book and O&M duration?
qa_highlights.answer: Water execution INR2,700 crore over 18-24 months; renewables INR2,000 crore over 12-18 months; water O&M 5-15 years (about 10 years average), renewable O&M 5-12 years for EPC and 25 years for IPP.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify raw material impact and segment EBITDA margins; any price pass-through on new orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Water 21-22%, renewables 15-18%, blended 19-20%, around 20% for the year. Raw material impact about 1-2% of topline; WPI/CPI-linked price variation covers part, with some increase absorbed in EPC pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Wind revenue contribution and renewable EPC vs O&M split?
qa_highlights.answer: Wind (Suyog Urja) contributed INR80 crore of INR359 crore Q1 revenue; renewable execution order book about INR2,000 crore and O&M/IPP about INR1,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Peak debt, bidding pipeline and exit FY27 order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 renewables saw no margin downside; pipeline of about INR3,000 crore under evaluation plus INR6,000-7,000 crore being bid; renewables not being pushed aggressively; wind EPC INR600-800 crore targeted. No peak debt figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Unbilled revenue and working capital status; will operating cash flow turn positive in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital described as still bloated and funds flow slow, with management expecting a healthier cash flow position when cash flow numbers come out in September. Service concession receivables take about INR85 crore out of OCF; OCF turning positive is hoped for but not guaranteed. JJM exposure about INR150-160 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Suyog Urja tranche payments and FY27 revenue and profit contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisition valued INR311 crore: INR111 crore paid, INR100 crore second tranche after FY27 (around July) subject to KPIs, third tranche after FY28. Suyog FY27 revenue expectation INR400-450 crore at 15-16% EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 revenue (about INR360 crore) below the run-rate implied by historical seasonality, and is the INR2,000 crore guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is on target as guided at about 20% of the year; a significant jump is expected from Q3 when NTPC BESS (930 MWh) procurement starts. Guidance of INR2,000 crore revenue and INR260-270 crore PAT reaffirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 revenue reach INR2,500-3,000 crore, and what about desalination and overseas projects?
qa_highlights.answer: INR2,000 crore is the threshold guidance, with about 50% conversion of the INR2,700 crore water execution book implying INR1,300-1,350 crore. Overseas bids submitted; desalination projects being pursued; operations in 17 states; ZLD and CBG projects under way.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook beyond FY27 and margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a bare-minimum growth target of 25-30% a year while maintaining healthy margins, and said it will avoid low-margin projects. Margin upside possible but guidance based on minimum levels.

capex_capacity: Suyog Urja acquisition total value INR311 crore: first tranche INR111 crore paid; second tranche INR100 crore after FY27 (around July), based on KPIs; third tranche after FY28, funded by internal accruals and some debt.
Renewables: INR75 crore invested in the renewable segment so far; management framed it against an expected renewable profit of INR60-70 crore.

Five HAM projects now in portfolio (two new Varanasi projects, INR256.9 crore total, 18-month construction plus 15-year O&M); one completed, one near completion at Mathura, Saharanpur at 3 of 8 milestones; two new HAM projects expected to start construction in October-November.
Team size grew from about 900 at IPO to about 2,300 currently, ahead of execution ramp-up.
NTPC BESS order of 930 MWh: material procurement to start in Q3 FY27, expected to drive a significant revenue jump from Q3.
Operating footprint in 17 states; first JJM commissioning expected by October, with five JJM projects commissioned one by one and O&M of 10 years to follow.
demand_pricing: Total order book approx INR6,721 crore: water and wastewater INR3,694 crore (INR2,696 crore execution, INR998 crore O&M); renewables and BESS INR3,027 crore (INR1,948 crore execution, INR1,079 crore IPP and O&M).

Q1 FY27 new wins include INR113 crore EPC and O&M from Sardar Sarovar Narmada Nigam (Gujarat), INR207.5 crore renewable contract via Suyog Urja, and INR256.9 crore in two Varanasi HAM projects (INR130 crore Lohta 60 MLD STP; INR126.8 crore DDU Nagar 45 MLD STP).
Water execution timeline 18-24 months; renewable execution 12-18 months; water O&M tail 5-15 years (average about 10 years), with O&M expected at about INR100 crore topline and 3-5% of value.

Pipeline: bids submitted and under evaluation about INR3,000 crore; further INR6,000-7,000 crore of water/wastewater projects where bids are being invited or submitted; wind EPC pipeline INR800 crore with INR500-600 crore more expected.
FY27 order inflow target about INR2,500 crore at about 20% strike rate; INR256 crore won so far.
Quarterly revenue split expected at about 20% for Q1-Q3 and about 40% in Q4; Q1 revenue about INR359 crore vs FY27 guidance INR2,000 crore.
Pricing: raw material price impact about 1-2% of topline; tenders carry WPI/CPI-linked price variation clause, but some increase must be absorbed in EPC pricing.
Segment margin guidance: water 21-22% EBITDA; renewables 15-18%; Suyog Urja EBITDA 15-16%, PAT about 12%+; blended 19-20%; PAT margin about 13.5-14% guidance.
risks_watch: Margin compression: Q1 EBITDA margin 21.07% vs 26.65% YoY; FY27 guidance cut to 21-22% (water) and blended 19-20%, with raw material cost and partial price-variation recovery uncertain.
Working capital: management said the working capital cycle remains bloated and government cash flows have slowed; OCF turning positive is not guaranteed; watch September cash flow disclosure.

Execution conversion: FY26 revenue was flat against an opening order book of about INR1,200 crore, and FY27 needs about 50% conversion of the INR2,700 crore water book; order inflow of INR2,500 crore at 20% strike rate depends on pipeline awards.
Rising employee cost (about 7% of revenue in Q1) and finance cost (about 4%) versus guided normalisation to 5-5.5% and 3-3.5%.
Suyog Urja deferred consideration: INR100 crore second tranche after FY27 subject to KPIs, plus debt funding; the acquisition-linked profit contribution depends on hitting targets.
Quarterly back-loading: about 40% of FY27 revenue expected in Q4; NTPC BESS procurement starting Q3 is critical to the target.
key_quotes: Our EBITDA margins right now are 21% at the standalone level and we are happy to confirm that our EBITDA margins have remained at the same level of 21% even at the console level where it is getting consolidated with the business of renewables.

The position still I will say is bloated. But we are hoping since the funds are already allocated, even in the last quarter we had confirmed the movement of funds should be there, but it remained slow.

544305|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 EBITDA positive at INR 174 mn (5.9% margin) and PAT INR 44 mn; FY26 EBITDA still negative INR 52 mn after heavy reinvestment.
544305|2026-03.overview: MobiKwik reported back-to-back EBITDA- and PAT-positive quarters in Q3 and Q4 FY26, with Q4 total income of INR 2,960 mn (+6% YoY) and contribution margin of 46% versus 23% a year earlier. FY26 EBITDA improved to negative INR 52 mn from negative INR 794 mn, and full-year PAT narrowed to negative INR 621 mn from negative INR 1,215 mn. Management said it is deliberately reinvesting core payments and lending profits (about INR 55 crore spent in FY26) into four growth engines: offline and online merchant payments, an NBFC, and AI. Analysts pressed on the gap between UPI-led GMV growth and flat payments revenue, on the timing of breakeven for merchant businesses, and on NBFC rollout.

from negative INR 794 mn in FY25
from negative INR 1,215 mn in FY25

segments.name: Payments (wallet, UPI, recharge and bill payments)
segments.commentary: Wallet is the largest in India by GTV with about 20% share as of March 2026. Customer-initiated UPI transactions grew 170% YoY vs industry 26%. Recharge and bill payments GMV reached INR 269 bn in FY26 (2.2x). Payments revenue has been flat for 4-5 quarters as UPI mix rises and gross take rate falls.

segments.name: Lending (digital credit, LSP model)
segments.commentary: Management cited a 59% gross margin in Q4, with super-prime share of disbursements up from 10% to 32% and repeat loans up from 20% to 63.5%. Lending spread was 5.3% (analyst cited 5.4%); management sees 4.5% as more sustainable, with 4% as the sweet spot. FY26 digital credit GMV was about INR 3,200 crore.

segments.name: Merchant payments (offline and Zaakpay online)
segments.commentary: Offline targets 5x device scale-up for 10x revenue by FY28; Zaakpay targets 10x GMV by FY28. Both are guided to reach EBITDA breakeven by FY28. Merchant partners stand at 4.9 mn.

guidance_outlook: GMV growth of 30-35% expected in both payments and lending in FY27 (per management).
Digital credit GMV growth of 30-35% in FY27.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided in the same broad range as the current ~5%, with better unit margins offset by higher investment.
Merchant-business investment of roughly INR 55 crore in FY26 expected to be similar in FY27; investment to continue for at least 18 months.
Fixed costs at INR 115-120 crore per quarter; 15-20% increase expected in FY27 from depreciation and device-distribution people costs.
Payments margin guided at 12-15 bps mid-to-long term; management advised against modelling 16 bps over two years.
NBFC timeline: move LSP business into a wholly owned subsidiary in 2-3 months, set up NBFC in 3-6 months, launch co-lending disbursals in 6-9 months.
Target of 10-20% of the market leader's size in offline merchant categories in 18-24 months; Zaakpay 10x GMV in about 18-24 months.
Management expects payments revenue to follow GMV growth from the next few quarters once PPI-over-UPI MDR is implemented.
capex_capacity: Merchant device investment is capitalised and depreciated; other merchant spend (people, product) is expensed through P&L. INR 55 crore total FY26 investment excludes device capex.
Depreciation rising as merchant devices are deployed.

NBFC to be funded by parent capital infusion into the wholly owned NBFC subsidiary, subject to board and shareholder approval.
demand_pricing: Payments revenue flat for 4-5 quarters despite GMV growth: UPI mix dilutes gross take rate, and some low-margin categories were added.
PPI-over-UPI MDR has not yet been implemented; management expects it to add revenue.
UPI credit and RuPay credit transactions generate MDR; plain bank UPI does not.
Net payments margin remains positive; gross take rate has moderated in existing businesses.
Lending: digital credit GMV growth was subdued QoQ as the company prioritised quality over volume.
Offline merchant focus on three categories: organised retail (mid-market and above), petrol and oil/gas, and small mom-and-pop stores. Zaakpay targets education, government and BBPS categories.

qa_highlights.question: What is being done to fix payments revenue growth, and is there long-term guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue lags GMV because growth is UPI-led and PPI-over-UPI MDR has not yet come; consistent revenue growth is expected in the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How much investment is needed in the merchant business over two years, and is it through P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 55 crore was invested in FY26, and a similar range is expected in FY27. Everything except device capitalisation hits P&L, and IPO proceeds are being used for it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the merchant breakeven timeline move from 3-4 quarters to FY28, and what does baseline profitability mean?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed costs were raised deliberately to build new businesses; without the merchant investment FY26 EBITDA would have been about INR 50 crore. Management aims to stay PAT-positive while reinvesting, with FY27 EBITDA hypothetically between 1x and 2x of the reinvested base.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ex-UPI GTV growing above 30% while payments revenue is flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited gross take rate moderation and mix shift to lower-margin categories; the non-UPI revenue growth has been below expectations.

qa_highlights.question: What are the NBFC timelines and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: LSP business moves to a subsidiary in 2-3 months, NBFC set up in 3-6 months, and co-lending disbursals launch in 6-9 months. Parent will infuse capital after board and shareholder approval.

qa_highlights.question: Why is working capital debt still INR 261 crore when cash is INR 434 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Part of the cash is still IPO proceeds not yet accessible; the short-term lines cover weekend and holiday settlement gaps when bank funds are delayed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 5.3% lending margin sustainable and what is the payments margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management prefers 4.5% as more sustainable and 4% as the sweet spot, and guided 12-15 bps for payments mid-to-long term, though Q4 ran above that.

qa_highlights.question: What fixed-cost increase is expected next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed costs are INR 115-120 crore per quarter; a 15-20% increase is expected in FY27.

Gross take-rate compression from UPI mix and low-margin categories.

Working capital dependence (INR 261 crore) and finance cost reduction; IPO proceeds still being drawn down.

544305|2026-06.headline: MobiKwik posted Q1 FY27 PAT of INR76 million, its third straight profitable quarter, with payments GMV up 50% YoY to INR587 billion.
544305|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as its most profitable quarter yet, with PAT of INR76 million and EBITDA of INR158 million, up INR470 million YoY. Payments gross profit rose 31% YoY to INR777 million and financial services gross profit grew 5.6x to INR433 million. Lending disbursements dipped in Q1, while payments revenue fell as card-linked categories were paused under regulatory pressure and UPI (near-zero take rate) grew. Management targets full-year PAT of about INR400 million and EBITDA of about INR750 million including other income, and is scaling a merchant acquiring business that is still loss-making.

financial_highlights.change: Swing of INR495 million vs Q1 FY26; up from INR45 million in Q4 per management
+50% YoY; 14th straight quarter of payments GMV growth

segments.name: Payments
segments.commentary: Gross profit INR777 million (+31% YoY) on revenue of about INR208 crore versus INR59 crore a year ago on similar revenue; net payments take rate 13-15 bps in recent quarters, guided at 12-14 bps long term. Zaakpay (payment gateway) GMV INR25.6 billion; revenue not disclosed.

segments.name: Financial services (lending)
segments.commentary: Gross profit INR433 million (5.6x YoY). Net financial services margin 4.1% in Q3, 5.4% in Q4 and 5.9% in Q1; management guides 4.5-5.5% long term. About 18% of gross lending revenue came from write-backs on past books (about INR16 crore).

segments.name: Merchant (Zaakpay online + offline acquiring)
segments.commentary: Merchant GMV INR125 billion, up 17% QoQ. Business is loss-making with an expected full-year burn of INR50-60 crore; breakeven targeted for FY28. Management expects 10x ramp over two years.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 PAT target of about INR40 crore (INR400 million) and EBITDA of about INR75 crore (INR750 million) including other income; management said it is 'fairly confident'.
Lending disbursements to rise from about INR700 crore per quarter to INR1,000 crore per quarter; management says Q2 is already running at that rate.
Consumer payments revenue expected to grow 5-6% QoQ; merchant revenue expected to grow about 25% QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Why has quarterly revenue growth been muted over the last seven to eight quarters, and what levers will accelerate it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 was spent re-stabilising businesses and Q1 is the baseline. Lending disbursements are to rise from about INR700 crore to INR1,000 crore per quarter via new lending partners, pre-approved offers to about 96 million engaged users, and an AI funnel engine. Card-linked categories were paused in Q4 and Q1 and are to be relaunched, while merchant revenue is to scale.

qa_highlights.question: Non-UPI GMV trend and whether take rate is falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-UPI GMV rose to INR317 billion from INR300 billion in Q4 (about 6%). Management said card-linked categories with higher take rates de-grew under regulatory pressure. Net payments take rate guidance remains 12-14 bps long term, at gross profit level, versus 13-15 bps in recent quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Merchant roll-out: what numbers and how should it be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Merchant GMV was INR125 billion, up 17% QoQ from INR107 billion. Management targets a 10x ramp over two years, expects merchant revenue to grow about 25% QoQ and consumer payments revenue 5-6% QoQ. Merchant counts, device counts and merchant revenue were withheld as too early. About INR25 crore of IPO proceeds remains for devices, and no more is expected to be needed in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Own NBFC timing and FLDG share of lending?
qa_highlights.answer: Digital lending transfer to a wholly-owned subsidiary is expected to close in August 2026 after shareholder approval on 2 July, then CoR will be sought; own NBFC lending is 'still some time away'. As of Q1, 32% of lending was pure distribution and 68% FLDG, with a possible 40/60 mix by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance of INR750 million EBITDA and INR400 million PAT still valid after Q1 operating EBITDA ex other income of about INR80 million?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident in the baseline and expects about INR400 million PAT for FY27 with some growth, plus about INR750 million EBITDA including other income. Q1 PAT of INR76 million annualises to about INR302 million, and improving by INR20-30 million per quarter would reach about INR400 million.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lending disbursements fall in Q1, and what is the top-three lender concentration?
qa_highlights.answer: Top-three lender concentration was cut from about 91% in Q2-Q3 FY26 to 87% in Q4 and 71% in Q1, with two new partners added in Q1. Management said the digital lending transfer to the subsidiary consumed focus in Q1, and it is already at the INR1,000 crore run rate in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did wallet transactions grow 68% but GMV only 24%, and is PPI-on-UPI monetised?
qa_highlights.answer: Users shifted to lower-ticket wallet-on-UPI payments and card-linked pauses removed high-ticket transactions. No MDR is earned on PPI-on-UPI although RBI mandated it; NPCI has not rolled it out in about 2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Merchant business burn, breakeven timing and employee cost trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Merchant burn for FY27 is capped at INR50-60 crore (about INR15-16 crore in Q1); breakeven targeted for FY28. Employee benefit expense rose to INR53 crore from INR46 crore in Q4, and merchant-related manpower cost may grow 5-15% YoY, linked to breakeven.

We are targeting full-year PAT profitability for this financial year, and Q1 is of course the baseline.
So yes, INR75 crores EBITDA and INR40 crores PAT is the kind of numbers that we are fairly confident of achieving.
It's too early. Apart from the GMV for merchant, we are not revealing any other numbers yet.

544306|2026-06.headline: Sai Life Sciences Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR553 crore, with CRO up 26% and CDMO up 6%; management guides to a stronger H2.
544306|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR553 crore against INR496 crore a year earlier, up about 12% YoY. CRO (about 40% of revenue) grew about 26% YoY, while CDMO (about 60%) grew about 6%. Management said the quarter was in line with expectations and reiterated a stronger H2 as new capacity comes online, with the Discovery facility already commissioned and sold out and Bidar production block 1 due in H2/Q3. Management reaffirmed the mid-term revenue growth guidance of 15-20% and EBITDA margin of 28-30%, and FY27 capex of INR1,100-1,300 crore.

financial_highlights.change: about +12% YoY vs INR496 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: CRO / Discovery
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 26% YoY. About 65% of customers now use integrated discovery services, mainly biotech; a pilot with a large pharma converted to a long-term high-volume discovery chemistry partnership. Discovery capacity came on stream in Q1 and is already sold out.

segments.name: CDMO / CMC
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 6% YoY, described as lumpy. Portfolio is 33 active commercial molecules and 14 late-phase molecules. Three of the four commercial contracts expected this year were added in Q1; management said three are commercial supplies, primary supplier in about two of three (anecdotal).

guidance_outlook: Mid-term (3-5 year) revenue growth guidance of 15-20% reiterated; management said guidance should be viewed over a longer horizon, not quarterly.
EBITDA margin range of 28-30% reiterated.
H2 FY27 expected to be stronger than H1, with capacity coming on stream by end-Q2 or early Q3; management referenced a 40/60 historical H1/H2 split, with FY26 at about 48/52.
FY27 capex guidance INR1,100-1,300 crore unchanged; no FY28 capex guidance yet.
Target of about 1,150 KL capacity by FY27 reconfirmed.
Expects to convert at least two large pharma customers to integrated models in FY27.
Formulation (oral solids up to Phase 2) expected to be operational in about six months, within the current fiscal year.
capex_capacity: Discovery capacity came on stream in Q1 FY27 and is sold out, ahead of the one-to-1.5-year fill timeline management had assumed.
Bidar: two production blocks of 225 KL each (450 KL total); first block due for completion and operation in H2/Q3 FY27, on track.
First dedicated peptide development lab coming online shortly for a top-tier pharma company; GMP pilot-scale peptide facility coming online soon for clinical supply.
Commercial peptide manufacturing at a new greenfield site near Hyderabad expected to be operational in 2028; groundbreaking planned. Peptide spend to end-2028 likely below INR300 crore.
XDC Center of Excellence close to opening; ADC pilot-scale space under build.
demand_pricing: Management said Indian outsourcing demand is strengthened by geopolitical concerns and IP worries, with customers using India for diversification.

FTE (dedicated team) model: one top-tier pharma FTE relationship expanded from small scale to a sizable dedicated contract running end-to-end from discovery to commercial; another large pharma process development FTE deal expected to close by end-Q2, with work from Q3.

Pipeline sourced via three routes: biotech molecules acquired by pharma partners, molecules transferred from acquirers, and FTE-led progression. Five of six late-phase molecules added in 15 months came via large pharma FTE relationships.
Phase 3 pipeline: one customer approved in FY26, two more with regulatory milestones in FY27, one expected Q2 FY28.
Modalities: about 4-5% of revenue from new modalities, all in development and discovery, none in commercial. Peptide work is mainly early-stage discovery.
Sai works with 19 of the top 25 pharma companies. Five FDA-approved molecules in calendar 2025 involved Sai in discovery, development or commercial manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: Has the shift to integrated CRDMO and big pharma FTE engagements accelerated this calendar year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is still early, with relationships growing from one service at a time; FTE model started about 15 months ago and acceleration is seen mainly in scale and scope.

qa_highlights.question: Is the H2-weighted FY27 guidance due to capacity, given the historical split?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said FY26 was about 48/52 H1/H2 versus a historical 40/60, and capacity additions are behind the stronger H2 call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex threshold and what would cause a slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal hurdle rates are set above the company's ROCE/ROE targets. Capacity-addition capex can be slowed if demand slows; capability-building capex is harder to defer absent severe circumstances.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide 15-20% when the pipeline is large and recent quarters slowed?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is framed over 3-5 years given lumpiness; management said it is not constraining growth and FY26 grew close to 30%, with quarterly revenue driven by delivery timing.

qa_highlights.question: Is the AI initiative the same as the high-throughput experimentation platform?
qa_highlights.answer: No. HTE generates more data points per experiment; the AI initiative targets non-value-added chemist and operator work, with an update expected before year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the commercial profile of the four new commercial contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Three of four are commercial supplies, described as decently sized by value; one is a lower-volume product. Primary supplier in about two of three, anecdotally.

rows.why: FY27 capex of INR1,100-1,300 crore is heavy and FY28 capex guidance not yet given; the Hyderabad peptide greenfield site (operational 2028) has a groundbreaking planned, with peptide spend to end-2028 below INR300 crore.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated 15-20% mid-term revenue growth and 28-30% EBITDA margin without raising them, and framed guidance over 3-5 years rather than quarterly; Q1 CDMO growth only 6%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: CDMO grew only about 6% YoY and is lumpy; H2 recovery depends on Bidar block 1 and formulation start-up timelines, and formulation is not yet commercial.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Formulation (oral solids up to Phase 2) expected operational in about six months, within FY27; XDC Centre of Excellence close to opening and a dedicated peptide development lab coming online shortly.

rows.label: Integrated CRDMO conversions of large pharma
rows.why: Management expects to convert at least two large pharma customers to integrated models in FY27; one FTE deal expected to close by end-Q2 with work from Q3, and ~65% of customers now use integrated discovery services.

rows.when: end-Q2 FY27 close, work from Q3 FY27
rows.why: Another large pharma process development FTE deal is expected to close by end-Q2, and three of four commercial contracts were added in Q1 (three commercial supplies, primary supplier in about two of three, anecdotal).

rows.why: One Phase 3 customer approved in FY26, two more with regulatory milestones in FY27, and one expected Q2 FY28, supporting future CDMO commercial volumes.

tone.note: Management was confident on the FTE model, Discovery sold out and H2 capacity ramp, but cautious on quarterly CDMO lumpiness, customer-level revenue and capex phasing beyond FY27; analysts pushed on why 15-20% guidance holds given slowing recent quarters and the 6% CDMO growth.

544307|2026-03.headline: Vishal Mega Mart Q4 FY26 revenue rose 22.2% to INR 3,114 crore with same-store sales growth of 13.2%, while management flagged input inflation from May.
544307|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 3,114 crore (+22.2% YoY), with same-store sales growth (SSSG) accelerating to 13.2% from 11% for FY26. Adjusted EBITDA margin widened to 8.8% from 8.2% and PAT rose 45.9% to INR 168 crore. Management attributed the strength to a consumption uptick after income tax and GST cuts, plus heavier promotions ahead of the spring/summer season. Management said input inflation, mainly petroleum-linked materials and fabric, began in late April and May, and it committed to keep private-brand discounts to third-party brands at least at current levels (about 40% on apparel).

segments.name: Apparel (fast fashion, biggest category)
segments.commentary: Q4 SSSG by price point: entry 11.1%, mid-price 13.6%, fashionable (top 2-3 price points) 14.7%. Management said fashion was the fastest-growing segment in Q4 and FY26.

segments.name: Private brands
segments.commentary: 74.1% of FY26 revenue; two brands above INR 1,000 crore and six more above INR 500 crore revenue.

segments.name: Quick commerce
segments.commentary: Expanded to 745 stores across 505 cities; registered users reached 1.3 crore.

segments.name: Small format stores
segments.commentary: 13 stores in total, 3 opened in Q4 FY26; management said store EBITDA and revenue per sq ft match large-format stores.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 guidance given; management said it is difficult to model the West Asia situation and fuel price impact.
Private-brand discount to market leaders on apparel (about 40%) to remain at least the same, with a possible wider gap.
Store expansion will not slow; management said it aims to open more stores where practical.
Input inflation (petroleum-linked plastics, polyester, detergent inputs) is starting to flow through; full impact expected in the balance of May and June.
Fabric prices rising about 10-11%, per management's current range for suppliers.
Working capital cycle expected to stay at FY26 levels, per the CFO.
capex_capacity: Store count 795 at March 2026 after 105 openings in FY26 (25 in Q4); presence in 535 cities after adding 77 cities in FY26.
47 of the 105 FY26 openings were in South India (Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka); 5 in Gujarat and 3 in Maharashtra.
Trading area 1.34 crore sq ft at March 2026.
Karnataka store areas reduced in many stores; sales per sq ft has risen and is now in line with the national average, per CFO.
Lease escalation about 15% every three years (about 5% a year), per CFO.
demand_pricing: Management attributed Q4 SSSG acceleration to a consumption uptick after income tax and GST rate cuts, plus extra investment in growth and promotions.
FY26 SSSG of 11% split: 7 points from new customers and transactions, 2 points from more items per customer, 2 points from higher price points.

Pricing is set by price point: no uniform price increases; opening and low price points are protected, higher fashion price points get more room, and management aims for price increases to be volume-neutral.
Suppliers facing gas and labour shortages earlier in the period; management said vendor supply is improving but labour has not fully returned.
Competition: management believes it is gaining share, citing 7 of the 11 SSSG points coming from new customers; it did not name V2 or V-Mart directly.
Management expects down-trading benefits if demand weakens, given private brands are 30-50% cheaper than third-party brands in food and grocery.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 SSSG acceleration, and was there pre-buying?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a general consumption uptick after income tax and GST cuts, plus higher growth investment in the quarter. It did not frame it as pre-buying.

qa_highlights.question: How will private-label pricing respond to rising leader-brand prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management committed to keep the discount to leader brands at least at 40% for apparel, and to try to widen it if possible.

qa_highlights.question: How did the company handle the cotton inflation of 2021-22?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it took a margin hit then, absorbed much of the increase, and used cost initiatives such as removing poly bags, using gunny bags, shipping shoes without outer cartons, and CAD cutting to reduce waste.

qa_highlights.question: Are price increases neutral, incremental or negative to apparel sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims for neutral, since high-fashion price points show lower elasticity, and it avoids raising opening price points.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dividend policy given strong free cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management deferred to the Board and gave no dividend commitment.

qa_highlights.question: Are the new small-format and newer-state stores performing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Kerala is above average, Gujarat and Maharashtra (6 stores each) are in line with the network, and small-format stores match large-format stores on sales per sq ft and store EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 gross margin compress, and why did working capital improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cleared old spring/summer stock ahead of the April-June season and increased promotions to capture a consumption uptick. The CFO said working capital days are about the same as last year and that is the intended operating level.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for rent and operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said rent rises about 5% a year under lease terms, so double-digit SSSG should keep producing operating leverage. He said Q4 rent looked low because of lease renewals in Q4 FY25.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (petroleum derivatives, plastics, polyester, fabric at 10-11%) reaching shelf prices from May-June, and its effect on SSSG and gross margin.
Q4 gross margin compression linked to promotions; whether promotional intensity stays high into the April-June season.
Geopolitical and crude-price shocks, currency depreciation and possible weak rural demand from a poor monsoon.
Vendor labour and gas availability constraints, which the company says are easing.
Rising competition in apparel from e-commerce and value-fashion players moving into Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.
Dividend policy remains undecided despite strong cash generation.
544307|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and on private-brand resilience, but cautious on the outlook: management repeatedly declined to model the West Asia and fuel-price impact and said the coming months could be challenging. It was evasive on dividend policy, deferring to the Board.
key_quotes: So, it is clearly correlated with crude pricing in that sense.
We will not slow down our expansion at all because we are very excited about the long-term consumption story in this country.
So, our pricing is totally consumer -led.
The coming months and quarters could be challenging. I don't know.

rows.why: No capex guidance or board-approved capex plan was discussed; store roll-out is funded through the existing lease-led model, and no utilisation figure was disclosed.

rows.why: No numerical FY27 guidance was issued, and management's tone on the outlook was cautious, so an upgrade is not signalled.

rows.why: Management said the coming months could be challenging and declined to model West Asia and fuel-price impact; fabric prices are rising 10-11% and input inflation hits shelf from May-June, though no numerical FY27 guidance was given to cut.

rows.why: No new product, brand or category launch was discussed; fashion growth was described only as fastest-growing within existing categories.

rows.label: Volume-neutral price increases
rows.why: Management aims for price increases to be volume-neutral, with higher fashion price points getting more room, while fabric is rising 10-11% and opening price points are protected.

rows.label: Small-format and newer-state stores
rows.why: 13 small-format stores (3 opened in Q4) match large formats on sales per sq ft and store EBITDA, with Kerala above average and Gujarat and Maharashtra (6 stores each) in line with the network.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q4 SSSG of 13.2% and private-brand resilience but cautious on the outlook, declining to model West Asia and fuel-price impact and warning the coming months could be challenging; analysts' questions focused on promotions, gross margin, and private-label pricing, and manage

544307|2026-06.headline: Vishal Mega Mart Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.7% to INR 3,727 crore on 10% same-store sales growth; operating EBITDA margin 10.4%.
544307|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached INR 3,727 crore, up 18.7% YoY, driven by 10% same-store sales growth. Operating EBITDA was INR 387 crore (up 19.3%, margin 10.4% vs 10.3%) and PAT was INR 259 crore (up 25.6%, margin 6.9% vs 6.6%). Gross margin improved to 28.7% from 28.4%, mainly from lower promotional spend rather than price hikes. The company added 27 stores to reach 819 across 559 cities, with management flagging elevated inflation as a demand headwind expected to ease in later quarters.

segments.name: Store network
segments.commentary: 819 stores in 559 cities at June 2026 end after 27 openings in the quarter, including 10 in South India; total trading area 13.8 million sq ft.

segments.name: Small format
segments.commentary: 3 small stores opened in the quarter (16 in total cited); currently run only in UP and Haryana, with a stated opportunity of about 3,000 small-format stores nationally.

segments.name: Private brands
segments.commentary: Contributed 75.2% of revenue; 100% of apparel, about 75% of general merchandise, about 60% by volume of FMCG, and about 50% of kitchen appliances (Tandem brand).

segments.name: Quick commerce
segments.commentary: 767 stores across 520 cities and over 1.4 crore registered consumers; contributes 2-9% of store revenue, at least 5% in most locations; average bill about INR 800; 20% of customers are new to Vishal.

guidance_outlook: Management expects inflation-driven demand impact to taper in subsequent quarters.
Small-format stores to accelerate; current guidance cited as 80 to 100 small-format store additions.
RFID rollout: Delhi NCR stores live; full network rollout expected to slightly exceed one year.
No further price increases planned beyond those already taken, assuming current conditions persist.
Gross margin sustainability depends on current cost structure; management says no significant issue if circumstances hold, but declined to forecast West Asia-linked developments.
Foreign ownership to be capped at 49.99% to keep the company Indian owned and controlled; foreign holding is close to 20% today.
capex_capacity: Store additions: 27 in Q1 FY27 (819 total); small-format openings were slow at 3 in the quarter, with some large-format stores opened alongside.
New format: first pilot store said to be very close to launch, followed by one or two more pilots before a roll-out decision.
RFID: pilot in 2 stores in Delhi NCR, now extended to all Delhi NCR stores; stock counts possible in 4-5 hours, enabling weekly counts.
Minimum wage increases in Haryana, UP, Telangana, Karnataka and others lifted employee cost per sq ft about 13% YoY.
demand_pricing: Same-store sales growth of 10%: new customer acquisition up 8%, existing customer spend up 3%.

Price increases were limited to higher price points and selected categories; opening and mid price points were not raised, and price-sensitive categories such as children's clothing and staple foods were left unchanged.
Highest-priced apparel fashion grew 13.9% same-store sales growth.
Gross margin gain came mainly from lower promotional intensity, with little contribution from price hikes.
Management says no new competitors entered apparel and expansion pace from existing players did not rise sharply this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why is small-format expansion slow when small towns may suit it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said small-format stores were a test phase; they now match larger formats on revenue per sq ft and ROCE, and expansion will accelerate, with UP and Haryana as the only states so far. Large-format stores are still being opened alongside.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin improve despite cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin rose from 28.4% to 28.7%, mainly because promotional spend was lower YoY; prices were held to protect same-store sales, with little price-hike effect.

qa_highlights.question: What is the organisational change and the foreign ownership cap?
qa_highlights.answer: Sashi Gumma replaces Manoj, who is leaving after more than 10 years, in the same role, with no change to the org structure. The 49.99% foreign cap is to stay Indian owned and controlled; it applies because subsidiary Airplaza runs multi-brand retail.

qa_highlights.question: What is quick commerce's contribution and profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Quick commerce contributes 2-9% of store revenue, with most locations at 5% or more; average bill is about INR 800, slightly above offline, and 20% of quick commerce customers are new to Vishal.

qa_highlights.question: Is the rise in employee cost per sq ft structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Gupta said the increase came from significant minimum wage hikes across several states, which is a structural change; management will try to optimise but cannot fully offset it.

qa_highlights.question: What is closing inventory and status of the new format?
qa_highlights.answer: Closing inventory was INR 1,900 crore. The new format is near its first pilot store launch, with one or two more pilots planned before a roll-out decision.

risks_watch: Elevated inflation weighing on demand; management expects easing but gave no firm timeline.
Gross margin sustainability: the gain depends on lower promotions and holding prices; West Asia developments are an open risk.
Structural rise in employee costs from minimum wage increases across several states.
Competitive pressure in apparel from value retailers; management says the competitor set is unchanged, but pace is a watch item.
Leadership change: COO Manoj departs and Sashi Gumma replaces him; further org changes not discussed.
Small-format and RFID roll-outs are gradual; timing and benefits remain to be proven at scale.

Several analyst questions were lost to audio issues and management answered some only partially.
key_quotes: Operating EBITDA was INR 387 crores, which was a growth of 19.3% over last year, and our operating margin (Operating EBITDA margin) improved from 10.3% last year to 10.4% this year.
The fact is that the small format is half the size of a regular format.
But I'm not saying that I can see the future any better than any of us on the West Asia crisis and so on.
Under no circumstances, would we allow a price discount to the market leader become lesser than before.

rows.why: Same-store sales grew 10% in Q1 (new customers +8%, existing customers +3%), and management expects the inflation drag on demand to taper in subsequent quarters, though no firm timeline was given.

rows.why: No explicit revenue or margin guidance was raised; management held its statements on demand easing and small-format additions and gave no numeric year guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.why: A new format's first pilot store is 'very close to launch' with one or two more pilots before a roll-out decision, but no date was given.

rows.label: Structural employee cost rise from minimum wage hikes
rows.why: Employee cost per sq ft rose about 13% YoY across Haryana, UP, Telangana, Karnataka and others; management calls it structural and says it can only partly offset it.

rows.why: Delhi NCR stores are live and stock counts can take 4-5 hours, enabling weekly counts; full rollout is guided to slightly exceed one year.

tone.note: Management was confident on 10% SSG and gross margin gains from lower promotions, but cautious on inflation, West Asia exposure and forward gross margin, and gave no firm dates for the new format or small-format scale-up; some analyst questions were lost to audio issues.

544307|2026-09.headline: Vishal Mega Mart Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14% to INR3,399 crore, but same-store sales growth slowed to 5.4% as festivals shifted into Q3.
544307|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations grew 14% YoY to INR3,399 crore in Q2 FY27, with same-store sales growth (SSSG) of 5.4%, which management says would have been about 9% without the festival shift. Operating EBITDA rose 3.7% to INR262 crore, but margin fell to 7.7% from 8.5% on operating deleverage from low fixed-cost absorption. Adjusted PAT grew 6.4% to INR172 crore, with margin at 5.1% versus 5.4%. Store network reached 844 with 26 gross additions in the quarter, and management said it sees no demand moderation despite inflation.

financial_highlights.change: About 9% adjusted for festival shift (3-4pt impact)

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted PAT (Q2 FY27, after ESOP charges)

financial_highlights.change: About 9.5% adjusted for festival shift (1.5-2pt impact)

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted PAT (H1 FY27, after ESOP charges)

segments.commentary: Core format; management sees room for about 2,000 large-format stores against roughly 850 today, and is prioritising these in all states. 24 of 26 Q2 openings were in Tier 2/3 towns.

segments.name: Small format stores (UP and Haryana pilot)
segments.commentary: 18 small-format stores now, with 2 added in Q2. Management sees potential for upwards of 3,000 stores nationally, but will open them only where large-format opportunity diminishes.

segments.name: Belong & Co. (apparel format)
segments.commentary: First pilot store launched in Q2 targeting young affluent urban shoppers. Management reports footfall-to-purchase conversion above 50% but says it is still learning and has not set a rollout plan.

segments.name: Quick commerce
segments.commentary: Expanded to 781 stores across 532 cities, with over 1.5 crore registered users. Management is increasing advertising and digital spend, starting in Delhi.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for double-digit SSSG for full FY27; Q3 SSSG must be above 10% for the nine months to look double-digit, per the analyst's arithmetic that management accepted.

Gross margin expected to hold YoY in Q3 and Q4 with no material impact from vendor price increases, supported by cost re-engineering; Q2 gross margin was down 30 bps, of which 20 bps came from apparel shift to Q3.
More than 100 new stores targeted for FY27, with the aim of beating the prior year's count every year.
EBITDA margin expected to improve about 30 bps a year over time, assuming double-digit growth against 6-7% store-level cost inflation.
No further price increases planned at the current inflation level, including after the festive season.
Employee cost pressure to ease: management says 8-10% SSSG is enough to offset the higher employee cost from minimum wage increases and new stores.
capex_capacity: Store additions: 26 gross in Q2 and 53 in H1 FY27; total 844 stores. Q2 split: 15 South (6 in Kerala, which now has 35 stores), 5 North, 4 East, 2 Western.
Management said the Kerala store plan was roughly doubled from the original estimate, with smaller stores, because the state is contiguous with no gaps between cities.
Large pilot in Gujarat and Maharashtra with smaller-format stores based on a hypothesis that higher affluence supports higher revenue per sq ft; management called it too early to conclude.
A fully automated large warehouse has been commissioned in North India, with plans for East, then South, then West warehouses.
Retail trading area is 1.41 crore sq ft. Area growth has trailed store growth; management said store size is set by catchment and that it solves for stores first.
demand_pricing: Management said demand is steady with no moderation; Q2 growth came mainly from market-share gain rather than existing customers buying more.
Price increases were taken mainly at higher price points. Opening price points had no increase and mid price points had very few changes.
Revenue mix: about 18-20% from opening price points, about 50% from mid, and about 24-25% from highest price points.
Rentals grew slowly versus area addition, which management attributed to Tier 2/3 expansion, not renegotiation. It expects this gap to continue.

Inventory days were around 65 in the base period versus 59-60 in H1 FY27 per an analyst's calculation; management attributed the gap to the festival shift, with the stock build happening three weeks later this year.
Weather and rainfall were uneven, causing one- to two-day revenue disruptions in some regions, but no regional demand weakness was reported.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 3-4% festive shift carry into Q3, and what Q3 SSSG is needed for a 9% first-half-equivalent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed Q3 SSSG must be above 10% for the nine months to look double-digit, since festivals (Durga Puja, Dussehra, Navratri) moved from September to October.

qa_highlights.question: Will vendor price hikes hurt gross margin in Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost re-engineering has protected gross margin and vendors are already charging higher prices, so no material impact is expected in Q3 or Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise about INR10 crore QoQ, and what SSSG offsets the wage pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the rise reflects incremental ESOP cost and new stores, with minimum wage increases already in Q1. He said 8-10% SSSG is enough to offset the higher employee cost.

qa_highlights.question: How are price increases split across price points, and will there be more?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no further price increases are planned at the current inflation level, including after the festive season, and that opening price points were protected.

qa_highlights.question: How are new store openings split by region, and will Tier 1 entry follow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 24 of 26 Q2 openings were in Tier 2/3 towns and 15 were in South. It is piloting in Maharashtra and Gujarat, with stores in Ahmedabad, Surat, Pune and Baroda.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cash on the balance sheet be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to more stores each year, Belong & Co. and small-format capacity, warehouses in East, South and West India, and quick commerce advertising. It said the board is still evaluating options.

Capital allocation of a large cash balance is under board review, with no decision yet.

544309|2026-03.headline: IKS agreed to acquire TruBridge for ~$557M enterprise value (~3x EBITDA), funded by $565M debt; management guides to ~INR3,000 crore revenue ambition by FY30.
544309|2026-03.overview: IKS signed a definitive merger agreement to acquire TruBridge, a US listed EHR and RCM provider, on April 23, 2026, with closing expected in 90 to 120 days subject to HSR/FTC clearance. TruBridge's trailing CY2025 revenue was $347M ($126M EHR, $221M RCM) and adjusted EBITDA was $69M, versus $186M-plus on a reported-to-adjusted basis cited by management. Management framed the deal as adding an EHR installed base of about 700 clients as a distribution and data moat for IKS's AI-led RCM and clinical workflow platform. The call focused on strategic rationale and TAM, with limited detail on synergy quantum or timing beyond G&A-first sequencing and a four-year timeline.

financial_highlights.change: Equity value $427M; net debt assumed about $130M as of March 31
Reported EBITDA $159M; management-adjusted figure cited as $186M on $698M revenue basis, after removing ESOP ($43M), public-company and one-time costs ($9.5M and others)
5-year term loan at SOFR+275 bps, stepping down to SOFR+175 bps as leverage falls; starting leverage ~3x EBITDA
Management said instantly EPS and PAT accretive; analyst noted a $12M amortisation item not included in the calculation

financial_highlights.value: INR1,000 crore gross cash, net cash INR300 crore

segments.name: TruBridge RCM
segments.commentary: CY2025 RCM revenue $221M; management estimates about 30% of TruBridge's ~700 EHR clients (about $220M RCM spend) already outsource RCM, leaving a white space of roughly $450M.

segments.name: TruBridge EHR
segments.commentary: CY2025 EHR revenue $126M; roughly 2,200 hospitals in the US, with ~700 clients in the 0-50 bed segment where penetration is about 40%, and about 30% penetration across the broader base.

segments.name: TruCode (encoder)
segments.commentary: Management cited a $650M TAM for the encoder tool, which is sold stand-alone; competitors named are 3M and Optum.

segments.name: IKS base business
segments.commentary: IKS has ~17,000 people (2,000 clinically trained, 800-plus technologists); 8 of its 18 service lines are technology-led; the RCM programme ran at about $220M-equivalent spend on about 3,500 FTEs globally in the cited comparison.

guidance_outlook: Management's FY30 north star: about INR3,000 crore revenue (from INR1,000 crore base), a ~31% CAGR from Dec 2025 to Mar 2030; explicitly not formal guidance, with a stated fallback that if not achieved, net debt would be reduced to zero.
Management will not change its aspirations to grow faster than the ~12% US industry rate; it expects to be fairly confident on margin but less certain on growth over 2-3 years.

Synergy timing: G&A synergies first (Q1 post-close learning, Q2 actioning single organisation structure); operational synergies from Q3 post-close; management expects the transformation to take 4-5 years.
Deal closing expected in 90-120 days, subject to HSR approval from the FTC.

Management said the combined TAM for the RCM outsourced market is $3.5-4B against about $1B outsourced today, with serviceable immediate TAM of about $660M (2% take rate on 700-client base of $32B revenue).
capex_capacity: Plan to migrate TruBridge EHR to a cloud-native, AI-first architecture; management believes this will allow penetration of 0-50 bed hospitals and gradual upstream move into 50-200 bed range.
Small language models (SLMs) sitting on top of LLMs are planned to reduce compute and build proprietary self-learning loops for RCM.
Acute RCM offering to be launched; Scribble ambient scribing product to be upgraded into a live encounter co-pilot.
Management described the EHR modernisation as costly for TruBridge, previously a drain on financials, and said IKS would bring agile, cost-optimised development.
demand_pricing: RCM is fragmented: top players hold under 20% share, with 400-plus players and a long tail; US healthcare RCM spend about $1.75-1.8 trillion, of which management's modelled addressable base is around 2% take rate.
Management modelled 2% take rate for RCM outsourcing (versus about 3% today) to conservatively allow for price compression from AI.

Competitors named: Med-Metrix and CorroHealth (RCM BPO); 3M and Optum (encoders); Epic, Athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, NextGen (EHR); Oracle Cerner challenger; MEDITECH; Phreesia, Augmedix, Abridge, Ambience and Microsoft DAX in ambient AI.
Management argues outcome-based pricing will replace per-user SaaS pricing as AI orchestrates tasks; TruBridge's 700-client base is outpatient-heavy (60-70% of volume).
Management said the parent's own attempts at globalising RCM and building a captive in India had not succeeded, and that IKS brings an offshore-enabled model.

qa_highlights.question: How intense is competition in EHR and RCM, and do IKS's learnings help win the segment? Any overlap between RCM and EHR clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EHR is a two-player market with Epic and Oracle Cerner dominant and MEDITECH a challenger; RCM is largely unmanaged, and about 230-240 of TruBridge's ~700 EHR clients already buy RCM, leaving a large white space. The 500-odd clients without RCM and 1,500 non-TruBridge EHR clients are targets.

qa_highlights.question: Can you quantify the initial synergies or the financial outcome of the merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify synergies beyond saying the INR1,000 crore to INR3,000 crore north star is a definition of success, and said the target contains uncertainty for learnings and mistakes; drivers are RCM transformation, globalisation and G&A, with 2,000-plus RCM FTEs in India versus about 1,000 in US.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the deal structured with a 4-year timeline and why is the organic path hard?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said synergy timing is not being given in detail; G&A synergies come first and operational synergies later; organic growth to 700 clients would take about a decade and IKS's global RCM model is a differentiator given earlier failed attempts.

qa_highlights.question: What are the steps post-close and how will IKS retain customers and talent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management outlined Q1 learning, Q2 actioning new structure, Q3 operational synergies; customer retention was called the gold mine of the transaction, along with identifying and retaining key talent in the first quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How does TruBridge's headcount and RCM proposition compare with IKS's model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EHR has low marginal cost and RCM is tech-led and AI-first; RCM spend at large systems runs about 4-5% of revenue and about 7-10% at hospitals, strengthening the outsourcing proposition.

qa_highlights.question: Does IKS plan to compete with the large EHR vendors at scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the intent is not to take EHR to larger hospitals; EHR is for the 0-50 bed segment, with the 50-200 bed range a later addition, and EHR is to be a sticky source of data for RCM.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth guidance change after closing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not changing aspirations of growing faster than the ~12% industry rate, and is less certain on growth than margins over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PAT accretion of about $5M excluding a $12M amortisation item?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the intangible amortisation schedule is being separately evaluated for EHR and RCM relationships, with new asset lives under valuation by experts; the $5M accretion was presented as the highest-possible level, with minor changes possible.

Reported vs adjusted EBITDA gap (CY2025 $159M reported vs $186M adjusted vs $69M cited elsewhere as the adjusted figure) needs reconciliation before valuation work.

544309|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY (12% constant currency) to INR893 crores, with reported EBITDA of INR294 crores at 33% margin.
544309|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue reached about INR893 crores, up 21% YoY and 12% in constant currency, with forex gains neutral versus Q4. Reported EBITDA was INR294 crores (33%); management says it was about 35% after adding back roughly INR20 crores of one-time TruBridge acquisition costs. PAT was INR193-194 crores, up about 28% YoY. TruBridge closed on July 10, 2026, so Q1 figures are legacy IKS only; management reset TruBridge's steady-state revenue to about $300 million a year (from $340 million pre-close) while keeping its roughly $68 million EBITDA, and reaffirmed a FY30 EBITDA True North of at least INR3,000 crores without further dilution beyond ESOPs.
