Epic relationship described as strengthening; TruBridge also collaborating with Epic in rural market.

qa_highlights.question: What organic constant-currency growth is healthy over the medium term, and is margin expansion coming from currency?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin growth is not from currency: revenue grew 12% CC on 4.2% headcount growth; adjusted EBITDA is 35% with neutral forex. Aspiration is 12%+ CC on legacy IKS, not guidance; TruBridge growth to be set in two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How does SLM fit with LLMs, and where does glass-box/explainable AI sit?
qa_highlights.answer: Three SLM approaches: standalone SLMs, LLM-distilled SLMs, and hierarchical SLM-plus-LLM. Explainability comes from knowledge graphs acquired via ARAI. Management would not commit to a 60% token-usage reduction, saying it will emerge over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why acquire TruBridge and what criteria govern acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Chosen because the rural market is large, TruBridge holds 30%+ share as one of two dominant rural EHRs, and its service mix resembles ambulatory. Criteria: strategic thesis first, leverage tolerable relative to EBITDA, and accretive price; $68 million EBITDA bought for ~$550 million.

qa_highlights.question: Is TruBridge's margin of 22-23% fixable, and does the INR3,000 crore target rule out M&A?
qa_highlights.answer: Levers include existing and in-build technology plus offshore human-in-the-loop to restore early-to-mid 30s margins. INR3,000 crores is achievable without another acquisition, but M&A is not ruled out; white space seen as large.

qa_highlights.question: Does Abridge's platform move threaten IKS, and is pricing under pressure in renewals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management respects Abridge but sees ~30 vendors aspiring to platforms and rising competition. Recent five-year deal signed at healthy price; pricing pressure expected but margin leverage maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Is TruBridge still EPS accretive for FY27 after revenue reset?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; EBITDA is unchanged, so management says EPS accretion is absolute and possibly a bit higher than previously expected.

544310|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 57% to INR235.1 crore with EBITDA margin of 25.7%; order book above INR400 crore and FY27 order-booking target of INR500+ crore.
544310|2026-03.overview: Yash Highvoltage reported record FY26 revenue of INR235.1 crore (up 57%), EBITDA of INR60.4 crore (up 75%, 25.7% margin, about 260 bps higher) and PAT of INR37.4 crore (15.9% margin). H2 FY26 revenue was INR135.5 crore (up 46% YoY), with H2 EBITDA of INR37.2 crore and PAT of INR23.7 crore. Order book stood at over INR400 crore on 31 March 2026. Management said the Greenfield RIP facility is in final commissioning, with trial production by end Q2 FY27 and commercial production targeted around October 2026.

segments.commentary: Roughly half of FY26 volumes (about 3,500-3,600 units out of about 7,200); management says OIP is in shortage and deliveries are constrained by capacity, with a brownfield expansion planned.

segments.name: RIP bushings
segments.commentary: Roughly half of FY26 volumes (about 3,500-3,600 units); core is still imported (about 95% per the presentation), and localisation via the Greenfield facility at Jarod is targeted in H2 FY27.

segments.name: HCP / high current
segments.commentary: Balance of volumes in FY26 (combined with OIP, about 15-18% of order book per management).

segments.name: Retrofit
segments.commentary: About 6-7% of overall revenue per management; described as high-margin, with no segment EBITDA disclosed.

segments.name: Sukrut Electric (acquired)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR25-26 crore; management targets INR150-160 crore in 4-5 years (5-6x growth). No Sukrut EBITDA guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new RIP plant contribute revenue in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Trial production by end Q2 FY27; job-work assembly and testing revenue starts earlier, with indigenous RIP commercial revenue expected towards year-end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross and EBITDA margins improve in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited seasonally higher H2 volumes, scale-driven negotiation, customer price recovery, supplier price negotiation and currency hedging; no single specific reason.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of margin compression if lower-kV capacity comes online across the industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins to hold given rising global demand, localisation of RIP cores and export pricing for RIP, and sees input-stage margin expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sukrut revenue potential and EBITDA?

544310|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 95% YoY to INR194.5 crores, with EBITDA margin up to 28.1% and PAT of INR36 crores (18.6% margin).
544310|2026-09.overview: Yash Highvoltage reported H1 FY27 revenue from operations of INR194.5 crores, up 95% YoY, with volume up about 40% to roughly 4,000 bushings. Gross margin expanded to 48.3% from 42.4%, and EBITDA rose 139% to INR55 crores, lifting margin to 28.1% from 23.3%. Order book stood at INR760 crores as of 30 September 2026, against INR400 crores at the start of FY27, with execution over 15 to 18 months. Greenfield capex of INR220 crores is INR106 crores spent so far, with the balance over the next 12 months, and management reiterated the Brownfield expansion completing by Q3.

544311|2026-03.headline: IGI Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue and EBITDA each grew 21% YoY to INR 3,686 mn and INR 2,360 mn, with volumes up 16% to 3.64 mn reports.
544311|2026-03.overview: Q4 (Jan–Mar 2026) was the first quarter reported after the switch from calendar to financial year, so the 15-month period (Jan 2025–Mar 2026) is the main comparison basis. Growth was led by lab-grown diamonds (LGD +35%) and LGD jewelry (+29%), while natural diamond jewelry fell 19% on gold and silver price volatility. The AGL acquisition (closed 30 Jan 2026) contributed about 2 pts to revenue and 3 pts to EBITDA growth in the quarter. Management guided to 15% revenue growth and 20% EBITDA growth for FY27 and said margins would be held at last year's levels.

qa_highlights.question: Has LGD and ND pricing remained stable, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: No structural pricing changes in Q4. Mix is an outcome rather than a driver, and the company focuses on the growth of each segment.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the decline in natural diamond jewelry, and what is the US leadership progress?
qa_highlights.answer: The decline is attributed to gold and silver price increases and volatility in India. A new US leader has been in place for 3–4 months and the sales team is being strengthened.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs not rise after the gemologist hiring plan, and how do exports square with the growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost rose 16% QoQ as costs built up. Management said export values in rupees or dollars understate volume, since LGD carats have roughly doubled while value per carat has fallen.

544311|2026-06.headline: IGI Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 23% YoY to INR 3,708 million and EBITDA 29% to INR 2,238 million, with 60.4% margin.

Group EBITDA rose 29% to INR 2,238 million and margin expanded 270 bps to 60.4%, while PAT grew 31% to INR 1,657 million. India standalone growth was slower on EBITDA (15%) because of commission payouts to overseas subsidiaries, front-loaded IPL sponsorship and headcount additions. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 15% revenue and 20% EBITDA growth, with AGL adding a couple of percentage points on top.

544311|2026-09.headline: IGI Q2 FY27 revenue rose 31% to INR 3,980 million and management now expects FY27 to beat its 15% revenue and 20% EBITDA guidance.
544311|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 was the company's best quarter by volume, revenue, EBITDA and profit, with 4.35 million reports issued (up 26%). Revenue from operations reached INR 3,980 million (up 31%), EBITDA INR 2,445 million (up 39%, margin 61.4%) and PAT INR 1,858 million (up 43%). H1 revenue grew 27%, EBITDA 34% and PAT 37%. Management said H2 will keep outperforming, but did not give a new numeric target. India standalone EBITDA margin fell about 340 bps to 69.5% due to people, marketing and commission spend.

financial_highlights.change: +4% YoY; c.8% QoQ growth in realisation cited
89% of EBITDA, 118% of PAT; working capital release c.INR 662 million
as of quarter end; spoken figure corrected in a note
down from peak of c.INR 2,885 million

segments.name: Lab-grown diamond (LGD) loose certification
segments.commentary: Consolidated LGD revenue grew 37% in Q2 and 31% in H1, at INR 2,111 million in Q2 versus INR 2,095 million in Q1. Loose LGD certification volumes grew 37%.

segments.name: LGD jewellery certification
segments.commentary: Grew 47% in Q2 and 46% in H1. Management cited growth in Europe, Latin America and Australia alongside the US.

segments.name: Natural diamond certification
segments.commentary: Natural loose certification grew 8% in Q2 (up 5% QoQ) and 7% in H1. Natural jewellery certification grew only 3% in the quarter.

segments.name: Gemstones and other certification (incl. AGL)
segments.commentary: Grew 331% in Q2 and 261% in H1, largely from the AGL consolidation since January. AGL added about 3% to group revenue growth in Q2 and H1.

segments.name: Overseas subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Subsidiary revenue grew 49% in Q2; 31% excluding AGL. Overseas certification revenue grew 31% without AGL.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance from May was 15% revenue growth and 20% EBITDA growth. Management now says it expects to outperform this for the full year, similar to H1 (revenue +27%, EBITDA +34%), but gave no new numeric target.
Management said no LGD slowdown is expected in coming quarters, citing grower capacity additions. Natural diamond business is expected to keep momentum for the next two quarters.
October trends were described as rock solid, with Diwali on 8 November 2026 versus 20 October 2025, which shifts some festive stocking into October.
Capital allocation order: growth investment first, then M&A, then dividends. Dividend decisions are made by the Board with each results set.
Management expects EBITDA growth to keep outpacing revenue growth through operating leverage, but did not give a steady-state margin figure.
capex_capacity: Large Indian growers are adding reactors and doubling capacity within 3 years, per management; supply is described as at its base rather than its peak.
Operations started in Italy this year, Saudi Arabia is being prepared, and a company was set up in Botswana in September.
AI-based work allocation and scheduling is now in use in labs, letting the same team grade more stones faster without changing grading standards.
AGL colour-stone methods are being rolled out in IGI's other labs, with dedicated setups planned for large customers. Global expansion of AGL services is planned but locations were not disclosed.
demand_pricing: Lab-grown wholesale prices have stabilised in the INR 118-120 range per management's Investor Day deck. Certification costs 2-3% of retail price.

Q2 ARP rose 4% YoY to INR 891: AGL added 2%, and the base business added 2% from a higher LGD mix (54% vs 52%). Sequentially, ARP fell about 12% on a lower LGD loose mix (down 4%) and a higher jewellery mix.
Natural diamond buyers are delaying purchases due to high and volatile gold prices.
Management said 4Cs grading remains the reporting standard and that it sees no demand shift to simplified classification. It said there are no printing rights for certificates granted to anyone.

qa_highlights.question: Is the LGD revenue surge a pre-festive stocking effect, and will Q3 taper?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LGD revenue has been steady at about INR 2,100 million in Q1 and Q2 and expects no slowdown, citing grower capacity additions. Natural growth is expected to pick up, with traction starting and momentum expected to continue for two more quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Should guidance be raised given H1 overshoot?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 will outperform the 15% revenue and 20% EBITDA guidance, similar to H1. It did not give a new number, but confirmed when asked that H2 growth would be above the original guidance.

qa_highlights.question: How will the surplus cash be used: M&A or higher dividends?
qa_highlights.answer: Priority is growth investment first (Italy, Saudi Arabia), then M&A, then dividends. The September interim dividend was INR 2.55 per share.

qa_highlights.question: Is there grading inconsistency at IGI, and are the top Surat manufacturers printing certificates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied giving printing rights to anyone. It said grading involves multiple checks, is ISO accredited for 18 years, and that there is no gap versus other labs.

qa_highlights.question: Does the AI push allow smaller labs to compete cheaply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IGI's image dataset from c.4.5 million certificates a quarter is hard to replicate and is used to build its AI and ML capability, improving turnaround times.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin in India fall and when will the investments pay off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the India margin drop of about 340 bps to leadership hiring, marketing and commission spend. It gave no timeline for payback, but said the group margin was 60.1% for FY26, 60.4% in Q1 and 61.4% in Q2.

risks_watch: Natural diamond certification growth of 8% lags LGD, and natural jewellery grew only 3%. Watch whether festive-season recovery materialises.
India standalone EBITDA margin fell to 69.5% from 72.8%. Watch whether the people and marketing spend yields a return.
Diwali timing shift means some Q2 festive demand was pulled from Q3 by September stocking. Watch Q3 for payback.
AGL integration: gemstone growth is driven by acquisition and the organic base is not disclosed. Watch the AGL contribution and the global rollout.
Grading consistency questions were raised by a市场 participant and a Surat source. Management denied them. Monitor for any disputes or customer complaints.
544311|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth and tailwinds, but evasive on quantifying the new FY27 target and on Surat grading and printing-rights questions. Management pushed back on pricing and competition questions with general statements rather than data.

We expect to keep outperforming for the full year as well, similar to the H1 delivery.
We don't anticipate any slowdown as far as lab-grown business is concerned for the coming quarters as well.

rows.why: No new product, brand or molecule launch was discussed beyond the AGL colour-stone methods being rolled out to other labs.

rows.why: Italy operations started this year, Saudi Arabia is being prepared and a Botswana company was set up in September, and overseas subsidiary revenue grew 49% in Q2 (31% excluding AGL).

544314|2026-03.headline: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue rose 59.7% YoY to INR 1,169.2 crores as Punjab ramped up; management guides FY27 consolidated EBITDA north of INR 500 crores.
544314|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue grew 3% YoY to INR 752.8 crores with EBITDA up 16.9% to INR 82.5 crores and margin at 11%. Consolidated Q4 revenue of INR 1,169.2 crores and EBITDA of INR 94.4 crores (8.1% margin) reflect the first full quarters of Punjab Phase 1 ramp-up, which management says reached full capacity only at end-March 2026. Consolidated FY26 PAT was INR 77.3 crores, weighed down by higher depreciation and finance cost after Punjab capitalisation. Management guided FY27 consolidated revenue of INR 5,600-5,700 crores and EBITDA north of INR 500 crores, with Phase 2 at Punjab targeted for end-FY27.

segments.commentary: Phase 1 ramp-up completed end-March 2026 after running a quarter late; Q4 utilisation guided at 80-85%. Targets about INR 2,600 crores revenue from Q2 FY27 and about 10% value addition currently. Products are tuned to North India coarser yarns.

segments.commentary: Capacity doubling from 9,000 to 18,000 MT per annum; commissioning by end Q1 FY27, with about INR 150 crores of incremental revenue expected at peak.

FY27 consolidated EBITDA guided north of INR 500 crores; management aims for double-digit consolidated EBITDA margin but calls its stance conservative given the global situation.
FY27 PBT guided at about INR 225-250 crores after interest and depreciation, per management's reading of the outlook.
Finance cost to stay north of INR 125 crores consolidated; debt repayments of INR 100-125 crores per year, with no big debt planned near term.
Peak consolidated revenue of INR 7,500-7,700 crores expected by end of FY28 after Phase 2 Punjab (about INR 4,000 crores), Silvassa (about INR 3,200 crores) and cotton yarn (about INR 400 crores).
Punjab Phase 2 targeted for commissioning by end FY27.
Solar power of 32 MW hybrid from Serentica, with a payback of about 3 years; negligible cost benefit in FY27, full benefit in FY28.

Gas-based heating at Silvassa; Punjab runs on agri-waste fuel and uses no gas.

Punjab PTA and MEG linked projects: about 2.5 million tonnes of PTA capacity (GAIL and Indian Oil) had not commissioned by the call; GAIL now expects supply from July and Indian Oil targets year-end start-up.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Silvassa ran at full capacity through the war-related disruption, and Punjab ramp-up finished only in March after a one-quarter delay. Product line-up realignment is expected to show margin benefits from Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital: why did inventory and payable days rise (payables from about 59 days in FY25 to about 104 days)?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Punjab ramp-up raised material and FG inventory, and about INR 180 crores of raw material was in transit. Punjab stock is lower than Silvassa, and days should fall as full-quarter COGS builds.

qa_highlights.question: Debt and interest cost: is FY26 gross debt the peak?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said gross debt of about INR 1,500 crores is the peak, with repayments of INR 100-125 crores a year. Average cost of debt is about 7.25% after including trade payables carrying LC interest beyond 68 days; finance cost stays above INR 125 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to the INR 7,000 crore-plus revenue target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 is INR 5,600-5,700 crores, and peak revenue of INR 7,500-7,700 crores is expected by end FY28 after Phase 2 and cotton yarn.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Punjab margin reach Silvassa levels and double-digit consolidated EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for double-digit consolidated EBITDA margin, calls its guidance conservative given the global situation, and tracks performance on EBITDA per tonne rather than percentage.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Punjab Phase 1 utilisation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 80-85% utilisation in the current quarter, with the facility aiming to run flat out like Silvassa over time.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to currency, raw materials and PTA supply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Euro-denominated ECB is hedged for the full tenure, imports are booked on arrival, and the import and export balance limits raw material risk. PTA supply depends on GAIL and Indian Oil start-up timing.

risks_watch: Crude and cotton volatility: pass-through lags, and management said inventory was held back in some quarters when crude was expected to rise.
Punjab execution: utilisation of 80-85% in Q1 FY27, product realignment and the gap in gross margin versus Silvassa.
Phase 2 Punjab and cotton yarn timelines (end FY27 and 10-12 months after ground-breaking) and the still-unannounced equipment orders.
PTA supply delays from GAIL and Indian Oil and the duty waiver status.

Management did not provide a segment split between cotton and technical textiles because it does not track them separately.

544314|2026-06.headline: Sanathan Textiles Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 79.08% YoY to INR1,334.74 crores, but PAT fell to INR23.82 crores on Punjab depreciation and finance costs.

Consolidated EBITDA rose 55.38% YoY to INR108.08 crores, but depreciation (INR34.7 crores) and finance costs (INR38.6 crores) rose sharply as Punjab moved from capitalisation into the P&L. Management maintained FY27 consolidated EBITDA guidance of INR520-540 crores.

544317|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 30% to INR6,880 crores with record EBITDA; FY27 guidance trimmed to 20-22% growth and about 11% EBITDA margin.

Q4 FY26 was softer: revenue INR1,863 crores, EBITDA INR207 crores (11.08% margin) and PAT INR96 crores, which management attributed to project-cycle timing and supply-chain delays in February and March. Management guided FY27 to 20-22% revenue growth and around 11% EBITDA margin, citing geopolitical and commodity cost pressure, and reported an unexecuted order book of about INR16,361 crores with FY26 order inflow of INR8,520 crores (below the earlier INR10,000 crore expectation). Working capital days fell to 81 from 91 and net debt reduced to INR274 crores.

544322|2026-03.headline: Unimech to acquire Hobel Bellows for about INR450 crore EV, all-cash from internal funds, at roughly 7x EV/EBITDA on ~INR129 crore FY26 revenue and >50% EBITDA margin.
544322|2026-03.overview: Unimech announced the acquisition of Hobel Bellows, a metallic bellows and precision assemblies maker, via a subsidiary, for about INR450 crore EV on an all-cash basis funded from internal balance sheet cash. Management said Hobel reported about INR129 crore revenue for FY26 with EBITDA margin above 50%, and projected 15-17% growth over 3-4 years on existing customers without new-customer wins. Management said the core business saw demand recovery and better Q4 FY26 momentum, and that the FTWZ facility awaits only customs clearance, expected by end-May 2026. Q&A centred on customer concentration (two OEM groups ~93% of revenue), valuation rationale, NPCIL and AS9100 certification timelines, and capacity utilisation of 50-60%.

segments.name: Hobel Bellows - metallic bellows
segments.commentary: Over 75% of Hobel revenue per management; bellows range 2 to 16 inches, 500 g to 330 kg, for engines of 900 to 9,000 BHP. About 70% of products are single-source.

segments.name: Hobel Bellows - exhaust manifolds and structural components
segments.commentary: Remainder of revenue (under 25%) per management; margins said to be similar to bellows.

segments.name: Unimech core business
segments.commentary: Management said demand is normalising after a muted prior year, with improved momentum in Q4 FY26 and a healthy order book; no quantified figures given.

guidance_outlook: Management guides 15-17% growth over the next 3-4 years for Hobel, described as conservative and excluding new customers.
Synergies expected mainly on revenue (cross-selling, nuclear, marine/naval, aerospace), not cost; cost optimisation described as limited.
No new borrowings planned; no major capex expected near term beyond maintenance, with capex deferred until utilisation reaches 80-90%.
FTWZ facility: all approvals received, only customs clearance pending, expected by end-May 2026; delayed versus earlier timelines.
NPCIL qualification expected in about one year; AS9100 certification needed before aerospace work, timing not specified.
Payback on the acquisition estimated at 8-10 years (initial calculation).
capex_capacity: Hobel operates from a 200,000 sq ft facility plus 20,000 sq ft warehouse in Visakhapatnam SEZ; current utilisation 50-60%.
Management targets 85-90% utilisation before deploying new capex; automation and robotics expected to lift effective capacity.
Unimech had planned about INR100 crore capex for metal forming, tube bending and sheet metal; acquisition used instead.
Recent machinery additions include FANUC welding robots, seam welders, automated underwater leak test machine and 3D printer; some yet to be commissioned.
Management said no additional capex needed for AS9100 certification.
demand_pricing: Management cites a global metallic bellows addressable market of about $2.6 billion growing ~6% annually.
Two OEM groups contribute ~93% of Hobel revenue; end uses include power generation, locomotive engines, automotive and industrial systems; exports ~90%.
Cummins QSK95 gensets are an end use; Hobel's wallet share with Cummins described as small.
Margins attributed to high entry barriers, long qualification cycles, proprietary drawings and pricing power rather than cost; previous competitors were European and American.
Management says it will not sacrifice margins for growth, including avoiding automotive volume segments.
Aerospace and semiconductor customers have shown initial interest in tube bending and metal forming capabilities; no quantified pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the seller exiting at ~7x EV/EBITDA when peers trade at 25-30x?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the promoter had no succession plan (daughters settled abroad) and had crossed retirement age, so wanted an exit to a suitable buyer.

qa_highlights.question: What is client concentration and working capital position?
qa_highlights.answer: Two OEM groups contribute ~93% of revenue across 10-12 geographies; about INR60 crore working capital retained and monthly cash generation said to be sufficient.

qa_highlights.question: Is the CCD a dilution risk and what are its terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the CCD is an internal instrument between holding and subsidiary, with no near-term intent to convert and negligible interest; the transaction is all cash apart from a 10% holdback for one year.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be amortisation or goodwill?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no amortisation because the investment is in a subsidiary; fixed assets are small and the deal is capability-led and asset-light.

qa_highlights.question: Can Hobel supply NPCIL reactor-island components such as expansion joints?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Hobel is not NPCIL certified; qualification is needed, taking about a year, and tubular assemblies are the target.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split between bellows and manifolds, and by industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Bellows over 75%, with manifolds and other structural components the rest; industry-level split not available and to be taken offline.

risks_watch: Customer concentration: two OEM groups ~93% of revenue, with a single-source product base.
Execution risk on FTWZ customs clearance (expected end-May 2026) after prior delays.
Aerospace and nuclear expansion depends on AS9100 and NPCIL qualification, with timelines of roughly one year or more.
Growth guidance (15-17%) is below the analyst view of 10% standalone CAGR being conservative and Cummins-linked demand; watch actual growth.
Retention of senior and technical staff at Hobel, with compensation benchmarking and ESOPs planned over the medium term.
Integration of metal forming and tube bending operations, which stay at the Hobel facility.
544322|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the strategic and margin story, but guarded on growth and certification timelines. Management was non-committal on aggressive growth targets, NPCIL, and the CCD, and deferred several detailed questions (installed capacity, industry split) offline.
key_quotes: This debt-free business acquisition is margin accretive with strong annual cash generation, enhancing the overall quality of Unimech's earnings profile.

So it's basically exhaust systems, fuel lines in a high temperature are some of the applications in the aerospace.

544322|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 71% YoY to about INR108 crore, with Hobel Bellows consolidated for two months and a 36.5% EBITDA margin.
544322|2026-06.overview: Revenue for Q1 FY27 was about INR108 crore, up 71% YoY and 32% QoQ, with Hobel Bellows contributing about INR22 crore over two months. PAT was about INR28 crore (24% margin), up 46% YoY, though other income of INR7 crore (vs INR15 crore in Q4 FY26) flatters the quarter less than in the prior quarter. Management guided Q2 to be stronger, with three months of Hobel and a heavier precision component (PCA) contribution in H2. Confirmed order book stood at about INR280 crore including Hobel, slightly lower QoQ, which management attributed to customer pull-ins; the company also signed a USD7.5 million five-year supply agreement with FACC Austria.

segments.commentary: Contributed approx. 76% of Q1 revenue; management said demand visibility is constructive for next quarter and is dominated by aero engine tooling. Tooling orders are largely PO-to-PO.

segments.name: Precision component and assembly (PCA)
segments.commentary: Covers nuclear, semiconductor, aerospace and Hobel Bellows, making up the remaining 24% of revenue. Management expects a much heavier PCA-led contribution in H2 FY27; about 80% of qualified PCA parts are moving into serial production.

segments.name: Hobel Bellows
segments.commentary: Contributed 21% of Q1 revenue (about INR22 crore for two months). Management guides 15-20% growth for this business; AS9100 certification for Vizag facility targeted by Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Nuclear
segments.commentary: Cumulative nuclear order wins of approx. INR87 crore, with about 50% of the existing order book to execute in FY27, mainly in H2.

Blended gross margin of 65% seen as sustainable for FY27.

Other income expected to be roughly half of Q1 level in Q2 onwards.

New nuclear bits are in the pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Expected revenue growth and gross/EBITDA margin range for FY27, and capex needs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guides one quarter at a time: Q2 to be stronger with three months of Hobel, and H2 to see a much heavier PCA-led contribution. Blended gross margin of 65% is seen as sustainable for FY27. The company is open to further investment and will plan capacity early.

qa_highlights.question: Tooling mix between engine and airframe, and growth from SKU expansion versus existing programmes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a precise mix but said it is dominated by aero engine components, with airframe tooling an opportunity being explored. Growth will come from both SKU expansion and underlying end-consumer demand.

qa_highlights.question: Where Unimech sits in the value chain across precision components and aerospace?
qa_highlights.answer: In semiconductors and PCA it is already Tier-1 and deals directly with OEMs. In aerospace it is largely Tier-2, with some direct OEM work. In nuclear it is mostly Tier-2 where EPC contractors are involved.

qa_highlights.question: Nuclear margins and the nuclear mix two years out?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not disclose segment margins. Consolidated EBITDA margin is guided at 30-32%+ long run and about 34-35% for FY27. Four new nuclear reactors are being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: Hobel Bellows revenue and margin, and expected growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Hobel contributed about INR22 crore over two months. Segment margin is not disclosed; consolidated EBITDA was 36.5%. Growth is guided at 15-20%, though management called it premature to treat as a trend.

qa_highlights.question: Will other income normalise, and what is the FY27 trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 other income fell to INR7 crore because investable funds were deployed into the Hobel acquisition. Q2 onwards other income should be about half the Q1 level. FY26 other income was about INR46 crore.

qa_highlights.question: FACC agreement scope over two to three years, and ROCE and asset turn outlook as utilisation rises?
qa_highlights.answer: The FACC deal is a wave-specific agreement, and scope grows as new RFQs arrive. Asset turns are about 2x currently, expected at 2.5x over two to three years. ROCE of 15-16% holds for calendar 2026, rising to 20-21%+ with higher utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of potential US tariffs and the QIP plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is hard to quantify. Mitigants include the free trade warehousing zone, European customers and the Saudi JV. The INR750 crore QIP is an enabling resolution to meet the minimum public shareholding requirement within 18 months, not an immediate raise. M&A is open for both organic and inorganic growth.

544328|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 2.73% YoY to ₹128.58 crore while FY27 guidance calls for 20–25% revenue growth and ~12.5% operating EBITDA margin.

FY26 turnover grew 14.39% to ₹419.54 crore, with tractors up 42.85% to ₹201.45 crore and cranes down about 3% to ₹218.09 crore. Management attributed the crane weakness to the Term III to Term V emission norm shift and steel cost spikes, and said pass-through is now complete. The new Bhud (Himachal Pradesh) pick-and-carry crane plant and a tower crane line are guided to start commercial production in Q2 FY27, after repeated delays. Several answers on order book, cash flow and the NBFC provisioning were vague or deferred to email.

segments.name: Cranes (pick-and-carry, existing plant)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹218.09 crore (about -3%) on 1,003 units; existing plant utilisation about 80%+ in FY26 vs 90%+ in FY25. FY27 guided to grow 15–20%. Q4 margin fell to about 10.4%, attributed to emission-norm cost pass-through and steel inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Why is crane margin down in Q4 and what is driving it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the drop to the emission-norm upgrade cost, only partly passed on earlier, plus a sharp steel price rise in Q4. Management says full pass-through is now done and the market will accept it from the next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the crane capacity commissioning delayed and why are dealers flat?

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for other costs and the working capital cycle?

qa_highlights.question: What is the tower crane order book and margin outlook?

qa_highlights.question: What is the executable order book and export contribution?

544328|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 14.98% YoY to ₹104.93 crore, driven by tractors (+36.29%) while cranes were flat at ₹52.86 crore.

Management maintained FY27 guidance of 20–25% overall revenue growth and 12.5–13% standalone EBITDA margin. 544339|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as a recovery quarter with highest-ever quarterly revenue of Rs 74 crore, up 21.9% YoY, and broad-based growth across dental lab, aligners and pediatric segments. EBITDA rose 41.8% YoY to Rs 13.5 crore and PAT reached Rs 10.1 crore, helped by a Rs 1.3 crore tax benefit tied to a labour code gratuity item. FY26 closed with revenue of Rs 277.9 crore, EBITDA of Rs 43.4 crore and PAT of Rs 28.9 crore, against a weak Q3. Management declined to give FY27 margin or growth guidance, and cited the company's Rs 99 crore cash balance and ongoing scanner deployment as strategic priorities.

financial_highlights.change: Minor sequential improvement; ~76% excluding scanner sales
vs Rs 4.3 crore in Q4 FY25; includes Rs 1.3 crore tax benefit
vs Rs 1.3 crore last year; company debt-free

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and bank balance incl. investments

segments.name: Dental lab (total)

segments.name: Bizdent (domestic clear aligners)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 10.9% YoY in Q4 after a sequential recovery; management said margins were prioritised over pricing, which had been under pressure in prior quarters.

segments.name: Vedia (aligner raw material, mainly export)
segments.commentary: Revenue of Rs 7.3 crore, stable sequentially. Some March shipments slipped to April because freight costs roughly doubled, and in some cases nearly tripled, which delayed revenue recognition.

segments.name: Kids-e-Dental (pediatric)
segments.commentary: Quarterly revenue of Rs 5.4 crore. International registrations are in progress, with some regulatory steps cleared; no firm timeline given.

segments.name: Scanners
segments.commentary: Scanner sales were 211 units in Q4 FY26 and 1,009 units in FY26. Scanners carry lower margins and weighed on consolidated gross margin in Q4.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 guidance. Management said it wants to do better than the 16.2% FY26 growth over the next two to three years, but did not endorse a 20% CAGR.

Management did not reaffirm the earlier target of 18-20% EBITDA margin, 75-80% gross margin and 13-15% PAT margin by FY27 or FY28. It said Q4 margins were in line with that range but would not give a timeline today.
Operating leverage is expected as people costs grow less than revenue; COGS will scale in proportion to sales. Automation and digital dentistry investments are planned.
Capex for FY27 will be set based on operational needs and revenue growth, funded from IPO proceeds still on hand.
US tariff is now about 10% (was about 50%). Management said this is not a deal breaker and expects US business to keep growing.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about Rs 18.4 crore. FY27 capex will be balanced against operational capabilities and revenue growth, with no fixed amount given.
Scanner deployment remains a strategic priority: 211 units in Q4 FY26 and 1,009 units in FY26. Management wants to place as many as possible before scanners become commoditised.
Investment in automation and AI (AI Dent) continues to support cost structure and digital dentistry.
demand_pricing: Export share of revenue is about 33-34%. US is about 20% of revenue, and management said it is well diversified across customers, not dependent on Heartland Dental.
Management said the US tariff eased to about 10% from about 50%, and it absorbed higher tariff costs in the first half of Q4. It said the scale-up in the US was gradual and cautious.
Domestic aligner pricing was under pressure in prior quarters; management chose to protect margins, with Bizdent recovering in Q4.
Vedia orders were delayed by freight costs, but management said YoY growth is good and the business is not facing structural uncertainty.

The iScope 360 remote oral-health and aligner-monitoring product launched about two weeks before the call. It is sold through dentists at about Rs 2,000 retail with points-based subscription, and it may also be offered in export markets.
Competition is rising in domestic aligners and from funded players. Management said 22,000 dentists are active with Laxmi, against about 3 lakh dentists in India.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Bizdent revenue stay flat FY25 to FY26, and how much of the Q4 recovery came from pricing versus volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it chose to protect margins over price cuts during the pricing pressure. It did not split Q4 recovery between price and volume, and said it will keep balancing price against growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Vedia lower QoQ despite rupee depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight costs roughly doubled, and in some cases nearly tripled, which delayed March shipments into April. Management said YoY growth is good and there is no structural problem.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the lab business run rate of about Rs 40-45 crore per quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot give a number today, but expects growth in both domestic and international lab over the next two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for margins and growth for FY27 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give FY27 guidance. It said it wants to improve margins over the next two to three years and that Q3 was an exception. Q4 EBITDA margin was 18%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Heartland Dental's contract under review, and are more US DSOs coming?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there has been no change to the Heartland contract. It said more DSOs are being added but will not be announced individually, and that the business is diversified.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will evaluate opportunities that add value and will disclose them only once completed. It gave no specifics.

544339|2026-06.headline: Laxmi Dental Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13.9% y-o-y to about INR75 crore, a record, with EBITDA margin at 19.2% and PAT up 23.8%.
544339|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue, with consolidated revenue from operations of INR74.7 crore against INR65.6 crore a year earlier. Gross margin was 78.6% and EBITDA rose 20.6% y-o-y to INR14.4 crore at a 19.2% margin, helped by favourable mix and a scanner trading contribution. Dental lab grew 23.5% y-o-y, with international up 37.4%, while aligners grew 28.6%. Management flagged a new US CEO hire, a planned Palghar land purchase to replace rented facilities, and FY27 scanner deployment of 800 to 1,000 units. The company remains debt-free.

segments.name: Dental lab
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 23.5% y-o-y across domestic and international. Domestic lab excluding scanners grew about 12% y-o-y in Q1, per the analyst's question and management's confirmation.

segments.commentary: Grew 37.4% y-o-y. CFO said USD moved from about INR85 to INR95, roughly 12% y-o-y currency tailwind, so constant-currency growth is lower but still strong.

segments.commentary: Grew 28.6% y-o-y. Bizdent grew 27.8% and Vedia grew 29.3%. Management linked growth to the iScope at-home monitoring launch and dentist education.

segments.commentary: Grew 54.4% y-o-y in the quarter. The company holds 60% of its PAT in its adjusted EBITDA calculation.

AI-led automation costs are elevated this year and expected to fall next year as scale rises.

capex_capacity: Planned FY27 investment in new machinery to modernise and expand manufacturing capacity; no amount disclosed.

Letter of intent executed to acquire land in Palghar, Maharashtra, to replace two rented domestic facilities (Illusion Dental Lab and aligners). Rent is about INR2 crore a year; management said a 3x-size owned facility could otherwise cost INR5 to 6 crore in rent.
No disruption to revenue or productivity expected during the transition, which will be phased. Management cited a 2020 export-unit move from Kandivali to Boisar as precedent.

Digital penetration in domestic network about 75% to 80% (dental lab and aligner combined); international is mostly digital.

Aligners are sold only through dentists, not B2C. Management targets general dentists and orthodontists alike.
Branding push includes a brand ambassador, in-clinic branding and social media. Management described itself as the only branded player in crowns.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 36 years of trust, global quality standards and ISO-certified systems, and innovation, and said it is the only branded crown player.

qa_highlights.answer: Scanners are a trading item with a 15% to 20% margin. Excluding scanners, margins are stable and rising; Q1 margin was 19.2% vs about 15% in the previous quarter and 18% a year ago.

qa_highlights.answer: Aligners at about 70% utilisation. Lab runs at a constant 90% to 95% because of custom work.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was 12% y-o-y, attributed to satellite labs adding customer proximity, and expects faster growth from Q2 onwards.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the USD moved from about INR85 to INR95, roughly 12% y-o-y, with the rest from existing DSO and retail business. Management expects the tailwind to persist for some quarters but is unsure beyond that.

544340|2026-03.headline: Rikhav Securities H2 FY26 PAT fell to INR1.20 crore (EPS 0.31) on cash-market investment losses; FY26 PAT INR18.96 crore.
544340|2026-03.overview: H2 FY26 total income was INR1,604 crore (as stated), EBITDA INR6.57 crore and PAT INR1.20 crore. FY26 total income was INR1,991 crore, EBITDA INR32.53 crore and PAT INR18.96 crore, with EPS of 4.95. Management attributed the weak profit to a loss of roughly INR18-23 crore on legacy cash-market equity investments, valuation losses at the 31 March 2026 market low, higher depreciation from about INR5.40 crore of technology spend, and an unrecognised SLBM profit of INR4.33 crore expected to be realised in coming quarters. Management is cutting cash-market exposure and SME inventory, and is building institutional broking, ETF market making and commodity arbitrage. Several answers were vague or deferred to email, and the call was disrupted by line dropouts.

segments.commentary: In-house algo and arbitrage were the only area that improved, per management. Algo and delta-hedging income is guided to grow 20-25% in FY27.

segments.commentary: SME exposure was cut to about 30% of last year's level, roughly INR20-25 crore. Market making in ETFs has started with Kotak Mutual Fund, with two or three more mutual funds planned.

segments.name: Institutional broking
segments.commentary: Empanelled Kotak Mutual Fund, Bank of India and RBL Bank, and 8-10 FPIs have started. Management said real revenue will start next year and expects SBI and LIC empanelment.

544342|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 14.4% to INR 434.12 crore and PAT 35.61% to INR 43.84 crore; management reiterates 30-35% CAGR target.

The Bhilwara 10,000 MT R-32 plant received environmental clearance and is guided to start production by October 2026. Q4 revenue of about INR 110 crore was flat-to-down versus prior quarters, which analysts questioned; management attributed this to LPG and energy disruptions hitting end-customer industries. Management reiterated 30-35% revenue CAGR and 3-4% margin improvement over three years, with FY27 PAT guided at about INR 100 crore and a 2030 aspiration of INR 3,000 crore revenue and INR 500 crore PAT.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 30-35% growth target on track given FY26 growth of 14% and a sharp QoQ revenue decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target was INR 430 crore revenue and INR 40 crore PAT for FY26, which was surpassed; 30-35% growth is for the next three years; FY27 needs about INR 560 crore for 30% growth and is expected to exceed it if R-32 starts on time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timing and revenue contribution from Khalapur and Mumbattu, and the HFO plant?

qa_highlights.question: Why is Bhilwara CWIP only about INR 35 crore against a roughly INR 200 crore capex plan?

qa_highlights.question: Will the Saudi helium tie-up and Qatar disruption affect sourcing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Sharjah Oxygen tie-up is strategic; Qatar helium output is curtailed, but helium prices have risen sharply, which management views as an opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 PAT margins and the assumed R-32 price?

544342|2026-06.headline: Stallion Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12.78% YoY to ₹124.68 crore while PAT jumped 79.15% to ₹18.57 crore; management says margins are partly one-off.

The high-purity helium plant at Khalapur (1,200 MTPA) is complete with commercial operations expected next quarter, while the 10,000 MT R32 plant at Bhilwara slipped from a July 2026 target to end-December 2026, and Mambattu (HFO blending) is now due by year-end. Management reiterated 30-35% revenue CAGR guidance but cut the FY27 contribution expectation from the R32 plant and opened the door to dilution or debt for expansion.

544343|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue from operations rose to INR105.05 crore (from INR99.7 crore), with EBITDA flat at INR35.80 crore and FY27 guidance of minimum 35% growth.

EBITDA was INR35.80 crore versus INR35.69 crore, with the margin (31%, computed on total income including other income of about INR10.55 crore) moderating on Middle East investments, Gurgaon expansion, senior hires and AI build-out. PAT fell to INR25.50 crore from INR25.80 crore and basic EPS to INR10.44 from INR11.83, partly on a full-year post-IPO share count. The company remains debt-free with about INR171.3 crore of cash and investments, and announced a proposed acquisition of Epitome Cloud Inc. for about INR40 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the EBITDA margin 31% when the reported EBITDA is about INR25 crore?

qa_highlights.question: Why were trade-show and marketing costs reduced, and why did other expenses rise about 30%?

qa_highlights.question: What are the parameters for M&A and Epitome's margin effect?

qa_highlights.question: Why is there no buyback given the cash position, and what is the dividend policy?

544344|2026-06.headline: SPR Auto Technologies Q1 FY27: consolidated total income up 51% YoY and EBITDA up 27% YoY, with PAT up 9% after higher finance costs.
544344|2026-06.overview: Management reported 51% YoY growth in consolidated total income and 27% YoY growth in consolidated EBITDA for Q1 FY27. Consolidated PBT rose 7% and PAT rose 9% YoY, with higher finance costs from the debt used to fund the automotive interiors and lighting (Antolin) acquisition. Management attributed a near-term margin squeeze to commodity cost pass-through lagging by about a quarter, which it said it expects to recover next quarter. Standalone legacy growth of about 12% trailed the industry, which management attributed to mix shifts and weak exports.

financial_highlights.value: INR 300 million (per investor presentation, as cited by analyst)

financial_highlights.metric: Powertrain-agnostic businesses share of consolidated total income

segments.name: Legacy engine components (standalone)
segments.commentary: Management said manufacturing growth in the industry was about 12-14% against company growth of over 16%, though the analyst cited ~12% standalone growth. Two-wheelers grew ~19-20%, passenger cars ~11%, CV and tractor ~7-8%, and other segments ~4-5% (per management). Exports were hit by the West Asia situation.

segments.name: Automotive interiors and lighting (Antolin)
segments.commentary: Margins improved from 7-8% to early-to-mid teens after synergies and fixed-cost cuts. Management said the segment won several new customer programs post-acquisition. Ex-Antolin consolidated topline growth was said to be over 16%.

segments.name: Electric motors and controllers (EMFI)
segments.commentary: Management said the business doubled turnover in FY26 after Coimbatore capacity commissioned by end-December 2025, and expects full-year benefit in FY27. Management declined to disclose capacity or market share.

segments.name: High precision injection molded components / plastics (Takahata, TGPEL)
segments.commentary: Management said the injection-molded business saw very significant growth in Q1 and that plastics revenue grew about 2x last year. Takahata phase-four expansion has started, with new business revenue expected from early next year; TGPEL second Noida plant is filling up.

segments.name: Non-auto components
segments.commentary: Management said non-auto (compressors, marine, defense, railways, snowmobiles, lawn mowers, medical, music keyboards) has grown 15-20% a year over four years, but did not disclose its share of revenue.

guidance_outlook: Management expects volume momentum after GST 2.0 to continue through FY27 across two-wheeler, passenger car, CV and tractor segments.
Commodity cost increases are passed to customers with a one-quarter lag; management hopes the gap normalises in the current quarter (Q2 FY27).
Finance costs are expected to be temporary and normalise as acquisition-related debt is repaid.
Management said export markets (US, Europe, Middle East, Turkey, Egypt) have not yet recovered and expects normalisation to take more time.
Management expects to recover the lost margin from commodity inflation and said it will not lose margin.
Management said it targets consolidated EBITDA margins in the high teens and aims for Antolin margins closer to mid-teens.
capex_capacity: Acquired the piston manufacturing plant and machinery from Sunbeam Lightweighting Solutions Ltd; completed in Q1 FY27, adding piston capacity.
Capacity expansion underway across plastics, EV motors and controllers, interiors and legacy pistons; management did not disclose capacity figures.
Takahata phase-four expansion started, building a new plant adjacent to the existing facility on five acres of additional land; new business revenue expected from early next year.
TGPEL: second Noida plant has full capacity available and is filling up.
EMFI: Coimbatore capacity commissioned around end-December 2025.
Legacy CAFE-compliant piston and ring coating technologies already available at Ghaziabad and Pathredi plants; management said products are under customer testing and validation.
Management said all the tested flex-fuel products up to E85 are ready, requiring different plating with capacity already available.
demand_pricing: Management said realisation may rise to some extent with newer CAFE-compliant technologies, which cost more; management said it is leading the competition on these.
Mix shift toward smaller vehicles post GST 2.0 lowered value realisation per piece, per management.
Management said commodity prices have started to fall from unprecedented levels, and it expects normalisation within the next quarter.
Standalone gross margin was around 56-57% in the past two quarters versus 59-61% historically; management attributed this to product mix and commodity impact.
Management said it has back-to-back pass-through arrangements with customers across legacy, plastics, motors and interiors, with a one-quarter lag.
Management said the Q1 wage hike, effective 1 April, had a small impact on employee cost percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone legacy growth (~12%) trail the industry growth of ~20% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said manufacturing growth was 12-14% versus company growth over 16%, and that exports were hit by the war situation, so manufacturing shifted toward OE customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone gross margin hold while EBITDA margin fell ~200 bps QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a mix of product, market, and volume effects, plus aftermarket lag in Q1 and the commodity pass-through lag.

qa_highlights.question: Is any price increase needed from OEMs to recover the commodity impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said back-to-back contracts exist with a one-quarter lag, so the increase for the prior quarter's average commodity price is recovered the following quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is net debt and what are the leverage thresholds?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated net debt was about INR 550 crore as of June; net debt to equity is 0.2x, and management said it will not cross 1x.

qa_highlights.question: How is the fundraise going to be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said funds are fungible and will be split across acquisitions, debt repayment and ongoing investments; no split was given. It said the fundraise is progressing as per target.

risks_watch: Commodity-cost pass-through lag: management expects normalisation in Q2 FY27, so the Q2 margin is a key check.
Export weakness in the US, Europe and Middle East, with no clear recovery timeline per management.
Finance cost burden from acquisition debt, which management said will normalise over time; watch the repayment schedule.
Standalone legacy growth trailing industry manufacturing growth in Q1.
Undisclosed segment breakup: management declined to give plastics, Antolin and EMFI revenue and EBITDA for the quarter.
544344|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand, integration and margin recovery, but evasive on specifics: management declined to give segment splits, EMFI capacity, market share, non-auto revenue share and the wage-cost impact. On exports, it was candid that recovery is slow.
key_quotes: As far as fundraise is concerned, I think we are progressing as per target.
We are not going to lose on our margins.
So, we have outgrown the industry even as we speak.
At present it is only 0.2x. So, we don't see any reason why we have to even go up to 1x.
I'd really request all of you to reach out to our secretarial department for the questions so that we can answer back one on one.

rows.why: Takahata phase-four is under construction on five acres with new business revenue expected from early next year (about 2 quarters out), TGPEL second Noida plant has full capacity available and is filling up, and the Sunbeam piston plant was completed in Q1 FY27; management did not disclose capacity figures.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects volume momentum after GST 2.0 to continue through FY27 across two-wheelers (~19-20% growth), passenger cars (~11%) and CV/tractor (~7-8%), with plastics revenue up about 2x YoY, though exports are weak.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said capacity expansion programs are running across plastics, EV motors and controllers, interiors and legacy pistons, and the fundraise is progressing to target, but utilisation was not disclosed so the call rests on stated programs rather than a utilisation read.

rows.why: CAFE-compliant piston and ring coatings are under customer testing and all flex-fuel products up to E85 are ready, but no launch dates or revenue were given.

rows.why: Net debt was about INR 550 crore with net debt to equity at 0.2x, and management said it will not cross 1x while acquisition debt is repaid, so finance costs should normalise.

rows.why: Management said these export markets have not yet recovered and normalisation will take more time after the West Asia situation hit exports.

rows.why: Contracts across legacy, plastics, motors and interiors recover the prior quarter's commodity cost, and management said commodity prices have started to fall from unprecedented levels, so the lost margin should be recovered next quarter.

544345|2026-03.headline: Denta FY26 revenue rose over 23% to Rs 2,503.8 mn with order book of Rs 7,278 mn, but Q4 EBITDA margin fell to about 19%, and management gave no firm order-inflow guidance.
544345|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue from operations of Rs 2,503.8 mn (over 23% growth), EBITDA of Rs 834.9 mn and PAT of Rs 609 mn, with an order book of about Rs 7,278 mn across 38 ongoing projects as of March 31, 2026. Analysts pressed on a sharp Q3/Q4 run-rate slowdown and a Q4 EBITDA margin of about 19% versus roughly 33% in the first three quarters, which management attributed to the Iran-US war, petroleum-linked raw material costs and a mix shift to smaller projects. Order-book inflow was described as pending new tenders under the new Karnataka government, with no order value committed. Working capital of about Rs 295 crore (inventory, receivables and other assets) is expected to convert largely in December-January, and management guided to about 20% FY27 revenue growth with an EBITDA margin of around 25%.

segments.name: Water management (core)
segments.commentary: Management says about 90% of the water order book sits in the water sector, covering drinking water, STP, irrigation and tank regeneration. The company has bagged 3-4 FTP projects covering about 15-16 cities in Karnataka.

segments.name: Amrut 2 and Jal Jivan Mission
segments.commentary: One Amrut 2 order of Rs 232 crore (Kuknuru and Yelburga, Koppal) and four Jal Jivan Mission projects in Karnataka. Management says about 70% of these projects is complete, with the balance 30% targeted this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 20% stated as the minimum projection; closing remarks cited a 20-25% target.
EBITDA margin guided at about 25% (confirmed in Q&A), down from about 33% run-rate in Q1-Q3 FY26.
No firm order-inflow number given; management expects to announce new orders shortly and aims for a healthy order-book increase by end-March 2027.
Management declined to give an absolute FY27 profit figure, saying it depends on project execution and raw material investment.
Government payments expected to accelerate from July-August 2026, with many payments in Q2-Q3 FY27, per management.
Possible price-escalation relief for HDPE/PVC items expected in July or Q2 FY27, per management.
capex_capacity: Inventory, receivables and other assets of about Rs 295 crore are tied up in working capital; management expects about 60% (about Rs 200 crore) to be realised in FY27, mainly by December-January.
Payment on supply is roughly 55% after material is laid, with the balance 35% on laying and the remainder on completion, per management.
Company is adopting NEBR and CAMUS-based STP technologies, claiming about 95% purity, largely through subcontracting to patent holders.
Bidding pipeline of about 5-6 projects worth about Rs 600 crore; management is aggressively bidding for 5-6 tenders and 2-3 major tenders.
Four to five projects identified in Madhya Pradesh under the National Water Management Programme (NWMP); a Mahanadi barrage tender in Odisha is yet to be floated.
demand_pricing: Karnataka's new government (formed late May/early June 2026) is expected to push infrastructure tenders after a roughly six-month slowdown.
Raw material risk: 20-30% of raw material is UPVC and HDPE pipe, with prices up in Q4 FY26, April and May 2026 after the Iran-US war; some suppliers seeking higher prices.
Price escalation clauses exist on projects above Rs 100 crore but not on smaller projects, per management.
Management said the company is taking smaller-value projects (Rs 10-50 crore) alongside larger ones (up to Rs 300 crore), which dilutes margin.
Q3 and Q4 FY26 execution slowdown was attributed to war-related disruption and irregular payments.

qa_highlights.question: Trajectory of order flow and government payment status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is aggressively bidding for 5-6 tenders and expects to announce new orders in the coming quarter; payments are expected to pick up from July-August 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory and FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management first said margin would be maintained around 30%, then confirmed a 25% EBITDA margin guidance for FY27 after repeated questioning; it said smaller projects will dilute margin.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital liquidation timeline (Rs 295 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects cash in December-January, with about 60% (about Rs 200 crore) targeted in FY27, after laying and completion of projects by October.

qa_highlights.question: Order book fall from Rs 841 crore (Dec 2025) to Rs 727 crore (Mar 2026)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the reduction to revenue conversion and investment in completing old projects, and said the audit team would provide the exact reconciliation; it did not confirm any cancellation.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 revenue and profit outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to a minimum of 20% revenue growth but declined to give an absolute profit number, saying it depends on project implementation and raw material investment.

qa_highlights.question: Diversification beyond Karnataka and into private industrial segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited NWMP projects in Madhya Pradesh and a biogas project with a partner holding GAIL and BPCL contracts; no firm private industrial wins were disclosed.

risks_watch: Margin dilution: Q4 EBITDA margin about 19% versus about 33% in Q1-Q3; FY27 guidance of 25% implies lower profit growth against a 20% revenue rise.
Working-capital conversion: about Rs 295 crore in inventory, receivables and other assets; collection timing rests on government payments.
Order book fell from about Rs 841 crore (Dec 2025) to Rs 727 crore (Mar 2026), with no reconciliation provided on the call.
Government dependence and political transition in Karnataka; payment timing is uncertain.
Raw material inflation from petroleum-linked pipes (UPVC and HDPE), with suppliers seeking higher prices.
Management answers on key numbers were vague or deferred to later written follow-up, including order-book reconciliation, margin split by project size and profit guidance.
544345|2026-03.management_tone: Management was upbeat and forward-looking on the new government's infrastructure push and order prospects, but evasive on specifics: it deferred the order-book reconciliation, margin split, and absolute profit figures to a later written follow-up. Its margin and payment answers shifted between statements, and it only confirmed the 25% EBITDA guidance after repeated questioning.
key_quotes: There will be 20% growth in revenue, that is the minimum revenue projections which we are having.
Manish Jayasheel Shetty: We will try to maintain roughly about 30%.
Without getting the order, it is not correct on my part to indicate the exact amount.

Increased, per management; an analyst cited FY26 profit of about Rs 61 crore
Down from about Rs 841 crore at end-December 2025 per analyst
Up about Rs 12 crore vs Q4 FY25 (Rs 541.52 million) per management

rows.why: HDPE/PVC pipe makes up 20-30% of raw material and prices rose in Q4 FY26, April and May 2026; escalation clauses exist only on projects above Rs 100 crore.

544350|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue crossed INR 2,000 crore (up 21.6% to INR 2,080 crore) with PAT up 52.4% to INR 168 crore; FY27 plans 60 new facilities.
544350|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue from operations up 22.6% YoY to INR 564-565 crore, with Ind AS EBITDA of INR 174 crore (30.2% margin, the highest quarterly margin of the year) despite 19 facility openings. Full-year FY26 revenue from operations reached INR 2,080 crore, EBITDA INR 614 crore (28.9% margin) and PAT INR 168 crore (7.9% margin). Same-store sales growth was about 14%, split roughly equally between volume and value. Management guided to FY27 growth at a similar pace to FY26, EBITDA margins stable, 60 new facilities (40 surgical, 20 clinics), and a merger timeline of roughly Q3 FY27.

financial_highlights.metric: Share of PAT attributable to owners FY26

segments.name: Surgical services
segments.commentary: 67% of group revenue in FY26; about 323,000 surgeries (+14.5% YoY), with cataract about 73% of surgeries (volume +14.3%).

segments.name: Diagnosis, consultation and other non-surgical
segments.commentary: 12% of group revenue in FY26.

segments.name: Optical and pharmacy
segments.commentary: 21% of group revenue in FY26.

segments.name: Southern region
segments.commentary: INR 1,273 crore revenue in FY26 (+22.6%), 61% of group; 182 facilities across five southern states.

segments.name: West region
segments.commentary: INR 341 crore revenue in FY26 (+19%), 16% of group; 47 facilities.

segments.name: North region
segments.commentary: INR 191 crore revenue in FY26 (+20.7%), 9% of group; 26 facilities. Delhi NCR entered May 2025 and now has several centres.

segments.name: Africa
segments.commentary: About 10.1% of revenue in FY26, with revenue up 20.8% YoY for the full year; 19 facilities.

segments.name: Vintage cohorts FY26
segments.commentary: Pre-FY22 facilities INR 1,375 crore (+14% SSSG, 66% of revenue); FY23 cohort INR 257 crore (+14%); FY24 cohort INR 170 crore (+16%); FY25 cohort INR 223 crore (+72%); FY26 cohort INR 49 crore.

guidance_outlook: Growth in FY27 expected to sustain at a similar pace to FY26, driven by micro-market penetration, new geographies and premium procedures.
EBITDA margins expected to stay stable in FY27 while greenfield expansion continues.
FY27 capex of INR 380-400 crore, including the new Chennai CMS facility.
FY27 acquisition-related deferred payments of about INR 60-65 crore; FY28-30 payments together about INR 60 crore.
Merger of Dr. Agarwal's Healthcare and Dr. Agarwal's Eye Hospital: shareholder/creditor meetings on July 2, 2026; NCLT sanction expected to conclude in about 5-6 months, i.e. by Q3 FY27.
Chennai CMS facility launch targeted by October 1, 2026, subject to approvals; 12-18 months needed to stabilise.
capex_capacity: FY26 surgery mix: 30 surgical centres opened; FY27 plan of 40 surgical centres (+33%) and 20 clinics, 60 in total, split 30 in H1 and 30 in H2.
Regional FY27 additions: South 24, North 16 (highest ever), West about 15; West and North to more than double additions versus FY26.
Eleven new facilities already launched in FY27 to date (including Faridabad, Ludhiana, Bikaner, Kollam, Mulshi, Nellore).
Delhi NCR: 7-8 more centres planned over 12-18 months; 30 letters of intent in hand for properties.
FY26 network: 269 facilities in India plus 19 in Africa; 19 greenfield openings in Q4 and 148 greenfield facilities added since FY23.
demand_pricing: SSSG of about 14% in FY26: volume about 7% (OPD growth about 5.5%, rest from surgical conversions) and value about 7% (premiumisation about 5.5%, price hikes 1-1.5%).
Average cataract revenue per eye is about INR 41,000-45,000; high-end cataract share rose to 26.3% of 62,800 cataract procedures (FY25: 22.5%).
Femto cataract procedures grew 87% YoY to over 5,900; lenticular (SMILE) refractive procedures grew 19%; retinal surgeries over 12,800 (+23%).
Refractive volumes grew more slowly than cataract; management is in talks with insurers for refractive coverage.
Walk-ins rose to about 10,000 patients a day from about 8,000 (+25%).
Payor mix FY26: 62.4% cash, 28.5% insurance/TPA, 9% government; domestic mix 72% cash.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex breakdown and the acquisition-related cash outflow?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is INR 380-400 crore including the CMS facility; acquisition payments are about INR 60-65 crore, versus about INR 85 crore in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What losses do new greenfield facilities carry, and will they recur?
qa_highlights.answer: New FY26 branches had unit-level operating losses of about INR 30 crore (FY25 cohort about INR 21 crore). Management expects a similar drag in FY27, with per-branch losses falling from FY27 onwards, mainly in Delhi.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise in the listed subsidiary?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 one-off merger costs of about INR 80 lakh; corporate office rent of about INR 1 crore for the year; about INR 3.3 crore extra Facebook marketing spend. Merger costs are one-off, rent recurs.

qa_highlights.question: Are the FY27 facility additions all organic, and how many facilities closed in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: All 60 planned centres are organic; partner deals are not in the pipeline. Five eye clinics were closed in FY26, and AEHL's rental outflow for FY27 is about INR 32 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What limits the pace of openings?
qa_highlights.answer: Real estate at the right cost and compliance with state clinical licences, which can delay openings. Management will ramp up only if the new centres perform.

risks_watch: New-facility drag of about INR 30-40 crore per year could weigh on margins if FY27 openings are weighted to Delhi NCR and the North.
Chennai CMS facility approvals; launch targeted by October 1, 2026, and the timeline already slipped due to election code-of-conduct delays.
Refractive softness relative to cataract; insurance coverage for refractive is still under negotiation.
Paramedical attrition of 21-25% and fixed increments of about 9.5-10%.
Merger completion depends on the July 2, 2026 meetings and final NCLT sanction, expected around Q3 FY27.
Cash-to-insurance mix and the sustainability of about 1.5% price hikes alongside premiumisation.
544350|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins and the FY27 pipeline, with specific numbers given readily. Management was more cautious on the timing of approvals (Chennai CMS, merger) and on new-facility losses, and deferred some questions (FY27 new-market count, FY25 subsidiary Q4 cost detail) for later follow-up.
key_quotes: For the first time in our company's history, we crossed over INR 2,000 crores of revenue, a milestone made possible by the trust of over 30 lakh patients and the dedication of every doctor and team member across our network.
On the margin front, we expect our EBITDA margins to stay stable even as we continue to invest aggressively in greenfield expansion, reflecting the underlying operating leverage in our model.
The biggest bottleneck for us, obviously, will be getting the right real estate because one is you want to ensure that you get the right real estate at the right cost.

rows.why: SSSG about 14% in FY26 split roughly 7% volume and 7% value, with surgeries up 14.5% to about 323,000 and walk-ins up 25% to about 10,000 a day, supported by 60 new facilities.

rows.why: Capex guided at INR 380-400 crore for FY27 and 7-8 more Delhi NCR centres planned over 12-18 months with 30 letters of intent in hand; utilisation was not disclosed, so a fresh capex round beyond FY27 is a reasonable expectation rather than a firm call.

544350|2026-06.headline: Dr. Agarwal's Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 26% YoY to INR614 crores, with Ind AS EBITDA of INR177 crores (28.5% margin) and PAT margin at 8.9%.
544350|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 delivered revenue from operations of INR614 crores (+26% YoY, +8.8% QoQ) and Ind AS EBITDA of INR177 crores (+25.2% YoY), with EBITDA margin up 30 bps to 28.5%. PAT margin expanded 127 bps to 8.9% despite greenfield losses of about INR20 crores at corporate EBITDA level. The company commissioned 18 new facilities (16 surgical), a record for a single quarter, and reiterated a FY27 plan of 60 additions including 40 surgical centres. Same-store growth for the oldest cohort (pre-FY23) was 16.3%, driven roughly equally by volume and value.

segments.commentary: Contributed 22% of group revenue.

guidance_outlook: Plan to add 60 new facilities in FY27 including 40 surgical centres; Q1 delivered 18 (16 surgical), with 12 planned for Q2 and 30 in H2.
Pipeline of 30-plus signed LOIs supports the full-year launch plan.
Management expects to sustain growth through deeper micro-market penetration, new geographies and adoption of advanced technologies.
Management said a same-store sales growth of 12-13% would be phenomenal, while volume growth is expected to continue at current pace.
Three to five more Delhi NCR facilities planned for the rest of FY27.
Merger expected to close around mid-November 2026.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27: 18 greenfield facilities commissioned, including one large tertiary facility in Thane and 15 secondary facilities; two primary facilities launched in J&K and Tamil Nadu.
Network at 285 facilities across 14 states and 5 UTs and 165 cities; 31% in Tier 1, 63% in other markets, 6% international.
Since FY23, 166 greenfield facilities added; additions rose from 10 in FY23 to 18 in Q1 FY27 alone.
Management said it is working to improve launch pace; some pipeline sites are delayed by compliance requirements.
Doctor headcount at 1,057, up about 23% YoY; about 100 doctors added in last four months, mostly for new centres.
demand_pricing: Q1 surgeries close to 91,000, up 15.5% YoY; cataract surgeries up 16.5% YoY; other surgeries up 13.3% on blended basis.
Growth split: volume about 16% and value about 16% for India revenue; premiumisation about 7.5% and price hikes about 0.5% year-to-date (about 8% like-to-like).

Average cataract realisation has risen from about INR28,000-30,000 four years ago to about INR42,000; Femto cataract adds about INR35,000 per procedure against a license fee of about INR10,500-11,000.
Payer mix: cash 63.6%, insurance and TPA 27.7%, government schemes 8.6%.
Pre-FY23 SSSG of 16.3%: volume about 8% (OPD growth 6% plus about 2% conversion) and value about 8%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of revenue growth came from case mix and price versus volume?
qa_highlights.answer: COO Rahul Agarwal said premiumisation contributed about 7.5% and price hikes about 0.5% so far this year, so close to 8% like-to-like value growth against about 15-16% volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: What are the losses from new facilities?
qa_highlights.answer: Greenfield losses are about INR20 crores at corporate EBITDA level, covering FY26 and FY27 centres and including pre-operating losses.

qa_highlights.question: What were the deferred consideration payments and lease interest?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Yashwanth Venkat said about INR25 crores of acquisition liabilities were paid in Q1, and lease liability interest was about INR18 crores; interest on deferred acquisition payables fell to INR3.6 crores from INR6.8 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Is the North growth only from Delhi NCR?

qa_highlights.question: Will doctor additions drive future revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most of the doctor additions are for new centres and productivity should improve as centres mature; senior doctor attrition is 2-3% versus 16-17% group-wide attrition including juniors.

qa_highlights.question: Can realisation growth of about 10% continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth should continue, while value growth depends on lens upgrades and Femto adoption; it could not confirm whether 10% or 8% realisation growth would persist, but the direction is upward.

qa_highlights.question: Why is facility addition pace constrained given cash flow?

Delhi NCR and North: growth partly reflects Delhi being a new entry and a rebound from Operation Sindoor and floods in the prior year, and management said Delhi is a long way from South-level maturity.
key_quotes: This new fiscal year commenced with record-breaking results.
Q1 has set the base, 18 facilities launched, out of which 16 surgical, a record for any single quarter in the history of this company.
So, it's difficult to answer whether same 10% will be there or 8% will happen.
We are working on improving the launch pace. I think we have set that benchmark by this quarter.

544354|2026-03.headline: FY26 total income rose 60% to ₹368 crores, but PAT only edged up to ₹20.5 crores as finance costs hit ₹10.5 crores and gross margin fell to ~30%.
544354|2026-03.overview: Solarium Green Energy reported FY26 total income of ₹368 crores (up 60% YoY) and EBITDA of ₹35.3 crores (~9.6% margin), with PAT of ₹20.5 crores. Growth came from large ground-mounted EPC projects, which carry lower gross margins; gross margin fell to ~30% from 34.5%. Finance costs rose to ₹10.5 crores from ₹3.5 crores as the 1.2 GW module plant was financed, and receivables and inventory built up. The 1.2 GW Ahmedabad module facility began production only in mid-March 2026 and was running at ~45% utilisation at the time of the call.

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹79 crores at 34.5% in FY25; gross profit +40% YoY

segments.name: C&I and ground-mounted EPC
segments.commentary: Revenue rose to ₹227 crores from ₹114 crores in FY25. Management attributes growth mainly to large EPC execution; a 50 MW AC ground-mounted project in Maharashtra was won at over ₹185 crores.

segments.name: Essential rooftop / residential
segments.commentary: Revenue of ₹80 crores in FY26 (end-to-end installations); management says a ~₹10-12 crore monthly run rate excluding kits over the last 3-4 months.

segments.commentary: Revenue of ₹61 crores, partly reflecting reclassification of solar kit revenue into this vertical; kit sales added ~₹14 crores in FY26.

segments.name: Module manufacturing (1.2 GW, Ahmedabad)
segments.commentary: Commissioned in FY26 with production starting mid-March 2026; ~45% utilisation, with output so far used in distribution sales. External module orders on hand are ~₹35-40 crores.

Revenue expected to grow at least at the rate of the past couple of years, with growth expected to accelerate as the manufacturing facility goes live.
Manufacturing targeted at gross/overall margins above 15% on a cost-plus basis.
Finance cost to fall as a share of revenue as manufacturing assets generate returns; absolute interest cost expected to stay in a similar range or rise marginally.
