Pipeline conversion of ~60% of the ~300 MW EPC pipeline expected within 2-3 months (per Ankit Garg); separately, conversion expected over 3-6 months per Himanshu Garg.
capex_capacity: 1.2 GW fully automated module plant in Ahmedabad commissioned; capable of 4,000 panels/day at up to 23.5% cell efficiency, including G12 panels up to 725 Wp.
Plant utilisation ~45%; utilisation was cut for ~10 days to assess market response to the ALMM-II circular.

CAPEX for the module plant ~₹90 crores, plus ~₹100 crores working capital.

Management says cell capacity of ~30 GW is expected to be sufficient within 6-8 months; cost-plus pricing means cell price increases are passed through to customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the factory utilisation and how will output split between captive and external sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is ~45%, reduced for 10 days due to ALMM-II. Management targets 50-60% in-house consumption (EPC, solar kits, other EPC players), with the rest sold externally.

qa_highlights.question: How is client and project concentration managed in large EPC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said concentrated large sites reduce the number of decision-makers versus many distributed sites (200-250 sites executed earlier), so focus has moved to bigger ground-mounted projects.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins expected to be minimally protected at FY26 levels; revenue growth expected at least at past rates, accelerating with the factory. No numeric FY27 guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the debt levels, interest cost and repayment?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹100 crores-plus of working capital overdraft, repayable on demand, plus a ~₹50 crore term loan repayable over six years. FY26 interest cost was ₹10.5 crores; management did not expect it to reach ₹30-35 crores in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the increase in other current liabilities from ₹4 crores to ₹36 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹19 crores is payable to creditors for fixed assets (capex) classified as current liabilities, ~₹2 crores is year-end employee payables, and ~₹5.5 crores is advances from customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for the manufacturing business and how does domestic cell sourcing affect it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets above 15% gross/overall margin on a cost-plus model and expects at least ~15% margin to hold, though market conditions may shift over 3-6 months.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from the shift to lower-margin ground-mounted EPC; FY26 gross margin ~30% vs 34.5%.
Finance cost burden: ₹100 crores-plus of repayable-on-demand working capital debt; FY26 finance cost ₹10.5 crores vs ₹3.5 crores.

ALMM-II and domestic cell availability/pricing; management noted a new MNRE circular requiring monthly price declarations.
Low factory utilisation (~45%) and reliance on captive demand; conversion of the 300 MW pipeline is uncertain (a single 100 MW award is binary).
Project concentration in a 150 MW Maharashtra project; analyst noted it is a significant portion of revenue.
Inconsistent figures on call: EBITDA margin cited as ~9.5% and ~8-9%; management's FY27 guidance of 10-12% exit margin is a key test.

544356|2026-03.headline: AJAX FY26 revenue rose to INR2,103 crore (from INR2,074 crore) while EBITDA margin fell to 12.6%; Q4 EBITDA margin recovered to 15.1% after a 2% price hike.
544356|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue was about INR2,103 crore against INR2,074 crore in FY25, with SLCM revenue flat at INR1,758 crore on a 4% volume decline. EBITDA fell to INR266 crore (12.6% margin) from INR318 crore (15.3%), reflecting CEV5 production costs, lower operating leverage and calibrated pricing. Q4 FY26 was the turnaround quarter: revenue was flat YoY at INR758 crore, gross margin rose 170 bps to 25.8%, and EBITDA grew about 4% to INR115 crore with a 15.1% margin, helped by a 2% January price increase and direct material cost reductions. Management said it has regained market share to 73.5% in FY26 from about 69.8% in Q1, and that competitors have not taken price increases. Management gave no FY27 volume or margin guidance beyond an intent to reach early double-digit growth and 13-15% margins over the medium term.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR2,074 crore in FY25 (modest growth)
largely flat vs FY25 despite lower volumes
vs INR756 crore in Q4 FY25 (flat)
up 170 bps vs 24.1% in Q4 FY25
EBITDA up about 4% YoY; margin up about 40 bps (management cited 14.7% base)

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA to operating cash flow FY26

segments.name: SLCM
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,758 crore, flat YoY on about 4% volume decline vs industry about 11%; market share 73.5% for FY26 (about 69.8% low in Q1). Q4 SLCM volumes down about 7% YoY with revenue flat on price and mix.

segments.name: Non-SLCM (pumps, batching plants)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 7% in FY26 on volume growth. Management cites 4-series and 7-series pumps and 38m and 44m boom pumps, and higher-capacity batching plants as picking up.

segments.name: Spares and service
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 9% in FY26 despite lower average machine running hours, supported by dealer and service network expansion.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue has grown to about INR103 crore from about INR74 crore; one slipform paver sold to Saudi Arabia in March with revenue expected in Q4. Management guides 20-25% export growth for FY27.

segments.name: Udaan (SLCM sub-line)
segments.commentary: FY26 Udaan volumes about 202 units. Management says Udaan sits within SLCM and it aims for 2-3x that volume in FY27.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 guidance. Management's stated intent is early double-digit growth (mid-to-early double digits), not 15%, with FY27 H1 weaker and H2 stronger (about 40:60 split).
Medium-term aim to return to mid-teens growth and 13-15% EBITDA margin; management says FY27 achievement depends on demand, steel prices and pricing.
Working capital guidance of about 30 days as a normalised level (25-30 days as aggressive range).
Export growth of 20-25% expected for FY27.
Udaan volume target of 2-3x FY26 levels (about 202 units) if conditions allow.
Management expects some Maharashtra turnaround in H2 FY27, a possible Gujarat and Rajasthan contribution, and a weaker outlook for Madhya Pradesh.
Capital deployment: an opportunity to be examined with a decision expected in H2 FY27; the company says it will not pursue turnarounds, weak governance or sunset sectors.
capex_capacity: Dealer inventory about 35-40 days in most locations, with some markets 4-5 days higher on slowing demand.
Active machine population about 35,000-38,000 units; trade-in programme being built on a database of customers aged 5-8 years.
Product scope: AJAX claims to be the only Indian player doing slipform pavers and 3D printing at scale; it is an asset-light model.
Management says it has no concrete acquisition target on the table.
demand_pricing: Central capex FY26 budget INR11.21 lakh crore, revised to INR10.96 lakh crore; utilisation about 55% until December 2025. State payment delays in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Uttar Pradesh constrain customer cash flow.
Price increase of 2% taken in Q4 (January), applied across the ARGO portfolio; management says peers have not taken any increase.
Management cites a 5-6% average price gap vs competitors (range 4-10%), after CEV5 transition.
Market share 73.5% in FY26; about 76% in April 2026; Oct-Dec quarter about 76-78%. Management says share held through Feb and March.
Input cost pressure from steel, fuel and cement; geopolitics, El Nino and interest rates flagged as risks.

Gujarat is strong on agrarian-to-commercial land conversion and the Commonwealth Games infrastructure; Uttar Pradesh is expected to see spending ahead of elections; Andhra Pradesh is doing well; Madhya Pradesh has no green shoots yet.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 demand outlook: can volume growth reach 15%, Udaan volumes, and state-level recovery (Maharashtra, MP, Rajasthan)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not commit to 15%; it expects mid-to-early double-digit growth with a stronger H2. Maharashtra may turn around in H2, MP shows no green shoots, and Gujarat, Odisha, Chhattisgarh and Rajasthan are expected to grow.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital outlook for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: A normalised 30 days is a good number for the year, with 25-30 days as an aggressive range. The key watch item is government cash flow reaching contractors and dealers.

qa_highlights.question: Will SLCM realisations rise another 1-2% on the higher base?
qa_highlights.answer: The company took a 2% price increase in Q4 and intends to recover further cost increases from the market where possible; steel and fuel costs remain pressures. No further figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook for FY27 given commodity inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: The medium-term aim is 13-15% margin. Management said it is hard to predict FY27 and that holding current margins is a good outcome until volumes recover.

qa_highlights.question: Udaan volumes and targets?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 volume was about 202 units, and management would be delighted with 2-3x that in FY27. Udaan revenue sits within SLCM.

qa_highlights.question: Cash deployment and inorganic options?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will not do turnarounds, invest where governance is weak, or enter sunset sectors. No acquisition is on the table; a decision may come in H2 and is aimed at growth through M&A or assets with quick market traction.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk that competitors dump inventory at lower prices and force AJAX to reverse its price hike?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says competitors have had the same period to act and that the 5-6% price gap has not hurt demand. It would respond with calibrated action rather than cutting prices.

Steel, fuel and cement cost inflation and possible geopolitical effects on export markets (Africa, Middle East).
Working capital back-up if receivables stretch; dealer stock in some markets 4-5 days above norm.
Capital allocation: about INR1,121 crore cash with an M&A decision expected in H2 FY27; dividend policy is for the board.

544356|2026-06.headline: AJAX Q1 FY27 revenue rose 1.7% to INR475 crores and EBITDA margin fell 70 bps to 12.5%, with SLCM market share at 75.1%.

Profit after tax rose 5% to INR55.6 crores. Management said industry SLCM registrations fell 27% and AJAX's fell 21%, yet SLCM and retail market share rose to 75.1% from about 69% a year earlier. 544367|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue crossed INR 1,000 crore (INR 1,007 cr, +157% YoY) with 23.5% EBITDA margin, despite a INR 25.7 crore non-cash Ind AS 29 charge.
544367|2026-03.overview: Management reported first-ever INR 1,000 crore+ annual consolidated revenue, FY26 EBITDA of INR 236 crore (up 98%) and PAT of INR 185 crore (up 85%), above the revised guidance of about INR 900 crore revenue and 22% margin. Q4 was the highest-ever quarter at about INR 310 crore total revenue, but consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 19.1% from 27.9% in Q3 because of a INR 25.7 crore Ind AS 29 net monetary loss at Turkish subsidiary Endoks and one-time Labour Code provisions. Order book exiting FY26 was above INR 1,400 crore. FY27 guidance is muted at about 15-20% growth as new capacity ramps, with management expecting above 50% growth in FY28.

544367|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue INR256.4 crore with reported PAT INR46.7 crore; gross margin rose to 47.2% and order book stood at INR1,945 crore.

BESS orders execute in about six to nine months, faster than the core business; IGBT supply is the bottleneck and BESS in India is targeted by end of next year.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 revenue guidance, margin guidance and FY28 growth; can revenue reach INR1,400 crore this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 20% FY27 growth and asked investors to model 20% or high-teens EBITDA, with a possible revision at Q3. On FY28, management pointed to the order book and delivery timelines; an analyst's 50% figure was confirmed as the FY28 growth guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Endoks and Mehru margins, debt position and fundraise purpose and size?
qa_highlights.answer: Mehru delivered about 18% EBITDA versus an internal 22-23% target, and revised Mehru guidance to around 18%. Endoks' existing lines run around 25%, but blended margins will be clearer in Q3. Group debt was about INR23 crore; the raise, under INR500 crore with no number set, funds the WS acquisition, a INR50 crore capex and US sales entry, with roadshows from 20 August.

qa_highlights.question: Winwin (WS Insulators) rationale, margins, timing and capex.
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidation expected from Q4 after SEZ approvals; purchase consideration about INR50-60 crore per management, and the EV was cited at about INR315 crore. Standalone potential is INR250-300 crore without capex and INR450-500 crore with capex; margins are currently 15-25% and should stabilise within about four quarters. Internal demand is about INR40-45 crore a year, and the insulator order target is at least INR200 crore over nine months.

risks_watch: Sangli execution: machinery installation, last-mile utility and statutory issues, building completion certificate pending, and about 60 customer audits over roughly six months before full volume can shift.
Q3 FY27 standalone margin moderation from new fixed costs and aluminium cost pass-through, with copper, oil and aluminium price swings already hitting Mehru in April.
Revenue visibility: FY27 guidance held at 20% with revision deferred to Q3; FY28 50% guidance rests on order book and delivery timelines.
Winwin/WS Insulators: SEZ approvals and bureaucratic process could delay Q4 consolidation; margin range of 15-25% and capex plans need to be validated.
Fundraise of under INR500 crore (roadshows from 20 August, raise before AGM) and US sales entry; size and use still not finalised.
Endoks PCS facility operational timing (Q3 FY27), no contribution guidance yet; Endoks margin not yet disclosed by segment; IGBT supply constraints.
Chinese HVDC bidder entry: management sees limited near-term threat, but local content norms at 60-70% and the policy remain watch items.
Pending follow-up: Gupta's asset-base question on Turkey pre-Ind AS 29 was taken offline; reply not on the call.

Every executable order currently in our order book has been booked above the margin guidance communicated to the market. We have not compromised pricing discipline to build volume.

So please don't build your castle based on these numbers, please build your castle based on the numbers we've guided.

544370|2026-03.headline: Nukleus FY26 total income rose 25.49% YoY to INR 36.19 crore, with PAT of INR 213.53 lakh and EBITDA of INR 917.34 lakh.
544370|2026-03.overview: FY26 showed strong growth in income and EBITDA, with management attributing margin expansion mainly to technology-led sales and operating productivity. Operational footprint is about 25 centres (17 co-working, 8 managed office) across Delhi NCR and Bengaluru, with roughly 7.3 lakh sq ft under management, about 3.06 lakh sq ft operational (figures differ across answers), and occupancy near 85%. Management is shifting the mix toward managed office and back-to-back deals, guiding to about 10 lakh sq ft operational by end FY27, but declined to give revenue numbers for that capacity. Several slides had revenue-mix errors that management said would be corrected later.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 92.75 lakh earlier; management stated about 8% increase, which conflicts with the figures quoted

segments.name: Co-working
segments.commentary: Management said co-working grows about 10% a year and carries the highest margin (illustratively about 30%). Its share of the portfolio is falling, from about 70% at IPO to roughly 50% now.

segments.name: Managed office
segments.commentary: Growing about 30-40% a year per management. Targeted to reach about 70% of portfolio in the expansion phase and about 90% over 3-4 years. Illustrative margin about 25%.

segments.name: Back-to-back / enterprise deals
segments.commentary: Illustrative margin about 20%. Landlord-funded fit-outs and revenue-sharing deals are increasing, reducing Nukleus's capex needs.

guidance_outlook: Operational area is expected to reach more than 10 lakh sq ft by end FY27, up from about 3.5 lakh sq ft now; management said this is a 10x rise from the IPO's about 1 lakh sq ft.
Management declined to give a revenue estimate for the current 3.5 lakh sq ft, saying it was too early to quantify.
Management said it intends to sustain the pace of square-footage addition for at least five years, without giving a percentage target.
Plans to expand beyond Delhi NCR and Bengaluru into Pune and Hyderabad, and eventually be a national brand in major cities.
Management said it will be among the biggest operators in three years, without quantifying this.
Management said accounts will move to Ind AS in FY27.
capex_capacity: Centre set-up takes about 3 months; bookings start around month 2; occupancy typically reaches a good level within about 6 months of opening.
Around 7 lakh sq ft under management; about 3.06 lakh sq ft operational per the presentation, while the call cited 3.5-3.6 lakh sq ft operational; the rest is CWIP or under development.
Committed area of about 7.5 lakh sq ft against about 2.5 lakh sq ft expected at IPO; RHP commitment was 1.04 lakh sq ft and the company said it delivered 1.24 lakh sq ft.
Flagship centres include Noida Sector 142 (about 1.5-2 lakh sq ft inventory), Logic Cyber Park, Skymark, IFCO Tower Gurugram and Prestige Blue Chip Bengaluru (Dairy Circle).
demand_pricing: Management cited office leasing of 82.6 million sq ft in CY2025, with GCCs taking about 44% of Q1 2026 absorption (9.1 million sq ft, 48% in Bengaluru).
Management said it is equipped to serve current GCC requirements and has started participating in RFPs; no GCC client signed yet, though it expects to sign its first one soon.
Pricing is set manually per centre to target 85-95% occupancy; dynamic pricing is not used and management said it is four to five years away for the sector.
Management said managed-office clients sign 4-9 year agreements, with revenue starting from day one and no vacancy gap for back-to-back deals.
Management said the client base has moved from startups and SMEs toward Fortune 500 and blue-chip companies, without naming clients.

qa_highlights.question: How will finance costs and leverage evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said finance cost rose to about INR 11.5 lakh from INR 92.75 lakh, described as an 8% increase, while long-term borrowings grew materially. The figures quoted do not reconcile, so the change needs checking against the filed accounts.

qa_highlights.question: What ROCE is targeted on new fixed-asset investment, and when do new centres stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: No ROCE target was given. Management said centres take about 3 months to build, reach a good occupancy level in about 6 months, and that revenue impact from the 10 lakh sq ft pipeline will fall mainly in FY27-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin gain came from operations versus accounting adjustments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed most of the gain to productivity. An AI call-filter reportedly cut calls handled per salesperson by 60-70%. No capitalisation adjustment was quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Is demand-based dynamic pricing used, and how does Nukleus compete with larger players?
qa_highlights.answer: Dynamic pricing is not used. Management said the largest operator holds about 1.5 crore sq ft and nobody in the sector is large yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current operational area, and how much will be managed office vs co-working?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 7 lakh sq ft under management, about 3.5 lakh sq ft operational, and over 10 lakh sq ft operational by end FY27, with a mix moving toward 70% managed office and 30% co-working.

qa_highlights.question: Why focus on managed office, and what are the margins and contract terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said managed office and back-to-back deals deliver scale and longer contracts, while co-working has higher per-sq-ft profit but is slow to grow. Contracts run 4-9 years.

qa_highlights.question: Will Nukleus adopt Ind AS and use NDS-based EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Nipun Gupta said the accounts will be converted to Ind AS in this financial year (FY27).

risks_watch: Inconsistent figures: the operational area was stated as 3.06 lakh, 3.5 lakh and 3.6 lakh sq ft in different parts of the call; the revenue-mix slide was flagged for correction; and the finance-cost numbers do not reconcile.
Execution risk on the pipeline of more than 10 lakh sq ft operational by end FY27, given a 3-6 month occupancy ramp and the need to fill newly added space.
Rising debt to fund expansion, with management not giving a leverage target and ROCE falling as capital employed grew.
No GCC client signed yet despite RFP participation; GCC conversion is a key watch item.
Related-party and governance questions: a management board member (Pooja Gupta) handles finance, and the company is only about a year post-SME listing.
544370|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, technology and national ambitions, but cautious and evasive on numbers: it declined to quantify revenue potential, ROCE targets and client names, and admitted errors in its slides.

We will be one of the biggest in next three years. That is what I can assure you today.
I think there will be a significant growth is better put, putting a number to this is something I don't think is a good idea at this kind of a stage.

544387|2026-03.headline: Desco Infratech H2 FY26 revenue rose 99.28% YoY to INR 118.79 crore, with PAT of INR 16.38 crore, though margins were squeezed by new power distribution and solar EPC work.
544387|2026-03.overview: Management reported half-year/full-year FY26 revenue of INR 118.79 crore (up 99.28% YoY), EBIT of INR 23.43 crore (up 76.30%) and PAT of INR 16.38 crore (up 80.87%). CGD EPC contributed INR 83.24 crore and power distribution plus solar EPC INR 35.37 crore. Management attributed margin compression to the H2 entry into power distribution and solar EPC, and guided FY27 revenue growth of 70-80% YoY. Operating cash flow stayed negative at roughly INR 18-19 crore, which management called growth-driven, with a promise of improvement. Management also outlined a CBG build-out (2 TPD commissioning in Q1 FY27, plus 15-18 TPD of planned expansion) and new subsidiaries in the UAE and India.

financial_highlights.change: Improved to roughly 3-4.5% of revenue per management, from approx INR 12 crore negative last year

financial_highlights.metric: Power distribution and solar EPC revenue

segments.name: City gas distribution (CGD) EPC
segments.commentary: Contributed INR 83.24 crore of FY26 revenue with management citing PAT margin of about 15.3%. Management guides CGD at 60-65% of revenue in FY27 and beyond; the order book has about INR 330-332 crore in CGD, with EPC timelines of 18-24 months and O&M of 24 months.

segments.name: Power distribution and solar EPC
segments.commentary: Contributed INR 35.37 crore, started in H2 FY26, with management citing EBITDA margins of about 9.5-10% (on a PAT basis in one answer) and 20% EBITDA margin on a later answer, which was not reconciled. Working capital days are 10-15 versus 30-35 for CGD; order book is about INR 1 year execution timeline.

segments.name: CBG (compressed biogas) via SGAEPL and Desco Biogreen
segments.commentary: First 2 TPD plant to commission in Q1 FY27 (delayed 15-25 days, targeting end-May, June at latest). Capex about INR 3.5-4 crore, opex about INR 60-65 lakh, revenue about INR 1.4-1.5 lakh per day, PAT margin 22-23% claimed, payback 3.5-4 years. Management expects CBG revenue of about INR 170 crore by FY30.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 70-80% YoY, described by management as conservative.
Management targets INR 1,000 crore revenue by 2030 (may slip about 1 year), citing PNG penetration of only 6.5% and a government mandate of 12-15% by 2030 and 25-30% by 2040.
Operating cash flow expected to be at par or slightly positive next year, and positive within about two years, per management.
Debt-to-equity may rise to a maximum of 0.3x over about 1.5 years as structured debt is raised.
CBG breakeven (EBITDA and PAT) expected within 18-20 months.
Expansion of 15-18 TPD CBG capacity (12 TPD Gujarat and 4-5 TPD Madhya Pradesh) with about INR 25 crore capex, funded via bank debt, not equity; cost of debt expected to fall to 8.5-9.5% from 16-17%.
capex_capacity: CBG 2 TPD plant in SGAEPL to be commissioned in Q1 FY27, capex about INR 3.5-4 crore, with one PSU LOA for 5 TPD capacity cited.

Planned additional 15-20 TPD CBG capacity over about 18 months: MOU signed in South Gujarat (capex INR 12-15 crore) and talks with farmers in Dhar, Madhya Pradesh (capex about INR 9 crore), MOU expected within about 30 days.
Desco Global FZ-LLC (Ras Al Khaimah) incorporated; EPC work there delayed due to the Middle East crisis, with no investment made so far.
Desco Biogreen Private Limited incorporated for sustainability-oriented segments; management said SGAEPL may later merge into it.
demand_pricing: CGD order book about INR 330-332 crore out of total INR 345 crore order book; power distribution and solar make up the rest. Pipeline of about INR 650 crore, of which about INR 470-480 crore is CGD and about INR 100 crore is solar and power distribution, with tenders delayed by the Middle East crisis.
Customer mix in CGD order book: about 70-72% PSU/semi-government (BPCL, GAIL, IOCL, IGL) and 25-28% private (Torrent, Adani, and others). KP Group cited as a key power and solar client.
Management said it is declining low-margin orders in CGD amid crisis-driven demand, and is now providing surety bonds rather than bank guarantees.
Likhitha Infra named as a direct competitor that management described as stronger; management plans to take share from it, though it does not regard it as a rival.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for cash flow and the INR 1,000 crore revenue target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said negative cash flow is growth-led, from working capital in project ramp-ups; operating cash outflow improved to about INR 18-19 crore on INR 118 crore revenue, and it expects at-par or slightly positive operating cash flow next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin contraction and the revenue mix going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the squeeze to H2 entry into power distribution and solar EPC, and said CGD will remain 60-65% of revenue in FY27 with the rest from power distribution and solar.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost and timeline of the unsecured NBFC borrowings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NBFC loans at about 16-17% per annum fund 90-120 day solar EPC projects; it plans to restructure debt after H1 and repay from internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book mix and execution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Of INR 345 crore, about INR 330-332 crore is CGD (EPC 18-24 months, O&M about INR 35-40 crore over 24 months); power distribution averages a 1-year timeline.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors view the margin sustainability in solar and power distribution given tender-based bidding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are sustainable and it will avoid aggressive bidding, accepting only selected work; it quoted about 20% EBITDA margin for this business versus 23% last year, as stated by the analyst.

qa_highlights.question: What are the CBG economics and expansion plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 2 TPD capex of INR 3.5-4 crore, revenue of INR 1.4-1.5 lakh per day, 22-23% PAT margin, and a 3.5-4 year payback, with 15-18 TPD expansion requiring about INR 25 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital profile and why are receivables high?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CGD working capital days are about 30-35 versus 10-15 for power and solar; high receivables reflect unbilled work-in-progress from O&M jobs started on January 1, 2026, and retention amounts released after a 36-48 month defect liability period.

Promoter stake increase and any equity raise remain unclear; management declined to comment on equity.

544396|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 2.4x YoY to INR 68.46 crore; FY26 revenue about INR 209 crore with EBITDA near INR 65 crore, with management guiding ~70% CAGR to INR 850-900 crore by FY29.
544396|2026-03.overview: Management framed FY26 as a transformation year, shifting mix away from PPaaS toward TSP, with international, SaaS and RegTech as the planned growth drivers. Q4 revenue was about INR 68.46 crore, EBITDA INR 19.26 crore and net profit INR 12.24 crore, and the call noted Q4 as the lowest EBITDA margin quarter. FY26 operating cash flow was negative, which management attributed to longer TSP credit periods. Management guided to ~70% revenue CAGR over three years, with the first-year (FY27) run-rate on the order of INR 340-350 crore, and said the mix shift would lift margins over time.

financial_highlights.change: full-year EBITDA margin cited at 31% vs 37% prior year (analyst figure)
net profit fell 9.7% per analyst question; PAT margin about 20% vs 25%
reason: longer credit period in TSP business

financial_highlights.value: about 180 days expected going forward (analyst interpretation, not confirmed by management)
financial_highlights.change: expected to decline gradually as mix changes

segments.name: TSP (Technology Service Provider)
segments.commentary: Contributed nearly 90% of FY26 business per management; slide 17 shows TSP tapering to 30-40% of business contribution by FY29, with absolute value expected to rise. Carries longer credit periods and low-to-medium margins.

segments.name: PPaaS (Payment Platform as a Service)
segments.commentary: Management said more than a year of effort has not delivered desired results; engine being pivoted to domestic merchant orchestration and global PPaaS. Guided at 5-8% contribution in FY27-FY29 per analyst reading of slides; about 40+ accounts in funnel.

segments.name: RegTech
segments.commentary: AI-led RegTech product bought by one large public sector bank; close talks with multiple public and private banks. Purely SaaS; management expects revenue contribution from FY27 and guided 10-15% contribution range per analyst reading.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Zero base in FY26; guided to about 25% of business in FY27, 40% in FY28 and about 50% in FY29 per analyst reading. Management said about 40% of FY27 international business is already in hand, and bagged a large RegTech order including a central payment body abroad. Mix of license and SaaS.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR of about 70% over three years; FY29 revenue INR 850-900 crore per management (analyst cited ~INR 950 crore), from FY26 base of about INR 209 crore.
FY27 growth of about 70% targeted; analyst-proposed FY27 range INR 340-350 crore accepted as 'anything around that range'.

544397|2026-09.headline: Ather Energy Q2 FY27: wholesale volume up 42% YoY to 93,000 units, first positive PAT, and gross margin at 24% (H1 FY27: 23%).
544397|2026-09.overview: Management reported strong demand with preorders up about 108% and inquiries up about 109% YoY, supporting wholesale volume of 93,000 units (up 42% YoY) and registrations of about 92,500 (up nearly 60%). Average ex-showroom price rose to INR164,000 from INR150,000 in Q4 FY26, and adjusted gross margin reached 24% in Q2 FY27 versus 25.4% in Q4 FY26 after commodity headwinds. EBITDA turned positive at 4.9% (from -9.6% a year earlier) and the company reported its first positive PAT. Management is raising installed capacity to 11.4 lakh units per year by Q2 FY28 because demand exceeds supply, and Konarc launched in phases from late August.

segments.name: Zones (registrations growth)
segments.commentary: Industry registrations grew 82% YoY to about 6 lakh in Q2. Ather growth was 82% in South, 85% in Middle India and 79% in Rest of India; Rest of India was the fastest-rising zone as Konarc rolled out in northern states and sales were prioritised there.

segments.name: Konarc (new mainstream scooter)
segments.commentary: Launched 29 August 2026 with only one month of sales in Q2 and fewer than 10,000 units sold by quarter-end. Mid variants SR2 and SR3 are live, SR1 is due by Q4 FY27, and the Z variant is not yet in production.

segments.name: Non-vehicle revenue
segments.commentary: Non-vehicle revenue was 15% of total. AtherStack Pro is more than 50% of it, with accessories and servicing split roughly equally. Management indicated gross margins of about 30-40% for accessories, 40-45% for spares and 80-90% for AtherStack Pro.

guidance_outlook: Installed capacity to rise from 9.2 lakh units/year to 11.4 lakh units/year by Q2 FY28, through Hosur (+6,000 units/month, live later this quarter) and AURIC Phase 1 (base 42,000 units/month, plus 12,000 units/month incremental).

AURIC Phase 1 trial production expected in the next few weeks (Q3 FY27), with capex installation complete by Q4 FY27; full capacity realisation takes a couple of quarters, with ramp-up expected within FY28.
Dealer/experience-centre network expansion to restart from around end of Q3 FY27, with noticeable numbers from Q4 FY27; fewer than 50 experience centres were added in the last two quarters.

No further price hikes in Q3 FY27 and no planned price increases on the current portfolio for the next few quarters; Konarc's entry variants may lower average ex-showroom price without hurting gross margin.
Management expects like-to-like Konarc gross margin to be 6-7% better than Rizta in the long term; Konarc is already a few thousand rupees cheaper than Rizta on a like-to-like basis.
Commodities seen as flat in recent weeks; management says Q3 is not expected to be worse than Q2 but volatility remains high. Subsidy is broadly unchanged QoQ.
Electric motorcycle launch: no timeline given.
capex_capacity: Current manufacturing capacity averaged 33,000 units/month in Q2 FY27, up from 28,000 in Q1; Hosur is at 35,000 units/month capacity and is described as at its limit.
Hosur expansion adds 6,000 units/month, live later in Q3 FY27. Total installed capacity is about 77,000 units/month after AURIC Phase 1 base (42,000) before the additional expansion.
AURIC Phase 1 (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar) adds 12,000 units/month of incremental capacity by Q2 FY28, taking installed capacity to 11.4 lakh units/year from 9.2 lakh units/year.
Management estimates about 20,000 units/month of unrealised retail demand at current run-rate, with demand in the 50,000-60,000 units/month range.
Ather Node (apartment EV charging) is being industrialised and will begin deployment in the next few months; Ather Bedrock 5th-gen battery packs are live across 450, Rizta and Konarc.
demand_pricing: Preorders rose about 108% YoY to about 1.8 lakh; inquiries rose about 109% YoY to over 10 lakh; Ather searches rose about 94% vs about 34% for EV searches industry-wide.
Pan-India E2W penetration crossed 10% for the first time, at about 11.2% for Q2 FY27 (industry commentary cites 11.6% as the quarterly figure).
Average ex-showroom price rose to INR164,000 from INR150,000 in Q4 FY26, helped by price hikes and SKU/incentive management. Management says part of the gain is temporary.
Commodity inflation (aluminium, copper, plastics, memory chips) hit gross margin by about 9.4%. Management says SKU management recovered 2.7pp of this, a more temporary lever.
Structural gross-margin gains of about 5.3pp over two quarters came from price hikes, VAVE and cost reduction.
Konarc early Stack Pro attach rates are said to be as strong as Rizta, but management wants at least two quarters before assuming ~90% attach for Konarc, given a more non-South-heavy mix.
Tier 2 penetration is rising fastest; Maharashtra Tier 2 penetration is about 18-19%. Company is not yet present in rural markets.

qa_highlights.question: How quickly will the new AURIC Phase 1 capacity ramp up, given it is greenfield, and when will the 6.5 lakh figure be realised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AURIC Phase 1's base 42,000 units will take about two quarters to ramp; the additional 12,000 units going live in Q2 FY28 may ramp faster. Full ramp is expected within FY28, while Hosur ramp is expected to be rapid from the end of Q3.

qa_highlights.question: How much pricing headroom remains if commodities stay elevated into next calendar year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not want to raise prices on the current portfolio for the next few quarters. Konarc's more aggressive entry portfolio gives better unit economics, so it could lower average ex-showroom price without hurting gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: How are Konarc bookings and cannibalisation trending in launched regions?
qa_highlights.answer: Konarc has only one month of sales in Q2 and fewer than 10,000 units sold by quarter-end. Inquiries, preorders and walk-ins are up several times in Rajasthan and UP, and Konarc Z demand is strong.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ASP rise driven by scooter buyers or motorcycle buyers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the buyers are still scooter buyers paying for better experience, quality and features, not motorcycle buyers. Stack Pro attach is high across the base.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 5.3% margin gain sustainable, and does the 2.7% SKU lever reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 5.3% is broadly structural (price hikes, VAVE, cost reduction). The 2.7% SKU/incentive lever is more temporary and can be reopened if supply is tight or commodities stay high, but it is not one-off.

qa_highlights.question: How are dealer network expansion and experience-centre additions planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Fewer than 50 experience centres were added in the last two quarters as dealer expansion was held back. Expansion restarts around end of Q3 FY27, with noticeable numbers from Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Konarc variant rollout sequenced with mid variants first and entry variants later?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity constraints on 450 and Rizta changed the plan. SR2 and SR3 launched first, SR1 is due by Q4 once Aurangabad capacity is available, and Z comes later. Geographic rollout started in the North.

risks_watch: Commodity costs (aluminium, copper, plastics, memory) have stayed elevated for longer than expected; management says Q3 is unlikely to be worse than Q2, but the outlook is volatile.
The 2.7pp SKU and incentive lever is temporary and may reverse if supply eases, which could weigh on gross margin.

Capacity ramp risk: AURIC Phase 1 takes about two quarters to ramp, and the 12,000 units/month add-on is due by Q2 FY28; demand is 50,000-60,000 units/month against 77,000 installed capacity after Hosur and AURIC.
Konarc ramp and attach-rate uncertainty: early Konarc attach rates are strong, but its mix is less South-heavy, and management wants at least two quarters of data.
PAT is positive for the first time but management says it can fluctuate; PAT is not the near-term focus.
Dealer network expansion has been slowed; it restarts around end of Q3 FY27, so store additions and reach may lag demand.
Electric motorcycle timeline is not guided.

544399|2026-03.headline: Srigee DLM FY26 revenue INR 72.31 crore, PAT INR 6.87 crore (9.06% margin); H2 PAT more than doubled to INR 5.53 crore.

H2 FY26 total income was INR 54.34 crore, EBITDA INR 6.89 crore and PAT INR 5.53 crore, which more than doubled YoY. The core message is that existing capacity is over 100% utilised, so growth depends on moving to a larger Greater Noida plot (R11A, 10,850 sq m) targeted for commissioning around August 15, 2026. Management set an aspirational target of about INR 100 crore turnover in FY27 and INR 200-250 crore in FY28, though it is not formal guidance.

544402|2026-03.headline: Jash Engineering FY26 consolidated revenue rose only 1% to INR757 crore; FY27 guidance is INR875 crore at 12-13% PAT margin.
544402|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated income was INR757 crore versus INR746 crore, with management calling the growth disappointing. US tariff volatility (25% in January, 50% in June) led to slower US production, and the Middle East war disrupted Middle East deliveries and shipping to Far East and Southeast Asia. Domestic business grew 18% and held margins, so standalone PAT margin fell only from 14.38% to 13.38%. Management guides FY27 revenue of INR875 crore against an order book of INR899 crore (as on 1 May) and about INR45 crore already billed.

financial_highlights.change: vs 14.39% in FY25 and 14.21% in FY24 (management quoted 14.38% for prior year in opening remarks)
INR827 crore at end-March per BSE monthly data cited by analyst; INR627 crore export, INR272 crore India

financial_highlights.value: INR67 crore total (INR37 crore plant and machinery, INR30 crore acquisitions)
Includes about INR10 crore one-off US bank charge
INR9 crore vs about INR3 crore normal

segments.name: Waterfront Fluid Controls (UK)
segments.commentary: Revenue guided to about INR60 crore, 75-85% of last year; UK AMP cycle slowdown delayed growth, with GBP5.5-6 million (about INR65-70 crore) projected and strong growth expected from H2. Penstocks UK acquisition completed early April, to merge with Waterfront.

segments.name: Rodney Hunt (US)
segments.commentary: Order book about USD38-39 million; FY26 revenue around USD30 million, FY27 target USD38 million, more than 25% growth on last year. New Houston plant and Saudi plant targeted for commissioning by December 2027.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: Water control gates are the largest product line, followed by screens and valves (valves rose to 13% of mix from 11%); hydro power, pumping and other about 8%. Mix shift away from Far East (16% to 10%) noted by analyst.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Management cites about 44.5% of business in India and about 55% outside India. US was about 45% of revenue per analyst.

segments.name: WestTech / Jash Process Equipment
segments.commentary: Acquired mid-January 2026; contributes a small share of FY26 revenue. Guided to about INR40 crore in FY27 (analyst reading); outsourced manufacturing to be moved into Jash plants to cut costs.

segments.name: Shivpad (India)
segments.commentary: Merged into Jash Engineering; Q4 quality and labour issues described as largely resolved after retraining team at Indore; no incremental capacity added.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue target INR875 crore, backed by INR899 crore order book and about INR45 crore billed as of early May; INR28 crore negotiated and INR80 crore under negotiation.
FY27 PAT margin guided at 12-13%; gross margin guided at 50-55%.

Five-year target to double revenue from INR757 crore to above INR1,500 crore; capacity of about INR1,200 crore on 2-3 shifts with current Indian plants, rising above INR1,500 crore once Houston and Saudi plants are online.
Rodney Hunt USD target: USD75 million in five years, from about USD30 million today.
Q4 gross margin gain attributed to forex (billing at about INR92/USD against INR82 estimate); management says it lasts while the dollar stays high.
FY27 capex planned at about INR15-16 crore for the five Indian plants; US and Saudi capex not yet quantified.
Singapore sea-level projects: offers of about USD800-900 million submitted; first orders possibly from 2029, awards from 2028.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR67 crore: INR37 crore plant and machinery and INR30 crore acquisitions.

Rodney Hunt Orange (Massachusetts) constrained by production staff shortage; new capacity chosen in Houston.
demand_pricing: US tariff: management says stability matters more than level; 25% to 50% increase mid-year led to under-estimated costs on January-June orders. Section 232 shift cited as continuing uncertainty.

Raw material prices rising: about 20% rise in India raw material cost per CFO; US steel also more expensive.

qa_highlights.question: Is domestic revenue flat in FY27 given INR327 crore FY26 base versus INR320 crore projected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the mix is balanced by choice; domestic margins are higher because low-margin domestic jobs are not taken. Domestic may rise if exports fall short.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 gross margin improvement only forex or pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Forex-driven: orders quoted at INR82/USD and billed at about INR92 gain INR10 per dollar. Gross margin guided at 50-55% for next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance conservative given WestTech and carry-over?
qa_highlights.answer: Management calls it conservative given WestTech integration and the US tariff history; it expects growth of 13-17% and margin of at least 12%.

qa_highlights.question: Rodney Hunt capacity and growth after Houston and Saudi plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Target USD75 million in five years; USD100 million not planned. Plant costs rose sharply, and US hiring constraints shaped the Houston decision.

qa_highlights.question: Are there more acquisitions planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it is open to opportunities that are small and scalable; it is merging subsidiaries of similar businesses to reduce their number.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Singapore sea-level opportunity size INR5,000-6,000 crore and when does it start?
qa_highlights.answer: Clarified as offers of USD800-900 million, not an order; awards start 2028, first orders 2029, spread over 20-25 years; market share targeted 20-40%.

Middle East war delaying dispatches; Saudi plant land acquisition and commissioning timeline (December 2027) at risk.
Rodney Hunt Houston plant cost overrun (USD4.2 million to USD7-8.5 million) and hiring constraints in Orange, Massachusetts.
Other expenses inflated by one-off bank charge; overheads growing 7-10% against low revenue growth.
Forex-driven margin gain may reverse if the dollar falls; order book conversion and Q1 billing (INR36 crore overflow from March).
WestTech and Penstocks integration; margin outlook at WestTech not yet guided.
544402|2026-03.management_tone: Candid and conservative on guidance, while confident on the order book and domestic business. Management is cautious on US expansion and attributes the weak year mainly to tariff and war disruption.

rows.why: WestTech (acquired mid-January 2026) guided to about INR40 crore in FY27 with outsourced manufacturing moving in-house to cut costs, and Penstocks UK (acquired early April) is to merge with Waterfront, which is guided to about INR60 crore, 75-85% of last year.

544402|2026-06.headline: Jash Engineering Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 17% YoY to Rs156 crore and PAT turned positive at about Rs5 crore; FY27 target Rs875 crore reiterated.
544402|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs156 crore, up about 17% YoY, with PAT moving from about minus Rs5 crore to plus Rs5 crore and gross and EBITDA margins both higher YoY. Management said shipments to Qatar, Singapore and other Middle East customers were held back (about Rs15 crore in total), so the quarter was below what management expected. Consolidated order book stands at Rs932 crore (India Rs293 crore, outside India Rs639 crore). Management reiterated FY27 revenue of Rs875 crore and PAT of about Rs100-105 crore, and said Rs1,500 crore revenue is targeted by 2031.

financial_highlights.change: from about minus Rs5 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: India Rs70 crore; outside India Rs80 crore

financial_highlights.change: PAT up significantly; standalone PAT margin about 13% in Q1

segments.commentary: Revenue up about 21% YoY with significantly higher PAT; order book Rs559 crore. Management says standalone PAT margin is about 13% in Q1.

segments.name: Rodney Hunt (US)

segments.commentary: Order book only Rs29 crore; management said Rs150-200 crore of orders were lost in the last three to four months and a full review is under way. Management called this entity a concern.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of Rs875 crore (India Rs320 crore; outside India Rs555 crore), reiterated; management said there is potential to go beyond this but size is premature until Q2 or Q3 results.
FY27 PAT of about Rs100-105 crore stated in closing remarks; separately, PAT margin of 13-14% described as achievable for the year, depending on geopolitics.
Rs1,500 crore revenue targeted by 2031; FY28 revenue guidance of about Rs1,025 crore mentioned.
Further tariff refund of about Rs7.5 crore pending, expected to be filed and resolved in FY27 after legal vetting.
Saudi Arabia plant: land expected by end of CY2026, plant ready by December 2027, operations by March 2028. US (Houston/Orange) plant: land already acquired, contractor being finalised.
capex_capacity: Foundry expansion and gate and valve manufacturing expansion commissioned in Q1 FY27; management says capacity is up about 30%.

Capex estimates of about $12 million for the US plant and $4 million for Saudi Arabia; about $3 million already held as deposits in the US; the rest from internal accruals and debt (management expects debt of about $3-4 million); US banks reportedly willing to fund.
Data-centre pressure vessels: capacity of about 75-80 vessels a year in the existing Indore setup; management says a new plant may be needed if order flow is sustained.
Chennai plant ramp-up is still in progress; new production head moved there two weeks before the call.
demand_pricing: Pipeline: orders worth Rs72 crore already negotiated; a further Rs60 crore under negotiation; management expects about Rs72 crore more to be added in the current month.

Data-centre vessels: first order for 4 units; a 32-unit order under negotiation; more than 600 vessels quoted. Management says per-vessel value is Rs30-60 lakh and margins will be similar to other business.
US tariff: 15.6% currently (10% special tariff plus 5.6%); management is budgeting for 25% and says it will not price for 100%.
About 70% of US orders are to be made in America and 30% in India; management is cautious on new US order booking. A few large orders above $7 million each are under negotiation but not being pushed.
Mahr Maschinenbau (Austria): taking orders now, with manufacturing in UK and India; first jobs are 16 screens (2 for UK, 14 for Iraq); expected revenue about Rs15 crore per the presentation.
Competition in domestic water control gates and industrial process equipment: Tega, Delkor, Metso Minerals named as main competitors.

Singapore: a Rs6,000 crore figure discussed earlier was for project reports, not a bid; management says the overall Singapore investment is around Rs50,000-60,000 crore, spread over 15-20 years, and Jash's equipment is about 10% of project cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why was product-wise and region-wise breakup dropped from the presentation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the IR team concluded order mix changes too much quarter to quarter, so data will be shown year-on-year going forward; a Q1 split of Rs70 crore India and Rs80 crore outside India was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 margin gain is from tariff refund versus manufacturing benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a combination; the Rs5.6 crore tariff refund was booked in consumption. Dharmendra Jain also said the revenue reversal for deferred March recognition (Rs27-28 crore) was offset in June, leaving about Rs10 crore positive.

qa_highlights.question: Rodney Hunt margin profile and path to 10% PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 40% of revenue is from old orders and 60% from new orders; expected PAT margin is 8-9%; 10% may be reached by FY28 if things go well.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Russia-sanctions/tariff risk and bidding in the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bidding continues but aggressive order-chasing has slowed; it will review after the next US visit, and a US Senate bill was cited as a risk.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Saudi and US plant timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Saudi: approvals received, land application submitted, plant ready by December 2027 and operational by March 2028. US: land acquired, contractor to be finalised; both targeted in operation by March 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs875 crore FY27 target expected to be exceeded and what is executable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said order book of Rs932 crore is not all executable this year because some orders are deferred to FY28; there is scope to exceed Rs875 crore but it is too early to say.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Jash Process Equipment (WesTech) underperform?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said costing systems differed from what was expected at acquisition and marketing was not aggressive; a two-to-three-quarter transition is needed to set a clear direction.

Order book conversion: Rs932 crore order book is not fully executable in FY27 as some orders are deferred to FY28; Rs875 crore target depends on Rs72 crore pipeline additions this month.
Rodney Hunt: Q1 described as a weak quarter ('first quarter blues'); 8-9% PAT margin path to 10% depends on geopolitics; monitor Q2 and Q3 execution.

Tariff refund pipeline: further Rs7.5 crore refund pending legal vetting, expected in FY27; US and Saudi plant timelines (Saudi land by end CY2026, US contractor not yet finalised) and funding mix (about $3-4 million debt).

Bidding has not been slowed down, but aggressively trying to get orders has been slowed down because the situation is so alarming that if something goes wrong, we spoil the margin.
Whenever you acquire a new company, we always think everything is very rosy at the time of acquisition.
And so, with that on positive note, I will say that we would meet our projections given earlier, which is Rs.875 crore with around Rs.100-105 crore profit after tax for the year.

544403|2026-03.headline: ABLBL Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR 2,174 crores, with consolidated EBITDA up 14% to INR 375 crores and margin at 17.2%.
544403|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered double-digit revenue growth of 12% YoY, led by Lifestyle Brands (+11%) and Emerging Businesses (+18%), with retail like-to-like at 6%. Consolidated EBITDA rose 14% to INR 375 crores and margin expanded about 20 bps to 17.2%, helped by a one-time PLI benefit of about INR 20 crores in the quarter. Reported PAT was INR 55 crores after a one-time labour code exceptional item; normalized PAT was INR 60 crores (+58%). Management flagged softer wedding demand and moderating sentiment late in the quarter from geopolitical uncertainty and volatility.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 38 crores YoY; includes one-time labour code exceptional item
vs INR 781 crores in March last year

financial_highlights.metric: Operating cash flow before capex and security deposit FY26

segments.name: Emerging Business (Reebok, Van Heusen Innerwear, American Eagle)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +18% YoY across 390+ stores; EBITDA margin up 420 bps YoY. Management puts FY26 Emerging Business EBITDA at about 4%, up from roughly breakeven last year.

segments.name: Van Heusen Innerwear

segments.name: American Eagle
segments.commentary: Profitable, with double-digit like-for-like growth in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Store expansion: what is the FY27 pipeline and how many closures?
