Van Heusen Innerwear profitability timing (at least one profitable quarter in FY27) and Reebok break-even ambition.
Standalone versus consolidated raw material cost difference was raised; management deferred to offline reconciliation.
544403|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth momentum, Reebok and Emerging Business, but cautious on near-term demand and input costs, which management described as not yet visible in numbers. Management was evasive on margin headroom and on the consolidated other-expenses question, deferring several points offline.
key_quotes: Expansion momentum also remained robust, building further on the strong sales witnessed in last quarter, while emerging brands continued to see encouraging recovery and regained a sharp growth trajectory.
So, have we peaked out? No, not yet. But can you expect dramatic changes in margin profile? Not really.
Going ahead, there won't be a PLI scheme that you will get.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided Lifestyle margins to basis-point improvements, not dramatic expansion, and Emerging Business EBITDA rose from about breakeven to nearly 4%, but the Q4 margin included a one-time INR 20 crore PLI benefit and input cost pressure may lag.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: FY27 expansion spend guided at INR 250-300 crores (about INR 200 crores retail) with 300+ stores added in FY26 to a 3,348-store footprint, and Reebok adding 40-50 stores a year on a network over 210 stores.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Lifestyle LTL projected at about 7% over a steady state, Reebok grew 30% in Q4, and Others channel rose to INR 120-130 crores from INR 65-70 crores run rate, though wedding demand softened.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex guided lower at about INR 300 crores vs about INR 325 crores in FY26, with management saying there will be some overall reduction, and no utilisation figure or new plant plan was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Lifestyle LTL is guided at about 7% steady state and no FY27 revenue number was given, while management described demand and input costs as cautious.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged softer wedding demand and moderating sentiment late in Q4, plus crude-linked polyester and bottom-wear cost pressure not yet quantified, while Q4 EBITDA was helped by a one-time INR 20 crore PLI benefit.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or molecule launches were discussed.

rows.label: Van Heusen Innerwear at least one profitable quarter in FY27
rows.why: Management is targeting at least one profitable quarter in FY27, with Q3 FY27 a possible break-even quarter, after double-digit Q4 growth and sharply lower full-year losses.

rows.label: Working capital release in FY27
rows.why: Management said working capital will be tightened in FY27, releasing cash from pre-produced inventory, supporting the path to net debt-free (net debt INR 726 crores vs INR 781 crores a year ago).

rows.label: Net debt-free in about three years
rows.why: Net debt fell to INR 726 crores from INR 781 crores and operating cash flow was INR 450 crores in FY26, but management is not chasing it aggressively.

tone.note: Management was confident on Reebok, Emerging Business and store expansion, but cautious on wedding demand and input costs, and evasive on the consolidated other-expenses and gross margin questions, deferring them offline.

544403|2026-06.headline: ABLBL Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to Rs 2,046 crore and EBITDA 14% to Rs 327 crore, with margin up 50 bps to 16%.
544403|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 11% YoY to Rs 2,046 crore, the third consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, with EBITDA up 14% to Rs 327 crore and PAT up 21% to Rs 29 crore. Lifestyle Brands grew 10% to Rs 1,725 crore at an 18.5% EBITDA margin, while Emerging Brands grew 19% to Rs 332 crore at a 4.3% margin. Management attributed a modest demand moderation to adhik maas during the peak wedding period and a 10-15 day festive primary-billing shift into Q2 that depressed wholesale growth to 5%. Gross margin contracted about 150 bps, which management attributed to channel mix and provisioning rather than raw material costs.

financial_highlights.change: Down ~150 bps YoY per analyst question; management called it marginally lower

segments.name: Lifestyle Brands
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 1,725 crore (+10% YoY) and EBITDA Rs 319 crore at 18.5% margin. Retail grew 10% with 7% LFL across almost 3,000 stores; e-commerce grew 23% group-wide and over 50% on the company's own platform.

segments.name: Emerging Brands (Reebok, Van Heusen Innerwear, American Eagle)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 332 crore (+19% YoY), with retail LFL of 11% and e-commerce growth above 30%. Retail network crossed 400 stores; EBITDA margin 4.3%, up 240 bps.

segments.name: Channels (group)
segments.commentary: Retail grew 10% with 8% LFL, the seventh straight quarter of LFL growth. Wholesale grew 5% on primary billing, though underlying secondary growth was early double-digit.

guidance_outlook: Gross store additions of more than 300 in FY27, with net additions of 150-200 after closures of about 120-140 stores.
Cost inflation of 3-4% expected for Q2-Q3 FY27 from raw materials, logistics and minimum wages; mostly to be offset by productivity and cost rationalisation, plus small price hikes.
Management expects Q1+Q2 wholesale primary billing to even out, with the Q1 shortfall moving into Q2.
Small-town retail (about 500 stores) is about 15-16% of retail revenue and is expected to exceed 20% of portfolio over the next three to four years.
Management aims for sustained double-digit growth and margin expansion; it expects retail to grow in early double digits.
Reebok revenue is about Rs 500 crore (from about Rs 250 crore at acquisition); management sees close to 20% long-term growth possible.
capex_capacity: Retail footprint of 3,362 stores (about 5 million sq ft) across more than 800 cities and towns at quarter end; more than 65 gross openings in Q1 (Aditya Bansal's question: 68 gross).
Manufacturing is about 40% of production, diversified across Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha; Karnataka concentration is limited.
Reebok has about 200 stores versus 500-700 for other premium brands, indicating a long retail runway.
Van Heusen Innerwear distribution is about 38,000-40,000 outlets; management expects roughly 20% network addition over the next couple of years.
Two Reebok factories still operate outside India pending BIS annual renewal; domestic sourcing is being built up.
demand_pricing: Q1 demand was broadly consistent with the prior-year trend; adhik maas caused modest moderation in the peak wedding period.
Wholesale grew 5%, with a 10-15 day festive primary-billing shift into Q2; management says secondary was early double-digit.
Small-town stores grew over 15% versus about 10% in Tier 1 metros; small-town growth has been double-digit for five consecutive quarters.
Price hikes were small and varied by brand and category, taken to offset input-cost increases; management says no meaningful apparel inflation is visible.
Marketing spend was about 3.5% of sales in Q1, down from last year because of IPL spend in the base quarter.
E-commerce profitability is said to be close to retail profitability, with growth now coming without deep discounting.
Quick commerce is small for the company; innerwear is the largest category there.
Casual wear share is rising by 2-3 percentage points a year.

qa_highlights.question: Why the divergence between primary and secondary sales in Lifestyle wholesale, and how will it evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: A 10-15 day festive timing shift moved primary billing into Q2; management expects Q1 and Q2 combined to be as strong as other channels.

qa_highlights.question: What cost inflation is expected and will prices rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 saw marginal to no cost pressure. Management expects 3-4% cost increase in Q2-Q3 from raw materials, logistics and minimum wages, offset mainly by productivity and some price increases.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly 150 bps gross margin contraction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited channel mix and slightly higher inventory-age provisioning, not raw material costs, and said the effect is not material and will even out.

qa_highlights.question: What is the exposure to Karnataka minimum wage hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Garmenting was never part of the notified hike, which is under High Court challenge. Manufacturing is about 40% of production, diversified across Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.

qa_highlights.question: How are the net store adds and LFL growth reconciled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to more than 300 gross and 150-200 net additions in FY27 after 120-140 closures; network growth of 5-6% plus 7-8% LFL supports early double-digit retail growth.

qa_highlights.question: How do small-town and Tier 1 growth compare, and how is Gen-Z targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Tier 3-4 is growing above 15% versus about 10% in Tier 1 metros. Gen-Z is served through sub-brands and collections (for example Peter England's Vybe), with no share figures disclosed.

risks_watch: Wholesale growth of 5% and gross margin contraction of about 150 bps in Q1; watch whether the festive shift reverses in Q2.
3-4% cost inflation in Q2-Q3 and the wage-regulation outcome in Karnataka at the High Court.
Consumer wallet pressure from inflation; management says it has seen no meaningful demand shift so far but is cautious about H2.
Reebok BIS certification risk on imports from factories outside India, renewed annually.
Net store additions of 150-200 against a gross plan above 300; watch LFL sustainability through closures.
key_quotes: So, when you look at Quarter 2, you will find the Quarter 1 plus Quarter 2 in as strong a place as rest of the channels.
We expect a major part of it comes through productivity and the rest through cost rationalization.
But we are cautious that this may play out in the second half of the year.
Over the years, we have managed to bring this channel profitability very close to our retail profitability.
544403|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on headline growth, margin expansion and store roll-out, and openly described Q1 wholesale as a timing shift. It was cautious on H2 demand from consumer wallet inflation and on 3-4% cost inflation in Q2-Q3, and it deflected on brand-wise revenue splits and gross margin drivers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA margin rose 50 bps to 16% and Emerging Brands margin rose 240 bps to 4.3%, but gross margin fell about 150 bps and 3-4% cost inflation is expected in Q2-Q3, mostly to be offset by productivity and small price hikes.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Guided more than 300 gross and 150-200 net store additions in FY27 after 120-140 closures, on a base of 3,362 stores (about 5 million sq ft), with 65-68 gross openings already in Q1; Van Heusen distribution to add about 20% over the next couple of years from 38,000-40,000 outlets.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Retail grew 10% with 8% LFL, the seventh straight quarter of LFL growth, and management expects early double-digit retail growth backed by 150-200 net store adds and small-town stores growing above 15% versus about 10% in metros.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided only early double-digit retail growth and no explicit revenue or margin upgrade; Q1 wholesale was 5% on a festive timing shift and H2 caution was voiced.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged 3-4% cost inflation in Q2-Q3 and caution on H2 consumer wallet pressure, with wholesale at 5% growth in Q1 and gross margin down about 150 bps.

rows.label: Q1+Q2 wholesale primary billing evens out
rows.why: Wholesale grew only 5% in Q1 on a 10-15 day festive primary-billing shift into Q2, and management expects Q1 and Q2 combined to match other channels, with underlying secondary growth in early double digits.

rows.label: Small-town retail share rising to over 20%
rows.why: Small-town (about 500 stores) is 15-16% of retail revenue, growing above 15% versus about 10% in Tier 1 metros for five straight quarters; management expects it to exceed 20% of portfolio.

rows.label: Reebok BIS certification renewal for imports
rows.why: Two Reebok factories outside India still operate pending BIS annual renewal, and Reebok revenue of about Rs 500 crore relies on imports while domestic sourcing is being built up.

tone.note: Management was confident on double-digit growth, margin expansion and store roll-out, and framed Q1 wholesale as a timing shift; it was cautious on H2 wallet pressure and 3-4% Q2-Q3 cost inflation, and deflected on gross margin drivers and brand-wise splits, which analysts pressed on.

544405|2026-03.headline: Belrise Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR25,528 mn with EBITDA margin at 11.4%; FY26 adjusted PAT up 41% to INR5,020 mn.
544405|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated total revenue grew 12% YoY to INR25,528 mn and manufacturing revenue grew 21% to INR21,763 mn, while EBITDA rose only 5% to INR2,901 mn, with margin at 11.4%. Adjusted PAT rose 17% to INR1,290 mn, with a one-time INR94.7 mn operational loss at the aerospace and defence subsidiary absorbed in the quarter. For FY26, total revenue grew 15% to INR95,091 mn and adjusted PAT grew 41% to INR5,020 mn. Management reported new two-wheeler and exhaust/fuel-tank orders, the Chester Hall acquisition in the UK, and guidance of mid-teens growth with broadly stable margins for FY27.

segments.name: Two-wheeler and three-wheeler
segments.commentary: Contributed 83.2% of Q4 manufacturing revenue and 82.0% in FY26. Content per vehicle rose 65-70% during FY26 (management also cited 60-65% on another basis), with two-wheeler content per vehicle moving from about INR12,000 to INR20,000 including the Badve Auto Comps and Eximius merger.

segments.name: Passenger vehicles
segments.commentary: Contributed 6.2% of Q4 and 5.2% of FY26 manufacturing revenue. Suspension business currently serves two- and three-wheeler OEMs only, not PV OEMs.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Contributed 8.4% of Q4 and 8.3% of FY26 manufacturing revenue. CV segment grew 32% in Q4 and 35% in FY26.

segments.name: Four-wheeler
segments.commentary: Four-wheeler business grew 71% in Q4 and 37% in FY26 (transcript initially said 31%, corrected to 37% in footnote). Content per vehicle rose from about INR25,000 to INR40,000-45,000 with the H-One acquisition.

segments.name: Aerospace and defence (Belrise Aerospace and Defense)
segments.commentary: Acquired SDM (France) in Q3 FY26 and Chester Hall (UK) in Q4 FY26. Q4 carried a one-time operational loss of INR94.7 mn from startup costs, legal and professional fees and personnel costs; management expects SDM to be EBITDA positive in 2027.

guidance_outlook: Mid-teens revenue growth expected to continue, supported by the order book.
EBITDA margins expected to remain broadly stable versus FY26 levels (FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin 12.1%); cost pressures seen as short-term and not expected to affect medium-to-long-term margins.
Capex expected at 6% to 6.5% of manufacturing revenue, with R&D included within this range.
Doubling four-wheeler and CV revenue versus FY25 within the current fiscal year requires about 40% to 45% growth, per management endeavour.
Final dividend of INR0.55 per share declared.
SDM expected to turn EBITDA positive in 2027 after the one-time Q4 loss.
capex_capacity: Bangalore brownfield expansion to supply exhaust systems and fuel tanks to a fast-growing two- and three-wheeler OEM; production slated to begin Q2 FY27 with peak annual revenue of INR90 crore.
Large order from a Japanese two-wheeler OEM for exhaust systems and metal components; peak annual revenue about INR220 crore, production starting Q4 FY26-27 (transcript says 'this fiscal year').
Haridwar plant ramp-up: trial parts dispatched to a large two-wheeler OEM; peak production targeted within FY27, sourcing from Greater Noida and Pantnagar.
Chassis, battery trays and metal components for an emerging EV player; supplies expected to start Q3 of the fiscal year.
Management declined to give plant-level utilisation or break-even timelines for new plants (Chennai, Pune, Bhiwandi).
Over 850 robots deployed across the company; medium-term vision is a large integrated aerospace and defence facility in India.
demand_pricing: Sector saw strong Q4 growth, helped by the GST rate cut late last year; management hopes for structural rather than pull-forward demand.
Back-to-back raw material pricing model passes steel and plastic cost changes to customers with a lag, limiting margin impact.

Q4 headwinds: oil-crisis-related supply chain disruption, higher raw material, energy and logistics costs, and Haryana minimum wage increase. Fuel and labour costs expected to be passed on over time; transport cost recovery still under discussion with key OEMs.
Two-wheeler segment only recently returned to pre-COVID peak; management sees long-term headroom.
Aerospace demand described as very strong, with OEM order backlogs of 8-10+ years; qualification cycles of 12-24 months cited as the main barrier.
Chester Hall: rejection rate 0.5%-1%; advanced discussions to transfer part of its subcontracted work to India.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins trend through the quarters, and how will the company absorb commodity, fuel and labour cost pressures to hold full-year margins stable?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 was hit by the INR94.7 mn one-time aerospace loss and acquisition fees, both called one-time. Fuel and labour costs to be passed on over time; transport costs still under discussion. Full-year guidance maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How large can the two new two-wheeler OEM customers become over two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects both to become very large over 2-3 years, with content per vehicle rising sharply and cross-model penetration. The Japanese OEM order is about INR200 crore annually, and the Bangalore program is one of the sharpest ramp-ups in three years.

qa_highlights.question: How much can aerospace contribute in four to five years, and can manufacturing move to India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets aerospace above 10% of revenue and sees India as a best-cost base. It is in talks with OEMs to shift Chester Hall subcontracted work and new orders from Europe to India.

qa_highlights.question: What is the QIP of INR2,000 crore for?
qa_highlights.answer: Only an enabling resolution has been approved; no specific use was given, and management will update when there is progress.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive edge in exhaust systems, and what margin is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Edge comes from automation (850+ robots), high verticalisation, NVH engineering and stainless-steel plating capability. Management corrected the INR400 crore figure: the orders are INR220 crore and INR90 crore, about INR310 crore peak combined. No margin guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: How will R&D spend scale with aerospace and steering/high-tensile products?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is included within the 6%-6.5% capex range. The R&D team has more than 163 people. Management directionally agreed on hiring and partnerships but gave no specific target.

qa_highlights.question: Will the trading business be localised, spun off or hived off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not commented on hiving off the trading business and will update later.

qa_highlights.question: Does suspension have passenger vehicle customers, and what are suspension and H-One revenue and PAT figures?
qa_highlights.answer: No PV customers yet; the suspension business serves only two- and three-wheeler OEMs, with four marquee customers, three onboarded in the last 18 months. Management did not have suspension, polymer or H-One revenue and PAT figures and will follow up offline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inorganic strategy for FY27, and what are the content per vehicle and plant utilisation trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets are chosen on customers, capabilities and verticalisation at mild valuations (book value to mid-single-digit EV/EBITDA); all four acquisitions are EPS and ROCE accretive. Content per vehicle has risen 60-65% in two-wheelers and is 40-45% in four-wheelers and CVs. Plant utilisation and break-even were not disclosed.

risks_watch: Margin trajectory: management guides FY26-level EBITDA margins (12.1%) but Q4 EBITDA margin was 11.4%; watch whether the one-time INR94.7 mn aerospace loss and acquisition fees recur or fade in Q1 FY27.
Oil-crisis cost pass-through: fuel and labour costs to be passed on over time, transport cost recovery still under discussion with key OEMs; a lag in recovery could compress margins.

Execution of new programmes: Bangalore brownfield (production from Q2 FY27), Japanese OEM exhaust/metal order (production from Q4 FY26-27), Haridwar ramp to peak within FY27, and EV-player chassis supplies from Q3; monitor ramp timing.
Aerospace: SDM expected EBITDA positive in 2027; Chester Hall transfer of subcontracted work to India is in advanced talks but not yet signed; qualification cycles of 12-24 months.

Capital and disclosure gaps: QIP of INR2,000 mn-equivalent (INR2,000 crore) approved only as an enabling resolution with no use specified; plant-level utilisation and break-even not disclosed; suspension, polymer and H-One standalone revenue and PAT to follow offline; trading business hive-off undecided.
key_quotes: Our first commitment was to deliver mid -teens revenue growth while keeping our EBITDA margins stable. And I am glad to share that we achieved this.
We expect this loss to be one -time and expect SDM to be EBITDA positive in the year 2027.
At this point of time, it's only an enabling resolution.
We are unable to comment on plant-specific questions on utilization and break-even.
544405|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the headline commitments (mid-teens growth, stable margins, 4W/CV doubling, content-per-vehicle gains), with management repeatedly calling Q4 hits one-time. Evasive on specifics: declined plant utilisation and break-even, QIP use, trading business hive-off, H-One and suspension figures, and R&D hiring targets, deferring these to later updates.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides FY27 EBITDA margin broadly stable vs FY26's 12.1%, but Q4 printed 11.4% after the INR94.7 mn one-time aerospace loss, and fuel/labour costs pass through only with a lag, so expansion is not guided.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Bangalore brownfield (peak INR90 crore revenue) starts Q2 FY27, EV-player chassis supplies start Q3 FY27, and Haridwar peak production is targeted within FY27; plant-level utilisation was not disclosed, so the size of the uplift is unverified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides mid-teens revenue growth (FY26 manufacturing revenue +17%, Q4 +21%), backed by the order book and new two-wheeler programmes (Japanese OEM ~INR220 crore peak, Bangalore INR90 crore).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex guided at 6-6.5% of manufacturing revenue (about INR5,000-5,000 crore-equivalent on FY26 base is not stated, so no number is given), and the INR2,000 crore QIP was approved only as an enabling resolution with no use specified, so a new project announcement is conditional on use of proceeds.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was only held (mid-teens growth, stable margins, capex 6-6.5%), and management gave no sign of raising it, with Q4 margin at 11.4% below the 12.1% FY26 level.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 EBITDA rose only 5% against revenue +12%, margin fell to 11.4%, and oil-crisis supply, energy and logistics costs plus the Haryana minimum wage increase are not yet recovered from OEMs, with transport recovery still under discussion.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New two-wheeler exhaust/fuel-tank programmes start production: Bangalore in Q2 FY27, Japanese OEM order from Q4 FY26-27, and EV-player chassis, battery trays and metal components from Q3.

rows.label: Two new two-wheeler OEM customers scale over 2-3 years
rows.why: Management expects both new two-wheeler OEMs to become very large, with the Japanese order about INR200 crore annually and content per vehicle rising sharply (two-wheeler CPV about INR12,000 to INR20,000).

rows.label: Aerospace above 10% of revenue and India as best-cost base
rows.why: Management targets aerospace above 10% of revenue and is in talks to move Chester Hall subcontracted work to India, but the transfer is not signed and qualification cycles run 12-24 months.

rows.label: SDM turns EBITDA positive
rows.why: Management expects SDM (France, acquired Q3 FY26) to be EBITDA positive in 2027 after the one-time INR94.7 mn Q4 loss, but no quarterly figure was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on mid-teens growth, stable margins, the 4W/CV doubling and content-per-vehicle gains, and called Q4 hits one-time; it was evasive on plant utilisation, break-even, QIP use, trading hive-off and H-One/suspension figures, which analysts pushed on.

544405|2026-06.headline: Belrise Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR25,465 million, EBITDA margin 11.5%, PAT up 9% to INR1,217 million.
544405|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY, led by manufacturing revenue up 20% to INR21,979 million, while trading revenue fell about 19% on Middle East disruption. EBITDA rose 5% to INR2,933 million, with margin down to 11.5%, and manufacturing EBITDA margin at 12.7%. Management reported a INR17,000 million QIP and the Hyva India tipper acquisition (completion expected Q3 FY27), and a run of new order wins across two-wheeler, renewable energy, and commercial vehicles. Management said cost pressures from steel, polymer, staff and energy have peaked and FY27 EBITDA margins should stay broadly stable versus FY26.

segments.name: Two- and three-wheeler
segments.commentary: Contributed about 81.4% of manufacturing revenue in Q1 FY27; management said segment revenue grew about 18% YoY, below industry growth of roughly 20-25%, attributed to customer mix.

segments.name: Passenger vehicle
segments.commentary: Contributed 4.6% of manufacturing revenue in Q1 FY27; H-One high-tensile steel capability up to 1470 MPa cited as a differentiator.

segments.name: Commercial vehicle
segments.commentary: Contributed 8.5% of manufacturing revenue; four-wheeler and CV revenue grew about 18% YoY per management opening remarks; Hyva India tipper acquisition announced 4 August 2026.

segments.name: Others (incl. aerospace, defence, renewables, trading)
segments.commentary: About 5.5% of manufacturing revenue. Trading business fell about 19% YoY due to Middle East crisis and logistics; management expects mid-teens group revenue growth. Aerospace and defence target is at least 10% of consolidated revenue in the medium term.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 EBITDA margins broadly stable versus FY26, with no material margin impact from input costs given back-to-back pricing.
Group revenue growth guided at mid-teens with stable EBITDA margins.
Majority of INR17,000 million QIP proceeds to be deployed within FY27, mainly for inorganic opportunities in aerospace and four-wheeler/CV, plus some organic growth.
Hyva India tipper business acquisition expected to complete in Q3 FY27; deal to be EPS and ROCE accretive from day one per management's stated threshold.
Aerospace and defence to reach at least 10% of consolidated revenue in the medium term.

New programs (chassis for fast-growing 2W OEM, US solar tracker assemblies, Sambhajinagar 2W chassis, brake assemblies) to start production in Q4 FY27; margin pressure expected to ease in coming quarters as pass-through takes effect.
capex_capacity: Four new facilities coming up, including brownfield facilities; fixed costs ramping ahead of revenue, per management.
Bangalore brownfield facility to host new 2W chassis program (annual revenue above INR650 million), SOP expected Q4 FY27.
US solar tracker sheet-metal assembly setup to support about 2.5 GW annual supplies; peak annual revenue above INR1,500 million; production from Q4 FY27.
Expansion at existing Maharashtra facilities to support a 59-assembly EV localisation program for a large Indian CV OEM.
Hyva acquisition includes three manufacturing facilities in Pune, Jamshedpur and Bangalore.
Management declined to disclose utilisation or ramp-up details for specific facilities such as Bangalore and Haridwar.
demand_pricing: Order wins: 2W/3W chassis for fast-growing OEM (above INR650 million annual revenue, on top of about INR900 million fuel tank and exhaust win last quarter); cumulative about INR1,550 million with that OEM, about INR2,000 million including suspension and braking wins.
Suspension systems now supplied to five 2W/3W OEMs, including a new Vietnamese 2W entrant in India, with suspension and braking.
Two-wheeler chassis order for an existing model at a large 2W OEM's Sambhajinagar plant, potential annual revenue of about INR500 million.
Management attributed slower 2W/3W growth to a customer mix gap with faster-growing OEMs, with new OEM ramps expected in Q3-Q4 FY27.
Trading business decline was due to Middle East crisis hitting African, Asian and Middle Eastern demand and logistics; management says the worst is behind it.
Input cost pressure (steel, polymer, energy, logistics, minimum wage hike) persisted in Q1; management expects pass-through in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new chassis order additional to earlier two-wheeler wins from South India?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, it is over and above the exhaust and fuel tank win from last quarter (about INR900 million), making about INR1,550 million cumulative annual run-rate with that one OEM.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin pressure remains from commodities, staff costs and energy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commodity, staff and energy/transport cost pressures have largely peaked, with staff cost rise tied to the annual increment cycle and pre-hiring for four new facilities; pass-through expected in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Can management quantify the benefit from raw-material pass-through and the trading decline's margin effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify either on the call and offered to respond offline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did 2W/3W growth (about 18%) lag industry growth (about 20-25%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a customer mix issue, as some faster-growing OEMs it does not work with closely gained share; newly penetrated OEMs should add volumes in Q3 and Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the aerospace and defence revenue outlook and the Plasan Sasa defence opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets at least 10% of manufacturing revenue from aerospace and defence in the short-to-medium term; Belrise already exports parts to Plasan Sasa in Israel, with progress described as gradual given geopolitics.

qa_highlights.question: Can H-One and Mag Filters revenue be quantified?

544407|2026-03.headline: Aegis Vopak FY26 revenue rose 17% to INR923.1 crores and net profit 52.1% to INR341.9 crores; Q4 revenue up 22.2% to INR243.5 crores.

544407|2026-06.headline: Aegis Vopak Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12.4% YoY to INR233.8 crore, with liquid terminaling up 31% and operating EBITDA up 15.6% to INR179.4 crore.

Operating EBITDA rose 15.6% YoY to INR179.4 crore (about 76.7% margin) and cash PAT was INR124.9 crore. Management said the board approved a 52,000 MT LPG tank at JNPA and 49,577 cbm of liquid capacity at Kochi, and that the Pipavav ammonia terminal (36,000 MT static) was commissioned. Management framed a $5 billion capex plan through FY2030-31, of which about INR10,000 crore is to be commissioned by March/June 2027.

segments.name: Gas terminaling
segments.commentary: Revenue INR107.2 crore, down 3.5% YoY on LPG import disruption from the Middle East; management said volumes held up via diversified sourcing and multi-location distribution. Standard throughput rate about INR1,175/MT, INR1,200/MT for some principals.

qa_highlights.question: Are LPG throughput charges fixed by counterparty and term, and why haven't terminal charges risen while distribution margins did?
qa_highlights.answer: Standard rate about INR1,175/MT, INR1,200/MT for some principals; charges are per MT with no escalation. Management said terminaling is infrastructure usage, while distribution margins reflect sourcing and inventory risk during the geopolitical disruption.

qa_highlights.question: Why did AVTL gain share versus national LPG imports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited non-Middle East sourcing (none of its ships were stuck), a partner in ITOCHU, and wider distribution using freed-up ullage across more locations than Mumbai and Kandla.

qa_highlights.question: Is 25% volume growth sustainable, and what is the Haldia pipeline impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for at least 25% YoY growth; four pipelines are due this year (Jamnagar-Loni done; Kandla-Gorakhpur at Kandla and Pipavav in 2-3 months; Haldia-Panagarh in 2-3 months). Haldia-Panagarh is HPCL's 60 km line; the Panagarh bottling plant is 0.5 million MT/yr and currently about 0.25 million MT is expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and liquid capacity path to FY28, and what is the Pipavav take-or-pay economics?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR10,000 crore to be commissioned by March/June 2027; liquid capacity 1.7 to 2.2 million cbm in FY27 and close to 3 million cbm by FY28 end. The Pipavav 0.5 million MT is higher utilization of existing capacity via rail gantry, not new tankage.

qa_highlights.question: What are the growth plans beyond the INR10,000 crore phase and the $5 billion program?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is pursuing organic and inorganic options, inland depots, strategic storage and industrial terminals, and said binding agreements will be announced as signed. The $5 billion plan through FY2030-31 is reaffirmed, with timing expected to be lumpy.

qa_highlights.question: Why did liquid revenue jump when capacity did not change?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity added last year was only partly in the base year and has now matured, JNPA plot 1 is fully running, and product mix has changed, which takes time.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said a mix of debt and equity, with debt gearing capped at 0.6x and debt/EBITDA at 3.5x, about $3 billion of debt, a $2 billion equity net worth target, and mandatory dilution to 25% by 2 June 2028.

544408|2026-03.headline: Leela Palaces Q4 FY26: operating revenue up 12% to INR 484 crores and EBITDA up 13% to INR 266 crores, with ADR up 15% offsetting a March occupancy hit.
544408|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operating revenue rose 12% YoY to INR 484 crores and operating EBITDA rose 13% to INR 266 crores, at a 55% margin, while PAT increased to INR 172 crores from INR 117 crores. Growth was driven by ADR, which rose about 15% to around INR 32,000, while RevPAR grew only 6% as occupancy fell from 78% to 72% after the West Asia conflict disrupted international travel in March. For FY26, operating revenue grew 15% to INR 1,527 crores, EBITDA grew 19% to INR 743 crores at a 49% margin, and PAT reached a record INR 403 crores. Management said April occupancy had recovered to last year's level, with high single-digit to early double-digit RevPAR growth expected for April.

segments.commentary: Occupancy fell in March on the international, US and UK source-market disruption; management expects city occupancy in mid-70s in FY27. Non-resident covers at city hotels were 54% of the cover mix.

segments.name: Resorts
segments.commentary: Described as insulated from the war; management expects a strong rebound in May and June. Resort occupancy guided to mid-60s to late-60s for FY27.

segments.name: F&B
segments.commentary: F&B revenue grew 15% in FY26 and close to double digits in Q4; banqueting grew more than 10%. Non-resident covers rose about 9-10% in Q4 and about 12% for FY26.

rows.why: H1 EBITDA grew 38% against original mid-teens FY27 guidance and management said full-year outcome will be much better than initially guided, but it has held H2 at mid-to-high teens, so a formal upgrade is not yet committed.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 is tracking ahead of pace with double-digit RevPAR growth expected and CY27 corporate rate asks at mid-to-high double digits, though H2 guide implies a sharp slowdown from 36% Q2 EBITDA growth against a high base and Dubai ADRs are lagging.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: Q3 FY27 (Arq Chennai), Q4 FY27 (Leela Luxury Residences Mumb
rows.why: Arq Chennai opening this quarter, Jaisalmer in FY27, Leela Luxury Residences Mumbai first residents targeted Q4 FY27, and Coorg rebranded as The Leela on 8 July 2026 with wellness itineraries recently launched.

rows.label: Net debt/EBITDA falls to 1.4x
rows.why: Net debt INR 12,150 million at Sep 2026 and 1.4x LTM EBITDA, down from 1.6x in Mar 2026 and 3.7x in Mar 2025, though BKC FSI equity could add funding need.

rows.label: CY27 corporate rate increase
rows.why: Corporate rate ask is mid-to-high double digit and 60-70% of corporate static rates have moved to dynamic pricing, but renewals are still under negotiation.

rows.label: Coorg reaches EBITDA breakeven
rows.why: Coorg (71 keys) rebranded as The Leela on 8 July 2026 and reached EBITDA breakeven with ADR roughly doubled, but no revenue or EBITDA figure disclosed.

tone.note: Management was confident on RevPAR outperformance, pricing power, NPS of 87 and the pipeline, and more guarded on Dubai ADRs and EBITDA, BKC capex and funding; analysts pushed on whether H2 guidance and FY27 outcome were being revised, ADR sustainability and the BRICS effect.

544410|2026-03.headline: Prostarm Q4 FY26 operating revenue rose 27% YoY to INR105 crore but fell 35% QoQ, with FY26 revenue at INR386 crore (+10%) as March billings slipped into Q1 FY27.
544410|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue of about INR105 crore grew 27% YoY but fell 35% QoQ, as project executions scheduled for March were deferred to Q1 FY27 due to West Asia-linked supply chain and gas-availability disruptions. EBITDA was about INR11 crore (down ~3% YoY) at a 10.43% margin, and PAT was about INR8 crore (up ~16% YoY) at a 7.56% margin. For FY26, revenue was INR386 crore (+10%), EBITDA margin fell 98 bps to 12%, and PAT was about INR33 crore (+14%). Working capital days rose to 185 from 68 as receivables reached about INR254 crore, mostly from one large project, and management guided to FY27 operating cash flow turning positive and FY27 revenue growth of at least 25%.

financial_highlights.change: from INR22 crore in FY25; headcount 425 to 470
from INR64 crore and 68 days in FY25
about INR158 crore relates to one large project

financial_highlights.value: approx. INR80 lakh (company described as effectively net debt-free)
approx. INR1,106 crore; plus L1 orders approx. INR96 crore; total approx. INR1,202 crore

segments.name: UPS and power conditioning
segments.commentary: Core product made in two Pune facilities; Gujarat plant (1 kVA to 600 kVA UPS) now expected operational by Q2 FY27, delayed from Q1 FY27 by supply chain issues. Management expects UPS growth above 30-40% over the next two years.

segments.name: Lithium battery packs and BESS
segments.commentary: Navi Mumbai lithium battery pack facility is commercial; 1.20 GWh Jhajjar (Haryana) BESS plant is near commissioning, expected operational by end Q1 FY27, with a capex of about INR25 crore. BESS developer projects (rental model, about INR63 crore rental per year) are being sought for hive-off, with Bihar EPC targeted for FY27 and Karnataka subject to legal issues.

segments.name: Solar EPC, channel and services
segments.commentary: Management cites channel business of about INR100 crore per year (FY26: about INR107 crore). Services include installation, AMCs and rentals; EPC is executed for solar and BESS projects.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue: management cites at least 25% growth; visible base of about INR430 crore (INR336 crore order book excluding BESS developer projects plus about INR100 crore channel business), with minimum-revenue framing and additional orders excluded.
Q1 and Q2 FY27: expected to carry the deferred billings; Q1 FY27 revenue is expected to grow YoY.
EBITDA margin: 12-13% expected on a YoY basis, with possible short-term disturbances; base EBITDA margin should not be below 10% in models.
Q1 and Q2 FY27 margin target: EBITDA 12-13%, PAT 8.5-9.5%.
Operating cash flow: still expected to turn positive for FY27 as a whole, with improvement visible from Q3 FY27; receivable days targeted at 120-150 days exiting FY27.
Jhajjar BESS plant utilisation: 25-40% in FY27 and about 70% in FY28 (per management, assuming operations from around July 2026).
Working capital: no equity dilution planned; requirements to be met from bank borrowings and internal accruals. Promoter holding about 73%.
capex_capacity: Jhajjar, Haryana: 1.20 GWh BESS assembly plant, capex about INR25 crore, revenue potential about INR1,000 crore at full utilisation; machines largely installed, expected fully operational in Q1 FY27.

Gujarat UPS plant (1 kVA to 600 kVA): project cost not more than INR5-6 crore per management; capacity of 3,000-5,000 units per day (about 9 lakh units per year), revenue potential INR500-600 crore; now expected Q2 FY27, delayed from Q1 FY27 by supply chain issues.
Three facilities currently operational: two in Pune (UPS and power conditioning) and one lithium battery pack facility in Navi Mumbai; 100 MWh lithium expansion cost about INR3.5-4 crore.
Management says capacity is not constrained: imports from China are customised, and servo units, isolation transformers and some UPS are sourced from job workers and subcontractors.
Management estimates total potential revenue of about INR1,700-1,800 crore from all facilities at 100% localised manufacturing, excluding imports.
demand_pricing: Order book: executable order in hand approx. INR1,106 crore plus L1 approx. INR96 crore (total approx. INR1,202 crore) at end FY26; bids of approx. INR257 crore under evaluation.

Customers include Adani, Karnataka Power, Bihar Power, L&T, West Bengal Medical, South Central Railway, SAIL and India One. Government share of revenue is 43%; private is the rest, with the same payment cycle.
Q4 shortfall: a single Adani order of about INR40-43 crore was deferred from Q4 to Q1 FY27; management says Q4 revenue would otherwise have been about INR430 crore-plus.

Cost pressures: freight costs more than doubled in Q4 versus earlier; the USD rose more than 10% over three to four months; China removed BESS export incentives from April 1, 2026, raising costs on orders placed earlier. Management says Q1 onward pricing reflects these costs.
Gross margin pressure: cost of production rose to 72.78% from 72.2%. Management cites order-to-order margin mix and says EBITDA by segment is not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables jump and when will they be collected?
qa_highlights.answer: Debtors were about INR254 crore, with about INR158 crore from one large project executed in Q3 and completed in Q4. Most of that is expected in Q1 FY27, and excluding it, debtor days would be about 90 instead of 241.

qa_highlights.question: Is operating cash flow still expected positive in FY27 and is equity dilution planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated FY27 positive operating cash flow, with improvement from Q3 FY27. Cash flow was negative about INR48 crore due to receivables and about INR20 crore of supplier advances. No equity dilution is planned; promoter holding is about 73%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the base EBITDA margin for modelling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says overall EBITDA is in the 12-13% range YoY, with base margin not below 10%. Segment-level margins are not reported because projects are order-based and products are cross-sold.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 margins fall and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes the drop to project mix, higher employee costs (INR29 crore vs INR22 crore), a 72.78% cost of production and the USD appreciation. It expects 12-13% EBITDA going forward, with Q1 and Q2 PAT of 8.5-9.5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites at least 25% growth, a base of about INR430 crore (INR336 crore order book excluding BESS developer projects plus about INR100 crore channel business).

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the BESS developer projects and their IRR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is seeking to hive off both developer projects, with Prostarm retaining the EPC work. Project IRR is about 10-11%. Bihar EPC is targeted for FY27; Karnataka depends on legal issues.

risks_watch: Receivables: about INR254 crore at March 2026, with 185 working capital days in FY26 and target 120-150 days at FY27 exit. Q1 collection of the about INR158 crore project receivable is the key test.
Supply chain and cost: freight, USD volatility and China's removal of BESS export incentives from April 1, 2026 could keep pressuring margins.
Execution timelines: Gujarat UPS plant slipped from Q1 to Q2 FY27; Jhajjar BESS plant needs to be operational by end Q1 FY27.
Developer BESS hive-off: pending, with lithium price and currency issues cited; any one-time gain is undetermined. Karnataka EPC depends on legal issues.
Employee cost growth (INR22 crore to INR29 crore) ahead of revenue; ESOP pool of 40 lakh with about 13.26 lakh outstanding at March 2026.
544410|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on medium-term growth and FY27 visibility, but defensive on the Q4 miss, which management attributes to deferred billings and supply disruptions. Answers on segment margins, the Gujarat capacity ramp and the BESS hive-off were vague or deferred.
key_quotes: So, only one order gets postponed to Q1 and we got a hit of INR40 crores.
Base EBITDA if you take, that should not be less than 10%. Should not be less than that.
No, as such we are not planning for it, for equity dilution.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides EBITDA 12-13% YoY (base not below 10%) versus Q4 FY26 margin of 10.43% and FY26 at 12%, but cost of production rose to 72.78% from 72.2%, freight more than doubled and employee cost rose to INR29 crore from INR22 crore, so expansion is conditional on pricing reset holding.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q1 FY27 (Jhajjar BESS) and Q2 FY27 (Gujarat UPS)
rows.why: Jhajjar 1.20 GWh BESS (INR25 crore capex, machines largely installed) is guided operational end Q1 FY27 and Gujarat UPS (3,000-5,000 units/day, ~9 lakh units/yr) is guided Q2 FY27, though Gujarat has already slipped once from Q1.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: Q1 FY27 onward, FY27 full year
rows.why: Management guides FY27 revenue at least 25% growth off a visible base of about INR430 crore (INR336 crore order book plus ~INR100 crore channel), with Q1 FY27 revenue expected to grow YoY as the INR40-43 crore Adani order deferred from Q4 is billed.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only guided at 25-40% for the Jhajjar BESS in FY27 rising to ~70% in FY28, and management says capacity is not constrained with subcontractors, so a fresh capex announcement is not signalled by the call.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is framing FY27 as a minimum 25% growth and minimum-revenue basis with additional orders excluded, while the Gujarat plant has slipped and Q4 revenue missed (down 35% QoQ), so an upgrade is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gujarat UPS already slipped Q1 to Q2 FY27, Jhajjar must be operational by end Q1 FY27, receivables of INR254 crore (INR158 crore from one project) need collection, and freight/USD/China BESS incentive removal pressure costs.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Gujarat UPS (1 kVA to 600 kVA) and Jhajjar 1.20 GWh BESS are both new product/capacity lines guided for commissioning in Q1-Q2 FY27, plus a 100 MWh lithium pack expansion (INR3.5-4 crore) listed as planned.

rows.label: Receivables collection of INR158 crore project debtor
rows.why: Most of the ~INR158 crore receivable from one large project is expected in Q1 FY27, which would cut debtor days from 241 toward ~90 ex that project, with receivable days targeted at 120-150 exiting FY27.

rows.label: FY27 operating cash flow turning positive
rows.when: FY27 full year, improvement from Q3 FY27
rows.why: FY26 operating cash flow was hit by about INR48 crore of receivables and INR20 crore of supplier advances, but management reiterated positive OCF for FY27 with a net-debt-free balance sheet (fixed deposits over INR102 crore, long-term debt ~INR80 lakh).

rows.label: BESS developer project hive-off
rows.why: Two BESS developer projects (rental model, ~INR63 crore rental per year) are being sought for hive-off with Bihar EPC targeted for FY27 and Karnataka subject to legal issues; any one-time gain is undetermined.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 growth of at least 25% and the Q1 receivable collection, but defensive on the Q4 miss and vague on segment margins, the Gujarat ramp and the BESS hive-off; analysts pushed on receivables, margin trajectory and cash flow.

544410|2026-06.headline: Prostarm Q1 FY27 revenue rose 38% YoY to INR 76 crore, PAT up 156% to INR 5 crore, with a 25% minimum FY27 growth target reiterated.
544410|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 76 crore, up 38% YoY but down 27% QoQ from INR 104 crore in Q4, which management attributed to seasonality and deferred execution. EBITDA was INR 7 crore at an 8.55% margin (up 126 bps YoY) and PAT was INR 5 crore at a 6.05% margin. Management said the 12-13% margin guidance still holds on a full-year basis, while also guiding FY27 PAT margin to 8.5-9%. Order book stood at about INR 1,085 crore plus INR 5 crore L1, and working capital days fell from 185 to 168.

financial_highlights.change: +38% YoY; -27% QoQ vs INR 104 crore in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.value: approx INR 1,085 crore plus INR 5 crore L1 (about INR 1,090 crore total)

financial_highlights.change: from INR -49 crore in Q4 FY26
from about INR 254 crore as of March 2026

segments.name: BESS (battery energy storage) developer projects
segments.commentary: Order book includes about INR 855-857 crore of developer business (Bihar and Karnataka/KPTCL). Management said no revenue recognition from these in FY27, only EPC billing on the standalone books; Karnataka dispute was resolved in KPTCL's favour and the company is targeting a sale of that project.

segments.name: Solar EPC and EPC orders
segments.commentary: Solar EPC order of about INR 165 crore from Solarium Green Energy, which management expects to execute fully in FY27. Adani EPC billing was largely completed in Q1 (INR 36 crore of deferred work executed); a further solar EPC order of about INR 12 crore (8.36 MWh) was won.

segments.name: Utility vs C&I BESS
segments.commentary: Company has stopped bidding for utility-scale BESS for about 10 months and is shifting to C&I BESS (200-500 kWh installations), where management says margins are better. Adani project gave about 26% gross margin in FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target: minimum 25%.
Margin guidance of 12-13% EBITDA is maintained on a full-year basis, with H2 expected to be stronger; Q1 margin is affected by low turnover and high fixed-cost ratio.
FY27 PAT margin expected at about 8.5-9%, not 10%, due to higher costs from new plants, import costs and hiring.
Jhajjar 1.2 GWh BESS plant and Gujarat UPS plant both expected operational in Q2 FY27; SAP and Salesforce expected operational by end of H1 FY27.
Working capital days targeted at about 120-150 by March 2027; management aims for positive operating cash flow by year-end FY27.
Jhajjar BESS utilisation: not more than 20-25% in FY27, 40-50% in FY28 (around INR 500 crore revenue targeted in FY28); steady-state EBITDA margin 14-15%.
capex_capacity: Jhajjar, Haryana: 1.2 GWh BESS manufacturing facility in final stage of commissioning; earlier delayed, management cited cost and logistics movements and a strategy shift to C&I. Commercial operation now expected by end of H1 FY27.
Gujarat: new UPS manufacturing facility progressing as planned, expected to start commercial operations in Q2 FY27.
Existing manufacturing in Pune and Navi Mumbai.

Bihar BESS (developer/rental model): yearly cash flow of about INR 16 crore over 12 years plus capital subsidy of INR 32.40 crore; SBI facility tied up in SPV, LC-backed by Bihar DISCOM, no corporate guarantee.
Karnataka BESS (KPTCL): annual cash flow of about INR 45.72 crore over 12 years plus capital subsidy of about INR 81 crore; management prioritising a sale post-COD.
demand_pricing: Order book approx INR 1,090 crore including L1. Excluding developer orders (about INR 855 crore), in-hand orders are about INR 236 crore, plus dealer business of about INR 10 crore per month, giving about INR 306-307 crore additional order in hand.
Bids under evaluation of about INR 2,000+ crore, including two large orders of about INR 1,800 crore.
Utility BESS margins under pressure: management said bidders quoted below cost assuming Chinese supply negotiations; cited China export restrictions and a 2% battery tax from 1 September.
Q1 FY27 order wins included an INR 11 crore BESS project from a corporate customer and a INR 165 crore solar EPC order.

Trade receivables: about INR 46 crore realised from the CCTNS (Pune) project in Q1, with a large further amount expected by end-August; management said most of the INR 231 crore is government-funded with no realisation risk.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the deferred Q4 orders (Adani INR 43 crore, SAIL INR 7 crore, South Eastern Railway INR 13 crore) was executed in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 36 crore has been executed. Adani is almost fully billed; SAIL and South Eastern Railway are to be billed mainly in Q2, with some South Eastern Railway work spilling into Q3 pending site clearance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 revenue fall 27% QoQ, and is the margin guidance still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is seasonally low and that the Adani billing was the major Q4 item. It said the 12-13% margin is a full-year target, with H2 stronger, and that Q1 fixed-cost absorption is weak at INR 76 crore turnover.

qa_highlights.question: What are the working capital days targets and cash flow expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital days fell to 168 from 185; target about 120-150 by March 2027. Operating cash flow improved to about INR -16 crore from INR -49 crore, with a goal of turning positive by FY27 end.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue and margin should be expected from the Jhajjar plant, and what utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 utilisation not above 20-25%; FY28 40-50% with around INR 500 crore revenue targeted. Steady-state EBITDA margin 14-15%, with C&I focus preferred over utility BESS.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be further equity dilution or significant borrowing over the next 1.5-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no equity dilution is planned for at least the next year; the Bihar debt sits in an SPV, and the INR 43 crore warrant issue is for working capital. Any future dilution would be tied to a major expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What is the receivables position and realisation timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables fell from INR 254 crore (March) to INR 231 crore (June) and dropped further by mid-August. Management expects about half to be collected by end-Q2, with most of the Solarium EPC realised in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on order inflows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited INR 1,090 crore order book and bids of INR 2,000+ crore under evaluation, and expects the non-developer order book to grow over the next year as qualifications and bid participation increase.

risks_watch: Utility-scale BESS pricing: bidders reportedly quoted below cost assuming Chinese battery supply; a 2% battery tax from 1 September and China export restrictions could pressure C&I and utility margins further.

Execution timing: Jhajjar 1.2 GWh plant and Gujarat UPS plant both guided to Q2 FY27, after earlier delays; SAP and Salesforce due by end-H1 FY27. Slippage would push the H2-weighted margin and FY27 growth path.

Receivables and realisation: INR 231 crore of trade receivables as of June 2026, with the bulk tied to CCTNS (Pune); management expects roughly half collected by end-Q2. Watch for actual collections and concentration of debtors.
Margin trajectory: Q1 EBITDA margin of 8.55% versus 12-13% full-year guidance requires a steep H2 ramp; FY27 PAT margin guided lower at 8.5-9% on new plant, import and hiring costs.

Developer BESS projects (about INR 855-857 crore order book) recognise no revenue in FY27 per management; Karnataka sale and Bihar SBI facility in SPV are pending. Dilution: management said no equity dilution for at least one year barring a major expansion, while INR 43 crore warrant issue is for working capital.

Order inflow: bids under evaluation of INR 2,000+ crore, including two orders of about INR 1,800 crore; non-developer order book about INR 236 crore plus dealer business. Outcome of these large bids is a key swing factor.
key_quotes: And by the end of quarter two, you would find a significant drop in the overall data. And numbers coming almost half of it.
So that's the reason considering our size we are not focusing on utility at all.
So that's the reason we are targeting that utilization would not be more than 25% so that we can concentrate on a high margin and C&I segment business.
There are some more developments which are happening which I cannot discuss with you right now.
544410|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on the full-year targets (minimum 25% growth, 12-13% EBITDA margin, positive operating cash flow by FY27-end) but cautious and at times evasive on utility-scale BESS pricing, Jhajjar utilisation for FY27 ("I am not very confident on conveying the exact capacity utilization") and undisclosed "developments" in BESS. Answers on Q1 seasonality and receivables were specific, while the Jhajjar delay explanation was vague.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin 8.55% in Q1 (up 126 bps YoY) must reach 12-13% for FY27; H2 is expected stronger and C&I mix (Adani gave ~26% gross margin) is better, but new-plant, import and hiring costs weigh on PAT.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Jhajjar 1.2 GWh BESS plant in final commissioning with COD guided by end of H1 FY27, and Gujarat UPS plant guided to start in Q2 FY27; both are under construction with dates, though Jhajjar was delayed earlier.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets minimum 25% FY27 revenue growth on ~INR 1,090 crore order book (about INR 236 crore ex-developer plus ~INR 10 crore/month dealer business), a INR 165 crore Solarium EPC order, and Q1 revenue up 38% YoY, though Q1 fell 27% QoQ.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No new capex planned; management deferred peer-style expansion citing margin erosion in utility BESS, and said no equity dilution for at least one year barring a major expansion.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management cut FY27 PAT margin guidance to 8.5-9% and utility BESS bids are being quoted below cost, leaving little room to raise guidance despite a 25% minimum growth target.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin of 8.55% vs 12-13% full-year guide needs a steep H2 ramp, PAT margin already cut to 8.5-9% from 10%, and Jhajjar/UPS slippage risk after earlier delays.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Jhajjar 1.2 GWh BESS and Gujarat UPS plants are due to start operations in Q2 FY27, with SAP and Salesforce by end-H1 FY27 and a shift to C&I BESS (200-500 kWh) under way.

rows.label: Working capital days to 120-150 and positive operating cash flow by March 2027
rows.why: Working capital days fell from 185 to 168 in Q1 and operating cash flow improved from INR -49 crore to INR -16 crore; management is targeting 120-150 days and positive OCF by FY27-end.

rows.label: Bids under evaluation of INR 2,000+ crore, including two orders of ~INR 1,800 cr
rows.why: Large bid outcomes would add materially to the INR 1,090 crore order book, but are not yet awarded and utility BESS pricing is under pressure from below-cost quotes.

rows.label: Receivables collection from CCTNS and Solarium EPC
rows.why: Trade receivables fell from INR 254 crore to INR 231 crore in Q1 with about half expected collected by end-Q2 and a large CCTNS amount due by end-August; government-funded, so realisation risk is low.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 25% growth, 12-13% EBITDA and positive OCF targets, but cautious and evasive on utility BESS pricing and Jhajjar FY27 utilisation (20-25%); analysts pressed on margin ramp, receivables and dilution.

544411|2026-03.headline: Scoda Tubes FY26 revenue rose 7% to INR518.7 crore and PAT 22% to INR38.8 crore, while Q4 revenue was flat at INR123.6 crore after a March gas shutdown.
544411|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a transition year with revenue up 7% to INR518.7 crore, EBITDA of INR76.2 crore and margin down to 14.7% from 16.1%. Q4 FY26 revenue was flat at INR123.6 crore, EBITDA margin 13.5% and PAT down 7% YoY to INR6.3 crore, as a 15-17 day PNG gas-driven plant shutdown in March cut production by about 40% for the month. Management guides FY27 revenue growth of about 25% with 14-15% EBITDA margin, backed by a 8,000 MTPA welded expansion (INR40 crore) on top of the 13,000 MTPA welded line funded from IPO proceeds. Capex was INR110 crore in FY26 and about INR100 crore is planned for FY27.

financial_highlights.value: around INR175 crore, executable in 3-4 months

segments.name: Seamless (piercing mill)
segments.commentary: Seamless capacity raised to 20,000 MTPA, total capacity 21,000 MTPA in FY26; piercing plant was shut for about 15-17 days in March on gas shortage and resumed in April. Seamless utilisation expected around 70% in FY27 and optimum in FY28.

segments.name: Welded
segments.commentary: New welded facility targeted to be operational in H2 FY27 with trial runs by end-Q2 FY27; 13,000 MTPA line funded from IPO, plus 8,000 MTPA (INR40 crore) from internal accruals, taking welded capacity to 21,150 MTPA by H1 FY28. Welded utilisation expected around 25% in FY27; optimum FY29.

segments.name: Geography (FY26 revenue)
segments.commentary: India INR339 crore, Europe INR137.8 crore, Americas INR30.7 crore, others INR8.9 crore. Management cited domestic INR344 crore and export INR174 crore on the analyst's summation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 25%, with domestic about 20% and export about 25%; management called this conservative and will revisit in H1 FY27.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 14-15%.
Target FY27 revenue mix of roughly 40% export and 60% domestic.
Inventory days expected to fall from 217 days to about 160 days in FY27 and remain 160-170 days thereafter.
Peak debt expected to rise by about INR50 crore to about INR250 crore in FY27; debt to decline once new capacity is fully utilised.
No further equity dilution planned; new capacity funded by internal accruals and term loans. No new seamless capex planned; further capex decision deferred to FY29-FY30 based on market conditions.
Solar project (8.79 MWdc: 4.99 MW seamless, 3.8 MW welded) expected to generate about 137 lakh kWh a year and save about INR8-8.63 crore a year in power cost.
Power and fuel cost about 17% of total expenses; gas prices up about 25%, to be passed through to customers.
Management said operations are fully normalised for Q1 FY27 with a higher cost base, and the plant is running at full capacity.
capex_capacity: Seamless capacity 20,000 MTPA, total 21,000 MTPA as of FY26 after additional lines and equipment.

Welded: 13,000 MTPA from IPO proceeds (capex INR45 crore, still underway); equipment from China expected July-August 2026 after delay from geopolitical and logistics issues; trial runs targeted end-Q2 FY27.

Additional 8,000 MTPA welded (INR40 crore, internal accruals and term loans) expected around Q1 FY28; total welded 21,150 MTPA by H1 FY28; optimum utilisation FY29. Welded range extended to 16 inches.
IPO proceeds of INR220 crore: about INR27 crore spent on capex and INR50 crore on working capital; about INR74.2 crore remaining in bank.
FY27 capex planned at about INR100 crore. Mother hollow mill supplies 70% captive consumption, targeting full captive by FY28.
demand_pricing: Raw material is stainless steel round bar made from imported scrap; base-material prices up 25-30% due to the war. Management said these are passed through to customers at order booking or dispatch.
LPG and gas prices remain elevated; cost pressure passed to customers with a lag. Management said demand is intact and only pricing is affected.
Export end-use: about 50% oil and gas, the rest engineering, automotive, power, and cooling industries. Europe pending Rina marine approval for Italian market, expected within 3-4 weeks.

rows.why: Capacite contract is worth about INR 800 crore over five years and management aims to lock in 85-90% of FY27 top line in Q1 FY27, with combined visibility above INR 6,000 crore over five years.

544419|2026-06.headline: ArisInfra Q1 FY27 revenue rose 37% YoY to INR 291 crore, EBITDA up 68% to INR 31 crore, margin 10.49%, PAT INR 20 crore.
544419|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR 291 crore, up 37% YoY, with EBITDA of INR 31 crore (up 68% YoY) and margin of 10.49%, up 191 bps. PAT was INR 20 crore versus INR 5 crore a year earlier. Management attributed margin expansion to a mix shift toward contract manufacturing and DaaS, whose combined share rose from about 46% to 63%. Net working capital days fell to 56 from 66 at March 2026 (about 97 in the prior quarter per an analyst exchange), and management reiterated 35-40% annual growth guidance.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 5 crore in Q1 FY26
Guided to INR 75-80 crore by FY27 end

segments.name: B2B supply
segments.commentary: Entry point to the network; contributed about 37% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Covers almost all construction materials.

segments.name: Contract manufacturing
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 84% YoY and contributed about 53% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Covers stone aggregates, ready-mix concrete and asphalt; about 8.65 lakh MT delivered in the quarter.

segments.name: DaaS (Developer as a Service)
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR 28 crore, roughly 10% of top line, in Q1. New INR 650 crore mandate from Wadhwa Group (Mumbai); GDV under execution rose to over INR 1,800 crore from INR 1,250 crore at Q4 FY26. Management cited 60-65% EBITDA margin for DaaS.

segments.name: Asphalt (within contract manufacturing)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose to INR 53 crore from INR 30 crore in Q4 FY26; customers transacted rose to 38 from 28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10.5% EBITDA margin the new baseline, and is 10.5-11% the expected range?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin gain is mainly mix: contract manufacturing and DaaS, which carry higher margins than B2B, rose from about 46% to 63% of revenue; management expects this to sustain for the next few quarters. Directionally, 11% next year was agreed as fair.

qa_highlights.question: How much utilisation headroom is left in contract manufacturing and how will capacity grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 65-70% on about 9 million tonnes; 2-3 million tonnes to be added in the next two quarters by recycling existing deposits, taking capacity to about 11 million tonnes.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 35-40% guidance be raised, given Q1 and Q2 are seasonally lean?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is sticking to 35-40% annual growth; first six months about 40% of sales and second half about 60%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the credit losses and loss given default?
qa_highlights.answer: Cumulative ECL about INR 22 crore on about INR 3,800-4,000 crore lifetime revenue. Recoveries after legal process range from 25% to over 80%, and most new receivables are insured.

qa_highlights.question: How does supply chain financing work and does it cost interest?
qa_highlights.answer: Financiers pay vendors on day one and the company gets about 90 days to pay; interest is sometimes borne by vendors and is negotiated. Management said it accepts the interest cost to reduce working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Does DaaS expose the company to real estate risk and how is it paid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not a RERA promoter and does not lend or commit capital; income is a fixed monthly fee, a percentage of construction and a percentage of sales, with financial closure and bank loans in place on day one.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt path and what drives the rise to INR 75-80 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Current net debt INR 14.5 crore, net debt-to-equity 0.02x; the rise is to fund working capital for 35-40% growth, with Q3 and Q4 expected to be stronger on cash flows. Long-term net debt-to-equity to stay at 0.5-0.6x.

qa_highlights.question: How concentrated is the customer base and what is the DaaS sales commission benchmark?
qa_highlights.answer: Top 10 customers are 45-50% of revenue, spread across projects and regions. Management cited sales-only channels charging 2-3% and some 4-5% of GDV, arguing DaaS covers far more than sales.

qa_highlights.question: What is the asphalt outlook and when is the subsidiary merger completed?
qa_highlights.answer: Asphalt is about six months old, with Q3 and Q4 expected to be meaningfully higher; management expects a meaningful FY27 contribution without giving numbers. Subsidiary merger: three of four regulators have cleared it and it is at the last stage, timeline not committed.

544420|2026-03.headline: Raymond Realty FY26 total income rose 29% to INR3,039 crores; Q4 income up 53% to INR1,176 crores with 139% YoY bookings surge.
544420|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of validation, with total income of INR3,039 crores (+29% YoY), Q4 income of INR1,176 crores (+53%) and FY26 blended EBITDA of INR495 crores at roughly 16% margin, versus 13% in the first nine months. Q4 EBITDA margin was 21.5% as stated in the opening remarks and about 21% per the Q&A. JDA share of pre-sales reached 54% in FY26, a 50:50 own-land-to-JDA mix target achieved a year ahead of FY27 schedule. Management guided FY27 blended EBITDA margin of 16% to 18%, minimum 20% growth in pre-sales and top-line, and cash-negative operations for the next two years.

financial_highlights.change: vs around 13% in first nine months

financial_highlights.value: 139% YoY surge (quarter as stated, not specified)

segments.name: Thane (own legacy land, Pokhran Road)
segments.commentary: Pokhran Road 100-acre land has total revenue potential of INR25,000 crores, with about 60 acres under development. Thane pre-sales were INR1,360 crores in FY26 versus INR1,800 crores in FY25 and INR1,950 crores in FY24; management says the 4-5 year average of INR1,300-1,500 crores is achievable. Pokhran Road pre-sales were close to INR1,400 crores in FY27 to date.

segments.name: JDA portfolio (non-Thane)
segments.commentary: Seven JDA projects with combined revenue potential of about INR17,000 crores, including Kandivali (GDV INR3,000 crores, 70% revenue share to Raymond). JDAs were 22% of booking values in FY25 and 54% of pre-sales in FY26 from non-Thane land.

segments.commentary: First project launched by the company, about 3,100 homes, fully sold out and has received full OC during the year.

qa_highlights.question: Thane pre-sales have fallen from INR1,950 crores (FY24) to INR1,360 crores (FY26). Is competition rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Thane sales depend on each year's product mix; competition has been intense for 20 years. Average Thane sales of INR1,300-1,500 crores a year are achievable; no cause for concern.

qa_highlights.question: Why do JDA launch timelines vary so much (e.g., Mahim signed in CY23 still not launched)?
qa_highlights.answer: Each deal differs by maturity and counterparty speed. BKC took about 9 months from start; Mahim has taken about 2.5 years due to society governance issues. Average is 15-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin outlook and how is it booked?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended FY26 margin about 16%; new JDAs start in single digits but are contracted at 20%+. FY27 blended margin guided at 16-18%. Revenue recognised on percentage-of-completion basis.

qa_highlights.question: What is the effective economic interest in Kandivali and Sion sales response?
qa_highlights.answer: Kandivali GDV INR3,000 crores with 70% revenue share to Raymond, target margin about 20-22%. Pokhran Road pre-sales around INR1,400 crores in FY27 so far; Sion launched 24 March (about one week of selling) with strong response.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating cash flow turn positive in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No: management expects cash-negative operations for the next two years; internal accruals of INR600-650 crores to keep growing and be reinvested.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of commodity and Morbi gas-supply disruption on costs?
qa_highlights.answer: 3-4% cost impact possible if prolonged; no material impact if resolved in 2-3 months. Suppliers continue at contracted rates; no supply disruption; management sees no EBITDA impact.

Valuation remains low; management said market awaits consistency over 6-8 quarters.

544420|2026-06.headline: Raymond Realty Q1 FY27 booking value rose 129% YoY to INR700 crore; FY27 guidance of 20%+ presales growth and 17-19% EBITDA margin reiterated.

qa_highlights.question: How is capital allocation and funding aligned with the pipeline?

544420|2026-09.headline: Raymond Realty Q2 FY27 total income rose 7% YoY to INR757 crore, EBITDA margin 15%, booking value up 111% YoY in H1 to INR1,602 crore.

Quarterly pre-sales nearly doubled with no new launches, and H1 booking value reached INR1,602 crore (+111% YoY) while collections rose 67% to INR682 crore in Q2. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20% pre-sales growth, 17-19% EBITDA margin, 20% ROCE and 9-10% PAT margin, and dropped explicit revenue growth guidance. An ICICI Prudential AIF subsidiary investment of INR210 crore for the Mahim project and a INR400 crore promoter equity infusion were announced, with debt held near INR1,200 crore.

544421|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 reported EBITDA of ~260m (30% margin) included ~46m of one-offs; adjusted ~304m (35%), with gases segment margin 40% in Q4 and 38.4% for FY26.

Existing non-Uluberia capacity is fully utilised; growth depends on new capacity additions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the order book and what pipeline exists?
qa_highlights.answer: Current order book about INR700 crore; four tenders (~INR800 crore) awaiting opening; target at least INR500 crore new orders in 3-12 months, taking book to INR1,200-1,300 crore; next milestone INR1,500 crore by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables and inventory rise, and what is being done on cash conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables rose on Q4 final and pre-final bills (Aligarh NBCC billing expected to close by 15 September; Telecommunications India Limited by 30 September). Inventory rose on material bought in Feb-Mar 2026 ahead of price increases. Routine government and DPS bills take 30-40 days to realise.

qa_highlights.question: Why were some projects delayed and what is the stadium contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Stadium start was delayed by statutory approvals; it started scaling from March. Stadium revenue to date is about INR30-35 crore. Management said approvals for government projects now sit within EPC scope, making them faster.

qa_highlights.question: Will the current margins be sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident the current margins (about 17% EBITDA) are sustainable for the next one to two years.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR700 crore order book will be executed in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects INR300-350 crore of execution in FY27, based on current monthly run-rate of INR30-40 crore.

risks_watch: Receivable days elevated: final bills pending on NBCC Aligarh and Telecommunications India Limited; collection timing is key to cash flow.
Inventory and working capital rose faster than revenue; watch whether it normalises as orders scale.
Order inflow needed to reach INR1,200-1,500 crore target; four tenders (~INR800 crore) pending with no guaranteed wins.
Project start delays from statutory approvals (Bathinda, cricket stadium) can push revenue recognition out by 6-8 months.
Heavy reliance on government clients and top 5 projects (~70% of turnover).
