rows.why: Three new launches are planned in H1 FY27 (Aquaria and Trident this quarter, Sky Plaza in H1 with about 80% approvals), with three more H2 launches expected to get approvals in Q1 FY27, but Monarch, Avalon and Solana are delayed and the Ghatkopar matter is pending, so timing carries risk.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 pre-sales guided at INR1,800-2,000 crores versus INR1,157 crores in FY26 (about 55-73% growth), and revenue growth of 55-60% is guided, backed by six launches worth INR5,000-5,500 crores GDV, though collections of INR82 crores in Q4 against INR308 crores revenue show execution still lags.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided FY27 pre-sales of INR1,800-2,000 crores and revenue and PAT growth of 55-60%, with no sign of running ahead of this; Q4 PAT grew only 17% against 62% revenue growth, so there is no evidence yet of an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Monarch, Avalon and Solana are delayed, Sky Plaza is only about 80% approved, and collections (INR82 crores in Q4, INR376 crores in FY26 against INR769 crores revenue) lag, so FY27 pre-sales of INR1,800-2,000 crores depend on launches that are not yet fully approved.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Six named launches (Aquaria, Trident, Aurelia, Sky Plaza, Portofino, Odyssey) with GDV INR5,000-5,500 crores, three of them in H1 FY27 with combined revenue potential of INR2,500-3,000 crores, and Aquaria and Trident already at approval stage with launches planned this quarter.

rows.label: Collections catch-up as new projects reach plinth
rows.why: Collections were INR82 crores in Q4 against INR308 crores revenue and INR376 crores for FY26 against INR769 crores, with management expecting improvement as the four new projects move from basement to plinth and superstructure.

rows.label: Ultra-luxury pricing premium of 10-20% (up to 25%)
rows.why: Management says pricing is 10-20% (up to 25%) above competitors in each micro market, with Lotus Celestia booking INR155 crores within 7 days of launch and Q4 pre-sales of INR462 crores.

rows.label: Ghatkopar matter at Supreme Court (about INR600 crores GDV)
rows.why: The matter is pending at the Supreme Court with an outcome expected this year, and it covers about INR600 crores of GDV that could be affected either way.

tone.note: Management was confident on ultra-luxury demand, pricing power and the INR1,800-2,000 crore FY27 pre-sales target, but was evasive on weak collections, approval delays for Monarch, Avalon and Solana, and the Ghatkopar matter, and gave little numerical detail on cost and margin impact.

544469|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 pre-sales rose 567% YoY to INR409 crores and PAT grew 77% to INR46 crores at a 34.5% margin.
544469|2026-06.overview: Sri Lotus reported strong Q1 FY27 growth: pre-sales INR409 crores, collections INR150 crores (+115% YoY), revenue INR132 crores (+116%), and EBITDA INR48 crores (36.4% margin). Management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR1,800-2,000 crores pre-sales and 55-60% revenue and PAT growth. A new Juhu commercial redevelopment (GDV about INR1,600 crores) was won, and the company reported a net cash balance sheet of INR623 crores. Q&A surfaced some inconsistencies on launch timing and the split of Q1 pre-sales between new and existing launches.

segments.name: Residential redevelopment (Mumbai ultra-luxury)
segments.commentary: Core focus; 17 of 22 pipeline projects are redevelopment-led. Management says micro-market pricing is 10-15% above other developers, with 5-10% price rises seen over the past year.

segments.name: Commercial
segments.commentary: Two commercial projects in the pipeline; Juhu commercial-cum-retail redevelopment (GDV about INR1,600 crores) won, expected to start next year after approvals and take 3-4 years to complete.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales guidance maintained at INR1,800-2,000 crores; management said it will 'easily achieve' INR1,800 crores.
FY27 revenue and PAT growth guidance of 55-60% maintained.
EBITDA margin guidance 35-40% and PAT margin 25-30% stated in the prepared remarks; in Q&A the CEO quoted EBITDA margin of 33-36%, a discrepancy.
FY27 cash collections target of about INR1,000 crores, supported by billing on Arcadian and Varun (each about 90% complete) and Amalfi (60-70%) by year-end.

Four further launches in FY27 with combined GDV of INR3,500-4,000 crores: Lotus Sky Plaza (Oshiwara, about INR1,500 crores, H1-end or early Q3), Lotus Odyssey (Bandstand, about INR1,000 crores, Q4), Lotus Portofino (Versova, about INR500 crores, within 3-4 months), Lotus Aurelia (Napean Sea Road, INR600-700 crores).
Gift City project: mixed-use approvals (commercial, retail, residential) expected by end-2026, with construction to start after approvals.
Promoter stake about 82%; management targets dilution to 75% or below within the remaining two years of a three-year window, with no investor discussions yet.
capex_capacity: Two projects launched in Q1 FY27: Lotus Trident (Andheri West) and Lotus Aquaria (Prabhadevi), together GDV of INR1,350 crores; Aquaria company GDV about INR800 crores (saleable, excluding tenant areas), starting price about INR85,000 per sq ft.
Varun: plinth just completed, about 20 slabs; RCC work targeted by January and 90% of work by March.
Arcadian and Varun targeted at 90% of project cost and Amalfi at 60-70% by end-FY27.

Juhu commercial redevelopment: plot over 5,000 sq m; start next year after plan approvals, 3-4 years to complete. Part of the area to be rehoused for existing tenants, remainder for commercial pipeline; no rental retention decided.
Of the INR550 crores earmarked for subsidiary projects (Amalfi, Arcadian, Varun), INR271 crores deployed as of 30 June 2026. Net IPO proceeds about INR732 crores after INR792 crores fresh issue.
demand_pricing: Q1 pre-sales of INR409 crores: management said only about INR25 crores came from the two new launches; the remainder came from projects launched in FY26 and earlier. Trident already reported about INR150 crores of sales within one month, in July-August.
Management said about INR400-plus crores of sales came from Trident, Aquaria and Celestia over the last two quarters.
Sales pace: 20-30% of inventory sold at launch, then about 30% of stock offloaded per year over a roughly three-year build cycle.
Brand campaign across 11 Mumbai coastal projects is ongoing; sales and marketing spend about 1% of pre-sales, which management expects to be offset by lower brokerage.
Management cited Mumbai luxury housing demand growth of more than 11% while the broader market moderated; constrained supply in Worli, Bandra and South Mumbai.
Versova: three existing sea-facing projects with more society talks under way.

qa_highlights.question: Can the INR409 crore pre-sales support the INR2,000 crore FY27 guidance, and what supports 55-60% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO Sanjay Jain said the company is confident of easily achieving the INR1,800 crore pre-sales guidance, citing four new launches and strong response to Trident, Aquaria and Celestia.

qa_highlights.question: Timing and GDV of the upcoming launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Lotus Sky Plaza (Oshiwara, about INR1,500 crores) at H1-end or start of Q3; Lotus Odyssey (Bandstand, about INR1,000 crores) in Q4; Lotus Portofino (Versova, about INR500 crores) within 3-4 months; Lotus Aurelia (Napean Sea Road, INR600-700 crores).

qa_highlights.question: Juhu project details, margin and rental plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is more than 5,000 sq m plot in middle Juhu with existing shops and offices to be rehoused; no rental retention for this project. EBITDA around 40% and PAT 25-30% expected, which management said it will achieve or beat.

qa_highlights.question: Gap between Q1 pre-sales split and launch-driven sales?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Rakesh Gupta said about INR25 crores came from the two new launches, with the balance from FY26 and earlier launches. The CEO had earlier cited Trident's INR150 crores within one month, which relates to July-August rather than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Cash collection goal and EBITDA margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Collection target about INR1,000 crores this year as billing rises on Arcadian, Varun and Amalfi. CEO said EBITDA margin is in the 33-36% range, which differs from the 35-40% guidance in the prepared remarks.

qa_highlights.question: Price increases and premium versus peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Price rises of 5-10% over the past year. Pricing about 10-15% above other developers in the same micro-markets, per the CEO.

qa_highlights.question: Leverage plans and net worth?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment is about 10% of GDV in redevelopment. Management cited total GDV of about INR18,000 crores and net worth of about INR1,900 crores, with annual net worth additions expected.

qa_highlights.question: Promoter stake dilution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoter stake about 82%; management said there are three years to reach 75% or below, with two years remaining, but no investor discussions yet.

risks_watch: Q1 pre-sales of INR409 crores is mostly from FY26-and-earlier launches (about INR25 crores from the two new launches per CFO), so FY27 guidance of INR1,800-2,000 crores relies on four launches totalling INR3,500-4,000 crores GDV landing on schedule.

Launch timing is inconsistent: Lotus Sky Plaza is guided to H1-end or start of Q3, Lotus Odyssey to Q4, and Portofino within 3-4 months; the answer on the number of FY27 launches also shifted between four and six projects in Q&A.
EBITDA margin guidance conflicts: prepared remarks say 35-40%, while the CEO cited 33-36% in Q&A; Juhu project margin was given as about 40% EBITDA. Track which range is reiterated next quarter.

Cash collection target of about INR1,000 crores depends on billing milestones on Arcadian and Varun (about 90% complete) and Amalfi (60-70%) by March 2027; Varun is only just past plinth with about 20 slabs done.

Juhu commercial redevelopment (GDV about INR1,600 crores) starts only after plan approvals next year, with 3-4 years to complete; Gift City mixed-use approvals are targeted by end-2026, and Lotus Monarch paperwork is still ongoing.

Pipeline GDV figures differ across answers (INR17,500-18,000 crores on the call versus about INR16,500-16,700 crores as of March plus INR1,600 crores Juhu); the promoter stake is about 82% with a 75% target within two years and no investor talks yet.
key_quotes: So, we are very confident that we will easily achieve the INR1,800 crores guidance.
So, this INR800 crore s is company part only. What we disclose as a GDV is our saleable portion only.
So, we have got total three years. One year has passed, so we have still two years to go.
544469|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and promotional on demand, pricing and the launch pipeline, with firm reiteration of FY27 guidance. Less precise under questioning: the CFO and CEO gave conflicting answers on the Q1 pre-sales split, launch count and EBITDA margin range, and several answers were corrected mid-stream.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin 36.4% and guidance of 35-40% in prepared remarks, but CEO cited 33-36% in Q&A, so the range is unsettled and the Juhu project is guided at about 40% EBITDA.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Four further launches worth INR3,500-4,000 crore GDV are planned, with Sky Plaza at H1-end or early Q3 (about INR1,500 crore), Odyssey in Q4 (about INR1,000 crore) and Portofino within 3-4 months (about INR500 crore); only about INR25 crore of Q1 pre-sales came from the two new launches.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 pre-sales guided at INR1,800-2,000 crore against INR409 crore in Q1, and revenue and PAT growth guided at 55-60%, with Q1 revenue up 116% YoY to INR132 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Juhu redevelopment (GDV about INR1,600 crore) is won and starts after approvals next year, and Gift City approvals are targeted by end-2026, but no new capex quantum is stated and investment is about 10% of GDV in redevelopment.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said it will 'easily achieve' INR1,800 crore pre-sales, but Q1 pre-sales were mostly from FY26-and-earlier launches, so an upgrade depends on launches landing and Trident's INR150 crore sales continuing.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Four launches totalling INR3,500-4,000 crore GDV must land on schedule, the launch count shifted between four and six in Q&A, and Varun is only just past plinth with about 20 slabs done against a January RCC target.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Four launches are guided (Sky Plaza, Odyssey, Portofino, Aurelia) with combined GDV of INR3,500-4,000 crore, though launch timing is inconsistent across answers.

rows.label: Juhu commercial redevelopment won (GDV about INR1,600 crore)
rows.when: start next year after approvals; 3-4 years to complete
rows.why: Project is won, but at 3-4 years to complete it adds little to revenue in the window and it starts only after plan approvals.

rows.label: Net cash INR623 crore; promoter stake dilution to 75% or below
rows.when: within two remaining years of three-year window
rows.why: Promoter stake is about 82% and the target is 75% or below, but management says there are no investor discussions yet.

rows.label: Brand campaign with lower brokerage offset
rows.why: Sales and marketing spend is about 1% of pre-sales, which management expects to be offset by lower brokerage, though no quantified saving is given.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, pricing (10-15% premium, 5-10% price rises) and the launch pipeline, and reiterated FY27 guidance. Analysts and the answers exposed inconsistencies on the Q1 pre-sales split (only about INR25 crore from new launches), launch count and timing, and the EBITDA margin

544469|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 pre-sales rose 83% YoY to INR470 crore and EBITDA more than doubled to INR107 crore at a 39.9% margin.
544469|2026-09.overview: Management reported strong Q2 and H1 FY27 growth in pre-sales, revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with margins above 38%. Three redevelopment projects were added in the quarter, adding an estimated INR2,700-2,800 crore GDV, taking the pipeline to 24 projects and about INR20,000 crore GDV. Collections were weaker at INR60 crore in Q2 and INR209 crore in H1, which management attributed to construction-linked billing and expects to improve in H2. Analysts focused on collections, the INR300 crore business development outflow, Prabhadevi sales traction and project timeline slippage.

segments.name: Lotus Trident (Andheri West, luxury commercial)
segments.commentary: Contributed INR178 crore pre-sales in its first full quarter after end-June launch, about 35% of sales sold within three months per management. Management guided EBITDA margin of 33-35%.

segments.name: Residential luxury projects
segments.commentary: Celestia reported 36% sales within six months of launch. Lotus Aquaria (Prabhadevi) reported healthy inquiries, but Lotus Prabhadevi (GDV ~INR800 crore) contributed no pre-sales in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales guidance reiterated at INR1,800-2,000 crore.
FY27 revenue and PAT growth guided at 55-60% over FY26.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 35-40% and PAT margin at 25-30%.
Four H2 FY27 launches planned: Lotus Aurelia, Lotus Sky Plaza, Lotus Portofino and Lotus Odyssey, combined GDV INR3,500-4,000 crore; about 90% approvals in place.
Project-level surplus estimated at about INR9,500 crore over the development cycle; projects expected to complete over the next 4-4.5 years.
Management expects H2 collections to be much better than H1 as projects reach plinth level; FY28 collection guidance to be given at the start of FY28.
Amara and Athena expected to receive OC in FY27 (Amara within the quarter or by March; Athena before March).
capex_capacity: Pipeline of 24 ongoing and upcoming projects, aggregate GDV ~INR20,000 crore, of which 19 are redevelopment-led.
Business development: Lotus Impressa (Shivaji Park, Dadar West), Lotus Stellar (Versova) and Lotus Supremus (Juhu) added in Q2.
INR550 crore of IPO proceeds earmarked for subsidiary (Amalfi, Arcadian, Varun); INR305 crore deployed as of 30 Sep 2026 of INR732 crore net proceeds.
Upfront premium paid to government for new projects in Q2, which management said is to save costs and secure supplier discounts; new projects typically need 8-10% of project cost to start.
GIFT City plot of 5.5 acres on Sabarmati riverfront; expected 1.3-1.5 million sq ft mixed-use development subject to town planning scheme approval.
Lotus Monarch timeline pushed out by one year due to society, trust, Charity Commissioner and government approvals; Ghatkopar (Salona) timeline also extended.
demand_pricing: Management says the luxury segment is less sensitive to RBI's 25 bps repo hike to 5.5% (first hike since early 2023); buyers rely less on home loans.
Mumbai H1 CY2026 sales of homes priced above INR10 crore reached a record INR18,500 crore; prime residential prices up 6.2% YoY per management.
Management says prices have risen across almost all projects in H1 and will rise further as construction progresses if the market supports it.
Management says it is the only suburban player to have completed a commercial redevelopment (Arc One), and has 2-3 more commercial redevelopment projects; about five commercial projects in portfolio.
Prabhadevi (Lotus Aquaria) pricing set at a premium, with 270-degree sea view and ~200 m Art Deco tower; management says no pushback, pre-sales expected to show in next two quarters.
Collections as a share of pre-sales: management said completion-stage projects carry 90-95% balance due, and expects 95-100% collection on three projects completing next year.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are margins above 35% during expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited net debt-free status (no interest burden), minimal marketing spend, a 2.5-3.5 year project cycle that speeds fund deployment, and premium pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected for Trident and what is the commercial redevelopment outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO guided Trident EBITDA margin at 33-35%, in line with guidance. Management expects commercial redevelopment to carry sustainable margins and cited 2-3 more projects.

qa_highlights.question: How will collections catch up with pre-sales?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said collections are construction-linked: about 5-10% at launch and about 25% at plinth. Of about INR800 crore H1 pre-sales, INR200 crore was collected, and H2 should improve as two of three recent projects move past basement.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term growth beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gives annual guidance only. It pointed to ~INR20,000 crore GDV and ~INR9,500 crore project surplus, with completion over the next 4-4.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did timelines shift for upcoming projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Lotus Monarch moved out by one year due to multiple approving bodies. Ghatkopar (Salona) timeline also extended. Management says overall guidance is unchanged and new projects will replace slipped ones.

qa_highlights.question: Why no Prabhadevi pre-sales, and will the business development outflow constrain the company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Prabhadevi is a new micromarket with marketing under way and results expected in two quarters. The INR300 crore outflow was upfront government fees and discounted supplier payments; management said cash is sufficient. Operating cash flow will stay negative in launch periods, though Arcadian is working-capital positive.

risks_watch: Collections lag: Q2 collections of INR60 crore and H1 of INR209 crore against H1 pre-sales of about INR800-879 crore; track whether H2 collections rise as two of three recent projects move past basement to plinth.

Timeline slippage: Lotus Monarch pushed out by one year (society, trust, Charity Commissioner, government approvals) and Ghatkopar (Salona) extended; watch whether replacement projects keep FY27 guidance intact.

Cash deployment: INR305 crore of INR732 crore IPO net proceeds deployed by 30 Sep 2026; management says operating cash flow may stay negative in launch periods, with no FY28 collection guidance until start of FY28.
Prabhadevi (Lotus Aquaria, GDV ~INR800 crore) had no Q2 pre-sales; management expects results in next two quarters at a premium price point.
Delivery of four H2 FY27 launches (combined GDV INR3,500-4,000 crore, about 90% approvals) and the FY27 pre-sales guidance of INR1,800-2,000 crore versus H1 INR879 crore.
key_quotes: Delighted to share that we recorded pre-sales for the quarter at INR470 crores, up 83% year-on-year.
Collections in our business are linked to construction milestones and can vary from quarter -to-quarter.
So, right now, it's not a good time to because we need to evaluate and update you.
So, project-wise, yes, but overall, maybe we cannot give that.
544469|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on sales, margins and launch plans, with the CEO and CFO more cautious and non-committal on collection timing, FY28 numbers and operating cash flow, deferring to the start of FY28 or project-level answers. Management repeatedly stressed the net debt-free balance sheet and construction-linked billing as the reason collections trail pre-sales.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin was 39.9% and H1 38.8%, against FY27 guidance of 35-40%; management cites net debt-free status, minimal marketing spend and premium pricing, while Trident is guided at 33-35%, which dilutes the blend.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No unit capacity is measured for a developer; the four H2 FY27 launches (combined GDV INR3,500-4,000 crore, about 90% approvals) and the 24-project pipeline (~INR20,000 crore GDV) are the closest equivalent, but Lotus Monarch slipped one year and GIFT City is subject to town planning approval.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Pre-sales grew 83% YoY in Q2 to INR470 crore and 176% in H1 to INR879 crore, and FY27 revenue and PAT growth of 55-60% is held, with Trident contributing INR178 crore in its first full quarter; Lotus Prabhadevi (GDV ~INR800 crore) has yet to contribute pre-sales.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Three redevelopment projects were added in Q2 and INR305 crore of INR732 crore IPO proceeds is deployed, so further business development is likely but no new capex plan with a date was stated; utilisation is not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated all FY27 guidance rather than raising it, and the H2 ramp required to hit pre-sales of INR1,800-2,000 crore leaves little room for an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 pre-sales of INR879 crore against FY27 guidance of INR1,800-2,000 crore requires a steep H2 ramp, collections were only INR209 crore in H1, and Lotus Monarch and Ghatkopar timelines have slipped.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Four launches are planned for H2 FY27 (Lotus Aurelia, Lotus Sky Plaza, Lotus Portofino, Lotus Odyssey) with combined GDV of INR3,500-4,000 crore and about 90% approvals in place.

rows.label: Collections lag pre-sales; H2 collections expected to improve
rows.why: Collections were INR60 crore in Q2 and INR209 crore in H1 against H1 pre-sales of about INR800-879 crore, and management expects H2 to be much better as projects reach plinth, with about 25% collected at plinth.

rows.label: Net debt-free with INR494 crore net cash
rows.why: Net cash position of INR494 crore at 30 Sep 2026 with the IPO proceeds still INR427 crore undeployed (INR732 crore less INR305 crore).

rows.label: Amara and Athena receive OC in FY27
rows.why: Management expects Amara (within the quarter or by March) and Athena (before March) to receive occupancy certificate, which would convert completed projects into revenue recognition and collections of 95-100% on three completing projects.

tone.note: Management was confident on pre-sales, margins and the four H2 launches, and cautious or deferred on collection timing, FY28 numbers and operating cash flow; analysts probed collections, the INR300 crore business development outflow, Prabhadevi sales traction and timeline slippage.

544470|2026-03.headline: M&B Engineering FY26 revenue rose 27% to INR1,259.7 crores, but Q4 EBITDA margin fell to 11.9% on forex loss and steel/freight costs; no margin guidance given.
544470|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 27% to INR1,260 crores and PAT rose 20% to INR92.6 crores, but Q4 revenue (INR364 crores, +16%) saw EBITDA flat at INR43 crores and margin down to 11.9% from 14%. Management attributed the margin squeeze to a INR3.9 crore Q4 forex loss (mostly unrealised translation), a 20%+ jump in domestic steel prices, and sharply higher export freight after the Iran conflict; it says adjusted EBITDA excluding forex is about 13%. Volume growth in Phenix was only about 8% in Q4 versus an expected ~15%, due to raw material and gas disruptions in March. Management guided top-line growth of 23-25% for FY27 but declined to give margin guidance.

segments.name: Phenix (PEB)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR985 crores, +29%; export revenue INR165.6 crores. Order book INR871 crores, of which export INR279 crores (32%). Sanand plant utilisation ~75-76% in FY26.

segments.name: Proflex (self-supported roofing)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR275 crores, +23%. Order book INR212 crores. One new unit from UAE commissioned January 2026; two US units expected Q2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth guided at around 25%; management later cited a 23-25% range, and 20-25% volume growth in PEB and Proflex.
No EBITDA margin guidance for FY27: management cited steel price volatility, uncertain freight, FX and the conflict; will reassess after at least one more quarter.
FY27 export target about INR275-300 crores (around 10,000 tons vs 7,400 tons in FY26); export EBITDA expected 16-17% vs 10-11% domestic at current cost structure.
H1 FY27 expected softer due to Q1 labour availability and Q2 monsoon; H2 historically stronger.
FY27 capex about INR100 crores, including Sanand expansion, part Cheyyar expansion (H2) and maintenance capex.
US sectoral tariff reduced by 25% (effective 6 April per management); benefit partly shared with customers under contract clauses.
capex_capacity: Sanand: adding about 20,000 MT, commissioning expected Q2 FY27, taking capacity to 92,000 MTPA; utilisation expected 65-68% after expansion, peak 75%.
Cheyyar (Tamil Nadu): FY26 utilisation 50-55%; target 68-70% in FY27, with 75% as peak; expansion planned to be operational Q1 or Q2 FY28.
Proflex: installed capacity to rise by about 200,000 sq m p.a. once two US units are commissioned in Q2 FY27.
Volume targets FY27: PEB 85,000-90,000 MT (from ~72,000); Proflex 1.70-1.725 million sq m.
IPO proceeds INR259.32 crores; INR137.81 crores (53%) utilised to 31 March 2026, INR7.5 crores in Q4.
demand_pricing: Order inflow Q4 about INR387-388 crores, down from INR480 crores in Q3 (per analyst); FY26 record inflow INR1,539 crores.
Bid pipeline cited at about INR1,000-1,100 crores across sectors; domestic inquiries in last three months exceeded the prior remaining part of the year.
Export order closures slowing: US cycle time rose from 6-8 weeks to 12-16 weeks amid US inflation and cost pressures.

Steel prices rose about 20%+ in the last quarter (cited INR49,500/t to INR58,500/t); fixed-price contracts with 6-12 month execution; 80-85% of raw material is covered at order booking, 15-20% left open for non-standard items.
New orders being quoted at higher prices; price not locked until advance received. Export freight: a USD 2,000 war surcharge added; cushion built into quotes.
Export realisation about INR2.3-2.7 lakh/t vs domestic about half, driven by US bought-out items costing INR1-2 lakh/t and freight/duties.

qa_highlights.question: How do you see FY27 EBITDA margins given the geopolitical situation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide, citing steel price swings (+20% in a quarter), uncertain freight and FX; it will wait at least one more quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export outlook and pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Export target at least INR300 crores in FY27 (vs INR165 crores) per Malav Patel; later cited INR275-300 crores and about 10,000 tonnes; US order closures have slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 volumes grow only ~8% vs ~15% expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material and steel mill disruptions in March (two major suppliers shut, gas shortages); management estimated 10-15% volume lost to the war.

qa_highlights.question: Are there any signs of demand slowdown in PEB?

544471|2026-03.headline: H2 FY26 revenue fell to Rs 28.97 crore with 5.32% EBITDA margin as management deferred loss-making fixed-price contracts amid component inflation.
544471|2026-03.overview: Takyon reported H2 FY26 (Oct 2025 to Mar 2026) consolidated revenue of Rs 28.97 crore, EBITDA of Rs 1.61 crore (5.32% margin) and PAT of Rs 0.44 crore. Full-year FY26 revenue was Rs 71.05 crore, EBITDA Rs 7.09 crore (near 10%), PAT Rs 3.65 crore and EPS Rs 3.29. H1 FY26 revenue was Rs 42.08 crore with EBITDA margin near 13%. Management attributed the H2 shortfall to component price inflation and lengthened lead times, and said it chose to defer unviable fixed-price contracts and protect the balance sheet. Total liabilities fell from Rs 50 crore to Rs 12.20 crore and trade payables from Rs 30.21 crore to Rs 3.77 crore.

544484|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 standalone revenue up 49.1% YoY and FY26 revenue of INR 2,441 crore, with same-store sales growth of 34% spread evenly across all three months. The store base reached 340 stores in 134 cities after adding 17 stores in Q4 and 65 in FY26, below the 83 added in FY25 and below the RHP plan of 290 stores over FY26-FY27. Management said pre-Ind AS EBITDA margins improved YoY despite a mix shift toward plain gold, and attributed the recovery to rapid entry-level repricing and vertical integration. Gold price inflation inflated closing inventory, which pushed inventory turns down to about 1.13x from 1.3x in FY25.

qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the fall mainly to a one-off rise in closing inventory value from gold prices. Mature stores (3-4+ years) run at 1.7x-1.9x turns.

544484|2026-06.headline: BlueStone Q1 FY27 revenue rose 49% YoY to INR 733 crore, with pre-Ind AS EBITDA up 135% to INR 55 crore and margin at 7.5%.
544484|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 49% YoY to INR 733 crore and pre-Ind AS EBITDA rose 135% to INR 55 crore, lifting operating margin to 7.5% (up 273 bps). Management attributed this to operating leverage despite a custom duty hike on gold from 6% to 15% that softened demand in May before June and July recovered. Same-store sales growth was 39%, repeat revenue share rose to about 60%, while new customer additions reportedly fell from about 50,000 to about 40,000 per quarter, which management tied to merchandise dislocation during the sharp gold rise. Management reiterated a long-term target of roughly INR 12,000 crore revenue in four years, around 30% SSSG and about 20% store distribution growth, though analysts questioned the arithmetic.

financial_highlights.value: About INR 50 crore, about 6.9% of revenue
financial_highlights.change: Flat vs 6.9% in same quarter last year
Up from INR 2,650 crore at March

segments.commentary: Management said more than 80% of sales originate online, with stores converting intent built online. Company describes itself as a consumer internet business that sells jewellery.

segments.name: Stores
segments.commentary: Network of 352 stores; recent stores are around 4,500 sq ft frontage, and management said operational sq ft and per-store unit economics are unchanged. Store additions guided to about 20% CAGR over four years, with a 70-80 annual run rate referenced.

segments.commentary: About 95% of products sold are manufactured in-house; management estimates a 300-400 bps margin delta versus peers but stresses design control as the main rationale.

Around 20% distribution (store) CAGR guided over next four years; store additions expected to be non-linear.
demand_pricing: Demand softened in May after the gold import duty hike (6% to 15%), then recovered through June; management said July trends were similar to June.
Gold exchange volumes rose as gold prices climbed; management said no significant change in the last 1-2 weeks.
New customer additions fell from about 50,000 to about 40,000 per quarter, which management attributed to merchandise dislocation; repeat revenue growth was strong.
Repeat AOVs are said to be 20-30% higher than new-customer AOVs; blended AOV about INR 78,000.
Management says no 9-carat plans; 14-carat experiments are used in lower price points. Lab-grown diamonds are said to be under 1% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How is demand trending into July after the May softness from the duty hike?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand softened in May, recovered through June, and July is tracking similarly to June with no major difference.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said stable gold is most supportive for demand and that Q3 last year was its slowest quarter in history during the sharpest gold rise; it does not expect a headwind.

qa_highlights.question: Why has new customer addition fallen to about 40,000 and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged the drop, attributed it to merchandise dislocation being fixed, and said month-on-month new customer trends are improving.

qa_highlights.question: Math behind the 50% revenue CAGR given 30% SSSG and 20% distribution growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 30% refers to mature-cohort SSSG at maturity (years 3-6), not reported SSSG, and that reported SSSG would be higher due to new stores.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin expanded about 100 bps excluding inventory gain; what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mix changes in studded share were not material; contribution margin, the more relevant metric, has been largely stable, and EBITDA expansion comes from operating leverage.

qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is about INR 2,800 crore at end June versus INR 2,650 crore in March; management said store additions and gold prices drive the balance and turns should improve.

qa_highlights.question: Why 20% distribution growth rather than a slower pace?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most operating leverage comes from corporate and marketing scale rather than store-level profit, so faster distribution growth is preferred.

qa_highlights.answer: Marketing was about INR 50 crore, 6.9% of revenue, same as last year; it fell from about 9.2% four years ago to 6.6% in FY26.

544484|2026-09.headline: BlueStone Q2 FY27 revenue grew 44% YoY to INR 738 crore, EBITDA more than doubled, and the company posted its fourth consecutive standalone profitable quarter.
544484|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue of INR 738 crore, up 44% YoY, with EBITDA more than doubling and a fourth straight profitable quarter on a standalone basis. Management said about 29% of the 44% growth came from AOV increase, with the rest from buyer growth, and that SSSG was around 28% in the quarter. The company crossed 1 million customers, opened 27 stores across 7 new cities, and reset entry-level price points, which lowered sequential AOV. Management said festive-season timing shifted some demand into Q3, and that early Q3 trends were in line with expectations, with most big buying days still ahead.

Management said repeat customers buy at higher AOV than new customers, and that repeat is strong (rejecting an analyst's flattish-repeat characterisation).
Management said new-customer growth was weaker last year after gold rose 50-70%, and that entry price points were redesigned from Q3 FY26.
Festive timing: Navratri started late, so only 10-11 days of the season were visible at the time of the call; Karwa Chauth and Dhanteras are still ahead.
Lab-grown diamonds: management said consumers in stores are not asking for LGD; the company's solitaire share is under 1%, and LGD is taking share mainly from solitaires.

544487|2026-06.overview: Total income reached INR310.24 crores, up 69.35% YoY from INR183.19 crores, while EBITDA grew 23.92% to INR19.68 crores and PAT rose 37.43% to INR9.52 crores (EPS INR2.85). Management attributed the margin compression (about 133 bps decline cited, and a 233 bps figure also mentioned) to a higher raw-material-intensity mix in manufacturing, export and commodity-linked business amid volatile raw material prices and odd order timing. The company added stores at Rasayani and Babgaon in Q1 and opened its 53rd store at Uran (Raigad) after quarter-end, and expanded Indian Chaska into Madhya Pradesh. Management guided to positive operating cash flow by H1 FY27 and 8 to 10 new stores in FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +69.35% YoY vs INR183.19 crores in Q1 FY26
decline of 133 bps as stated (233 bps also cited in same answer)

financial_highlights.value: around INR101 crores (as referenced by analyst)

financial_highlights.metric: Private label contribution to retail sales

segments.name: Retail (Patel R-Mart)
segments.commentary: 53 stores after Uran opening; average monthly sales per store put at INR80 lakh to INR1 crore, mature-store sales about INR20,000 per sq ft; ticket size INR500 to INR1,000; wastage below 0.1%. Payback about 24 months.

segments.name: Manufacturing / food processing
segments.commentary: Utilisation currently 50% to 55%, targeted at around 80% to 82% by FY27-FY28; automation expected to cut labour cost and improve quality consistency. Private label share of domestic sales cited at 45%, export sales at 37%.

segments.name: Exports and B2B
segments.commentary: Management stated about 40% of revenue from exports and rest from manufacturing and retail; export contribution to bottom line cited as 35% to 40%. These figures were not reconciled in the call.

segments.name: Indian Chaska (brand)
segments.commentary: Expanded to Madhya Pradesh in August 2026, taking presence to eight states and one union territory; MP averaging INR10 lakh to INR12 lakh per month; whole spices category to be added this quarter.

segments.name: Online / quick commerce
segments.commentary: App has more than 50,000 downloads but online sales were around INR50 lakh in Q1; private label not yet listed on Blinkit or Zepto, with per-SKU terms being finalised; pilot quick commerce running from first stores.

segments.name: Apparel and fashion (general merchandise)
segments.commentary: 8% to 9% of revenue; inventory holding period 15 to 20 days.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected to move back toward 8% to 9% over coming quarters, with margin in Q1 not treated as steady state.
Positive operating cash flow expected by H1 FY27; conversion of current assets built up in FY26 into cash targeted.
8 to 10 new stores targeted by FY27, each expected to generate about INR1 crore per month in revenue.
Capacity utilisation targeted at around 80% to 82% by end-FY27 to FY28.
Expansion into Western suburbs and Pune/PCMC over the next five years, cluster-based; more gaps still being identified.
capex_capacity: Current processing utilisation 50% to 55%; medium-term target 80% to 82%.
New store payback about 24 months to recover capex and inventory rotation; store size and investment about 5,000 to 6,000 per sq ft as stated.
Automation being introduced at processing facilities, aimed at labour cost reduction and unified quality.
Store additions in Q1 at Rasayani and Babgaon; Uran (53rd store) opened after quarter-end.
Pune/PCMC store economics said to be broadly similar to existing network; 2 to 3 pockets identified.
demand_pricing: Management attributed Q1 margin decline to higher raw material intensity in export and commodity-linked business and volatile raw material prices.
Mature-store sales about INR20,000 per sq ft (retail); average monthly sales per store INR80 lakh to INR1 crore.
Online remains touch-and-feel in Tier-2/3/4 locations; society-focused activation and 30-60 minute delivery trials underway.
Private label planned as combo packs (e.g., rice, dal, salt) to make per-SKU listing and ad costs sustainable on quick commerce.
Plans to launch 2 to 3 more Indian Chaska categories (e.g., protein-related) from next quarter, targeting categories with INR2,000 to 3,000 crore market size.

qa_highlights.question: What must improve to move EBITDA margin from about 6.3% back to 8% to 9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 decline was due to higher raw material intensity in manufacturing, export and commodity-linked mix and volatile raw material prices; it expects improvement in coming quarters and not treating Q1 as steady state.

qa_highlights.question: Positive operating cash flow by H1 FY27 still on track, and working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 balance sheet and cash flow not yet published; expects much better operating cash flow by H1, converting FY26 current-asset build into cash.

qa_highlights.question: How many new stores in FY27 and revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: 8 to 10 stores by FY27, expected to contribute around INR1 crore per month in revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Current utilisation and target?
qa_highlights.answer: Current utilisation 50% to 55%; targeted around 80% to 82% in the medium term, by end-FY27 to FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Share of own brands across channels?
qa_highlights.answer: Own brands about 17.5% of overall revenue; private label 17.55% of retail sales, 37% of export sales and 45% of domestic sales as stated by the CFO.

qa_highlights.question: Performance of recently opened stores vs older stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new stores are operationally breakeven since day one, with some growing strongly; payback target about 24 months.

risks_watch: Margin recovery to 8% to 9% depends on raw material cost stability; Q1 EBITDA margin about 6.3%.
Operating cash flow guidance for H1 FY27 unverified; balance sheet and cash flow not yet published; inventory and receivables elevated after FY26 build.
Online and quick commerce traction remains small (about INR50 lakh in Q1) and competition from platform in-house brands noted by analysts.
Internal inconsistencies in disclosed figures (133 bps vs 233 bps margin decline; export share 40% vs 35% to 40% export contribution to bottom line) need clarification.
Store maturity: some stores still not up to mark per management; 8 to 10 new stores in FY27 execution.
544487|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on growth and store ramp-up but cautious and somewhat non-specific on margin and cash flow timing; several answers deferred figures (e.g., online targets, five-year scale) and the call had audio breaks during key answers.
key_quotes: Total income stood at INR310.24 crores, registering a robust 69.35% year -on-year growth compared with INR183.19 crores in Q1 FY '26.
The payback period for my new store is almost 24 months to recover the entire capex and the rotation of the inventory

The private level contribution to our retail sales is almost 17.55%, and for our rest of sales is almost 37% in my export sales and 45% in my domestic sales.
Right. So, the current utilization is between 50% to 55%, but in the medium term by the end of FY27, FY28, we plan on getting this utilization to around 80%, 80%, 82%.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.why: Automation is being introduced to cut labour cost and unify quality, and is the stated lever to lift utilisation from 50-55% to 80-82%.

rows.label: Positive operating cash flow by H1 FY27
rows.why: Management expects much better operating cash flow by H1 as FY26 current assets convert to cash, but Q1 cash flow was not yet published and inventory and receivables are elevated.

544488|2026-03.headline: Vikram Solar FY26 revenue hit a record INR4,800 crore (+40% YoY) with EBITDA margin up to 19%, but guided FY27 non-DCR per-watt EBITDA lower at INR1.75–2.
544488|2026-03.overview: FY26 set records on revenue (INR4,800 crore), volumes (3.3 GW, +76%), EBITDA (INR917 crore, 19% margin) and PAT (INR470 crore, 10% margin), with Q4 revenue of INR1,450 crore and first 1 GW quarterly run rate. Management said Q4 per-watt cost rose INR0.80 against a INR0.60 realisation gain, compressing per-watt EBITDA to about INR2.35. The order book stood at 8.2 GW at 31 March 2026, with distribution orders removed from the book and C&I DCR orders under renegotiation. The company announced a 6 GW wafer-ingot phase at Gangaikondan (about INR3,700 crore, commissioning FY29) and a 15 GWh BESS target by FY30, while the 9 GW TOPCon cell plant has been pushed to a phased commissioning through Q4 FY27 and ramp in Q2 FY28.

financial_highlights.value: 0.03; working capital net debt INR64 crore; no long-term debt

segments.name: Modules
segments.commentary: Q4 production about 1 GW, the highest ever; nameplate 9.5 GW today rising to 15.5 GW after Gangaikondan 6 GW module plant (first output guided June 2026). Cumulative global deployment crossed 10 GW (over 25 million modules).

segments.name: Cells
segments.commentary: No captive cell capacity yet; 9 GW TOPCon Plus cell plant at Gangaikondan targets first cell December 2026 and completion of phases through March 2027, with a further 3 GW in FY28. A 2 GW DCR cell procurement agreement with Jupiter International supports FY27 DCR offtake, weighted to H2.

segments.name: BESS
segments.commentary: 5 GWh cell-to-pack facility targeted by March 2027 (assembly capex about INR150 crore); 7.5 GWh cell phase 1 in FY29 and phase 2 in FY30 against a 15 GWh FY30 target.

segments.name: Wafer-ingot
segments.commentary: 6 GW phase 1 at Gangaikondan approved by the Board (about INR3,700 crore, commissioning FY29 per call, March 2028 in Q&A); the balance 6 GW is at about INR600 crore per GW, with Board approval planned next fiscal.

guidance_outlook: FY27 production guided at about 8 GW (6 GW non-DCR, 2 GW DCR) and FY27 EBITDA of INR1,500–1,600 crore, about 74% above FY26.
Non-DCR volumes guided to INR1.75–2.00 per watt-peak EBITDA on average through FY27; DCR-linked procurement volumes guided to INR2–2.5 per watt.
Per-watt EBITDA guided to about INR5 in FY28 post cell integration, with a further INR1 reduction as more capex comes in; the current level is about INR6 per watt-peak.
Standard nameplate utilisation of 65–70% for modules and 70–75% for cells after FY27 ramp.
Closing FY27 debt guided at about INR3,200 crore (earlier plan INR3,500 crore); FY28-end debt about INR6,500–6,600 crore; interest and DSCR guardrails above 2.5 and net debt/equity below 1.5.
capex_capacity: 9 GW TOPCon cell plant: civil works by September 2026, cleanroom/MEP October 2026, equipment installation October–November, power by Siemens in November, first cell end-December/early January, commissioning through March 2027, ramp in Q2 FY28; total cell capex for 12 GW about INR5,400 crore, mostly spent in FY27 with the last 10% instalment in FY28 (cost up 10% after switching equipment sourcing from Thailand to China).
Gangaikondan 6 GW module plant in final stretch, first output on track for June 2026; Vallam 5 GW built in under nine months.

Wafer-ingot phase 1 of 6 GW at Gangaikondan (about INR3,700 crore, commissioning FY29; Q&A said March 2028), with advances of under INR100 crore in FY27; BESS cell construction from October 2026 over 24 months, FY27 land and initial spend under INR200 crore.
Management expects standard utilisation of 65–70% on modules and 70–75% on cells, on nameplate basis.
Capex to be funded through a mix of debt and equity, and internal accruals; the company expects to fund FY27 BESS and wafer-ingot outflows largely from internal accruals.
demand_pricing: India added 45 GW of solar in FY26 (against a 24 GW target, about 87% above FY25); cumulative base 150 GW. Utility-scale additions were a record 34 GW and rooftop 8.5 GW.

Management sees over 80 GW of grandfathered Non-DCR demand over two years, about 28 GW of live utility-scale DCR tenders and about 25 GW of inherent DCR demand from C&I, KUSUM and rooftop. Management expects DCR demand of 20–25 GW in FY27.

Cell costs rose during FY26 on higher silver prices and removal of China's export VAT rebate. Aluminium rose from $3,100 to $3,600 per ton; EVA cost rose with crude; partly offset by lower cell prices.
Approximately 80% of the order book has cell price pass-through clauses; FY26 per-watt overhead fell 16%.
Q4 realisations rose about INR0.60 per watt-peak while cost rose INR0.80, compressing per-watt EBITDA to about INR2.35 (DCR mandate from June 2026).

Distribution order book (about 1 GW) was removed from the 1.9 GW Q4 order inflow and moved to spot buying; distribution network about 110+ distributors and 550+ dealers/SIs. A US export project of about 0.6 GW was dropped after the IPP found it unviable.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the 1 GW distribution order book removed, and does the 1.9 GW order inflow include distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inflow excludes distribution; the recurring distributor order book moved to spot buying as volumes shift to DCR and outsourced cell supply. Distribution was about 20% of Non-DCR volumes last year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA per watt-peak in Q4 and in the non-DCR business?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 per-watt EBITDA was about INR2.35, with non-DCR volumes guided at INR1.75–2 on average for FY27 and about INR5 for FY28 post cell integration (current about INR6).

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume and order plan?
qa_highlights.answer: About 8 GW of production in FY27 (2 GW DCR, 6 GW non-DCR) against 8.2 GW order book at March 2026, of which 6 GW goes out in FY27 leaving 1.2 GW, with the rest to be won from the 87 GW grandfathered Non-DCR pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt trajectory and interest outflow?
qa_highlights.answer: Closing FY27 debt guided at about INR3,200 crore and FY28 at INR6,500–6,600 crore; interest on construction projects is capitalised until commissioning, so P&L impact is deferred.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company handling the US export orders and where would it source cells?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exports to the US have slowed to near zero since November; about 1 GW of export orders are with long-standing IPPs and are being executed via cells sourced from North Africa, with EU, Australia and Middle East also explored.

qa_highlights.question: How are silver and silicon cost increases passed on to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: MSAs allow pass-through of cell cost and dollar appreciation to the extent of about 80% of the order book; future pass-through depends on the market once cell and wafer-ingot capacity comes in.

risks_watch: Per-watt EBITDA compression: Q4 cost rose INR0.80 vs realisation gain INR0.60, and FY27 non-DCR guidance is INR1.75–2, well below FY26 levels.

Execution risk on 9 GW cell plant (first cell targeted end-December 2026, ramp Q2 FY28) and 6 GW Gangaikondan module plant (June 2026); a sizable part of FY27 volume relies on a third-party 2 GW DCR cell supply.
Order book quality: about 1 GW distribution orders removed, C&I DCR orders under renegotiation, and US export order risk.
Rising interest and working capital needs with Vallam inventory; debt guardrails (DSCR above 2.5, net debt/equity below 1.5) and the INR6,500–6,600 crore FY28 debt level.
Raw material and silver cost pass-through (about 80% of order book) and cell price competition from domestic capacity additions.
544488|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and expansive on sector growth and integration, with the most specific numbers on FY26 records and FY27 guidance. Less specific or deferring on pricing (2 GW Jupiter procurement commercials not disclosed), US export orders and pass-through terms beyond the current 80% coverage.
key_quotes: The order inflow does not include distribution. We have taken that out of order booking format.
Yes, so when we spoke about a debt level of INR3,500 crores, the plan was to have an entire 12 gigawatt of cell in place, which we have now phased it into 9 plus 3.
Approximately 80% of our order book carries cell price pass-through clauses, insulating the P&L from any input volatility.
So that INR0.20 Additional incremental cost has dented the per-EBITDA-watt-peak to that extent and hence you could see a slight percentage impact on the EBITDA margin level.

Our working assumption is that the sector will stabilize around an 80 to 100 gigawatt of nameplate fully integrated sustainable capacity held by a small group of serious full-stack players, and the total addressable market is heading towards a similar number.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Per-watt EBITDA is guided to INR1.75-2.00 on non-DCR volumes for FY27, versus about INR6 per watt-peak today and Q4 per-watt EBITDA of about INR2.35 after a INR0.80 cost rise against a INR0.60 realisation gain; margin only recovers to about INR5 in FY28 after cell integration.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q4 FY26 to Q4 FY27 (module plant June 2026; 9 GW cell plant
rows.why: 6 GW Gangaikondan module plant first output guided June 2026 (nameplate rising from 9.5 GW to 15.5 GW), and the 9 GW TOPCon cell plant is under construction with INR5,400 crore total cell capex mostly spent in FY27; FY27 production guided at 7.5-8 GW.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 production guided at 7.5-8 GW versus 3.3 GW sold in FY26 (+76%), against an 8.2 GW order book at 31 March 2026 that covers about 6 GW of FY27 output, though distribution orders (about 1 GW) were removed from the book.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: 6 GW wafer-ingot phase 1 (about INR3,700 crore, commissioning FY29) is Board-approved, 15 GWh BESS target by FY30 is set, and the balance 6 GW wafer-ingot at about INR600 crore per GW goes to Board approval next fiscal; the capex pipeline is already committed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA guided at INR1,500-1,600 crore (about 74% above FY26) with per-watt EBITDA compressing, and the 9 GW cell plant has already slipped to phased commissioning through Mar 2027, leaving little room to raise guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Cell plant execution (first cell end-Dec 2026, ramp Q2 FY28), reliance on a third-party 2 GW DCR cell supply weighted to H2, C&I DCR orders under renegotiation, and US export orders near zero since November; per-watt EBITDA is already guided to INR1.75-2.00.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: 5 GWh cell-to-pack BESS facility targeted by March 2027 (assembly capex about INR150 crore) and TOPCon Plus cells from the 9 GW plant starting first cell December 2026 are the planned new product launches.

rows.label: FY27 closing debt at INR3,200 crore (below earlier INR3,500 crore plan)
rows.why: Management guides closing FY27 debt to about INR3,200 crore versus an earlier INR3,500 crore plan, though FY28-end debt rises to INR6,500-6,600 crore as capex continues.

rows.label: Order book depletion and DCR demand replenishment
rows.why: The 8.2 GW order book at 31 March 2026 leaves 1.2 GW after about 6 GW ships in FY27, and management sees 20-25 GW of FY27 DCR demand and over 80 GW of grandfathered non-DCR demand to win from, but about 1 GW distribution orders were removed and C&I DCR orders are under renegotiation.

rows.label: Cell cost pass-through on about 80% of order book
rows.why: MSAs cover about 80% of the order book for cell cost and dollar pass-through, but future pass-through depends on market conditions once cell and wafer-ingot capacity comes in, and silver and aluminium costs have risen (aluminium from $3,100 to $3,600 per ton).

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 records, the 6 GW module ramp and FY27 production of 7.5-8 GW, but cautious on per-watt EBITDA compression, the slipped cell plant timeline, US export orders and pass-through terms; analysts pushed on pricing and order book quality.

544488|2026-06.headline: Vikram Solar Q1 FY27: record 1,006 MW volume (+32% YoY) and revenue ~INR1,563 cr, but EBITDA fell to INR126 cr (8.06% margin) as costs outran pass-through.
544488|2026-06.overview: Revenue rose about 8% QoQ and 38% YoY to roughly INR1,563 crore on 1.06 GW dispatched, with per-watt realisation up 8% QoQ to INR15.02/Wp on DCR mix. EBITDA was INR126 crore (8.06% margin) and PAT INR19.78 crore, as unit COGS rose INR1.86/Wp from metals, EVA, and cell costs that were only partly passed through. Management attributed the squeeze to ALMM-2 uncertainty, Gulf-conflict input inflation, and industry oversupply. It declined to give fresh FY27 guidance, deferring the update to H1 results, and the Gangaikondan module plant (first module 29 June) and cell plant (Q4 FY27) remain on schedule.

financial_highlights.change: Down sharply; prior-quarter level referenced as ~16%

financial_highlights.value: 76 MW (cited as ~75 MW later on call)

segments.name: Module – large accounts / IPP / utility / C&I (non-DCR)
segments.commentary: Base-load book of ~7.1 GW with tighter margins; management says pass-through under MSAs applies to cells only, not balance-of-materials. Price realisation for mid-market expected ~INR0.50/Wp higher.

segments.name: Module – DCR
segments.commentary: 76 MW sold in Q1 at materially higher realisation (DCR ~INR22+/Wp per management). Cell supply is from external domestic partners until own cell line starts; DCR volume expected to grow 2–2.5x each quarter.

segments.name: Distribution channel
segments.commentary: Monthly run rate roughly doubled from ~40 MW last year; network of 119+ distributors and 757+ dealers across 24 states. Management says distribution pricing is spot-linked and realises INR1–1.5/Wp above key accounts.

segments.name: BESS (VSL PowerHive)
segments.commentary: 7.5 GWh BESS assembly plant in Chennai: equipment ordered ~3 months ago, delivery Nov 2026, installation Jan 2027, COD from March 2027. First 20 MWh utility-scale order executed; 7.5 GWh LFP cell plant (Phase 1 of 15 GWh) targets COD Q4 FY29, with land and incentives expected by Sept 2026.

guidance_outlook: No updated FY27 guidance; management will revisit at H1 results. Prior FY27 outlook (given 8 May) referenced as including EBITDA of INR1,500–1,600 crore per an analyst's citation; management did not reaffirm it.
Q2 margins expected to remain under some pressure from unabsorbed prices, partly offset by DCR and channel mix; management declined to say whether 16% margin returns.
Gangaikondan cell line (9 GW) on track for commissioning in Q4 FY27, with ramp possibly spilling into Q1 FY28; FY28 cell utilisation targeted at 40–50% (six-month ramp).
Wafer-ingot capacity resized to 9 GW (from 6 GW, part of the 12 GW plan), project cost ~INR5,600 crore; ground-breaking announced for next month.
Capex of ~INR5,000 crore planned for FY27 and similar in FY28; funding targeted at 75:25 debt-equity, ~70:30 once scheme is in place.
capex_capacity: Gangaikondan: 6 GW module (commissioned 29 June 2026, fully funded); module capacity cited as 15.5 GW total across sites, with 9–9.5 GW expected to be deliverable in FY27.
Gangaikondan 9 GW cell plant: civil/PEB advanced, first cell targeted Q4 FY27; ~70% backward integration once live.
Gangaikondan 9 GW wafer/ingot: board approved increase from 6 GW to 9 GW; part of the 12 GW plan, project cost ~INR5,600 crore; phasing shifted with later capacity around FY29.
Earlier 3 GW cell phase kept for FY28 on upgraded (non-TOPCon) technology.
Module portfolio transitioned from M10R to G12R; manpower down ~40% on new automated lines. Production volume in Q1 about 1,085 MW.
demand_pricing: Management attributes weak Q1 order flow to ALMM-2 enforcement uncertainty (C&I 15 GW/yr demand waited); ALMM-2 deferred to December 2026 after the 18 July operating memorandum.
Pricing power in non-DCR is under pressure from oversupply (~210 GW cited); cell oversupply limited pass-through of cost escalation.
Analyst estimate: industry DCR demand revised down to ~17 GW for the year from 20–25 GW as C&I shifts to non-DCR.
Chinese landed cell price cited at ~4 cents/W before 27.5% BCD.
Tender pipeline: ~35–40 GW of fresh utility tenders post-August 2025; FY27 AC market estimated at 30–35 GW utility, ~15 GW C&I, 14–15 GW PM Surya Ghar plus KUSUM.

qa_highlights.question: What was the per-watt spread this quarter, and why was the 88% of order book with cost escalation clauses not passed through? Has the spread improved since ALMM-2 deferment?
qa_highlights.answer: Pass-through under MSAs covers only cells, not balance-of-materials (BOM). Cell oversupply also limited price recovery. EBITDA of INR126 crore on ~1 GW works out to about INR1.25/Wp. Management wants one more quarter before judging DCR vs non-DCR margins.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the ~8 GW order book is executable this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Module capacity is 15.5 GW, with 9–9.5 GW deliverable in FY27. Management will not take negative-margin orders and asked for another quarter of clarity on volumes and pricing.

qa_highlights.question: How does DCR spread compare with non-DCR, given cell makers retain most margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DCR delivers more margin than non-DCR but gave no number. Only 75–76 MW of DCR was sold in Q1, so it is too early to split margins.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 9 GW cell line on track for Q4 commissioning, and will all 9 GW come on stream then?
qa_highlights.answer: Commissioning is on track for Q4 FY27. Ramp-up may spill into Q1 FY28, and the full 9 GW may not be running in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 EBITDA margin return to the ~16% level?
qa_highlights.answer: Not a direct conclusion. Q2 will still see some unabsorbed price impact, partly offset by DCR and channel mix. Management declined to commit to a 16% margin.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 volume driven by an influx of non-DCR orders, and will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume depends on backlog and module ramp, and management sees no slowdown. Industry DCR demand estimate was cut to about 17 GW from 20–25 GW as C&I shifts to non-DCR. Country consumption was about 12 GW in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 production guidance of 7–8 GW and the INR1,500–1,600 crore EBITDA outlook be reaffirmed?
qa_highlights.answer: No guidance was reaffirmed. Management is waiting for ALMM-2 clarity and will revisit at H1 results, citing customer hesitancy and infrastructure delays.

qa_highlights.question: Chinese cell price and wafer-ingot capacity clarification?
qa_highlights.answer: Chinese landed cell price is about 4 cents/W before 27.5% BCD. The wafer-ingot 9 GW is part of the same 12 GW plan, now resized, with project cost about INR5,600 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 and FY28 capex and debt funding plan?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is about INR5,000 crore, with a similar amount in FY28, mostly debt-funded. Target gearing is 75:25, moving to about 70:30 once the scheme is in place. Disbursements were expected to begin around end-August.

544495|2026-06.headline: NIS Management Q1 FY27 consolidated income rose 15.68% YoY to INR115.44 crore, with EBITDA up 36.24% to INR9.22 crore at a 7.99% margin.
544495|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income reached INR115.44 crore, up 15.68% YoY, and EBITDA rose 36.24% to INR9.22 crore with margin up 121 bps to 7.99%. Net profit was INR6.40 crore (up 35% YoY, margin 5.54%), while EPS of INR3.23 grew only 3.53%. Management reiterated the INR500 crore FY27 revenue goal, flagged that the CCTV segment posted a Q1 loss due to project timing, and declined to commit to a margin expansion path beyond 1-2% over two years. Net debt, the share price fall since IPO, and buyback ideas drew pointed investor questions that management largely deflected toward growth investment.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR2.11 crore with a loss at PAT level in Q1, attributed to project execution costs ahead of bill raising; management expects stabilisation by September quarter and calls it the most profitable segment. FY26 CCTV loss was about INR1.5 crore.

segments.commentary: Q1 revenue nil (INR0 lakh); net loss about INR57 lakh across the LLP and Keertika Academy.

Management attributed margin dilution to delayed Jal Jeevan Mission receivables (provisioned, mostly in Q4), and to early-stage solar EPC projects. The company closed its acquisition of NOPL Solar (969 MW PM-KUSUM project) at end-April 2026 and guided FY27 revenue of INR2,200 crore plus, with a 14-15% EBITDA margin target.

segments.commentary: About 10% of order book; about INR12 crores of Q1 revenue. Carries a provision of about INR6.5 crores due to slow Jal Jeevan Mission receivables recovery; about INR120 crores of debtors are tied to JJM projects.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue from NOPL in standalone INR204 crores and why growth only 28%?

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins dip in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited higher project costs, about INR6.5 crores provision on Jal Jeevan receivables (reversible on collection), and NOPL overheads booked without revenue at consolidated level; standalone margins described as normal.

qa_highlights.question: Why is consolidated revenue lower than standalone and which to track?

qa_highlights.question: Status of Jal Jeevan Mission receivables and working capital?

qa_highlights.question: Status of NOPL debt financing (INR3,100 crores) from IREDA and other lenders?
qa_highlights.answer: Final IREDA committee sanction expected this quarter, with disbursement expected in the same window; financial closure targeted in Q1 per management, with 75:25 debt-equity cited.

qa_highlights.question: Status of INR29 crore disputed receivable in court?
qa_highlights.answer: Only INR29 crores certified by client is booked; claim is much higher; no timeline given as matter is in court, but management is hopeful of positive outcome.

qa_highlights.question: Debtor days at 296 — has it peaked?

544497|2026-03.headline: Anlon FY26 consolidated income rose 42.98% to INR 172.22 crore and PAT 41.77% to INR 29.09 crore, but Q4 PAT fell to INR 11.07 crore from INR 16.65 crore.
544497|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated total income of INR 172.22 crore (+42.98% YoY), EBITDA of INR 47.77 crore (+47.55%) and PAT of INR 29.09 crore (+41.77%), driven by the Apiqo and Bizotic acquisitions. Q4 total income rose to INR 50.90 crore from INR 48.97 crore, but PBT was flat at INR 14.44 crore and PAT fell to INR 11.07 crore, which management attributed to higher operating and development expenses and raw material cost spikes linked to the Middle East conflict. Management guided FY27 revenue to INR 380-400 crore, FY28 to INR 700-800 crore in one answer (INR 600-700 crore in another), and consolidated EBITDA margin of 24-25% as a floor, with a sharp reduction in receivables and cash-flow positivity targeted by end FY27. Several answers were inconsistent (EBITDA margin guidance ranged from 24-25% to 30-35%; FY28 revenue from 600-700 to 700-800 crore), and the call was disrupted by poor audio for several analysts.

vs INR 15.49 crore in Q4 FY25
vs INR 16.65 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: 130-140 days on average (some domestic customers 150 days)
-INR 23 crore prior period to -INR 47 crore after consolidation

segments.name: Pharmaceutical intermediates and APIs (Anlon standalone)
segments.commentary: Management says 5-6 DMF-linked products are already supplied to regulated markets, with 5-7 more expected to commercialise in FY27; export share targeted at about 60% in FY27. Products cited include Ketoprofen, Dexketoprofen and Loxoprofen Sodium in the NSAID category.

segments.name: Apiqo Organics (acquired, early Jan 2026 per management)
segments.commentary: Acquired and consolidated for about 2.5 months in FY26. Management said its EBITDA margin is structurally lower (approx. 22-23%) as a chemical/intermediate manufacturer, and backward integration into intermediates is planned to start from Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Bizotic Life Science (acquired)
segments.commentary: Consolidated for about 15 days in FY26. Management expects margins close to Anlon's, and says backward integration of intermediates has run for three to four years.

segments.name: Industrial and fine/specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: Early-traction vertical; management is discussing a dedicated Apiqo capacity expansion with one or two customers, with margins slightly below pharma. No revenue figure was disclosed.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Three molecules in development for two global innovators. One is in validation with batches of hundreds of kg since March; commercial supply expected by Q3 FY27, with the other two in validation by Q2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at INR 380-400 crore, with a clear order book of INR 280-300 crore and a further INR 80-90 crore expected from products under qualification.
FY28 revenue guided at INR 700-800 crore in one answer and INR 600-700 crore in another, assuming 50-60% utilisation of the new Rajkot capacity from Q1 FY28 (six months of trial and validation).

Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 24-25% as a floor, with management saying it will not sell below levels that breach that margin; a separate answer cited 30-35% for FY27 and the closing remarks used 25-30%.
Consolidated PAT: conservative FY27 estimate of INR 45 crore; management agreed INR 50-55 crore is achievable when asked.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive on an annual basis by end FY27; management said it was '100% sure'.
Revenue CAGR of approx. 30% over three years stated in prepared remarks; peak revenue potential of the current 1,400-1,600 MTPA capacity stated at INR 450-500 crore at 80% utilisation.
capex_capacity: Combined installed capacity after Apiqo and Bizotic: approx. 1,400-1,600 MTPA; consolidated utilisation approx. 62-65%, with management saying practical maximum is about 85%.

New greenfield capex at the existing Rajkot premises estimated at INR 130 crore; plant layout under approval, construction to start end of the month or early next month, commercial production targeted by Q1 FY28 (also referred to as mid-FY28).

Funding: term loan of INR 65-70 crore (about 50-60% of capex), balance from internal accruals; equipment orders placed 6-8 months ahead, with advance payments already made and part of the equipment installed.
Standalone peak revenue with expansion stated at INR 400-450 crore.
Capex and expansion of QC capacity already under way; management is considering a further INR 130 crore-type expansion to scale specialty chemicals at Apiqo, subject to customer commitments.
demand_pricing: Management said raw material prices (solvents, catalysts) have more than doubled since the conflict, and prices change daily; Q4 margin pressure came from holding purchase orders at old prices, and customers are now being asked to pay higher prices as a force majeure.
Management said price increases are being negotiated and expects Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin to be close to the prior full-year level, but acknowledged this is uncertain if geopolitical conditions worsen.

Ketoprofen US DMF is delayed: a customer will file on Anlon's behalf, and timing has moved from Q2 FY27 to Q3 or Q4 FY27. Dexketoprofen Europe DMF is at the EDQM query stage, expected to close in two to three months.

Competitive positioning: few Indian players in Ketoprofen and Dexketoprofen (two to three in India, five to six globally); management cites proprietary methylation and Friedel-Crafts chemistry and landing-cost advantage.

Receivables: a distributor dispute left INR 20-30 crore pending in late 2025; INR 11 crore recovered and about INR 17 crore still outstanding. Management has stopped supply to customers paying beyond 120 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue outlook and the peak potential of the current capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 visibility is INR 380-400 crore; peak revenue from 1,400-1,600 MTPA is INR 450-500 crore at about 80% utilisation (management said the practical ceiling is 85%).

qa_highlights.question: How much order book is in place and what are the CDMO timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Clear order book is INR 280-300 crore, with INR 80-90 crore more expected. One CDMO product is in validation, with commercial supply expected by Q3 FY27; the other two validations by Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin outlook, and why did Q4 fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided consolidated margin of 24-25% as a floor; Q4 fell because of unrecovered raw material cost increases, higher operating costs and the acquisitions. Management expects Q1 FY27 margins to recover to roughly the prior full-year level.

qa_highlights.question: What is the funding plan for the capex, working capital and any acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is funded with INR 65-70 crore of term loans and internal accruals; management said there is no current equity dilution plan, with rights issue or promoter unsecured loans as possible options later. Working capital may need cash credit from banks after commissioning.

qa_highlights.question: What is the receivables outlook and cash-flow timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days are 130-140 on average, and management expects them to stay at or above 180 days (per one answer), while also saying payments are running at 100-105 days now. Cash flow expected positive on an annual basis in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Credit rating and minority buy-out status?
qa_highlights.answer: CARE's 'issuer not cooperating' rating was linked to a dispute management called blackmail; Brickwork withdrew its rating and a fresh application is pending, with management expecting BBB- minimum within about 45 days. Management plans to acquire the remaining minority stake in Apiqo and Bizotic through share swaps, likely at the next AGM.

risks_watch: Margin guidance is inconsistent across answers: 24-25% floor in several answers, 25-30% in prepared remarks, 30-35% in other answers. Track which figure is reported in Q1 FY27.
Raw material prices (solvents, catalysts) more than doubled since the conflict and reset daily; Q1 FY27 margin recovery depends on customers accepting force majeure price increases.

Receivables at 130-140 days on average (some 150 days), with management saying they will stay at or above 180 days; cash flow turning positive on an annual basis by end FY27 depends on collections and inventory release of 20-25% in Q2 FY27.

Capex of about INR 130 crore at Rajkot with commercial production targeted Q1 FY28; funding relies on INR 65-70 crore term loan plus internal accruals, with working capital needs possibly requiring cash credit after commissioning.
Credit rating status: CARE rating marked 'issuer not cooperating' and Brickwork withdrew its rating; a fresh application is pending with management expecting BBB- minimum within about 45 days.
Ketoprofen US DMF timing slipped to Q3 or Q4 FY27 through a customer filing; Dexketoprofen Europe DMF at EDQM query stage, expected to close in two to three months.
FY28 revenue guidance differs between INR 600-700 crore and INR 700-800 crore; FY27 PAT conservative INR 45 crore versus INR 50-55 crore said achievable.
key_quotes: see, we are mainly in B2B business, so our price basically it is impacted on all the customer and they are it is taking time to convince for forward means forward to their customer.

But right now there is no planning, but I think once the capacity will be completed and we'll come with the commercial production, at that time we'll see that whatever the situation and if required, then our first preference is go with the financial institution instead of going further for the dilution.
So we are 100% sure by end of this FY27 it will be positive.
And by end of this FY27 with the positive cash flow and receivable days will remain at least 180 days, which is I think mostly API manufacturer is having.

Several answers were evasive or deflected (for example on tax rate, acquisition budget and the reason for the Q4 PAT decline), and the call was hampered by poor audio for several analysts.
