segments.name: Machines / technology and consumables
segments.commentary: About 109 machines placed in FY26 across five OEM lines (Konica Minolta, Eton, Pangda, SkyJet, HopeTech); management cites a shift toward higher-value machines. Installed base is about 900+ machines. Average machine realization was INR 25-27 lakh last year, and management declined to give a current-year average.

segments.name: Ink
segments.commentary: FY26 reported ink volume was 1,140 tons, with ink revenue about INR 74 crore. Ink is being moved from import/distribution to in-house manufacturing under INKIA; INKIA produced about 80 tons per month last year and 80 tons was added via the merger.

segments.name: Sublimation paper
segments.commentary: Capacity was raised from about 1 crore to over 2 crore meters per month, with FY26 utilization at about 52%. Realization fell as average GSM dropped from 45-55 to about 35; FY26 realization was about INR 5.6 per meter; paper revenue about INR 65-66 crore.

segments.name: Printed fabric / job work and fabric supply
segments.commentary: Digital fabric printing capacity is 75,000 meters per day. Revenue split is about 50:50 between customer-supplied fabric (job work) and company-bought fabric. About 6% of fabric revenue is direct export.

segments.name: Commercial printing (new)
segments.commentary: Early-stage entry into label, mica and packaging printing, starting as a trading/distribution business with no additional capex planned. No service team has been added yet.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term revenue growth guided at about 20-22% a year, with profitability growth expected to outpace the top line.
EBITDA margin: management says the 14-16% range is sustainable near term, with improvement over time from in-house ink and paper; it did not commit to a return to 18%.
Ink Phase-1 targets 150 tons per month in-house capacity in FY27 at capex of INR 40-45 crore, with production to start by end-2026 and realization in FY27.

Ink Phase-2 targets 500 tons per month in FY28 with additional capex of INR 20-25 crore; Phase-3 targets 1,000 tons per month over three to four years with land about 3.5 times the existing footprint.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter commercial printing (labels, mica, packaging)?

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from about 18% last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a mix effect: paper revenue was concentrated in H2 last year, and about 45-50 tons of ink bundled with machines this year was not reported as ink revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INKIA ink be accepted by customers versus imported ink?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INKIA has supplied about 2-2.5 years, with 2,000-2,500 tons of white-label ink consumed, and that compatibility testing is a 4-5 year journey that is already complete.

qa_highlights.question: How is the ink capex funded and what working capital days are targeted?

qa_highlights.answer: Management said machine realization varies widely by model and declined to give a current average; the bundled ink revenue is expected to show up in future ink revenue.

544532|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 235% YoY to INR591 crore, but EBITDA margin was 12.1% and FY26 PAT margin 8.5%, below the 11% promised earlier.
544532|2026-03.overview: Solarworld reported Q4 FY26 revenue from operations of INR591 crore (up 235% YoY), EBITDA of INR73 crore (12.1% margin) and PAT of INR49 crore (8.1% net margin). For FY26, total income was INR1,416 crore (up 1.57% YoY), EBITDA INR187.9 crore (13.3%) and PAT INR120.4 crore (8.5%). Management blamed a loss-making initial module ramp after ALMM approval in December 2025 and sharp raw material cost increases in Q4 linked to the West Asia conflict. The company is pivoting toward BESS, with a 582 MWac / 1.2 GWh DC BESS project pipeline and a 3.4 GW BESS line in trials.

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: FY26 EPC revenue about INR1,250 crore; management cites EPC PAT margin close to 10.5%. EPC margin guided at 9-11% through the cycle and 8-11% overall for FY27. Solar EPC order book about INR1,674 crore.

segments.name: BESS EPC
segments.commentary: FY26 BESS revenue was nil; management guides INR800-1,000 crore in FY27. BESS order book about INR1,136 crore. Q4 orders from NTPC at Solapur and Unchahar aggregate about 514 MWh, order value about INR5 billion incl. O&M. BESS margin guided at 14-15% PBT.

segments.name: Solar module manufacturing
segments.commentary: 1.5 GW Roorkee module line began operations after ALMM approval in December 2025; about two to two-and-a-half months of run-time in FY26 produced a slight loss. Breakeven at about 30-35% utilisation; FY26-27 utilisation expected at 40-45% on about 600 MW captive NTPC REL orders, rising to 60-65% with more orders. Line capex about INR146 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 order book conversion target at least 70% of about INR2,800 crore, i.e. about INR2,000 crore revenue; EPC about INR2,000 crore including BESS INR800-1,000 crore.
Management expects 40-45% revenue growth in FY27 and says it will not sustain FY26's 200-250% growth.
Overall EBITDA/PAT margin guided at 8-11%; sustaining current margins if the West Asia conflict eases, with slight downside if raw material prices keep rising.
BESS margin guided at 14-15% PBT; 3.4 GW BESS line capex about INR55-60 crore, potential revenue about INR3,000 crore at full capacity (740 containers at INR4.5 crore each).
Q1 and Q2 seasonally weak; Q3 and Q4 strong. Management declined to give a half-yearly split.
1.2 GW solar cell line at Pandhurna targeted for commercial operation by June 2027; cell-line funds to be deployed from Q3 FY27.
No near-term plans to add module or cell capacity until about 75-80% captive utilisation is visible.
capex_capacity: Module: 1.5 GW Roorkee facility (7.5 acres, automated ATW and Horad lines) operational; output 600-750 W TOPCon-type panels across M10R, G12R and G12 configurations.
BESS: 3.4 GW fully automated line (KUKA robotics) ready, trials underway; capex about INR55-60 crore already spent.
Solar cell: 1.2 GW line at Pandhurna, approvals mostly received, construction to start around June 2026, commercial operation targeted by June 2027.
Junction box: 5 GW line being set up in a joint venture; site ready for trials.

Operational capacity to be added on commissioning: a 272 MW project and a 70 MW project expected to complete in June 2026; management expects about 600 MW near term, about 700 MW next quarter and about 1.5 GW by year-end.
demand_pricing: PSU tenders were about 40 GW last year; the company executes about 1-1.5 GW a year, so it sees limited impact from a slower tendering market.
Raw material costs up sharply since Oct 2025: copper about +40%, aluminium about +50%, steel higher; INR depreciated from about 85-86 to about 96 per USD, affecting BESS imported inputs.
ALMM List-II (cells) applies from June 2026; management expects 90-95% of projects to shift to DCR cells, with a possible 6-12 month cell shortage.
Current order book has no ALMM-2 cell requirement, giving a headway of about a year. Lithium cells for BESS are sourced from China as no Indian supplier exists.
PPA signing delays after L1 bids and grid connectivity constraints are slowing the solar tender market; management expects connectivity to take 10-12 more months to resolve.
Claims filed with SJVN for about INR219 crore; only INR52 crore recognised as receivable. Ind AS allows recognition only after dispute-board award.

qa_highlights.question: PAT margin is 8-8.5% versus the 11% promised earlier, and top line is short of the INR1,500 crore target. What is the guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EPC PAT margin is about 10.5%, with the module loss from a short ramp and Q4 raw material headwinds dragging the total. Guidance is INR1,900-2,000 crore revenue and 8-11% overall margins.

qa_highlights.question: Battery cell unit timeline, and when will it contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: The 1.2 GW cell line at Pandhurna is now targeted for commercial start by June 2027, with construction starting around June 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expense rise, and what is the BESS capex and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expense rose to INR83 million from INR74 million; last year's base included a INR140 million write-off that was recovered this year. The 3.4 GW BESS line capex is INR55-60 crore; margin 14-15% PBT.

qa_highlights.question: How will the module line utilisation ramp, and what is breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven is around 30-35% utilisation. Utilisation should reach 40-45% on existing NTPC REL orders (about 600 MW), rising to 60-65% with new orders. All existing EPC orders can be serviced in-house.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company expand module or cell capacity, and why are PPAs being rescinded?
qa_highlights.answer: No expansion planned until 75-80% captive use is visible. PPA delays stem from DISCOM absorption and transmission constraints; management expects resolution by around end-FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for ROW, labour and the EPC tender pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: ROW compensation is moving to market rates, which helps, but management does not see it as the biggest hurdle; no major labour issues. Tender activity is slower, but the company's order book is full.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from copper, aluminium, steel and INR depreciation; management guides 8-11% overall margin range.
Execution risk on the 60-40 BESS to EPC mix, with BESS revenue ramp from nil to INR800-1,000 crore and most BESS projects due by June 2027.
Timing of the 1.2 GW solar cell line (June 2027) and its funding deployment from Q3 FY27.

SJVN claim recovery (INR219 crore filed vs INR52 crore booked) is uncertain and timing unknown.
Customer concentration in PSU and NTPC REL orders; PPA rescissions and slower PSU tendering.

544533|2026-03.headline: Seshaasai Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9.6% YoY to INR 405 crore with EBITDA margin of 30.8%; FY26 revenue fell 1.5% to INR 1,441 crore, no FY27 guidance.
544533|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was about INR 404-405 crore, up 8.1% QoQ and 9.6% YoY, led by communication and fulfilment and IoT. EBITDA was about INR 125 crore (30.8% margin, up 330 bps YoY) and PAT about INR 82 crore (20.2% margin, up 316 bps YoY), helped by lower finance costs after IPO debt repayment and interest income on IPO funds. For FY26, revenue declined 1.5% to INR 1,441 crore on a temporary moderation in Payment Solutions, while EBITDA reached INR 394 crore (27.4% margin) and PAT INR 240 crore (16.7% margin). Management declined to give FY27 guidance, deferring any update until after Q1 FY27.

financial_highlights.value: INR 398 crore, incl. ~INR 195 crore unutilised IPO funds

segments.name: Payment Solutions
segments.commentary: About 47.5% of Q4 revenue and ~50% of FY26 revenue; hit by PSU/private bank issuance moderation and low COVID-era renewal base. Added 21 new bank/fintech customers, lost none; won a multi-year PSU bank tender worth ~INR 8.7 crore. Metal cards are ~4% of the segment.

segments.name: Communication and Fulfilment Solutions
segments.commentary: 39% of FY26 revenue (39.8% of Q4) and grew 29% YoY; added ~8 customers. Management expects a marginal decline in FY27 but described the segment as stable.

segments.name: IoT Solutions
segments.commentary: 11% of FY26 revenue (12.4% of Q4), grew about 45-48% YoY (figures varied across the call). Added ~65 customers. RFID utilisation about 70% for FY26 and 80-85% in Q4. SIM division began material revenue in Q4.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 revenue guidance by segment; management will revisit after Q1 FY27 given geopolitical and macro uncertainty.
No margin guidance for FY27/FY28; management expects product mix shift to IoT, eSIM and other solutions to support good margins.
IoT revenue expected to grow faster than the ~47% achieved in FY26.
eSIM commercial revenue expected from H2 FY27, after a compliance step due July/August 2026.
Capex of about INR 160-200 crore through FY27 across Payment Solutions and IoT, plus modernisation, partly funded from IPO proceeds.
Payment card business expected to bottom out, with renewal volumes to recover.
capex_capacity: Navi Mumbai and Kundli facilities became operational in Q4 FY26; Nagpur and Bengaluru still under construction.
SIM capacity about 7 million per month, running at about 30% utilisation.
eSIM capacity of 2-3 million per month depending on form factor; commercial production not yet started.
RFID capacity utilisation about 70% for FY26 and 80-85% in Q4 FY26; three plants can do inlay manufacturing.
Bengaluru facility received GSMA SAS-UP certification for SIM/eSIM manufacturing and personalisation.
demand_pricing: Payment card demand weakened due to lower issuance from PSU and private banks, COVID-era renewal base effects, and tighter bank and fintech compliance.
Top 10 customers contributed about 62.8% of FY26 revenue; 96.6% of revenue came from existing customers.
Gross margin improved on 7-8% material cost savings from procurement consolidation and inventory planning; management said FX was an adverse factor in Q4.
Export revenue about INR 3 crore in FY26; international work is via partners, with some overseas fintech RFPs at evaluation stage.
Domestic payment scheme and global fintech RFPs for metal card variants still under evaluation.
Market share of payment cards in India was 31.6% in FY25 per industry analysts.

qa_highlights.question: Will rupee depreciation hurt gross margins going into Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin gains came from sourcing savings of 7-8% on top raw material categories plus operating leverage. Q4 FX was adverse but mostly hit materials bought earlier, so the exposure is still to be watched.

qa_highlights.question: Is working capital intensity rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory was built up to manage global supply risks in Q1 and Q4, and surplus IPO cash inflates the cash line. Receivables and inventory are said to be in line with the business, with monitoring under way.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any FY27 guidance by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management will wait until Q1 FY27 for better visibility on the macro and geopolitical situation before guiding.

qa_highlights.question: What is the eSIM timeline and SIM capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: SIM is at about 30% utilisation of 7 million per month capacity and already supplies a leading telecom player. eSIM commercial production is expected after a July/August compliance step, with revenue from H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the payment card business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the business to bottom out, with renewal volumes recovering from the COVID-era base and growth from premiumisation, transit and state-government card programmes; metal cards were about 4% of the segment.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any plan for backward integration into chips or inlays?
qa_highlights.answer: Inlay equipment has been in place for about 2.5 years and three plants can make inlays. Management said local inlay making will improve margins once it reaches scale, but gave no margin quantification and parked chip integration for now.

risks_watch: Payment Solutions volume recovery depends on bank renewal cycles and regulatory conditions; the segment is about half of revenue.
Rupee depreciation, input cost inflation and supply-chain constraints could pressure gross margins; management said input prices are rising.
eSIM commercial launch depends on the July/August compliance step and integration work; SIM utilisation is only about 30%.
Working capital days have risen over two years; inventory and receivables are being monitored.
Top 10 customers are 62.8% of revenue, so concentration risk remains.
Unutilised IPO proceeds of about INR 195 crore are to be deployed in later periods.

544533|2026-06.headline: Seshaasai Q1 FY27 revenue rose 21.1% YoY to INR 377 crore, but gross margin fell to 41.7% on war-linked input costs.
544533|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached INR 377 crore, up 21.1% YoY but down 6.9% QoQ against a seasonally strong Q4. Cost of materials consumed rose to 58.34% (about 411 bps above the FY26 average), compressing gross margin to 41.7% from 44.5% a year earlier. EBITDA grew to INR 94 crore at a 25.1% margin (up 135 bps YoY), and PAT rose 63.8% YoY to INR 60 crore at a 16% margin. Management reiterated an 8-12% medium-term revenue growth target and guided to a stronger H2 on mix and operating leverage, without giving a numeric margin guide.

financial_highlights.change: about 411 bps above FY26 average of 54.23%

segments.name: Payment solutions

544544|2026-03.headline: Telge Projects FY26 revenue rose about 57% to Rs 40.2 crore, with Q4 EBITDA margin of 35% and current order book of about Rs 25 crore.
544544|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue from operations of about Rs 40.2 crore (up from Rs 25.6 crore), EBITDA of Rs 9.55 crore at 24% margin and PAT of Rs 5.9 crore at 15% margin. Q4 revenue was Rs 14.4 crore (up 13.7% YoY, about 58% QoQ), with Q4 EBITDA of Rs 5 crore (35% margin) and PAT of Rs 3.3 crore (23% margin). The Edward Farr Architects acquisition closed on 3 March 2026 and contributed only about one month to consolidation. Management guided to 60-70% revenue CAGR and to sustaining Q4-level margins, but gave little visibility beyond the Rs 25 crore order book and a Rs 6 crore RFQ pipeline.

segments.commentary: Execution stays in India via the parent company, while US subsidiaries Midwest, Draftco and Edward Farr handle sales and client relations. Management said the subsidiaries' revenue cannot be separated cleanly from the parent.

segments.name: Architectural and interior design (Edward Farr Architects, US)
segments.commentary: Acquired on 3 March 2026 at about 2.5x EBITDA. Calendar 2025 revenue was about Rs 14 crore with PAT margin of 10-12%. Roughly Rs 10 crore of the current order book is attributed to this business.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term revenue CAGR of 60-70%, stated for FY27 and subsequent years.
Management aims to keep FY27 margins at Q4 FY26 levels (EBITDA about 35%, PAT 20-23%) and said it will not go below that.

US billing rates targeted at $45-60 per hour, up from $25-35 previously.
No debt planned; future acquisitions to use other funding. Management said no equity dilution this year.
Acquisition pipeline under evaluation, with Rs 5 crore of IPO proceeds earmarked for acquisitions. MEP services are a targeted capability addition.

qa_highlights.question: What are revenue and margin expectations for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident of a 60-70% CAGR in FY27 and subsequent years, and aims to keep EBITDA and PAT at Q4 FY26 levels (EBITDA about 35%, PAT 20-23%) without going below that.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Rs 25 crore order book is from the acquisition, and how much is US-based?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book is a mix of existing business and Edward Farr; Edward Farr architectural work is about Rs 10 crore, and about 80% of the order book is from the US.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 60-70% CAGR inclusive of acquired revenue, and what is the inorganic plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidiaries are now treated as organic since operations are shifting to the parent; future inorganic growth will come from new acquisitions, with no specific deal identified yet. MEP services are the targeted capability addition.

qa_highlights.question: Why is receivable days up to 108 from 73?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the major portion of receivables is from a related party; collections were accelerated in April and May, and 60 days DSO is being maintained now. Normal recovery is 30-45 days.

qa_highlights.question: What gives confidence in 30-35% EBITDA margins versus peers at 20-22%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the US local team enabling higher billing rates ($45-60/hour target versus $25-35), expansion into lower-cost regions such as Nashik and Latur, and AI-led productivity gains.

qa_highlights.question: Is any new debt or equity dilution planned?
qa_highlights.answer: No debt is planned; future acquisitions will use other funding arrangements. Management said no equity dilution is expected this year.

qa_highlights.answer: Leadership hires (BD heads, HODs, regional heads) and Nashik team expansion were made ahead of growth; FY27 leadership additions are not planned, so cost growth should be lower than in FY26.

544545|2026-03.headline: TruAlt FY26 standalone revenue fell to INR1,704 crore and PAT to INR80.26 crore as OMC ethanol allocation was cut to about 34% of bids.
544545|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a difficult year: ethanol tender allocation was cut to about 26 crore litres against a 72 crore litre bid, and private OMCs sought to revise prices on purchase orders already issued at about INR60 per litre. Standalone revenue fell about 9% to INR1,704 crore, while EBITDA margin rose to 19.81% from 18.98%. PAT fell to INR80.26 crore from INR140 crore, driven by depreciation (up to INR84 crore) after three dual-feed plants were capitalised, higher finance cost (INR157.85 crore) and deferred tax. Management is relying on a pending 15 crore litre court-ordered allocation, plus SAF, CBG and fuel-retail expansion for growth.

segments.name: Ethanol
segments.commentary: FY26 ethanol sales about 24-26 crore litres (about 3 crore litres ENA) at average realisation of about INR67 per litre; OMC allocation was about 26 crore litres vs 72 crore litre bid. Current sales run rate about 2.2 crore litres per month vs 5.5-6 crore litre capacity.

segments.name: Compressed Biogas (CBG)
segments.commentary: First plant (10 TPD) generates about INR42 crore revenue at 85%+ utilisation; Sumitomo JV (TruAlt Gas, 49% partner) plans three 20 TPD plants and GAIL JV (Leafiniti, 49%) plans six plants of 12 TPD, targeting 162 TPD gross by Q4 FY27. Management guides about 50% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Fuel retail
segments.commentary: Seven franchise outlets operating with zero capex, generating about INR100-105 crore revenue and about 5% EBITDA; target of 11 outlets near term and 87 total (11 plus 76 shortlisted) subject to crude stabilisation.

segments.name: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF)
segments.commentary: Planned 10 crore litre per annum plant in Andhra Pradesh (MoU signed); Honeywell UOP technology transfer agreement signed; FID awaits long-term offtake contract and pricing. Plans to divert about 20 crore litres of ethanol capacity to SAF.

segments.name: DDGS (by-product, within ethanol)
segments.commentary: DDGS revenue about INR28 crore in FY26, at base price about INR24 per kg; operations were mostly on syrup in Q3 and Q4.

guidance_outlook: FY27 ethanol volume target of at least 40 crore litres, with 55 crore litres if the pending 15 crore litre court-ordered allocation is implemented; management declined to give a revenue figure.

Management expects the 15 crore litre court-ordered allocation to be implemented by about September 2026 (H1 FY27), dependent on the Supreme Court LTOA matter being disposed of; courts resume about 3 June.

CBG: three TruAlt Gas plants (Sumitomo) and six Leafiniti plants (GAIL) to be commissioned by Q4 FY27, bringing gross capacity to about 162 TPD; EPC tenders for Leafiniti to be floated in early June 2026.
Fuel retail: 76 shortlisted outlets to be fast-tracked once crude prices stabilise, with total count above 90 by next financial year (earlier stated 87 by year-end).
Management says the INR150 crore PMG1 subsidy approval is at the final Secretary-level committee; receipt is linked to plant commissioning, expected in 24-30 months (FY29).
Management says no additional capex is planned beyond the capitalised dual-feed plants, but CBG and SAF expansions are in progress.
capex_capacity: Five ethanol plants fully commissioned; three of five converted to dual-feed (maize/broken rice), with more than INR400 crore capitalised, driving higher depreciation.

Ethanol capacity about 55-60 crore litres on 300-330 operating days; management targets syrup operation for about 100 days in the crushing season and 200-230 days on alternative grains for dual-feed units.
CBG: current 10 TPD operating; TruAlt Gas building three 20 TPD plants; Leafiniti targets six 12 TPD plants with six sites identified and land procurement advanced.
CBG funding is a 70:30 debt-to-equity mix; Sumitomo debt tied up with NABARD at 8.65%, and Leafiniti has four or five sanctions at lower rates.
SAF: land identified in Andhra Pradesh near a seaport; FID to follow a long-term offtake contract.
demand_pricing: Average ethanol sales realisation about INR67 per litre; ENA realisation about INR62 per litre; ENA market price fell from an expected INR62-63 to about INR55-56 per litre.
Public sector OMC contract prices: maize-based INR71, syrup-based INR65, damaged grains INR64, B-heavy molasses INR60, FCI rice INR58, C-heavy molasses INR58.
Private OMCs (8 crore litres allocated) requested price revision from about INR60 per litre; only about 1.6 crore litres lifted so far, with 6.2 crore litres still pending.
Court order (4 February 2026) values the pending 15.62 crore litres at about INR1,062 crore; management states inventory of about INR460-500 crore is built up.
CBG billed at about INR84-85 per kg; rumoured Sampoorn policy could lift gas price to INR100 and add INR5 per kg PLI (unconfirmed by management).
Management cites a blending increase from 20% to 21% (notified), with E22/E27/E30 BIS standards and E85/E100 notified; each 1% blending adds about 55-56 crore litres of demand.

qa_highlights.question: What was total FY26 ethanol volume and when did the allocation change happen?
qa_highlights.answer: About 24 crore litres sold versus 30 crore litres of tender allocation; management said the mechanism had not changed, but the 15 crore litre court-ordered carry-forward was not implemented.

qa_highlights.question: When will the 15 crore litre court order be implemented?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes for implementation by September or H1 FY27, after the court-pending LTOA matter is disposed of; the OMCs were past the 90-day period set by the 4 February order.

qa_highlights.question: What are the economics of ethanol, PLI and interest subvention?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income of about INR68.28 crore; Karnataka PLI at 1.75% of turnover; interest subvention up to 50% of term-loan interest capped at 6% per annum, per CFO explanation.

qa_highlights.question: How will CBG be funded and sourced?
qa_highlights.answer: 70:30 debt-equity; Sumitomo plants sourced from TruAlt's own spent wash and press mud; GAIL plants sourced from the open market, with at least three times raw material within 20 km of each site.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working-capital cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables about 21 days (realised in 15-17 days on average); payables up to about 60 days; net working capital about 40 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the feedstock split?
qa_highlights.answer: Group companies supplied under 55% of FY26 feedstock; over 45% was sourced from the open market, with the share from non-group sources expected to rise.

risks_watch: Pending 15 crore litre court-ordered allocation has not been implemented; timing depends on the Supreme Court LTOA matter and OMC compliance.
Private OMCs (8 crore litres) have sought price revision from about INR60 per litre; 6.2 crore litres still unlifted, and ENA prices have fallen to about INR55-56 per litre.
Higher depreciation and finance cost are compressing PBT and PAT, with standalone PAT down about 43%.
CBG expansion depends on the Sampoorn policy (rumoured, not notified) and on the Sumitomo land dispute that cut one plant from four to three.
Retail expansion (76 outlets) is paused due to crude price volatility; SAF FID awaits an offtake contract and pricing.
Standalone inventory of about INR460-500 crore is unsold and needs liquidation in FY27.
544545|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and combative on the policy and court outcome, with repeated apologies for the missed 15 crore litre allocation and for limited investor engagement. Management was evasive on FY27 revenue and on the Sampoorn policy, and declined to share rumoured terms.
key_quotes: We did not succumb to the pressure. We hold our grounds and we have been chasing the OMCs to honour the purchase orders and lift the quantities.
Trust me, we are leaving no stones unturned.
Once we get the implementation of this additional 15 crore litres, adding to the already 40 crore litres, including the private and the public sector OMCs, we will reach our peak production capacity.

544545|2026-06.headline: TruAlt Q1 FY27 ethanol revenue INR626.9 crore and PAT INR59.3 crore (vs INR4.7 crore in Q4), on ~60% capacity utilisation.
544545|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a strong quarter driven by three of five plants running on dual (grain plus sugar) feed, with ethanol sales of about 8.3 crore litres. Ethanol revenue was INR626.9 crore, EBITDA INR147.3 crore (23.5% margin) and PAT INR59.3 crore (9.5% margin). Management guided to 11-12 crore litres of sales in Q2 and about 44 crore litres of orders on hand for FY27, but flagged that maize prices at around INR25.5/kg have compressed margins, so earnings depend on inventory bought at lower prices. Several analyst answers were qualified by poor line quality and some questions went unanswered.

segments.name: Ethanol
segments.commentary: Revenue INR615.7 crore for the segment; sugar-based feed about 4.37 crore litres (INR277 crore), grain-based about 3.92 crore litres (INR314 crore), roughly a 50:50 split. DDGS revenue INR47.34 crore; ENA INR37.02 crore.

segments.name: Compressed biogas (CBG)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR11.2 crore and PAT about INR4-4.5 crore; plants at about 78% utilisation. Revenue split is about 58-60% gas sales and about 40% FOM/LFOM fertiliser.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 ethanol sales expected at about 11-12 crore litres, with no planned maintenance shutdown.
FY27 ethanol volume of about 44 crore litres from orders on hand (OMC plus private, ENA included); management said it could be higher; realisation about INR67-68/litre.
Capacity utilisation targeted at 80-90%, or 90-95% for the balance of the year if the 15 crore litre court-ordered capacity is implemented; currently about 60%.

CBG: three of four Sumitomo JV plants (20 TPD each) near commissioning, targeted for Q3 with revenue from Q4; GAIL JV six plants (10 TPD each) construction from August; about 72 TPD of additional capacity from Q4.
CBG FY27 run-rate expected at INR10-12 crore per quarter.
SAF: about INR2,000 crore capex; EPC tender pending, construction in 2-3 months; revenue targeted by end-2028 (FY29). About INR150 crore viability gap funding received under PM JI-VAN.
Management said a plan to de-lever the balance sheet would be shared in the next call or within days.
capex_capacity: Ethanol capacity of about 55 crore litres a year; management said no further ethanol capex is planned.

CBG: gross capex about INR760 crore for about 132 TPD across two JVs (51% TruAlt, 49% partner), funded 70:30 debt-to-equity. Sumitomo JV: four plants at INR330 crore; GAIL JV: six plants at INR425 crore.
Pledged shares tied to SBI and IREDA term loans: release requested, expected this quarter.
Plants located within 50-60 km of gas injection points; cascades used for transport to injection points.
demand_pricing: Maize prices rose to about INR25.5/kg from about INR21-22 earlier; management said margin falls to about INR6-7/litre at these prices versus INR15-16 on earlier purchases.
Management said it holds grain inventory bought at INR18,000-21,000/tonne against current prices of about INR25,000/tonne.
Private OMC realisation about INR60.50/litre; about 8 crore litres of unlifted private OMC inventory, of which about 3 crore litres sold and 5 crore litres targeted for Q3.

SAF expected offtake price INR180-190/litre with a 24-25% margin; CBG gas price INR84/kg; FOM prices range from INR2,500/tonne (open market) to about INR8,000/tonne (one large fertiliser company order).

qa_highlights.question: How is the dual-feed shift affecting costs and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said grain-based feed has about 6% better margin than sugar-based feed and a yield of about 450 versus about 317 for sugar-based, plus DDGS income.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CBG EBITDA margin dip despite higher revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee costs rose with CBG expansion hiring, and a one-off repairs and maintenance cost was booked; management called the impact minor.

qa_highlights.question: Is INR15 crore spillover included in FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No, the 44 crore litre guidance excludes the INR15 crore spillover, which management is still pursuing with OMCs with no timeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for ethanol volumes and the next ethanol supply year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects at least 44 crore litres in the next supply year on a conservative base, and more if it can achieve it.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk from sugar companies adding ethanol capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only three or four plants are near commissioning, adding 8-10 crore litres a year; demand and supply are roughly balanced at 20% blending.

qa_highlights.question: Realisation for SAF?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said expected offtake price is INR180-190/litre with a 24-25% margin; international ATF is about INR210-220/litre.

risks_watch: Maize prices (about INR25.5/kg) could compress ethanol margins once current inventory is consumed.

Finance cost is about INR180 crore a year; de-leveraging plan not yet disclosed.
Q2 volume of 11-12 crore litres depends on OMC lifting and the unlifted 5 crore litre private OMC inventory.
CBG offtake and government policy (SATAT vs Sampoorna, DPI pipeline scheme changes, FOM/MDA subsidy) remain uncertain.
Middle East crisis has delayed 76 additional fuel retail outlets.

544545|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 606% YoY to INR811 crore and PAT turned to INR35 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 14.03% on maize prices up 25-30%.
544545|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was about INR811 crore versus INR115 crore a year earlier, and up from INR627 crore in Q1, with PAT of about INR35 crore against a loss of INR38 crore. EBITDA margin compressed to about 14.03% from a higher H1 level of about 18.2%, as maize prices rose 25-30% during the quarter and raw material was bought at elevated cost. Ethanol allocations were increased during the quarter after a Supreme Court judgment, lifting the last supply year's allocation from 24.5 crore litres to 34.5 crore litres, with a further 5 crore litres reported. Management guided to a shrinking bottom line in the coming year due to El Nino-linked feedstock shortages, while CBG capacity is being added.

segments.name: Ethanol
segments.commentary: Ethanol volumes sold were 8.29 crore litres in Q1 and 10.78 crore litres in Q2 (19.07 crore litres in H1). About 8.5 crore litres of orders remain to be supplied in October-November, and management expects 6-7 crore litres of additional volume in November-December.

segments.name: CBG (compressed biogas)
segments.commentary: First 20 TPD JV plant with Sumitomo is ramping up; two more plants are expected in the quarter, taking installed capacity to about 72 TPD from four operating plants. Management expects about INR20 crore of CBG revenue from the two to three plants over the next two quarters.

segments.name: SAF (sustainable aviation fuel)
segments.commentary: Front-end engineering is ongoing and about INR150 crore of viability gap funding has been received under PM JI-VAN for the proposed plant. Capex awaits a government roadmap that has not yet been announced.

segments.name: Fuel retail
segments.commentary: About 7 outlets are operational with more nearing commissioning; outlet expansion is being slowed due to crude price volatility.

guidance_outlook: Ethanol capacity utilisation expected to rise to at least 75-80% on average, from 65-70% in the last supply year; new-year allocation expected at about 40-42 crore litres (one analyst question cited 45 crore litres as the expectation).

Ethanol EBITDA margin expected to dip about 1-2 percentage points on average versus the run-rate once new tenders are allocated; Q2 described as the seasonally weakest quarter, with margin recovery expected from Q3.
Management expects the bottom line to shrink due to El Nino-linked raw material price and availability pressure; intends to forward-buy and stock maize and rice.
Raw material cost as a share of revenue expected to be sub-70% going forward, versus 62-66% historically.
Ethanol gross margin currently about 30% per CFO, which management declined to guide forward.

CBG: expected capex of about INR300 crore for four to five add-on plants at about INR65 crore per plant, with incremental term debt of about INR70-80 crore; GOBARdhan subsidy of about INR2 crore per TPD (25% currently receivable) and about INR25-30 crore expected by December or January.

Badami (Unit 5) slump sale expected to realise about INR170 crore, with about INR125-130 crore of term loan repaid and about INR40-46 crore retained; management expects about INR22 crore annual cost savings.
capex_capacity: Ethanol installed capacity about 2,000 KLPD (about 1,900 crore litres per year industry view); management says all ethanol capex is complete and no ethanol capex is planned next quarter. Three plants converted to grain-based dual feed; one 400 KLPD plant to run on C-heavy molasses/ENA.
Ethanol capacity utilisation was 62% in Q2 at the 400 KLPD plant and about 64-65% in H1.
CBG installed capacity to reach about 72 TPD by end of quarter; plan to start construction of six additional units with GAIL.
Srikakulam SAF plant planned on the PM JI-VAN grant; capex to start only after the government roadmap is announced.
Expected Q3 CBG working capital requirement of about INR25-30 crore at 100 TPD scale; current 10 TPD plant needs about INR2.5-3 crore.
demand_pricing: Maize prices rose 25-30% in Q2; management expects maize availability down about 35% and rice and sugarcane down 10-12% next year due to El Nino.
Ethanol realisation this year: maize-based about INR68/litre, damaged food grain about INR64, FCI rice about INR60; blended average about INR64-65 versus about INR67 last year.
Government reduced maize-based ethanol price by about INR3/litre in the current tender; sugarcane juice and B-heavy molasses banned for the 2026-27 supply year.
ENA long-contract prices about INR62-63/litre, with ENA production cost about INR1.5-2/litre lower than ethanol from C-heavy molasses.
DDGS byproduct price about INR26-30/kg. CBG revenue per TPD about INR4-4.5 crore; gas price rises from INR84 to about INR104/kg (up to INR116-120/kg for higher purity) under GOBARdhan 2.0.
Management sees roughly 230 mono-feed sugar-based plants out of about 500 unable to supply continuous ethanol, and the OMC tender demand about 1,100 crore litres.

Chemical/industrial alcohol demand cited at 250-300 crore litres; management expects 40-50% to be met by Indian producers. Industrial alcohol imports (RS) now INR58-60/litre versus INR47-48 previously.

qa_highlights.question: What volume guidance for next two quarters, and what execution risks for the Srikakulam SAF plant and feedstock strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: About 8.5 crore litres of existing orders for October-November; new-year allocation expected at 40-42 crore litres, subject to bids. Feedstock to be sourced nationally (Bihar, MP, Punjab) with warehouses being secured.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and debt plans, and working capital risk from CBG expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: No ethanol capex; CBG capex about INR300 crore for four to five plants with about INR70-80 crore new term debt. Working capital need is minimal; CBG subsidy of about INR2 crore per TPD reduces term debt.

qa_highlights.question: Ethanol volumes this quarter, and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Ethanol sold: 8.29 crore litres in Q1 and 10.78 crore litres in Q2 (19.07 crore litres H1). Margin expected to rise from Q3 with a possible 1-2 point average dip once tenders are allocated.

qa_highlights.question: CBG revenue ramp and subsidy timing?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR20 crore CBG revenue expected over the next two quarters from two to three plants; subsidy of about INR25-30 crore expected by December or January.

qa_highlights.question: Realisation and raw material cost structure for ethanol and CBG?
qa_highlights.answer: Maize ethanol about INR68/litre, blended about INR64-65; raw material share below 70% of revenue. CBG EBITDA guided at about 50-55% at 20 TPD, against a track record near 60%; revenue about INR80 crore per 20 TPD plant.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory holding and margin sustainability in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory of INR206 crore at September is expected to clear with the new season. Management would not disclose the maize-based realisation for next year before allocations; about 4.5 crore litres remain to be supplied this quarter.

risks_watch: Maize and raw material price inflation and feedstock availability with El Nino; management expects a squeeze on the bottom line in the next supply year.
Ethanol price cut in the current OMC tender (about INR3/litre) and allocation outcome for 40-42 crore litres, not yet confirmed.
SAF project depends on an unannounced government roadmap; no capex has started.
Finance costs rose to INR87 crore in H1 (from INR76 crore), and debt-to-equity is about 0.55x; new CBG term debt of about INR70-80 crore is planned.
Promoter pledge and share purchase intent (stake about 71%, headroom to 75%) and a personal loan were raised in the call; management said it does not affect the company.
Subsidy receipt timing (INR25-30 crore expected by December or January) and the Badami slump sale completion.

Management was evasive on forward ethanol margin and realisation numbers, saying these depend on allocations, and it deflected a question on promoter personal financing.

544546|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 42.5% to INR84.22 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 17% and PAT margin to 10.9% as spending on talent, platform and new verticals rose.
544546|2026-03.overview: Chatterbox Technologies held its maiden earnings call for FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026), its first since its IPO. Revenue from operations grew 42.5% YoY to INR84.22 crores, and EBITDA and PAT rose in absolute terms to INR14.32 crores and INR9.2 crores. Margins moderated, which management attributed to investment in talent, platform capabilities and new verticals. Management declined to give formal guidance, though it said FY27 net margins would be similar to FY26 with an aim to expand them. Several questions focused on the sharp fall in market cap after listing, the possibility of a QYOU Media merger, the delayed results timeline, and the AAGE edutainment app; management answered most of these qualitatively or deferred them.

segments.name: Chatterbox Represent (exclusive talent management)
segments.commentary: Contributed 39.27% of FY26 revenue, the largest vertical. Management said margins are fixed but absolute contribution can grow as exclusive creators are added; it manages over 100 creators exclusively.

segments.name: Brand Solutions
segments.commentary: Contributed 36.18% of FY26 revenue. No separate growth or margin commentary was given in the call.

segments.name: ChtrSocial
segments.commentary: Contributed 24.55% of FY26 revenue. Management called it one of the fastest-growing verticals and among the highest-margin, and said it expects revenue to at least double in the coming period, without giving a percentage target.

segments.name: International (Chtr International / Dubai subsidiary)
segments.commentary: About 18% of FY26 revenue. Dubai subsidiary is the gateway to the Middle East; priority markets are MENA, with APAC and LATAM evaluated selectively. Management said it will expand in a lean way.

guidance_outlook: No formal financial guidance given. Management said the opportunity ahead is significantly larger and it remains optimistic on healthy medium- to long-term growth.
FY27 net margin expected to be similar to FY26 (about 10%); management said it is aiming higher and streamlining opex.
ChtrSocial expected to at least double its revenue in the upcoming period; no percentage target given.
AAGE edutainment app launch targeted within FY27 after development was paused for the IPO; it is still at the UX/UI stage with focus-group validation planned.
Management said integrated benefits from QYOU Media collaboration will become more visible in H2 2026.
capex_capacity: Intangible assets roughly doubled, while intangible assets under development stayed at INR4.68 crores; the AAGE app was on hold during the IPO and is being resumed.
Chtr Studios (video production) and Dubai subsidiary were established; the Dubai subsidiary is not 100% owned by Chatterbox (reason asked but not clearly answered in the call).
No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were disclosed.
demand_pricing: Management said growth came from a mix of higher ticket sizes, organic growth across verticals, new client wins and international expansion, with an equal-mix view endorsed by the analyst.
Over 500 brands served, more than 2,000 campaigns executed, and a team of over 100 professionals, per management.
Management does not disclose net revenue retention, but said a significant part of growth came from existing enterprise clients with larger mandates and cross-selling of ChtrSocial and Studios.
Creator economy said to grow at a 25-30% CAGR globally, and BCG estimate cited of over USD 1 trillion annual creator-economy spend by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Which verticals will drive growth over the next 2-3 years, and will ChtrSocial, Represent, international or technology lead?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will come from multiple engines: ChtrSocial, technology/AI platform, exclusive talent management and international (MENA first, then APAC and LATAM). No percentage targets were given.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments have the highest margins and where is operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Farrel Arora said ChtrSocial and the production arm (Studios) have the highest margin contribution. Represent is scalable in absolute rupee terms but its margins are fixed.

qa_highlights.question: Why has intangible assets under development stayed flat at INR4.68 crores, and what is the AAGE app?
qa_highlights.answer: AAGE was put on hold during the IPO. It is an edutainment app mixing short-form video, learning and gamification with AI; launch is targeted within FY27 after UX/UI curation.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR26 crore trade receivables is not yet due?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR17.5 crores is within the standard 60-day credit period. Management said collections usually realise in 60-90 days (around 70-75 days on average), and most of the not-due amount should now be realised.

qa_highlights.question: Did volume growth come from more campaigns, new clients or deeper wallet share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a mix of all three, with deeper wallet share from existing clients and international efforts contributing; no split was given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the reasons behind the Dubai subsidiary not being 100% owned, the top-five customers, and whether QYOU Media will merge with Chatterbox at a market cap of INR78 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Curt Marvis declined to comment on any merger, saying only that the company is always looking at ways to increase shareholder value and that a public vehicle enables accretive M&A. Top-five customer data and the Dubai ownership reason were not answered directly in the call.

risks_watch: Margin compression: EBITDA margin 17% and PAT margin 10.9% in FY26, with FY27 PAT margin guided at similar levels (about 10%). Watch whether opex is streamlined.
Receivables: INR26 crores of trade receivables at March 2026 against INR84.22 crores revenue. Track receivable days and cash conversion next quarter.
Results disclosure timing: results were announced on 29 May, with the investor presentation and call later, and a family matter was cited as the cause. Investor-relations sentiment was questioned.

Related-party and governance questions: the parent QYOU Media (listed in Canada/US) merger was raised but not addressed; the Dubai subsidiary ownership and the market-cap decline post-listing (analyst cited about INR78 crores vs about INR160 crores at debut) remain open.
Customer concentration: top-five customer contribution was asked for but not disclosed.
AAGE app launch in FY27 and its monetisation are unproven; management said it will validate the model first.

544547|2026-03.headline: Jinkushal Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 89% YoY to INR133 crore, a record quarter, but full-year PAT was only INR12.44 crore as logistics and HexL brand costs weighed.
544547|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered the highest quarterly standalone and consolidated revenue in company history, with standalone revenue up 89% YoY to INR133 crore and consolidated at INR192 crore. Full-year standalone revenue grew 48% to INR313 crore, but standalone PAT was INR12.44 crore and consolidated PAT was INR12.76 crore, with management attributing the margin pressure to freight and geopolitical logistics costs, HexL brand investment and higher employee costs. Consolidated net worth rose from INR86 crore to INR194 crore after the IPO, while working capital increased on higher volumes and overseas inventory. Management declined to give FY27 revenue guidance, citing the Middle East conflict, and reiterated a medium-term target of INR600-700 crore revenue in 2.5-3 years.

segments.commentary: Customised machines of other brands contributed about 62%, refurbished used construction equipment about 35%, and HexL own-brand about 5% (4.9-5% consolidated; about 7% standalone).

segments.name: Geography FY26
segments.commentary: Mexico about 46%, UAE about 19%, South Africa and Australia about 10% each (per management's approximate figures), with the rest in single digits. Management said exports are about 97-98% of revenue.

segments.name: HexL brand
segments.commentary: Own brand in early build-out with lower margins; management targets 11-12% of FY27 revenue and about 150 units in FY27.

Long-run margin targets: 12-14% PAT for HexL and refurbished used equipment; 2-4% for new equipment of other brands.

Cash conversion cycle expected to improve next year, not in the near term.

Management did not disclose a new manufacturing unit or specific capex plan.
demand_pricing: Management said demand for construction and mining equipment stayed resilient, supported by infrastructure, industrial capex and replacement demand in emerging markets.
West Asia crisis raised logistics costs, freight, insurance and currency volatility; management said freight costs were absorbed in P&L and were the main reason for profit decline.
Mexico Q4 performance was better than Q3, but management did not quantify FY26 Mexico decline.

544547|2026-06.headline: Jinkushal Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 37.4% to INR51.29 crores, but consolidated PAT fell to INR2.2 crores from INR6.51 crores.
544547|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 37.4% YoY to INR51.29 crores and consolidated revenue grew 15.9% to INR56.57 crores. Profitability fell sharply on a consolidated basis, with PBT at INR3.04 crores versus INR7.26 crores, as shipping costs and employee expenses rose. Africa contributed about 32% of revenue against about 4.47% a year earlier, partly replacing Middle East business disrupted by geopolitics. Management said inventory of about INR96.8 crores, mostly overseas, is being built as part of the international strategy, and that investments in people and systems will weigh on margins for several quarters.

segments.name: Africa (geography)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 32% of Q1 FY27 revenue versus about 4.47% in Q1 FY26, offsetting lost Middle East revenue. Management said it sees the shipping and business cycle as established.

segments.name: HexL (proprietary construction equipment brand)
segments.commentary: Management said it is in early stages, with heavy spending on marketing, discounting and dealer development. Management cited a long-term PAT target of 12% to 14% (also 12% to 15% in an earlier call) and a 20% to 40% retail price advantage versus global brands.

segments.name: New/customised equipment, used and refurbished equipment
segments.commentary: No segment revenue split was disclosed. Management said new customised equipment demand is strongest near term, and that used equipment and HexL should each grow to a larger share over 2 to 3 years.

guidance_outlook: Long-term revenue target of INR600 crores to INR700 crores, to be reached in 2 to 3 years; management declined to give a FY27 growth figure.
Management expects healthier profitability in 2 to 3 years once shipping, interest and manpower costs settle; near-term profit is being sacrificed for long-term build-out.
Inventory expected to stay at similar levels, plus or minus a few percentage points, in lower double digits, with conversion over about 2 quarters.
Expects to see results from strategic investments in 3 to 6 quarters.
Expects operational manpower costs to keep rising over the next few quarters.
capex_capacity: Consolidated inventory of about INR96.8 crores at June 30, 2026, of which about INR84.4 crores sits at overseas subsidiaries.
Inventory is positioned overseas to shorten delivery times for used and refurbished construction equipment.
Management says the investments are transient (inventory, working capital, manpower) rather than fixed capex or plant machinery.
Post-IPO capital base and enhanced banking facilities cited as capacity to support higher volumes.
demand_pricing: Africa is now a major market; management said the Middle East revenue gap was partly filled by Africa.
Freight and shipping costs rose on geopolitical route closures and longer shipping times, which also lengthened debtor cycles.
Commodity inflation is not expected to be fully passed through; costs are partly absorbed and partly passed to suppliers and customers.
Management said new customised equipment is in highest demand, driven by faster availability and lower breakdown times for end users.
Management said customer collections have generally met commercial timelines, but geopolitical disruptions have led to some customer payment delays.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving Africa's growth and can it be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Africa replaced Middle East revenue hit by geopolitics and board capital allocation decisions. Management expects the shipping and business cycle there to be sustainable, and it sees Africa, Latin America and the Middle East as equally important.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR97 crore inventory convert to sales, and how fast?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business cycle runs at least 2 quarters, so inventory should convert over the next 1.5 to 2 quarters, with inventory levels fluctuating by a few percentage points over the last 2 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and debtors rise: what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the debtor rise a planned overseas penetration strategy, with longer shipping times keeping receivables high until machines reach customers. It expects working capital cycles to stay elevated for now.

qa_highlights.question: Will freight costs ease and can they be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is taking a substantial hit on shipping costs, partly passing them to suppliers at purchase and to customers at sale. Management said it cannot forecast oil prices.

qa_highlights.question: Will employee costs yield operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it plans to add sales and purchase staff and to move from SME to mid-corporate or large-corporate operations, and will keep investing even at the cost of near-term reported margins.

qa_highlights.question: When will returns on these investments become visible, and what will the business look like in 3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects results in 3 to 6 quarters. In 2 to 3 years it targets INR600 crores to INR700 crores revenue with healthier profitability, a dominant international business, and roughly equal revenue from the three verticals.

risks_watch: Consolidated PAT fell about 66% YoY, and management is absorbing shipping, interest and manpower costs without a date for recovery.
Inventory of about INR96.8 crores with about INR84.4 crores overseas ties up working capital and raises conversion risk.
Africa accounts for about 32% of revenue; management said it is not viewing any single geography in isolation.
Freight costs depend on oil prices, which management said it cannot forecast; geopolitical route closures are extending shipping times.
Management declined to give FY27 revenue guidance and gave no segment-level margin or revenue numbers.

Management said the company manufactures backhoe loaders under contract in China, and an analyst raised natural calamities there as a supply risk; management said the locations it uses are unaffected.
544547|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term targets and the Africa shift, but cautious and evasive on near-term profitability, FY27 growth and HexL economics. Management repeatedly deferred forward-looking questions because of geopolitical uncertainty.

544550|2026-03.headline: Pace Digitek Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 60.5% YoY to Rs.1,097 crore; FY26 PAT Rs.307 crore (+10.1%), FY27 revenue guided Rs.3,200-3,400 crore.
544550|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations was Rs.1,097 crore versus Rs.683 crore a year earlier, driven by project execution. Full-year revenue grew 8.3% to Rs.2,641 crore and PAT rose 10.1% to Rs.307 crore, but full-year EBITDA fell to Rs.455 crore from Rs.482 crore as the mix shifted from telecom to energy. Working capital absorbed cash: inventory was built to Rs.540 crore and trade receivables reached Rs.2,442 crore, which management expects to ease by September 2026. BESS manufacturing capacity is being raised from 2.5 GWh to 5 GWh (July 2026) and 10 GWh (October 2026).

segments.commentary: Telecom & ICT is 21.9% of the order book (Rs.2,484 crore) and contributed 55% of FY26 revenue. Recent wins include further BSNL and Railways orders, a RailTel order for Railway Kavach infrastructure (tickets Rs.100-250 crore), and CCTV on coaches.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance maintained at Rs.3,200-3,400 crore; FY28 at Rs.4,000-4,200 crore (top line reported net of intra-company transactions).
FY27 PAT margin expected at 10-11%, down from 11.4% in FY26, as lower-margin energy orders rise in the mix.
BOO projects expected to contribute 20-25% of FY27 revenue (about Rs.800-1,000 crore) and about Rs.1,000 crore in FY28; BOO PAT margin targeted around 10%.
Cash flow from operations expected to normalise by September 2026; management said FY28 would be CFO positive.
Cell price rise of about 20% from 1 April 2026 expected to ease from the next quarter; bids include contingency for input cost increases.

In-house container fabrication expected to improve pricing and operating efficiency by about 4-5%.
capex_capacity: BESS manufacturing at 2.5 GWh operational in FY26 with about 80% utilisation; target is about 80% utilisation by end of FY27 once 10 GWh is running.
5 GWh expansion: machinery received from China, installation underway, operational from July 2026 (delayed about two months by West Asia shipping disruption).
5 GWh second line ordered, expected operational October 2026, taking total to 10 GWh; plant and infrastructure for a further expansion to 10 GWh already built.
In-house container fabrication plant ready, operational from July 2026.
Open order book about 5.32 GWh, of which 2.72 GWh is BOO; MSEDCL BOO project expected to generate about Rs.1,000 crore revenue in FY27.
Cell manufacturing is under consideration; an announcement is expected soon.

Cell prices rose about 20% from 1 April 2026 due to regulatory changes (China export rebate cut from 9% to 6%); the company used stocked cells bought at earlier prices to protect Q1 FY27 margins.
Government BESS tenders are won on L1 basis; private customers weigh manufacturing, field operations and support. First non-captive customer L&T placed a 250 MWh order in January 2026.
C&I BESS (kWh scale) is a new focus; state policies in Maharashtra, Gujarat and Rajasthan mandate BESS with solar of 50 MW and above.
Management said competition will rise; the company claims about 6 GWh open order book and first commissioned project (September 2025) as operating credential.

qa_highlights.question: Is the capacity commissioning delay a bottleneck, and are imports from China affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the delay was two months, caused by West Asia shipping disruption; equipment has arrived and will be commissioned in June and operational from July 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current cell cost and expected pass-through, and what are container realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Container realisation is about $82-84/kWh and cell cost $48-50/kWh (60-65% of container cost); management expects prices to ease from the next quarter and is not delaying projects currently.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 margins hold given energy is the bulk of the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Energy EBITDA margins are lower than telecom; PAT margin is expected to be 10-11% in FY27 versus 11.4% in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why do FY25 receivables differ from the RHP figures?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs.295 crore (FY26) and Rs.1,271 crore (FY25) were regrouped as non-current receivables, mainly a BSNL five-year milestone schedule; analyst still reported a gap and was asked to email for clarification.

qa_highlights.question: What is the unit economics of the MSEDCL BOO project?
qa_highlights.answer: Project cost about Rs.1.2 crore/MWh ex-GST, reduced to about Rs.93 lakh/MWh after VGF of about Rs.27 lakh/MWh; government pays Rs.2,19,000 per MW per month; SPV-level IRR about 12-13%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was working capital stretched and when will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory was built ahead of cell price rises; Q4 sales of Rs.1,097 crore created receivables on 90-120 day cycles. Rs.300 crore was collected in April-May and receivables are expected to ease by September 2026.

risks_watch: Input cost risk: cell prices up about 20% from 1 April 2026; if elevated prices persist, project timelines and margins may be hit, and force majeure provisions may be invoked.

Margin dilution as energy (lower margin) rises in revenue mix; FY27 PAT margin guided lower at 10-11%.
Execution risk on 5 GWh (July 2026) and 10 GWh (October 2026) capacity ramp, and on reaching ~80% utilisation by end FY27.
Reporting questions on receivables reclassification (Rs.295 crore non-current, Rs.1,271 crore FY25) were not fully resolved on the call.
Funding: no equity or warrant raise planned; BOO projects paused beyond the fourth project unless external investment is secured.

544550|2026-06.headline: Pace Digitek Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 51.3% YoY to Rs.555 crore; FY27 guidance of Rs.3,200-3,400 crore reiterated on Rs.10,803 crore executable order book.
544550|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs.555 crore (up 51.3% YoY) but down sharply from Rs.1,097 crore in Q4 FY26, which management attributed to milestone-based recognition and a high Q4 base. EBITDA was Rs.86.1 crore (15.5% margin vs 14.9% in Q4) and PAT was Rs.63 crore (11.3% margin vs Rs.55 crore in Q1 FY26). Order inflow in the quarter was about Rs.1,677 crore, with two energy EPC wins (NLC, DVC, ~Rs.1,412 crore) and a BSNL OFC project (~Rs.265 crore). Management said the 5 GWh BESS line is operational, with a further 5 GWh line due to be commissioned by December 2026, and reiterated the FY27 revenue guidance.

segments.name: Energy (BESS, renewable EPC, BOO)
segments.commentary: Contributed 79.5% of Q1 revenue and is the main growth driver; energy executable order book Rs.8,453 crore, split Rs.4,074 crore BOO and Rs.4,367 crore EPC. Management expects energy to be about 65-70% of the order book by year end.

segments.name: Telecom & ICT (BharatNet, Railway Kavach, BSNL OFC)
segments.commentary: Contributed 20.5% of Q1 revenue; executable order book Rs.2,350 crore. Kavach about 30% complete; BSNL OFC (~Rs.265 crore) to execute over about 2.5 years. Management said telecom has better margins but lower volume.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of Rs.3,200-3,400 crore reiterated; management said it sees no concern in achieving it, with most revenue expected from the existing order book.
H1 FY27 targeted at 40-45% of full-year revenue vs 35% in H1 FY26.
Q2 container supply planned at 210 units; management expects about 125+ containers per month in the next calendar year.
FY27 PAT margin guidance of 10.5-11% for BESS, with the lithium-ion cell cost increase said to be factored in.
Cash flow from operations expected to turn positive by March 2027; inventory and receivables expected to stabilise between December and March.
Energy-to-telecom order book mix expected to move to about 65:35 or 70:30 by year end.
capex_capacity: BESS capacity is 5 GWh operational (two 2.5 GWh lines); a third 5 GWh line is due for installation in October 2026, targeting 10 GWh by early December 2026 as India's largest operational BESS facility.
Total capex of about Rs.300 crore for the 5 GWh expansion phase, the container fabrication unit, and related setup, mainly land cost, funded from the earlier private placement.
In-house container manufacturing started with trials this month; batch production from next month. Over 300 containers supplied to date.

BOO projects: 975 MWh commissioned to date (MSEDCL standalone BESS, about Rs.900 crore recognised in P&L); four BOO projects expected to add about Rs.750 crore annual revenue once all are commissioned.
Pune R&D centre inaugurated about three weeks ago; cell manufacturing planning under way. Applying for 4 GWh under the government cell PLI scheme (10 GWh total scheme).
demand_pricing: Bidding for about 27 GWh of tenders; NTPC Renewable Energy and NTPC Green tenders noted, with NTPC Green tenders drawing only 7-8 bidders versus 32-51 in earlier state tenders.
Management said bidding aggression has eased after a 4 GWh Maharashtra project was cancelled and a Punjab tender saw a single bid at higher prices.
Management said cell cost is about 60% of total BESS cost, unchanged; recent tenders include price variation clauses while older tenders do not. Stock was built in March to lower Q1 cell costs.

C&I BESS (below 5 MWh) received product approval from large Indian customers; first trial order of about 25 units, with management referring to potential for thousands per year. Management guided C&I EBITDA margin about 4-5 points above grid-scale product margin of 13-15%.
Container unit value about Rs.4-4.5 crore; about 70 containers per month currently.
Early exports: small container supply to a Saudi company in Q1 and an MoU signed in Saudi Arabia.
MEGMEET tie-up for AI data-centre power solutions in India; demo equipment planned; management said a concrete revenue plan could come in about one quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Telecom & ICT order inflow break-up and execution timeline for the Rs.2,350 crore telecom book?
qa_highlights.answer: Of Rs.1,677 crore inflow, NLC and DVC EPC wins were about Rs.1,412 crore and BSNL OFC about Rs.265 crore. EPC projects run about one year; OFC about 2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 guidance not higher given the energy order book visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: BOO solar-plus-BESS capex is capitalised as a fixed asset and not recognised as revenue, so physical execution will exceed reported revenue. Revenue recognition comes from EPC and standalone BESS in BOO.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash flow and working-capital profile by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Telecom net working capital is about 5 months (~150 days); energy is expected at 90-100 days. Management expects operating cash flow to turn positive by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue path needed from Q2 onwards?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most of the remaining Rs.2,700 crore should come from the existing order book, with Q1 seasonally low due to government funding and approval cycles.

qa_highlights.question: How will rising lithium-ion cell prices affect EPC and BOO margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance of 10.5-11% margin already includes anticipated cell price increases; price variation clauses in new tenders and stock built in March mitigate impact.

544567|2026-09.headline: Infinity Infoway H1 FY27 revenue rose 106.22% to Rs 16.81 crore, with EBITDA margin at 50.68% and PAT margin at 29.89%.
544567|2026-09.overview: Management reported H1 FY27 (six months to 30 Sep 2026) revenue from operations of Rs 16.81 crore versus Rs 8.15 crore a year earlier, up 106.22%. EBITDA rose about 109.68% to Rs 8.52 crore (50.68% margin) and PAT rose 79.36% to Rs 5.02 crore (29.89% margin). Growth was supported by the ZeroTouch secured examination paper product, which began booking revenue in H1 with larger billing expected from Q3, and by a headcount increase from 156 to 178. Depreciation increased as products under development in FY26 went into use and as GPU and ZeroTouch device assets were added. Management also outlined plans to enter international markets, starting with the Gulf, then Southeast Asia and Europe.

segments.name: Education ERP (government and education clients)
segments.commentary: Serves 61+ education clients, with recurring revenue from 28; modules cover admissions, academics, examinations, finance, fees and HR (30+ modules). Management described it as the core business.

segments.name: Industry / enterprise ERP
segments.commentary: 35+ industry customers, with recurring revenue from 16; industrial ERP with AI-enabled solutions is a stated priority.

segments.name: ZeroTouch (secured examination paper solution)
segments.commentary: Early-stage revenue in H1 described as nominal; billing is per question paper printed and delivered, with exams started in October 2026 and a good amount of revenue expected in Q3. Management cites EBITDA margin above 50-60%, and 20-22% of revenue targeted from it within two years.

guidance_outlook: Management expects to maintain the current H1 run rate (about 100% growth) based on the Rs 78 crore order book and pipeline; beating it is described as difficult.
Management says H2 will be better than H1, citing a five-year pattern of Q3 and Q4 outperforming Q1 and Q2.
Margins are expected to be manageable for at least the next couple of quarters, with AI helping to lower costs; management cautioned that exponential growth could pressure margins initially.

International revenue is targeted in FY27 (Gulf first, then Southeast Asia and Europe), with an initial focus on private schools, colleges and universities. ZeroTouch is not planned abroad for at least one year.
ZeroTouch is expected to contribute 20-22% of revenue within two years, per management.
capex_capacity: Fixed-asset additions in H1 included upgrades to ZeroTouch devices after Q1 demonstrations and higher-spec GPUs for in-house AI model and LLM experiments on physical servers.
Depreciation of Rs 1.72 crore in H1 reflects ZeroTouch and one or two other products that moved from development into use in FY26. Management did not give a split between the two.
Team size rose from 156 to 178 during H1 to support sales, execution and outbound marketing.
Service presence now covers more than 10 Indian states.
demand_pricing: Order book of Rs 78 crore as of 30 Sep 2026.

ZeroTouch is priced per question paper printed and delivered; higher volumes attract a lower per-unit charge. Current focus is government examinations (competitive, board, university), with private clients as a second phase.
Gujarat Gyan Guru Quiz (G3Q) season 3 launched in September 2026 on a platform Infinity manages for the Government of Gujarat. Season 1 (2023) drew more than 27 lakh students.
AI Manthan 2.0 in Kanpur: live demonstration of ZeroTouch, with approval to pilot it in examinations.
Infinity reports 76 examinations conducted via its portals and more than 18 lakh students served.

544568|2026-03.headline: H2 FY26 revenue nearly doubled to INR 125 crore (+~100% YoY) with EBITDA up 42% to INR 15.9 crore, though margin fell to 13%.
544568|2026-03.overview: DSM Fresh Foods (Zappfresh) reported H2 FY26 revenue of about INR 125 crore versus INR 65 crore in H2 FY25, with EBITDA of about INR 15.9 crore (13% margin) and PBT of INR 11.5 crore. For full FY26, revenue was about INR 221 crore (+69%), EBITDA about INR 31 crore, and reported PAT INR 14.4 crore, which management says is INR 18.4 crore before a deferred tax impact. Growth was driven by B2B/HoReCa, fish and seafood, and early ramp of the Meevaa ready-to-eat range, while B2C volumes were flat to down. Management guided to 70-80% revenue growth in FY27 and a 3-4% EBITDA margin improvement over two years.

segments.commentary: Launched recently with over 5,000 orders in 48 hours. Current annualised run rate INR 30-40 crore, about 90% export (US, Canada, Europe); guided to 15-20% of FY27 revenue (at least INR 70 crore) and about 50% gross margin. Capacity INR 500 crore at Chandigarh plant.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target of 70-80%, with Meevaa contributing 15-20% of revenue and fish and seafood rising to 30-35% of mix.

EBITDA margin expected to improve by at least 3-4 percentage points over the next two years, driven by aquaculture (200-300 bps on fish), a higher ready-to-eat share (about 50% gross margin), and a B2B/B2C split near 50-50 or 53% B2C in the medium term.
Management said the deferred tax drag will not recur in H1 FY27, with underlying PAT around INR 18 crore at standard tax rates.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive in 2-3 years after working capital investment.
Partner store network to scale from about 100 stores to 300-400 by year end; each store averages INR 5 lakh monthly revenue and 8-10% net margin.
capex_capacity: Meevaa Foods plant in Chandigarh is state-of-the-art, with capacity of INR 500 crore revenue per year on land, plant and machinery already in place.
Marina Aqua integrated aquaculture platform on about 270 acres: land parcels in Kanpur, Ghaziabad, Nagpur and Assam; around 300 seafood farmers in the FPO.
Partner store (local meat shop) model: about 100 stores onboarded across Mumbai and Bangalore, targeting 300-400 by year end; pilot of 15-20 stores.
Planned new cities include Pune, Nashik and near-Bangalore markets; management did not disclose capex per new city.
demand_pricing: Management said the mix shift toward B2B and fish reduced gross margin; B2C gross margin about 45-50% vs B2B about 20-25%.
Ready-to-eat gross margin about 50%, roughly 25-30 percentage points above quick commerce-channel products after commission and marketing costs, per management.
Meevaa targets NRI consumers in US, Canada and Europe with northern Indian gourmet snacks, avoiding frenchfries and nuggets categories where large FMCG players compete.
Management views domestic frozen competition as high; domestic strategy to add seekh kebab and tikka products through partner stores.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the mix is intended to move toward about 50-50 over time; the B2B push is to absorb volume from the new Marina Aqua farming business. B2C is currently online only, with retail stores to be added.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from H2 FY25 to H2 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly the rising B2B share (close to 70%) with lower gross margin (20-25% vs 45-50% in B2C); a slight gross margin dip was also cited.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakdown of the 70-80% FY27 growth target?
qa_highlights.answer: Meevaa at 15-20%, fish and seafood rising from 27% to 30-35%, chicken at 40-45% and mutton declining. Meevaa run rate is INR 30-40 crore annualised, expected to deliver at least INR 70 crore in FY27.

qa_highlights.answer: Each store averages INR 5 lakh monthly revenue with 8-10% net margin, around INR 50,000 monthly profit per store.

qa_highlights.answer: Operating cash flow is negative due to working capital investment; cash is INR 20-25 crore, net debt to equity is below 0.5x, and management expects positive operating cash flow in 2-3 years. Debt headroom exists, and warrant exercise by the promoter is planned.

544569|2026-03.headline: Tata Motors Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 22% YoY to Rs 24,500 crore with EBITDA margin at 13.9%, but management guided only to single-digit Q1 growth amid commodity and diesel risks.
544569|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter of the year on volume and price, with wholesales of about 131.8K units (up 25% YoY) and standalone EBIT margin of 12.1%. FY26 standalone EBIT crossed 11% for the first time and free cash flow reached about Rs 9,200 crore. Management flagged a sharp commodity cost headwind (about 100 bps in Q4 and significantly higher in Q1 FY27), took only a 2% price increase in April, and said it will not pass through the full cost increase. Iveco deal closure has slipped to Q2 FY27 pending French and Spanish financial regulatory approvals.

544572|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 sales rose 9.8% QoQ to INR 9.5 billion; reported PBT margin 9.5%, or 11.5% excluding demerger one-offs.
544572|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 (Jan–Mar 2026) revenue grew 9.8% QoQ to INR 9.5 billion, led by OEM orders from wind, metals and rail. Reported PBT margin recovered to 9.5% from negative 7.8% in Q3, but this includes demerger-related one-offs; excluding them, margin was 11.5% versus 13.1% in Q3. Net working capital fell 2.8% QoQ to 18.7% of sales on lower inventory. Management guided margins back to around 13% after demerger costs end and about 15% by FY29-30, with capex of around INR 800 crore planned through FY30 for a new Pune plant. YoY comparisons were not presented because prior-period figures were extracted from SKF India Limited.

segments.commentary: Distribution fell in Q4, with share dropping to 32% from 38%, as volume shifted away from distributors with overdue payments and some shipments were held back. Management expects this to recover.

segments.commentary: Exports performed well in Q4, mainly to Europe and Southeast Asia; about 6% of FY26 revenue.

segments.commentary: Intercompany sales to SKF India Limited were the second-largest growth driver in Q4, linked to automotive demand; about 4% of FY26 revenue.

Tapered roller bearing capacity at Pune raised from 600,000 to 886,000 pieces via machine upgrades; cost down about 18%, changeover time down 20%, new product lead time down about 35%.
Until the new plant is ready, SKF India Limited continues job-work manufacturing; additional demand sourced from SKF Ahmedabad and Nilai.
