Other expenses rose on royalty and trademark payments (about INR 60 million higher) and manufacturing costs (repairs, power and fuel, stores). A transfer pricing margin on services from SKF India was also booked.
Competition described as intense, especially at OEMs. Rupee depreciation is a bigger cost headwind than steel and oil-linked inflation.

qa_highlights.answer: FY26: distribution about 35%, OEM about 51%, exports about 6%, SKF India sales about 4%, other income about 3%. Within OEM: railway 11%, general machinery 7%, wind and defence 7%, heavy industries 7%, metals 6%.

qa_highlights.question: How is raw material inflation trending, how much price has been taken, and how will margins evolve with capacity additions and demerger costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin to return to about 13% by end of calendar 2026; about 15% by FY29-30. Cost escalation projected at 3-4%, with FX as the bigger headwind. Pricing actions already taken with distributors; OEM price escalation being negotiated and expected to be harder.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the gap between current margins and the 13-15% historical range, and what drives the path to 16-18%?

qa_highlights.question: Will the company prioritise growth over margin, given exits and re-entries in wind, rail and tractors?
qa_highlights.answer: Strategy is growth while maintaining margin, with a target of about 15%. Re-entering wind, freight rail and tractor segments through localization means winning share at lower OEM margins, which management expects to improve through efficiency and pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex timeline and when will new capacity be commissioned?

544572|2026-06.headline: SKF India (Industrial) Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.3% YoY to INR 9,708 mn, but PBT margin fell to ~9% on FX losses and demerger IT costs.

Management reiterated a long-term PBT margin path of 14-16% through 2028, with a 17-19% aspiration, and a new Pune plant with INR 850-950 crore capex targeted for 2028.

qa_highlights.answer: Distribution is the higher-margin channel at high double-digit margins; OE is high single-digit. OE supports aftermarket share growth.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the solutions business and what is the doubling timeline?

544574|2026-06.headline: Tata Capital Q1 FY27 PAT rose 56% YoY to INR1,547 crore, with consolidated AUM up 22% YoY to INR2.91 lakh crore and credit cost at 1%.

AUM reached INR2.91 lakh crore, up 22% YoY and 5% QoQ, or 28% YoY excluding Motor Finance. Disbursements rose 33% YoY to INR46,212 crore, while the book grew about 10% YoY on a legacy run-off drag. 544576|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR80.54 bn (+8.1% YoY) but EBITDA margin fell ~250 bps YoY to 11.7%, with FY27 targeting early double-digit margins.
544576|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was LG Electronics India's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR80.54 bn, up 8.1% YoY, with EBITDA of INR9.45 bn (11.7% margin) and PAT of INR6.93 bn (8.5%). Year-on-year margin compression was attributed to channel promotion spend (~1.1 pp), rupee depreciation (~5.6% YoY, ~1 pp impact), and e-waste compliance cost (~0.2 pp). For FY26, revenue grew 1.0% to INR246.05 bn, EBITDA was INR24.08 bn (9.8%) and PAT INR16.85 bn (6.8%). Management guided FY27 to mid-teen revenue growth and early double-digit EBITDA margins, citing April-May sell-through and recent price hikes.

Margin down ~250 bps YoY; up 7% sequentially

segments.name: Home Appliances & Air Solutions (H&A)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR65.16 bn (+5.7% YoY); FY26 revenue INR181.60 bn. EBIT margin 11.9% in Q4, hit by commodity costs, rupee depreciation and channel investments for new launches. Premium washers, French door refrigerators and 5-star RACs saw higher ASPs.

segments.name: Home Entertainment (HE)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR15.37 bn (+19.6% YoY, +15.9% QoQ); FY26 revenue INR64.44 bn. EBIT margin 13.4% in Q4, after time-bound Cricket World Cup marketing spend. OLED market share 60.0% YTD March 2026.

Export expansion targeted 'very significantly' in FY27; large-capacity refrigerators exported to advanced markets from Q1 FY27; Essential Series exports to 22 countries.

Pune plant produces premium products: 674 litre and 790 litre side-by-side refrigerators, top freezers (790 litre plus) and front-load washing machines for export.
Sri City expected to double export-capable capacity and improve South India logistics (South India is 38-40% of business).
FY26 capex INR5.51 bn; localization rate 55.2%, up ~1.4 pp YoY.
demand_pricing: Channel: AC channel filled in Q4 (55% of annual AC business falls in Q4); >1 million ACs sold in Q4 FY26; industry entered Q1 FY27 with inventory at last year's levels, but March cold spell slowed sell-out. LG says its inventory was in line with plan and manageable.

Price hikes: RAC increased in two phases (BEE-rating driven, then input cost and FX), about 12-13% per analyst; refrigerators and washing machines also repriced. LG says competitive positioning unchanged and no impact on sales.

AC penetration in India cited at ~13%; B2B order inflows from government, corporate and hospitality; ID division hit record quarterly sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue growth of 8% not translate into operating leverage and a YoY margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul Khanna said margin fell ~250 bps: channel promotion ~1.1 pp (temporary, to drive sell-out and partner confidence), currency depreciation ~1 pp, and e-waste compliance ~0.2 pp as recycling target rose from 60% to 70%. Price hikes, lower promotions and summer demand are expected to restore margins in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is LG doing differently from peers, and how will margins recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Dongmyung Seo cited export scaling, the recovering B2B business, AMC as a high-margin recurring stream, and new categories. Margin levers: exports (core growth engine), localization (55.2%), and a higher mix of AMC and B2B. Lower oil prices after Middle East stabilisation could also help.

qa_highlights.question: What is the channel inventory now versus the start of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Gurpinder Singh said the AC industry entered Q1 FY27 with inventory at last year's levels, with dealers cautious after a slow March. LG's inventory was aligned with plan, and current high temperatures are easing channel pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Are price hikes enough to protect margins, and are more planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Chitkara said AC prices were raised in two calibrated phases and that LG was first to move, with competitors following. Similar hikes were made on refrigerators and washers with no volume impact. No immediate further hikes are planned, but the company is monitoring raw materials and FX.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex outlook for FY27 and the Sri City timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul Khanna confirmed the Sri City plant is on track: compressor line in Q3 FY27, RAC line in Q4 FY27, and washing machine and refrigerator lines later. About INR657 crore is spent to March 2026, with the full INR5,000 crore to be funded from internal accruals over the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: Does LG still target doubling exports, and what is the Essential Series response?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul Khanna reiterated a very significant export expansion, with premium products to developed markets from Pune and Sri City. Sanjay Chitkara said Essential Series sales were encouraging, with 100,000 washers and 80,000 refrigerators in Q4, and exports are going to 22 countries.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demand outlook for April-May 2026 and the industry growth comparison?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Chitkara said ACs are well supported by summer demand and the company expects good growth. He targets strong double-digit to mid-teen growth across all four categories in FY27, but gave no industry growth figures for April-May.

qa_highlights.question: Whether the new categories are for domestic or export use?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Chitkara said the new categories serve both: chest freezers (five models, market ~INR3,000 crore), fixed-speed RACs, and large refrigerators from Pune, which target new domestic business and global markets.

544587|2026-03.headline: Midwest Ltd FY26 consolidated revenue rose 3% to INR645 crores; Q4 EBITDA margin 27.0% and PAT margin 16.5%, with Quartz start-up weighing on profitability.
544587|2026-03.overview: Midwest reported FY26 consolidated revenue of INR645 crores, up about 3% from INR626 crores, with consolidated EBITDA margin of 27.01% (vs 27.43%) and PAT margin of 16.49% (vs 17.17%). Q4 revenue was INR215 crores, with EBITDA margin of 27% (vs 23.7% in Q3) and PAT margin of 17.16% (vs 13.48%). Granite standalone held margins at 27.55% EBITDA and 17.47% PAT, while the new Quartz segment absorbed about INR6 crores of cost in the year. Management said Quartz began full production in April 2026 and targets about 60% utilisation of its 300,000 tonne installed capacity in FY27, with Phase 2 commissioning expected in Q4 FY27. Debt fell by INR50 crores and working capital days fell from 122 to 104.

qa_highlights.question: Why are wholesale prepayments so high?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly operating cash flows ahead of underwriting in real estate; in CMML, refinancing by banks, capital-market raises and cash flows are all contributing.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the capital raise needed when leverage is comfortable?
qa_highlights.answer: Regulatory CRAR of 18.85% (against 15% minimum and 18% comfort level) is well below what a net-worth-to-AUM view implies; the gap is about Rs 9,000 crore. The enabling resolution keeps Tier 2 and other instruments open.

544597|2026-09.headline: Piramal Finance Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 67% YoY to INR545 crores; Growth AUM up 30% YoY and RoAUM 2% annualised.

Cost to income improved to 52%, and the company raised INR3,850 crores of equity (QIP INR2,100 crores plus INR1,750 crores promoter warrants). Management reiterated FY27 profit growth guidance of around 50% and a 2.5% exit RoAUM for Q4 FY27, and flagged a possible insurance commission headwind from IRDAI's draft proposal.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments will pass on higher rates to customers, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Pass-through follows PLR changes, which lag cost of borrowing by about one year; management expects no pass-through yet. Around 50% of assets (HL and LAP) are the main repricing book.

qa_highlights.question: Will yields rise as the legacy book runs off?

qa_highlights.question: Is the housing loan vintage uptick real?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, driven largely by one INR4 crore fraud case from Q2 FY26; management expects it to fall in Q3. Concentration in South India IT-sector home loans persists but has not spread.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan exposure and risk strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry data shows 15-23% of gross gold disbursements went to customers 90+ days past due. Piramal's October gold disbursements to such customers are under 1%, and it will not disburse to them.

qa_highlights.question: Why is consolidated provisioning lower than Growth credit cost?

qa_highlights.question: Path from 2% to 3% RoAUM?

544599|2026-03.headline: Studds Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11.9% YoY to INR 167.5 crore; FY27 guidance is 17-18% revenue growth with broadly flat EBITDA margin.

For FY26, revenue was INR 634.2 crore (up 8.6%), EBITDA INR 122.2 crore (up 16.4%, margin 19.3%) and PAT INR 82.7 crore (up 18.7%). Management took 8-9% price increases from 1 April 2026 to offset raw material inflation, but expects Q1 FY27 gross margin pressure before recovery. Management also announced Bharat Goyal's elevation to CFO effective 1 July 2026, an ESOP plan, and a dividend of INR 3 per share.

544600|2026-03.headline: Lenskart Q4 FY26 revenue rose 41% YoY to ₹2,516 crore, with reported EBITDA up 61% and pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin at 12.8%.
544600|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter since listing: revenue grew 41% YoY to ₹2,516 crore, PAT reached ₹204 crore, and EBITDA margin expanded 2.7 pp to 21.3%. India and international both grew, with India same-store sales growth at 24% and international revenue up 35.4%. FY26 crossed ₹1,700 crore EBITDA, ₹1,000 crore pre-Ind AS EBITDA and ₹500 crore PAT for the first time. Management kept the steady-state pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin at about 25% and guided FY27 net store additions to roughly FY26 levels (542 in India plus 61 international in FY26).

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹1,054 crore (+35.4% YoY; +25% constant currency) with eyewear units up 29%. Store count 718 after 13 net adds in Q4 and 61 in FY26; FY26 pre-Ind AS EBITDA ₹264 crore at 7% margin. Japan was the strongest market; Middle East had a temporary traffic dip that has recovered to near normal.

guidance_outlook: Net new store additions in FY27 expected to be around FY26 levels (FY26: 542 India, 61 international).
Long-term steady-state pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin unchanged at approximately 25% (India currently 14-15%, about 10 pp runway).

Step-up in R&D spend in FY27 for automated eye testing, smart eyewear (B by Lenskart) and AI; FY27 priorities include scaling to 100 million customers.

Hyderabad plant and Thailand JV cited as structural answers to reduce import dependence.

qa_highlights.question: What geopolitical, raw material, China-sourcing or market risks should investors monitor?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight and raw material have had no meaningful impact so far; currency is the biggest variable. 42% of business is international and vertical integration has offset rupee-import headwinds. No material demand impact seen in India or abroad; Middle East dip was small and brief.

qa_highlights.question: How was the India gross margin held near 64% in a low-ASP quarter, and does SSSG of ~25% with ~15% price imply ~10% volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin gains came from vertical integration and process changes, not price increases; OPP campaigns are paired with upgrades to offset margin. Management said the 10% volume estimate was not correct and that volume SSS is meaningfully higher; it does not disclose value/volume split.

qa_highlights.question: How will employee productivity and cost leverage trend, especially internationally?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating leverage came mainly from SSG and volume growth on a fixed cost base. HQ and tech costs were flat as headcount was not added; AI and remote optometry are expected to add more output per person.

qa_highlights.question: Does Tier 2 strength expand the 4,500-store runway and allow faster expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said more than 4,500 stores are possible; 200+ Tier 2 stores have been added and feed GeoIQ. Metros are also growing (eye tests +45%+) and are the main source of SSG.

qa_highlights.question: How should we think about competition in smart glasses (e.g. Google re-entry)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the category is very early with no clear form-factor winner; it sees Lenskart's role in prescription and distribution of smart glasses and its app/data layer as advantages. Launch focus is on learning, not near-term sales.

qa_highlights.question: How will international margins converge to India's level, and what is the KSA breakeven status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a quarter for reaching 15% international margin; it cited falling ACP and operating leverage after scale. KSA is about two years old and ahead of where UAE was at the same stage; no breakeven date was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will store expansion focus on saturating existing pincodes or entering new ones, and what about cannibalisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Site selection is bottom-up using mobility data within a 10-minute travel radius, not pincode-level. Management said stores tripled in many cities while revenue doubled, and that much of SSG came from multi-store pincodes.

qa_highlights.question: Is same-day delivery a near-term target and does the store network become an inventory model?
qa_highlights.answer: No delivery target set; same-day is in experiments in Singapore and some Indian markets. Stores are being used as micro-fulfilment nodes for OTC products and at-home frame trials, which management described as a chemist model rather than a warehouse.

qa_highlights.question: What is Meller's traction and scale target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Meller is ahead of plan, sold out across markets, and is being positioned as a Gentle Monster-type brand for Gen Z. No specific scale target was given.

Losses narrowed at EBIT (loss of INR18 crores) and PAT (loss of INR28 crores), and standalone borrowings fell to INR272 crores from INR314 crores at March 31, 2026. Management attributed the volume recovery to sequential trade-lane improvement after inventory corrections, while the Middle East conflict continued to weigh on FCL volumes.

segments.commentary: Mainstay and highest-margin business; about 14.5% global market share. Volumes up about 5% QoQ, but down about 4% YoY and about 10% below levels of two years ago.

segments.name: FCL (full container load)
segments.commentary: Volumes up about 1% QoQ and down double digits YoY, weighed by Middle East exposure. FCL market share is under 1%.

segments.name: Air freight
segments.commentary: Volumes up about 5% QoQ; double-digit YoY decline per management. Smaller part of the business.

guidance_outlook: Base case assumes no substantial volume growth; management expects marginal monthly volume uptick over the next few months, in line with typical seasonality.
Intent is to keep cost flat in USD terms over the coming couple of years, including employee and admin expenses.
Management expects marginal incremental profit improvement, with gross profit per unit (yield) expected to hold at current levels.
Ballpark of 12% to 15% volume growth from current levels needed to reach desired profitability trajectory; part from market share, part from trade rebound.
Net debt expected to fall significantly over the next two to three quarters via working capital reduction and non-core asset sales; update promised in coming quarter.
No guidance on return on capital employed, though management said it should return to the historical 'north of 20%' zone broadly.
capex_capacity: Business described as asset-light with minimal owned capital assets; capex a tiny fraction of P&L.
Non-core divestments: warehousing and office assets, combined about USD10 million to USD15 million.
Network optimisation: loss-making trade lanes reduced; focus on container utilisation.
Cost initiatives: AI/agentic automation, offshoring to lower-cost geographies, single global system for finance, HR and operations.
Management said no further acquisitions needed near term; growth to come organically by hiring teams for new products and markets.
demand_pricing: Volume growth in Q1 was about half market growth and half market outperformance, per management.
Middle East conflict has depressed volumes for about 5 to 6 months; inventory corrections drove momentum on transatlantic, transpacific and intra-Asia lanes.
Carrier capacity constrained by disruptions, keeping freight rates elevated; management said freight rates rose about 20% to 30% (per analyst question) and is passed through in revenue and costs.
Gross profit growth of about 6.6% QoQ versus about 4.1% implied by volume mix; management attributed the extra 2 to 2.5% to freight environment and efficiencies.
Industry volumes down about 13% to 14% over last two years; Allcargo outperforming by about 3% to 4%. Growth in Latin America, Southeast Asia and India offset declines in Europe and US.

qa_highlights.question: Is the industry cyclical and why have yields fallen since FY24?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the post-COVID 21 to 24 month period was exceptional for FCL margins, and excluding it yield has improved continuously; volumes, not yields, have been the drag. It described the business as shadowing trade conditions rather than cycling.

qa_highlights.question: Why are volumes declining when global trade is broadly flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LCL has declined more than the industry on a YoY basis, while FCL decline is higher for Allcargo due to Middle East exposure. No alternative to LCL exists except air for small shipments averaging 3 to 4 cubic metres.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost base and is it flat in USD?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the intent is to keep cost flat in USD terms; about 80 to 85% of business sits outside India and ocean freight is the largest cost in USD. Rupee translation affects both revenue and cost.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt composition and net debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is mainly working capital plus acquisition funding. Consolidated gross debt about INR942 crores and net debt about INR570 crores at June quarter-end.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA and ROCE normalisation path is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: No EBITDA margin guidance, since margins are not a relevant metric in this business. Management said ROCE was historically above 20% and should return there broadly; a 12% to 15% volume increase from current levels is the ballpark needed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company pursue acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Near term, no; management said the strategy is to grow by investing in people rather than buying businesses, as all key markets and products are already covered.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict continuing to depress FCL volumes, particularly in and out of the region, with knock-on impact on North Asia.

PAT still negative (loss of INR28 crores); profitability relies on volume recovery and cost discipline.

544603|2026-03.headline: Groww's Q4 FY26 call gave no hard financial figures; equity F&O market share rose to 10.6% from 9.1%, with active derivative customers at about 17 lakh per quarter.

Management said industry activity is still well below the peak, with FIIs negative and March 2026 volatility hitting MTF and commodity accounts. Management reiterated that cost to grow is roughly INR 450-500 crore a year and will be kept below revenue growth.

Credit (LAS) now makes up 34% of disbursements, bonds launched last quarter are scaling, and SEBI and CCI approvals were received for the State Street Global partnership in the AMC. Management attributed F&O and order softness to volatility and to gold/silver ETF slowdown rather than regulation, and said Q4 FY26 was an anomaly for MTF and derivatives. 544603|2026-09.headline: Groww's Q2 FY27 call centred on Cost to Serve rising on AI compute, one-time INR10-13 crore hit, and MTF book adding ~INR600-700 crore a quarter.
544603|2026-09.overview: Management explained that Cost to Serve rose in Q2 due to AI-related costs, higher compute on more trading days, and a one-time INR10-13 crore hit from delayed files on an expiry day. Cost to Grow fell because the IPL branding spend in Q1 did not recur. Management said the margin trading facility (MTF) book adds about INR600-700 crore a quarter on average, with volatility from stock-level moves and policy changes such as higher haircuts on crowded stocks. Other operating income rose on about 30 IPOs (including SBI AMC and NSE) and BSDA income. Management said the call was qualitative on several items, such as US stocks timing and UPI MDR outcome, and gave few new numbers on AUM or market share.

segments.name: Broking (cash and derivatives)
segments.commentary: Management said revenue in derivatives and commodities is driven by order count at INR20 per order, while cash revenue depends on both order size and count (lower of 10 bps or INR20). Cash market share has been about 15% and derivatives about 11% over the last three to four quarters, per analyst. August was the lowest volume month of Q2.

segments.name: Wealth (Groww Prime, MF Prime, Fisdom)
segments.commentary: Wealth AUM was disclosed for the first time; management said MF Prime is small. Users rose by almost 50% quarter-on-quarter, mainly from Groww Prime per analyst. Wealth income is reported within other operating income, and Fisdom users are now included in active customers.

segments.name: Lending (MTF, personal loans, loan against shares)
segments.commentary: MTF book adds about INR600-700 crore a quarter. Loan against shares was launched in the last two quarters with good early traction; personal loan book is growing gradually quarter-on-quarter. No figures were given for the lending book size.

segments.name: Other operating income
segments.commentary: Rose sequentially on about 30 IPOs in the quarter (including SBI AMC and NSE) and BSDA income. IPO and BSDA income were regrouped out of stocks revenue.

guidance_outlook: Cost to Grow for FY27 is expected to stay in the INR400-500 crore a year range, with more spend in good markets and less in weak ones.
Management expects the MTF book to keep growing, adding about INR600-700 crore a quarter, and MTF share of cash turnover to rise over time.
Management expects the CAS rule change to normalise volumes, with faster recovery depending on the effective date, which was awaited.
Management expects UPI MDR outcome to be not materially cost-changing, but the cap level (INR300 mentioned) is still under discussion with the regulator.
Management expects long-term convergence of cash and F&O market share toward NSE active share, but said this could take around 10 years.
capex_capacity: Management said 915 power-trading tools and web-based trading are not yet a material contributor to volume or revenue.
AI spend is rising: in-house AI stack being built to lower per-token cost; AI-related costs and compute costs rose in Q2.
Compute cost scales with trading days; management uses more compute on trading days and much less on non-trading days.
Company said the wealth integration (Fisdom) is complete and some products are being mainstreamed across apps.
demand_pricing: Management said competitive pricing approach is to give customers more value than they are charged, and it is not following competitors on price.
Analyst noted some discount brokers cut brokerage by half; management did not directly address this.
Volumes were affected by the CAS circular; management expects CAS changes to normalise volumes, with derivatives largely unaffected by the proposed options.

544609|2026-06.headline: PhysicsWallah Q1 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to INR1,054 crore; pre-Ind AS EBITDA improved to negative INR44 crore, with NEET calendar shift a drag.

544610|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 34% to INR 143 crore with 82.5% recurring; FY27 target INR 210 crore, with INR 190 crore visibility cited.
544610|2026-03.overview: Workmates reported FY26 revenue of INR 143 crore (up 34%) and PAT of INR 15.92 crore (up 16%, margin 11.1% vs 13%). Margins compressed: gross margin 32.8% vs 33.9% and EBITDA margin 16.2% vs 17.7%, which management attributes to a Dubai contract exit (about INR 4 crore), a gaming client exit (INR 3.5 crore) and about INR 6 crore of added headcount cost. Management set an FY27 revenue target of INR 210 crore (45%+ growth) and entered FY27 with MRR of INR 13.5 crore per month. This was the company's first earnings call since its BSE SME listing.

Three delivery centres (Kolkata, Bhubaneswar, Hyderabad); nine locations in total. 120+ AWS-certified professionals out of 170+ staff.

Enterprise client count rose from 34 to 38; 28 net new clients added; top 20 accounts contributed 73% of revenue; client retention 95%. Management said top-5 concentration has declined.

Management said customers negotiate hard on managed-services and implementation pricing in India, while accepting AWS consumption costs. Hardware prices reportedly doubled or tripled, which management views as a tailwind for cloud migration.

544612|2026-03.headline: FY26 value added revenue rose 12.3% to INR49,180 million with a record 18.8% EBITDA margin; Q4 EBITDA up 17.6% to INR2,573 million.

Phase 2 HPMC/PVP excipients not expected to be commercialised this financial year.

segments.name: Brand business (Honeywell, CyberPower, audio, air purifiers)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR369.61 crores, ahead of INR359-360 crores guidance; audio outperformed. Management aspires to 50-60% annual brand growth and says Honeywell itself should grow at least 40-50%. Honeywell licence renews March 2027.

segments.name: Own brand (Vertual, launched May 2026)
segments.commentary: New in-house brand with air purifier and similar Honeywell categories, to launch first online in the US (Amazon warehouses already stocked) and in India, with material available from 22-23 May 2026. Management guided INR10-12 crores initial marketing spend and about 8-9 months to gain footing.

guidance_outlook: Internal target of at least 25-30% annual revenue growth and 30% absolute profit growth over the next 5-6 years; management says growth rate is ambitious but achievable for about 3-4 years.
Brand business targeted to grow 50-60% a year; Honeywell alone at least 40-50%; Honeywell brand expected to grow about 50% in FY27.
Brand business EBITDA expected at about 13% now, aiming for 17-18% at INR1,000 crore scale; long-run EBIT target 18-19% above INR1,000 crores.
Vision of a 50:50 market entry to brand split by 2030; aspiration to reach 3-4 brands near term and 6-7 long term, with 2-3 brands above INR1,000 crores.
Plan to separate brand and market entry businesses in 2-3 years, with a demerger process that could start after about 15 months; no plan in the next 15 months.
Middle East brand sales could fall to about 50% of current levels if shipments stay disrupted; management says price hikes and consumer sentiment may hit margins in FY27.
capex_capacity: Intangible assets rose to INR406 crores on ERP migration (Microsoft Business Central) with CRM and supply chain modules, new servers and software licences.
New distribution centre opened in Noida; new offices and set-up teams in Delhi and other locations for new businesses.
Working capital expected to be funded through debt and internal accruals for the next 15 months; equity raise only for an acquisition of about 30% of company size or a brand purchase.
Management is actively looking to acquire a surveillance/AI brand with a legacy, team and sales; expects a small acquired business (INR5 crore) could scale to INR10 crores in a year.
Brand business inventory: company holds 30-40 days of inventory to secure supply and hedge price increases; partners hold 45-60 days stock in Middle East.
demand_pricing: Management says price escalation is possible but demand should hold for 3-4 years, supported by India demographics, government push on AI, digital infrastructure and Make-in-India.

Higher Q4 gross and EBITDA margins attributed to Make-in-India surveillance and AI customers (PSU or government end-users) served via smaller vendors; management expects this margin mix to flow to the bottom line over time.
Raw material costs for memory, storage and CPUs up 30-40%; management says costs are being passed on but customers are beginning to feel the pressure and consumption may fall.

Brand categories: audio market about INR25,000 crores (India and abroad), air purifiers about INR3,000 crores in India, data-centre cables about INR4,000 crores in India; US air purifier market about INR28,000 crores, with about INR8,000 crores sold on Amazon.

Honeywell air purifier and accessories ambition is to be number 1 or 2 in India; air purifier currently close to number 2. Quick commerce grew over 100% across India, UAE and Saudi Arabia; 1 product sold every 60 seconds online in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Would demerging the higher-return Honeywell brand business unlock value?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans separate brand and market entry businesses within 2-3 years, but there is no plan for the next 15 months; a demerger process is about 12-15 months and would start once the brand reaches about INR1,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the Middle East war on the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight on Red Sea routes rose from about $1,500-1,700 to $7,500-8,000 per container; short-term impact is manageable given 45-60 days of partner stock, but a prolonged disruption could halve Middle East brand business.

qa_highlights.question: Why were Q4 gross and EBITDA margins high?
qa_highlights.answer: Make-in-India surveillance and AI customers, served through smaller vendors, carry higher margins, and the mix is expected to scale as government demand for AI, IoT and data centres grows.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables rise to about 20% of turnover and how will they normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 turnover roughly doubled to INR721 crores from INR393 crores; extended credit for new AI, surveillance and data centre lines is expected to normalise receivables back toward 13-14% of turnover.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance costs stay low despite higher short-term debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt excluding MSME supply-chain finance rose only to INR83.72 crores from INR69.53 crores; the rest is about INR171 crores of government TReDS-type MSME payment finance at around 8-9% that started in the last two quarters, so only about 8 months of interest was incurred.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Honeywell licence be renewed and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Licence expires March 2027; management is very confident of renewal, citing Honeywell's 22-23 year average licences and its split into five companies, with two separated and two more by July-August 2026.

risks_watch: Middle East disruption: Red Sea freight costs and container availability; Middle East brand revenue could fall to about 50% if disruption persists.
Input cost inflation of 30-40% in memory, storage and CPUs, with customers starting to resist price hikes and consumption possibly falling.
Receivables at about 20% of turnover (INR565 crores) versus 13.4% last year; management targets return to 13-14% and inventory is also rising.
Honeywell licence renewal due March 2027; a new licence and trademark terms will need to be confirmed.
Working capital and MSME supply-chain finance (about INR171 crores) rising; watch debt levels and interest costs in coming quarters.
Acquisition plans in surveillance/AI brands and the own-brand launch (Vertual) add execution and funding risk; watch marketing spend of INR10-12 crores.

544632|2026-03.headline: Meesho says logistics disruption in Q2–Q3 FY26 is behind it; Q4 contribution margin exit rate of 4% is the new baseline.
544632|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as a strong quarter, with contribution margin up about 170 bps QoQ, of which roughly 110 bps came from lower logistics cost. The 145 bps one-time logistics headwind was concentrated in Q2 and Q3 FY26 and attributed to short-term capacity building during 3PL consolidation around May 2025. Ad revenue as a percentage of NMV rose QoQ, while reported revenue per order looked flat partly due to accounting changes (first-order discounts now netted against revenue) and a higher prepaid mix. Management gave no EBITDA break-even or FCF timing guidance; it pointed to LTM FCF as the guiding metric, and Q4 cash balance fell about INR300 crore, which management partly attributed to tax payments expected to be recovered.

segments.commentary: More than two-thirds of sellers by GMV are active on ads; ad catalogue count up over 40% YoY. Advertiser budgets over the last year grew more than double, and pricing increases are deferred until steady-state ad revenue is higher.

segments.commentary: Focused on value brands for mass India; contribution margin is deliberately below the core marketplace during an investment phase to onboard brands.

Contribution margin baseline is the 4% Q4 exit rate; further improvement expected to come from ad revenue and partial restoration of fulfilment margin, slower than Q3 to Q4 gains over the next two quarters.

Cloud contract renegotiation every 2–3 years to capture scale discounts.
demand_pricing: First-year user frequency has roughly doubled over three years; mature cohorts (FY24 and before) reach about 15 orders over roughly three years, per management.
Prepaid share rising, lowering COD costs; BNPL is early-stage and not yet a material driver of the shift.
CAC declined, which management attributes to AI-led tools (voice agent Vaani) and pricing improvements that lowered the barrier to first order in rural areas.
Ads ROAS described as among the best in the industry; pricing not yet increased, with management stating it will raise ad pricing at the right time.
Seller concentration continues to fall; 960,000 sellers referenced by an analyst, with growing non-GST seller onboarding.

qa_highlights.answer: Dhiresh Bansal said there is no specific target; the current cost structure, around 50%, is the most optimised, and mix is adjusted as costs change.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating cash flow turn more negative even as margins improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited one-offs from past periods and quarter-end NMV timing; it pointed to LTM FCF and offered to share a reconciliation.

qa_highlights.question: Why has revenue per order fallen while ad revenue is rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is now netted for first-order discounts and prepaid mix is rising; prepaid orders are net neutral to contribution margin, so management prefers contribution margin as the trend metric.

qa_highlights.question: Will the cash balance decline of about INR300 crore be explained?
qa_highlights.answer: Quarter-end NMV timing causes volatility, and some taxes paid are expected to be refunded, so the net cash figure was adjusted for them.

qa_highlights.question: Would BNPL drive lower COD share?
qa_highlights.answer: BNPL is early; the COD reduction so far has come from prepaid pricing and discounts.

qa_highlights.question: When will ad pricing rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will raise pricing at the right time; first it wants more sellers activated and budgets scaled (budgets more than doubled in a year).

Possible inflation impact on consumer AOV and frequency; management views value-focused players as potential gainers.

544632|2026-06.headline: Meesho Q1 FY27: management says logistics cost per delivered order fell about ₹1 QoQ, and it guides to ~25% five-year NMV CAGR.
544632|2026-06.overview: Management said fuel and minimum-wage hikes during Q1 FY27 were absorbed, with cost per delivered order down about ₹1 QoQ, and pricing rose at the same time as costs. NMV growth was about 2% QoQ, which management attributed to seasonality (Eid moved from Q1 last year into Q4) and a higher S&M spend base last year, not a change in the core business. Year-on-year AOV fell about 2% versus the roughly 5% annual baseline decline. New initiatives (Kirana Club, a low-cost local grocery logistics network) remain early and capped at about ₹200 crore annual EBITDA burn; Q1 operating loss was about ₹39 crore. The call also covered a GTA structure for middle- and last-mile logistics under VTPL and a Karnataka gig-worker fee, which management says is stayed and immaterial.

qa_highlights.answer: Management expects continued logistics cost reduction at a good pace. Cost per delivered order fell about ₹1 QoQ in Q1, offsetting the fuel and wage hikes.

qa_highlights.answer: Valmo share is about 50% and materially unchanged. VTPL houses only middle- and last-mile GTA operations, so its financials will not map directly to Valmo volumes.

qa_highlights.answer: No change in philosophy. The annual EBITDA budget cap for new initiatives is about ₹200 crore.

qa_highlights.answer: The GTA model is used by other horizontal e-commerce players. Management says no regulator or tax authority has raised a query, and no SEBI communication has been received; it sees no material exposure.

qa_highlights.question: Why did AOV stay flat sequentially, and what drives contribution margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases from fuel pass-through and raw-material costs offset the efficiency pass-through. Contribution margin is expected to rise as logistics fee margin is restored and ad revenue grows.

544633|2026-03.headline: Vidya Wires FY26 revenue rose 24.2% to INR 18,396.4 mn and PAT reached INR 576.1 mn; ALCU plant began production on 7 Feb 2026.
544633|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations was INR 18,396.4 mn (+24.2% YoY), EBITDA INR 857.8 mn at a 4.66% margin (+35 bps), and PAT INR 576.1 mn. Management said FY26 volume was about 18,024 MT (+6.5%), with revenue growth of roughly 17-18% on a volume basis, and Q4 revenue grew 58%, which management attributed mainly to higher copper prices and better utilisation. ALCU Industries, the wholly owned subsidiary, started manufacturing on 7 Feb 2026 and contributed about 800 MT in FY26; it is in a phased ramp-up with about 6,000 MT installed and 8,000-9,000 MT more due by Sep-Oct 2026 (before Diwali). Management also flagged working capital at about 60 days, which it aims to bring to 50-52 days, and debtors of 41 days targeted to about 35 days.

rows.label: ESOP and corporate overhead trajectory

544644|2026-03.headline: Corona Remedies Q4FY26 revenue rose 20.2% to INR 353 crore and FY26 PAT grew 33% (adjusted INR 199 crore), with Q4 EBITDA margin down ~90bps to 17.6%.
544644|2026-03.overview: Q4FY26 revenue was INR 353 crore (+20.2% YoY) and PAT INR 45 crore (+44% YoY), while EBITDA rose 14.4% to INR 62 crore and margin fell about 90bps to 17.6% due to new divisions, MR additions and R&D spend. For FY26, revenue grew 17.3% to INR 1,403 crore, EBITDA rose 22.3% to INR 293 crore (20.9% margin, +80bps), and adjusted PAT grew 33.4% to INR 199 crore after a one-time labour code charge. Management declared a 100% dividend (INR 2 per share) and guided to 15% organic revenue growth, 25% growth on acquired brands and 20%+ PAT growth in FY27.

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 adjusted PAT (ex one-time labour code impact)

segments.name: India business
segments.commentary: Contributed ~96% of FY26 revenue; India growth 16.8% in FY26 with domestic Q4 growth of 18.3%. Management says it outgrew IPM in volume, price and new launches.

segments.name: International business
segments.commentary: Grew 29.5% in FY26 and 70% in Q4FY26, but is only ~4% of revenue. Operates on a B2B model with lower gross margin and higher EBITDA than India B2C; management targets high-single to low-double digit growth.

segments.name: Chronic and semi-chronic portfolio
segments.commentary: Contributes 72% of revenue per PharmaTrac MAT March 2026 (71.9% in FY26). Two brands crossed INR 100 crore; two brands are in the INR 100-200 crore club and eight in the INR 50-100 crore club.

segments.name: Acquired brands (Bayer portfolio, Wokadine)
segments.commentary: Bayer seven-brand portfolio relaunched in Q4FY26 with an infertility division; Menodac and Fostine R named as focus brands. Wokadine (No. 2 in Indian povidone iodine, ~INR 20 crore revenue) expected to grow ~25% p.a. for 3-4 years with ~400bps gross margin correction in year one.

segments.name: Biosimilars and biologics / Semaglutide
segments.commentary: Three biosimilar launches in FY26 (Fostine R, Tricium DnaB, Wyntide, Tyvenza as named on the call). Semaglutide generics made via MSM as manufacturing partner; Wyntide targets super-specialists and Tyvenza targets tier 2/3 markets.

guidance_outlook: Maintain 15%+ organic revenue growth, 25% growth on acquired brands, and 20%+ PAT growth in FY27 and for the next 2-3 years.
Gross margin expected to be sustained around 80% in coming years, supported by product mix; Middle East/oil-linked API cost risk too early to quantify, with ~90-120 days of inventory on hand.
EBITDA margin expected to improve over time through productivity and operating leverage; management cited 24-25% as a question from an analyst but did not commit to a target.
Expects IPM growth of 10-10.5% in FY27 (volume 1.5-2%), with Corona volume growth of 3x-4x the market.
Bhayla hormone plant and 600-kg line expansion to become operational in Q1 or Q2 FY27; European and Eurasian market revenue expected to build over 2-3 years.
Management says the 15% revenue and 20% PAT framework is unchanged for international business; international expected at 8-9% CAGR over the next 3-4 years.
capex_capacity: Dedicated hormone manufacturing plant (Bhayla) expected operational in Q1 or Q2 FY27; new 600-kg line expansion under way.

EAEU GMP certification received, enabling entry into Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Armenia and Kyrgyzstan; Bhayla plant already EU-approved, with dossier filings in progress and 1.5-2 years needed per country registration.
Working capital for international expansion funded through internal accruals; R&D and bioequivalence studies needed for dossiers.
MR strength at 3,100 after adding ~450 in FY26 (2,630 prior base); management says it is comfortable with current MR strength for FY27.
demand_pricing: IPM grew ~8.6% in FY26 (volume 0.7%); Corona grew volume ~3% (4.6x IPM) and new launches contributed 6.4% (2.6x IPM 2.5%).
PharmaTrac pricing growth reported at ~7.8% per management slide; management attributes this to 92-93% non-NLEM portfolio, with volume outgrowing price.
PCPM rose to INR 4.11 lakh per month from INR 3.62 lakh a year earlier; MR tenure buckets targeted at INR 2 lakh (0-3 yrs), INR 4 lakh (3-6 yrs), INR 6-8 lakh (6+ yrs).
Advertising plus sales promotion ~19% of FY26 sales: ~10% KOL consulting, ~5% S&D promotion, ~4% scientific conferences.
Raw material imports under 1% of RM, so limited direct FX/import exposure; indirect cost pressure from API makers.
Semaglutide first-year India market estimated by management at INR 2,000-2,500 crore (range quoted by analysts INR 500-5,000 crore).

qa_highlights.question: Is 17-18% the right EBITDA margin range, or is 20%+ achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 margin dip reflected MR and employee additions; FY26 margin was 20.9% (+80bps), and it expects productivity-led improvement, with current MR strength considered sufficient for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of Q4 margin dip and whether Q4 seasonality is structural?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 9 crore employee cost for two new divisions and MRs, INR 5 crore MR allowances in other expenses and INR 1.6 crore R&D (BE) cost; management cited seasonality plus the two new divisions and asked analysts to look at H1 vs H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ~7.8% pricing growth sustainable and what is the Middle East impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pricing is sustainable given 92-93% non-NLEM exposure; too early to quantify Middle East/oil impact on gross margin, with 90-120 days of inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What are PCPM, export margin profile and AI use in doctor engagement?
qa_highlights.answer: PCPM is INR 4.11 lakh (vs INR 3.62 lakh); exports carry lower gross margin and higher EBITDA margin under B2B; AI is used in the SFE tool for reps and a diagnosis/prescription tool for doctors.

qa_highlights.question: How will Wokadine and the Bayer brands scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Wokadine expected to grow ~25% for 3-4 years with ~400bps gross margin correction in year one, shifting focus to non-NLEM SKUs; Menodac and Fostine R are the Bayer arrowhead brands, with a target of INR 50-100 crore over the next few years.

qa_highlights.question: Is IPM acceleration sustainable and will volume outperformance hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects IPM at 10-10.5% in FY27 with 1.5-2% volume; Corona expects 3x-4x volume outperformance versus the market, down from the historical 4-5x.

risks_watch: Q4 EBITDA margin at 17.6% after new divisions, MR hiring and R&D; watch whether the margin recovers as the new divisions scale.
API and crude-linked raw material inflation (Middle East) could pressure the ~80% gross margin; management flagged 90-120 days of inventory cover.
Wokadine gross margin correction of ~400bps in year one and possible further 600-700bps; Bayer infertility relaunch progress to be reviewed in 3-4 months.
Semaglutide market size estimates vary widely (INR 500-5,000 crore), and clarity is expected in 2-3 months.
Short-term borrowings of INR 143 crore are overdraft against FDs (net cash ~INR 15 crore) linked to the Wokadine acquisition; a INR 16 crore Myoril loan is to be repaid in FY27.
Export ramp-up depends on 1.5-2 years per country registration; international growth expected at 8-9% CAGR, so near-term contribution stays small.
544644|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and outperformance, reiterating 15%/25%/20% targets for FY27. Cautious and non-committal on the Middle East API cost impact and on EBITDA margin expansion, which management framed as longer-term.
key_quotes: Our philosophy is to grow 15% on a revenue and 20% on a PAT basis on a year-on-year basis for coming 3 to 5 years down the line.
So, we are open for all the things as far as complex, generic, and biologics biosimilar is concemed.
So, it is absolutely sustainable, Alankar.
These are all growth investments which will reap benefits for the future period.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY26 EBITDA margin rose ~80bps to 20.9%, and management expects productivity-led improvement, but Q4 fell ~90bps to 17.6% and management gave no EBITDA margin target and was cautious on gross margin given API cost risk.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Bhayla dedicated hormone plant and 600-kg line expansion guided operational in Q1 or Q2 FY27, with MR strength up ~450 to 3,100 (from 2,630), and management guides 15%+ organic growth on that base.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Corona guides volume growth of 3x-4x IPM (IPM volume 1.5-2% in FY27) after FY26 volume grew ~3% (4.6x IPM), with new launches contributing 6.4% of growth and MR strength at 3,100.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated 15%+ organic, 25% acquired-brand and 20%+ PAT growth for FY27 without raising them, while FY26 PAT grew 33.4% to INR 199 crore adjusted and IPM is guided at only 10-10.5% in FY27.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 EBITDA margin fell ~90bps to 17.6% on INR 9 crore new-division/MR employee cost and INR 5 crore MR allowances, and Middle East/oil-linked API cost risk is unquantified against ~80% gross margin with 90-120 days of inventory; Wokadine faces ~400bps gross margin correction in year one.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Bayer seven-brand portfolio relaunched in Q4 FY26 with an infertility division (Menodac and Fostine R as focus brands targeting INR 50-100 crore), and Semaglutide generics via MSM partner with a INR 2,000-2,500 crore first-year market estimate, though analysts' range is INR 500-5,000 crore.

rows.label: EAEU/European export ramp-up
rows.when: over 2-3 years; first contribution H2 FY27
rows.why: EAEU GMP certification received for Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Armenia and Kyrgyzstan and Bhayla is EU-approved, but 1.5-2 years per country registration and international is only ~4% of revenue growing 8-9% CAGR.

rows.label: Pricing sustainability on non-NLEM mix
rows.why: PharmaTrac pricing grew ~7.8% and 92-93% of the portfolio is non-NLEM, with PCPM up to INR 4.11 lakh from INR 3.62 lakh, supporting price-led growth.

rows.label: Short-term borrowings and Myoril loan repayment
rows.why: INR 143 crore overdraft against FDs (net cash ~INR 15 crore) linked to Wokadine acquisition, plus INR 16 crore Myoril loan due for repayment in FY27.

tone.note: Management was confident on 15%/25%/20% FY27 growth, MR strength and volume outperformance, but cautious on the Middle East API cost impact and on EBITDA margin targets; analysts pushed on the Q4 margin dip to 17.6%, whether 20%+ margins are achievable, and sustainability of ~7.8% pricing.

544644|2026-06.headline: Corona Remedies Q1 FY27 revenue rose 21.9% YoY to INR422 crore, with EBITDA margin up ~190 bps to 22%.
544644|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 21.9% YoY to INR422 crore, with India business up 22.7% against IPM growth of 11.6%, and organic growth of 21.4%. EBITDA rose 33.5% to INR93 crore and PAT rose 30.1% to INR60 crore, with PAT margin at 14.2%. Management kept FY27 guidance of 15% organic revenue growth and 20% PAT growth, but flagged raw material and geopolitical cost risk and said it is premature to extrapolate the Q1 margin. The Europe-GMP hormonal facility was capitalised on 30 June 2026 and export filings are targeted for FY28-29.

financial_highlights.change: +21.9% YoY (vs INR347 crore in Q1 FY26)
+33.5% YoY; margin up ~190 bps (from INR70 crore)
vs INR10 crore in Q1 FY26; mainly amortisation of Wokadine and Bayer brands

segments.name: India business
segments.commentary: Contributed about 97% of revenue and grew 22.7% YoY, roughly twice the IPM growth of 11.6%.

segments.name: International business
segments.commentary: Contributed about 3% of revenue and did not grow in Q1; management says it will stay in the low-single-digit share for the next few years.

segments.name: Therapy areas (PharmaTrac, per management)
segments.commentary: Women's Healthcare grew about 23.3% vs IPM 9.4%; Urology grew 27.6% vs IPM 14.9%; Cardio-metabolic and Pain Management outperformed IPM by 1.7x and 1.4x respectively.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: 15% organic revenue growth plus about 1.5-2% inorganic growth, for about 17% total revenue growth and 20% PAT growth.
Management says it aims to maintain margins 'within a similar range' but will not commit to sustaining Q1 levels given cost volatility.

Raw material: about 70-90 days of stock held at quarter end; new stocks began arriving in June 2026. Management sees possible 100 bps margin hit in coming quarters and is offsetting via other cost cuts.
Hormonal facility asset turnover expected below 1x in FY27, rising to 2-3x over about three years; depreciation on the INR130 crore capex is about INR6.5 crore a year.
Export ramp: dossiers ready by Nov-Dec 2026, then 12-18 months for registration; international launch targeted FY28-29.
Medical representative additions guided at 6-8% per year (about 200-250 MRs), with no MR additions planned in FY27 after about 400 were added in Q4 FY26.
capex_capacity: Europe-GMP hormonal (women's healthcare) facility commercialised on 30 June 2026, after INR130 crore capex; it handles tablets, soft gelatin capsules, ointments and gels.
Ahmedabad oral solid dosage facility Europe-GMP certification renewed.
Manufacturing mix is about 60% in-house and 40% outsourced, expected to stay similar through FY27.
API sourcing: about 60-65% of API needs are met by La Chandra Pharma Lab, in which the company holds a 31% stake (via Remedies Private Limited). La Chandra has EU GMP and a recent US DMF approval.
Hormonal plant to serve the domestic market initially; international dossier filings are in preparation.
demand_pricing: MAT June 2026 PharmaTrac split: volume growth 6.3% vs IPM 1.3%; price-led growth about 8.7% vs IPM 5.6%; new product contribution 3.4% vs IPM 2.9%.
Management says the Q1 India growth split is broadly in line with the MAT split.
Company ranks 26th in IPM (up from 29th a year ago). It is 5th in Women's Healthcare and Pain Management, 9th in Urology, and 20th in Cardio-diabeto (top 10 in new consolidated business).
Two brands now exceed INR100 crore annual revenue (one in MAT June 2023), and more than 40 brands exceed INR10 crore (from 32). Two new INR10 crore entrants are both organic.
Management expects IPM growth of about 9-11%, sustained since December 2025.
Semaglutide: management expects a INR1,500-1,800 crore market and targets a top-10 position, but says focus remains on engine brands.

qa_highlights.question: Is there scope for margin expansion if 20% growth continues, or will incremental growth be reinvested?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited favourable mix and operating leverage in Q1 but would not extrapolate. It said it aims to keep margins in a similar range and cited Southeast Asia and geopolitical cost risk.

qa_highlights.question: Did raw material inflation affect Q1, and will Q2 see more of it?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 was largely unaffected due to 70-90 days of inventory. Management sees a possible 100 bps hit and is trying to offset it with other cost reductions to keep the 20% PAT guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the acquired Bayer-Zydus molecule (Dr. Reddy's-sourced, per the analyst) seem to decline YoY, and what is the path to 25% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: External revenue was INR28-30 crore, plus INR20 crore internal. Management called Q1 the launch quarter and said supply-chain integration took priority; it is targeting INR20-40 crore over the coming years.

qa_highlights.question: Split of Q1 growth by volume, price and new launches, and IVF traction?
qa_highlights.answer: Split is in line with MAT: volume 6.3%, price 8.7%, new launches 3.4%. The IVF task force started in April 2026; management says it is too early to comment and will update in two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How big are the employee and other expense ratios vs peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost is high because about 1,000 MRs (35% of the 3,111 total) were added in three years and productivity per MR is lower; operating leverage should bring it down. Other expenses are mainly UCPMP-governed promotion costs, which are variable.

qa_highlights.question: Depreciation and amortisation impact from the Wokadine and Bayer acquisitions, and from the hormonal plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Wokadine (INR97 crore plus GST) and Bayer (INR7 crore) are amortised over 10 years. The hormonal plant is depreciated over 20 years (about INR6.5 crore a year).

risks_watch: Raw material and geopolitical (Southeast Asia) cost pressure could cut gross margin by about 100 bps in coming quarters.
Hormonal facility under-recoveries until asset turnover rises from below 1x in FY27 toward 2-3x.
International revenue was flat in Q1; export ramp depends on dossier approvals (FY28-29).
Wokadine and Bayer-Zydus brand ramp is early; management guides to 25% inorganic growth over 2-3 years.
Dependence on La Chandra for about 60-65% of API needs.
Next quarter: whether margin holds near 22% EBITDA and the India growth rate stays about twice the IPM.
key_quotes: At this stage, it would be premature to comment on the sustainability of current levels, although our endeavor is to maintain margins within a similar range.

While we are encouraged by this performance, we remain cautious about extrapolating the current margin profile into coming quarters given the evolving cost environment due to geopolitical Southeast Asia risk.
We continue to target 15% revenue growth and 20% PAT growth over the FY27.
So, first quarter can't be considered for the future coming quarters numbers perspective, but we are eyeing what we have committed of our 25% growth
544644|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the India growth story, volume and brand momentum, and the FY27 guidance, which was kept unchanged. Noticeably cautious on margins: management declined to extrapolate Q1 profitability, citing geopolitical and Southeast Asia cost volatility, and was evasive on the Bayer-Zydus molecule's YoY decline, attributing it to launch and supply-chain integration.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin rose ~190 bps to 22%, but management declined to extrapolate and flagged a possible 100 bps gross-margin hit from raw material as new stocks arrived in June 2026 after 70-90 days of inventory, with the aim to hold margins in a 'similar range'.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: The INR130 crore Europe-GMP hormonal facility was capitalised on 30 June 2026, but asset turnover is expected below 1x in FY27 (rising to 2-3x over about three years), so the capacity is in place but not yet a volume driver.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 volume growth was 6.3% vs IPM 1.3% on MAT June 2026 basis, and India revenue grew 22.7% vs IPM 11.6%, with management saying Q1 split is in line with MAT; volume is not as strong as price (8.7%).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure was disclosed and no new plant was guided; the hormonal facility was just commissioned and the company is still absorbing it with asset turnover below 1x in FY27.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance was held unchanged at 15% organic plus 1.5-2% inorganic and 20% PAT growth, and management did not signal a raise despite Q1 revenue growth of 21.9%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged a possible 100 bps margin hit from raw material and Southeast Asia/geopolitical costs, and is offsetting with cost cuts to keep 20% PAT growth; the Bayer-Zydus molecule's external revenue was INR28-30 crore and its path to INR20-40 crore is still early.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: FY28-29 for international; domestic hormonal launches ongoin
rows.why: Export dossiers are ready by Nov-Dec 2026 with 12-18 months for registration, targeting international launch in FY28-29; the hormonal plant serves the domestic market initially, and two new INR10 crore brands were added in Q1.

rows.label: Export registration and international launch
rows.why: Dossiers ready Nov-Dec 2026 followed by 12-18 months of registration; international revenue was flat in Q1 and is only ~3% of revenue, so near-term impact is minimal.

rows.label: Bayer-Zydus molecule ramp to INR20-40 crore
rows.why: External revenue was INR28-30 crore plus INR20 crore internal in Q1, and management called Q1 a launch quarter with supply-chain integration ongoing; target is INR20-40 crore over 2-3 years.

rows.label: Offsetting raw material cost with other cost cuts
rows.why: Management says it is offsetting a possible 100 bps margin hit through other cost reductions to keep 20% PAT growth, and it is working to reduce employee cost from about 1,000 added MRs (35% of 3,111).

tone.note: Management was confident on India growth (22.7% vs IPM 11.6%), brand momentum and unchanged FY27 guidance, but cautious on margins and declined to extrapolate Q1 profitability; analysts pressed on margin sustainability, the Bayer-Zydus molecule's YoY decline and raw material inflation.

544645|2026-03.headline: Park Medi World FY26 revenue rose 21% to INR1,679 crore and PAT 27% to INR274 crore, with gross debt cut to INR28 crore.
544645|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record year: revenue INR1,679 crore (+21% YoY), EBITDA INR444 crore (+20%, 26% margin) and PAT INR274 crore (+27%, 16% margin). Q4 FY26 revenue was INR460 crore (+30%), with operating EBITDA of INR127 crore (+44%, 28% margin) and PAT of INR77 crore (+47%). The bed network grew 610 beds to 3,610 at March 2026 (3,960 including Panchkula, commissioned 10 April 2026), and management reiterated a target of 5,460 beds by March 2028. Gross debt fell to INR28 crore from INR450 crore, and debtor days fell to 129 from 161.

financial_highlights.metric: Operating EBITDA excl. other income (Q4 FY26)

financial_highlights.change: +7% YoY for FY; Q4 vs INR28,423 in Q4 FY25

segments.name: IPD
segments.commentary: FY26 IPD volume was 95,525 (+18% YoY, highest ever); Q4 FY26 IPD was 25,329 (+29% YoY per the call).

segments.name: OPD
segments.commentary: FY26 OPD volume was about 7.78 lakh (+22% YoY); Q4 FY26 was about 1.88 lakh (+13% YoY). Total patients served about 8.7 lakh in FY26.

segments.name: High-end specialties
segments.commentary: About 56.9% of revenue came from high-end specialties in FY26, up 316 bps YoY. Oncology was about 6.5% of FY26 revenue versus 5% in FY25, and about 8% in Q4 FY26 versus 6% in Q4 FY25.

guidance_outlook: Bed capacity: 850 beds to be added in FY27 (350 Panchkula already commissioned, 200 Narela targeted for Q2 FY27, 300 Kanpur) and about 1,000 in FY28 (400 Gorakhpur, 200 Ambala oncology extension, 150 Mohali, 250 Rohtak Greenfield, which management said comes January 2028). Target 5,460 beds by March 2028 and, between FY28 and FY33, nearly 10,000 beds.

Capex: about INR55 crore planned in FY27 and about INR250 crore in FY28; management cited about INR500 crore total over the next two years. Capex per bed is about INR34 lakh through the 5,460-bed plan.

CGHS rate hike of about 12-15% is expected to add about 7-7.5% to revenue for nine months of FY27. Management's net impact estimate is 5-6% of total revenue. Actual flow-through likely visible after Q1 FY27.
Payor mix is expected to move from about 80:20 (government insurance vs cash/TPA) toward 75:25 and then 70:30 over 12-18 months. Management's end-FY26 target was about 65-70% government insurance.

Agra (commissioned February 2026) is adding about INR5 crore revenue per month, expected to contribute about INR90 crore revenue in FY27 and turn EBITDA positive. Bathinda (250 beds) is running at 65-70% occupancy.
Debtor days are expected to fall below 100 eventually, but management said this will take time; near-term target around four months of government collection cycle.
capex_capacity: Bed network: 3,000 beds at start of FY26, 3,610 at 31 March 2026, 3,960 with Panchkula (350 beds, commissioned 10 April 2026, capex about INR125 crore). Target 5,460 by March 2028.

Two FY26 additions: Bathinda 250 beds (acquired, Punjab) and Agra 360 beds (UP entry, commissioned February 2026). Narela, Delhi (200 beds, IBC acquisition): total capex about INR80 crore, of which INR55 crore spent. Kanpur (300 beds): about INR30 crore to invest.

Greenfield break-even takes 12-15 months and full recovery 2.5-3 years, per management. Acquired assets' EBITDA break-even is about 3-3.5 years on a weighted average basis; acquisition investment recovered through revenue in roughly 11 months.
Liquidity: FDs of about INR314 crore, about INR100 crore in bank, and INR135 crore non-current FDs at 31 March 2026. Management expects only a small debt raise if any.
demand_pricing: Management says ARPOB is kept in the affordable range and is one of several profitability drivers; expenses should be benchmarked to revenue, not ARPOB alone.
Demand described as strong across Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, with patients who previously travelled to metros now treated locally.

Collections are described as close to 100% by management. Government (central) accounts for 92% of debtors; government bills are cleared in about three months, and management is seeking to shorten this.
Disallowance on government revenue stayed at about 9% in Q4 FY26.
Oncology is being expanded across all 16 hospitals (medical and surgical), with radiation oncology in three hospitals.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 margin expansion, seasonality, CGHS or case mix?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said mainly higher occupancy at existing hospitals; Agra began operations in February 2026 and Bathinda in May (per CFO), so new units did not drive Q4 margins.

qa_highlights.question: Provision for receivables at FY26 end?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the provision made at 31 March 2026 is close to INR200 crore under Ind AS.

qa_highlights.question: Cost and break-even profile of Greenfield and acquired hospitals?
qa_highlights.answer: Greenfield EBITDA break-even in 12-15 months, with recovery over 2.5-3 years. Brownfield units such as Bathinda were said to turn PAT-positive within the first month. Acquisitions were said to recover investment via revenue in about 11 months.

qa_highlights.question: How much CGHS benefit flows into FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 7-7.5% uplift for nine months of FY27 and a net impact of 5-6% of revenue after mix, largely flowing to revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone revenue down QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Bathinda was operated under O&M by Park Medi World until it became a subsidiary on 5 January 2026; consolidated revenue is unaffected.

qa_highlights.question: Is capex or debt constraining growth beyond FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is not being curbed. Capex needs are funded internally, with debt possible for large acquisitions, and it targets about 10,000 beds between FY28 and FY33.

qa_highlights.question: Doctor attrition and incentives?

544657|2026-03.headline: FY26 total income rose 37.19% to INR256.92 crore, but EBITDA margin compressed to about 11% in H2 on forex and RCN prices; management guides 15-16%.
544657|2026-03.overview: Pajson Agro's first earnings call after its December listing covered FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026). H2 saw margin compression from a spike in raw cashew nut (RCN) prices, forex movement (rupee moved about 10.5% from April 2025 base) and shipping disruptions, with H2 total income up 37.38% to INR138.5 crore and H2 PAT up 8.97%. Capacity utilisation was 86% on an 18,000 MT Andhra Pradesh plant, and a greenfield 35,000 MT Vizianagaram facility (targeting 70,000 MT total by FY30) is being built with INR39.53 crore of POs committed by March 2026.

qa_highlights.answer: FY25 plant was shut for expansion and stock was sold off. FY26 focused on institutional customers, which carry more credit. Inventory about INR38 crore and debtors about INR18 crore; creditors rose to about INR20 crore from INR3 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of West Asia crisis and forex on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said shipments come directly from Africa to India, so no supply disruption. Forex (procurement side, since raw material is imported) drove the margin dip; hedging via banks is being initiated and shipping lines approached for longer-term contracts.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 23% PAT growth and what helped in Q1 despite geopolitics?

qa_highlights.question: Is staff cost going to moderate after Q1?

544664|2026-03.headline: KSH International Q4 FY26 revenue rose 101% YoY to INR 1,018 crore and EBITDA per ton reached about INR 74,000, with FY26 PAT at a record INR 110 crore.
544664|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was a strong quarter: revenue from operations of INR 1,018 crore (up 101% YoY), EBITDA of INR 56 crore (from INR 35 crore), and a record quarterly PAT of INR 34.5 crore (up 87%). Volumes were about 7,600 metric tons, up 29% YoY, though Middle East shipments of roughly 100-150 tons slipped from March into April. Management said FY26 EBITDA per ton was about INR 67,600 and guided sustainable EBITDA per ton to a 65,000-74,000 range, with the Supa Phase II expansion (to about 59,000 MT) on track for FY27. Working capital days remain high at 65-68, and management is negotiating bank terms to push payable days above 25-30.

segments.name: Standard winding wires
segments.commentary: Grew 58% in FY26 and 80% in Q4 YoY. Management is targeting EVs, AC compressors and motors. About 35% of the 43,445 MT installed capacity is standard.

Around 65% of current installed capacity is for specialized wires and the balance for standard wires.

demand_pricing: Repeat revenue above 95% in FY26 from more than 120 domestic and global OEM customers; the business is make-to-order with copper and FX passed through.

Middle East impact was limited: some Gulf shipments were delayed by a few weeks and rerouted. Management estimated 200-300 tons of volume effect in Q4 including orders not started.

India CTC demand estimated at 100,000-120,000 tons by 2030 versus about 40,000 tons in FY25 and 70,000-75,000 tons expected in FY27-28. Imports were about 1,000 tons a month earlier and are expected to decline.
New entrants could take 5-7 years to qualify for 765 kV/HVDC CTC, according to management.
Pricing is set via one-year or multi-year value-addition matrices agreed with OEMs, not linked to copper price.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said 65,000-70,000 per ton is sustainable long term, and later gave 67,000-74,000 as the range.

qa_highlights.answer: Payable days are targeted above 25 days, and inventory days rose because large transformer orders need full manufacture before dispatch.

qa_highlights.answer: Space exists for another 10,000 MT at Supa, with no decision yet. Management would not rule out adding capacity over 24 months.

qa_highlights.answer: No. The customer base is diversified and management said it can redirect volumes to other customers.

qa_highlights.answer: Management does not see a general trend toward backward integration, given available capacity and the process complexity.

544679|2026-03.headline: Amagi FY26 revenue rose 30% to INR 1,506 crores and turned PAT positive at INR 72 crores, swinging about INR 140 crores from a FY25 loss.
544679|2026-03.overview: Amagi reported its first full year as a listed company, with FY26 revenue of INR 1,506 crores (up 30% reported, 23% constant currency) and Q4 revenue of INR 397 crores (up 29%). Adjusted EBITDA rose to about INR 156 crores (10% margin) from INR 23 crores, and PAT was INR 72 crores versus a loss of INR 69 crores in FY25. Management stressed net revenue retention of 126% and growth across all three segments, while flagging Q4 gross margin compression tied to customer pricing, AI costs and parallel-running of lower-cost alternatives. NEWSPULSE, the first agentic AI product, has its first paying customer and is in trials with news networks.

segments.name: Streaming unification
segments.commentary: Largest segment at INR 838 crores, up 26% YoY, roughly more than half of revenue; serves OTT, FAST and CTV platforms.

segments.name: Monetization and marketplace
segments.commentary: INR 381 crores, up 36% YoY, about a quarter of revenue and the fastest-growing segment; monetized impressions grew about 62% YoY. Management does not yet report marketplace separately.

segments.name: Cloud modernization
segments.commentary: INR 286 crores, up 32% YoY, about a fifth of revenue; AccuWeather migration to Amagi Cloud completed end-to-end this quarter.

guidance_outlook: No prescriptive FY27 guidance; management aspires to keep growing at a healthy clip, citing the trajectory of the last three years.
Focus areas for FY27 are durable revenue growth, operating leverage and cash conversion.
Current margin levels are not steady state; management sees headroom and upside, and will make ahead-of-curve AI investments.

Gross margin: management said not to extrapolate quarterly moves to full year and expects volume growth to offset modest CPM/price compression; the gross margin impact of NEWSPULSE is too early to quantify.
Seasonality: Q1 is about 22% of full-year revenue and about 11% of adjusted EBITDA; H1 is about 45% of revenue and H2 about 55%, with EBITDA about 37% in H1 and 63% in H2.
Management said no hedging book is in place; it is considering hedging this year given the net USD revenue position.
capex_capacity: Cost-side plan: R&D is being redirected toward next-generation agentic products; R&D fell from 33% to 23% of revenue over FY24-FY26.
Cloud modernization is in early innings; serviceable addressable revenue grew about 11% to USD 1.9 billion this year.
Management is scanning for buy-or-build acquisitions in glass-to-glass gaps, with no deal size fixed and no specific target named.
demand_pricing: Dollar-based NRR is north of 120%, in a 120% to 125% range for several years; management says it is comfortable even after currency adjustment.
Monetized impression growth of about 62% YoY came with revenue growth of 36%, implying modest CPM pressure offset by volume.
Q4 gross margin fell sequentially on customer pricing (renegotiation), AI costs (minor) and double-running costs of lower-cost alternatives on mission-critical workflows.
NEWSPULSE targets traditional news networks; tens of POCs are running, and management said it is too early to share sales-cycle or unit-economics detail.
No competitor seen as credible at platform level; management says customers prefer one unified platform over many point solutions.
Partnerships: ADAMS (Latin America), Anoki (ad partner), Vodafone deal in Germany, with progress in Australia and the US.

qa_highlights.question: Split of NEWSPULSE paid customers between cross-sell to existing Amagi clients and new logos, and unit economics or gross margin of the agentic product.
qa_highlights.answer: Existing customers are the first port of call, but NEWSPULSE is also landing new logos; tens of POCs are running and detail will come in coming quarters. Gross margin impact is too early to quantify; outcome-based pricing mixed with fixed fees, and no major margin impact seen so far.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin compression QoQ: how much was client renegotiation versus AI and investment costs, and will it persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Three drivers: customer pricing, AI cost (minor), and double-running costs of lower-cost alternatives. Management says full-year gross margin has held at about 69% and sees volume growth offsetting modest price compression.

qa_highlights.question: Sales headcount efficiency and how many accounts one salesperson can handle over 3 to 5 years.
qa_highlights.answer: Account management is sublinear in scale given NRR of 126%; product-led growth and AI tooling should lift efficiency. No revenue-share model; commissions are sliding-scale by hunter or farmer role.

qa_highlights.question: Does accelerating monetized impression growth reflect market conditions, and how exposed is revenue to advertising macro?
qa_highlights.answer: Impression growth reflects the shift to streaming. Customers' ad economics flow through to Amagi pricing with a lag; no impact seen yet, though geopolitics is a risk.

qa_highlights.question: Customer count trend and new customer additions, which have slowed on a quarterly basis.
qa_highlights.answer: Customer count rose to 492 in FY26 from 463 and 396 earlier; Q4 added 27 and churned 30, mainly year-end cleanup of sub-USD 1,000 accounts. Growth is coming from the existing base and upmarket enterprise deals.

qa_highlights.question: Cash deployment and acquisition plans, and CC NRR.
qa_highlights.answer: Corp Dev is scanning buy-or-build options in glass-to-glass gaps, with no size set and no irrational valuations. Dollar-based NRR is above 120%.

qa_highlights.question: Path to higher PAT margin and whether 5% is steady state.
qa_highlights.answer: Management says current margins are not steady state and that there is headroom, but will keep making ahead-of-curve AI investments.
