544679|2026-06.headline: Amagi's July 7, 2026 "AI in Media" webinar was industry-level only; no quarterly financials, guidance or Amagi-specific metrics were disclosed.
544679|2026-06.overview: This transcript is of an educational investor webinar titled "AI in Media", hosted by Amagi on July 7, 2026 and filed under Regulation 30, not an earnings call. The moderator stated upfront that company financial performance, outlook and operational metrics would not be addressed. The CEO Baskar Subramanian framed AI as reshaping the video value chain across production, preparation (metadata, encoding, scheduling), distribution (agent-to-agent deals) and consumer discovery. He cited a claim that every $1 spent on technology brings $2 to $4 of human toil, and said most customers view AI as expansionary rather than a cost-saving tool today. No Q1 FY27 results, segment data or guidance were given.
guidance_outlook: No company guidance given; the moderator stated financial performance, business outlook and operational metrics would not be addressed.
Management described AI-driven production cost deflation as a multi-year shift, saying the next few years would bring a fundamental change, without quantifying it.
Management said outcome-based pricing is early and not yet visible in media, and that the core system is expected to stay as is while expansion revenue is driven by outcomes.
capex_capacity: Management said AI workloads are pushing customers from on-premise to cloud because they lack in-house GPUs and servers, and expects more progression in that direction; no Amagi capex or capacity figures were given.
Management said GPU costs are significant for video AI but did not quantify them; token cost is a small part of AI cost in video.
demand_pricing: Management says most customers are pursuing expansion (more channels, revenue opportunities) rather than AI cost savings today, citing Jevons' paradox.
Outcome-based pricing (per transaction, per result, per success) is being discussed in some markets, but management says it is not yet visible in media.

Management says token cost is a small part of AI cost in video; GPU costs are significant. It also cited an example of a scheduler's work falling from 8 hours to about 10 minutes of review under an agentic system.
Management described the metadata and preparation workload as a headcount constraint, with media companies creating about 6 hours of unique news daily and running content across 40-plus countries.

qa_highlights.question: What safeguards exist against hallucination and unpredictability given strict 99.9999% SLAs with clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the approach is to bring determinism to a non-deterministic problem through guardrails and engineered systems, noting that getting AI from demos to production is the hard part.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI improving prep-work speed and reducing pricing through deflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI mainly reduces human cost in preparation (e.g., speech-to-text making subtitling unnecessary) and expands what can be done rather than directly reducing price.

qa_highlights.question: Can AI move production and pre-production workflows to the cloud?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI workloads are pushing customers from on-premise to cloud because they lack in-house GPU and server capacity, and expects more of this shift.

qa_highlights.question: Are there real-life examples of cost reduction or higher OTT/cable content from AI?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said adoption is early, with some creators using AI for VFX and background creation, and microdrama as the most active area.

qa_highlights.question: Is there evidence of cost savings, given higher token costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said token cost is small relative to video GPU and human costs, and most customers are using AI for expansion, with cost savings secondary.

qa_highlights.question: Do agent-to-agent communications create network effects and first-mover advantage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said connecting two or more ecosystem parties through agentic infrastructure has high network-effect value, but the space is very early and standards are still forming.

qa_highlights.question: Does AI deepen client engagement and threaten horizontal SaaS or hyperscalers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued that vertical, mission-critical media software has a moat in enterprise context, which it sees as more durable than generic reasoning models.

qa_highlights.question: Will agentic AI materially cut customer operating costs and create pricing pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said per-job costs may deflate, but the volume of work customers want to do is expanding, which it characterised as a Jevons' paradox effect.

qa_highlights.question: How will vendor-client commercial models change as agentic AI spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said outcome-driven pricing is being explored in other industries, but it is early and not yet prominent in media.

risks_watch: Hallucination and unpredictability of agentic AI against strict uptime SLAs, which management said it addresses with guardrails but gave no metrics for.
Rising GPU and infrastructure costs for video AI, which management said are material but did not quantify.
Possible shift in vendor pricing toward outcome-based models, which would change revenue recognition, though management said it is not yet visible.
The webinar did not address Amagi's own Q1 FY27 numbers, so the company's operating and financial trajectory remains unassessed; the company directed investors to ir@amagi.com for follow-up.

544681|2026-03.headline: INDO SMC guided FY27 revenue to INR450-500 crores on an INR237 crore order book plus INR125 crore fresh orders, with margins targeted at 15%+.
544681|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the first full year after listing, with management saying revenue roughly doubled and PAT more than doubled, driven by higher-value CT/PT, bus duct, meter cubicle and panel products. Management attributed a softer March-quarter SMC and FRP output to geopolitics-driven resin and petroleum-product price swings and supply gaps. The company shifted to shorter (2-3 month) orders with price-escalation clauses (5% trigger) and said it is now choosing orders on margin. Inventory rose to about INR85 crores (around 100 days) because of pre-stocked raw materials, and the working capital cycle was cut from 83 to about 40 days. Management did not give a precise FY26 revenue or margin figure in the call; the 15% EBITDA margin cited by analysts was not confirmed by management.

segments.commentary: About INR120-125 crores of the order book; management said CT/PT is more engineering-intensive with margins above SMC/FRP, targeting above 18% EBITDA on standardised products. Currently operating at 11 kV and 33 kV, with 66 kV and above still in planning.

segments.name: Bus ducts, meter cubicles and panels
segments.commentary: Meter cubicle orders of INR10-15 crores were added, with new meter cubicle orders of INR10 crores-plus taken in the current period. Management described these as higher-margin lines bundled with SMC and CT/PT.

segments.name: SMC
segments.commentary: About INR80 crores of order book being executed month to month. Management said FY26 SMC and FRP output fell in March due to resin and petroleum-product shortages; the call did not give segment revenue figures.

segments.commentary: Remainder of the order book, executed against monthly clearances. Plan to add about 300 tons of FRP production capacity.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Early-stage: Oman and Gulf orders, samples sent to US and Germany, Dubai electrical fair planned from September. Management said UL 94 certification is a requirement for the US and that certification takes 1-2 months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR450-500 crores, subject to geopolitics and material availability; management said it can be met with existing capacity plus automation machinery.
H1 FY27 inflow target of INR200 crores-plus, lowered from an earlier INR250 crores-plus; management said H2 is expected to be stronger than H1.
EBITDA margin target of 15% or above; management said it expects to maintain FY26 margins in FY27 and aims for 1-2% better if conditions allow.
Medium-term aim of INR1,000 crores-plus revenue in about three years, with railways a major contributor from FY28 onward.
Railway clearance expected by end of the following month after the call, pending lab expansion; management said trial orders would grow over the next three years.
capex_capacity: Capex of INR25 crores (as disclosed in the IPO) is the first priority, covering machines and facilities across SMC, FRP and electrical engineering.
A 2,000-ton-plus SMC press is expected in 2-3 months, to enable larger railway products and big boxes; SMC capacity target is 6,000 tons-plus.
Nashik (Maharashtra) plant needs capex and more space; a second plant at Nashik has started production readiness. Ahmedabad is running well on utilisation.
Management said revenue above INR750 crores could come from the full capex once complete, and the company has land available so no major new building is needed.
Plans for 33 kV CTs and meter cubicles; a lab expansion funded from the IPO is expected to be completed by the end of the month after the call.
demand_pricing: Management said the utilities and electrical industry (SMC, FRP, CT/PT, LTCT, bus ducts, switchgear) is growing fast; it cited about 20 states served and a push to expand pan-India and export.
Pricing: management said recent orders are priced around INR450 per unit versus INR350-360 earlier, and that buyers are accepting the higher prices.
Competition in higher-kV CT/PT is limited: management said few players hold approvals, and cited ABB Crompton as operating at 66, 120 and 240 kV.

Raw materials: resin (SMC/FRP) and petroleum-linked inputs were the main pressure; glass fiber held in about 3 months' stock; copper and steel costs passed through at order time. Management said it took a hit on resin in March.
Order inflow pace: management cited INR3-4 crores in new orders on the day of the call and said small orders are taken to limit price-risk exposure.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said SMC and FRP fell from March due to geopolitics-driven resin and petroleum shortages and rate swings. Order book: about INR125 crores in CT/PT and LTCT, about INR80 crores in SMC, and the rest in FRP and tarpaulin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export plan?

qa_highlights.question: Will the company reach INR1,000 crores revenue, and when?

544684|2026-03.headline: Digilogic FY26 revenue rose 8.4% to INR78.27 crore and PAT 33.8% to INR10.43 crore, but a ~INR22 crore spillover from delayed imported hardware missed the 20-25% growth guidance.
544684|2026-03.overview: FY26 total income rose 8.4% YoY to INR78.27 crore, with EBITDA up 16.5% to INR15.18 crore and margin expanding 152 bps to 19.6%. PAT grew 33.8% to INR10.43 crore, and operating cash flow turned positive at INR12.63 crore. Management attributed the shortfall versus its January 2026 growth guidance to delayed imported OEM hardware, which pushed about INR22 crore of orders into FY27. Management guided to 20-25% growth for FY27, contingent on converting INR100-plus crore of orders by September 2026, and announced new subsidiary Abhedhya (RF systems), an SBC R&D effort, and Project UDAN manufacturing expansion.

segments.name: Measurement equipment
segments.commentary: About 49% of FY26 revenue; management said most of its value comes from software content with little material cost, supporting the margin gain.

segments.name: Checkout systems
segments.commentary: About 22% of FY26 revenue; ATEs about 17%. Management said ATE and checkout value was broadly flat YoY, and the share fell because measurement equipment grew.

segments.name: Prototyping vs production
segments.commentary: Management estimated roughly 30% of revenue from prototyping and 70% from production orders. This was not reconciled with a reported figure and was described as approximate.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-25%, reiterated on the call; management said it is confident of meeting it.
Management targets INR100-plus crore of purchase orders by end-September 2026, with billing for FY27 expected to be supported by that order intake.
Order book was about INR30-plus crore as of 30 May 2026, with most expected to bill by August 2026.

Project UDAN (new manufacturing facility, about four times the current capacity) expected operational by mid-2028; indicative revenue INR11-13 crore in FY29, INR28-30 crore in FY30, INR57-61 crore in FY31.
Current setup capacity estimated at INR150-160 crore revenue potential.
Abhedhya (RF subsidiary) expected to demonstrate systems in 8-12 months; management indicated revenue in FY28, not FY27.
capex_capacity: Project UDAN: a manufacturing and environmental testing facility, about four times current size; mid-2028 target; can deliver 20-25 systems per six months versus about six currently.
Guest house under construction; capitalised finance cost on exposure of about INR2.1 crore (not fully drawn), borrowing at REPO plus 2.5%.
Abhedhya, a new RF subsidiary for radar, EW and communication subsystems, with a 1-year build-and-demonstrate timeline.
R&D: custom single board computer (SBC) built in-house by an eight-member team, about 1.5-2 years old; qualification range -20 to +85 degrees C; environmental testing not yet completed.
Management said two to three new R&D products are in development.
demand_pricing: FY26 execution was held back by imported hardware from US/European OEMs; lead time rose from about 2 months to about 4 months, leaving roughly INR22 crore spilled into April 2026. Management said about INR20 crore additional revenue would otherwise have closed in FY26.

Order book fell to about INR31 crore from INR46 crore; the tender pipeline fell to about INR110 crore from INR200 crore. Management attributed this to Government fund reallocation and said projects are delayed 6-8 months rather than lost.
Management said OEMs are rerouting shipments, adding a week or 10 days and roughly 1-2% cost.
Competitors named: Data Patterns and Zen Technologies, mainly in prototyping. Management said production work under DCPP is nomination-based with limited competition.
Customer base is 100% government in substance (DRDO, BDL, BEL, public sector defence production agencies), with some transactions billed through BDL.
Management said the export route is via DRDO and BDL systems, and MoUs with Sperry and Eirad are at the evaluation stage toward Tier-1 aerospace supply chains.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 guidance of 20-25% growth missed, and what supports FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Imported hardware arrived about 4 months after order rather than 2, leaving roughly INR22 crore of spillover. Management cited INR30-plus crore of orders in hand by 30 May and a target of INR100-plus crore of POs by September.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book fall from INR46 crore to INR31 crore and the pipeline from INR200 crore to INR110 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said government fund reallocation changed priorities and projects are delayed 6-8 months rather than cancelled. The INR100-plus crore target covers only projects with budgets allocated or tenders out.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the revenue comes from production versus prototyping?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said roughly 30% prototyping and 70% production, and deferred exact figures to the CFO. No reported split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why set up Abhedhya as a separate company rather than a division?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RF work needs different people, salaries, infrastructure and design expertise than TMS, and separate accountability is needed. Tender qualification is to be built by demonstrating products first.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the ATE and checkout share fall from about 44% to 22%?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said measurement equipment, mostly software value add with low material cost, grew to a similar scale, and ATE and checkout value was broadly unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the order book converting to revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Current orders should bill by about August 2026. Pipeline orders are expected as POs by end-September, with 2-3 months of build and about one month of installation, and cash collection around Aug-Oct.

Project UDAN and Abhedhya are not yet operational; Abhedhya revenue is expected only in FY28, and the SBC still needs environmental qualification.
Governance: management's FY26 growth guidance was missed, and the call shows the company's first results call as a newly listed SME.
544684|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY27 targets and on the causes of the FY26 miss, which management attributes to imported-hardware delays. Less specific on the revenue split, timelines for UDAN and Abhedhya, and the exact reasons for the pipeline fall. Several answers were deferred to the CFO or to a future call.
key_quotes: So, my target is by September, by September I should have purchase orders in hand close to INR100-plus crores, with which our billing will be comfortably meeting the targets which have been projected.

Imagine a scenario, everything would have gone in the right direction without this international disturbances had these items come on time, I would have comfortably closed additionally INR20 crores apart from INR76 crores what we have closed.
Only thing is that might get delayed by few months, maybe 6 to 8 months, which might spill over to subsequent financial year. But opportunities are not lost.

rows.why: Project UDAN and guest house are already committed, but no new capex has been announced beyond them and utilisation was not disclosed, so further capex depends on order conversion.

rows.why: FY26 growth of 8.4% missed the 20-25% guidance, and the order book fell to INR31 crore from INR46 crore, so there is no basis for an upgrade yet.

rows.why: The FY27 target depends on converting INR100-plus crore of POs by September 2026 from an INR30-plus crore order book, and the tender pipeline fell to INR110 crore from INR200 crore with 6-8 month delays; FY26 already missed guidance by spilling about INR22 crore.

rows.why: Abhedhya RF subsidiary expected to demonstrate systems in 8-12 months with revenue in FY28 not FY27, the SBC still lacks environmental testing, and management says 2-3 new R&D products are in development.

rows.label: Order conversion to billing by Aug 2026
rows.why: Order book of about INR30-plus crore as of 30 May 2026 with most expected to bill by August 2026, the first test of FY27 growth.

rows.why: MoUs with Sperry and Eirad are at evaluation stage toward Tier-1 aerospace supply chains, with no revenue figure given.

rows.why: Receivables are INR42.87 crore with INR2.31 crore older than 180 days, and pipeline cash collection is expected around Aug-Oct, against a working capital cycle of 3.46 times up from 1.6 times.

544684|2026-09.headline: Digilogic H1 FY27 revenue rose 91% to INR34.96 crores and PAT rose 151% to INR4.76 crores, with management reiterating 25-30% FY27 top-line growth.
544684|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 revenue grew 91% to INR34.96 crores from INR18 crores, EBITDA rose 126% to INR7.81 crores, and PAT grew 151% to INR4.76 crores. Management said H2 is seasonally much stronger in defense, citing FY26 revenue of INR78 crores split as H1 INR19 crores and H2 INR59 crores. Order book of INR20 crores is to be billed by mid-February 2027, with a further INR54 crores in pipeline at various tender stages. Management also reiterated 25-30% top-line and 30-35% EBITDA/PAT growth guidance for FY27, though analysts noted that the EBITDA guidance was lowered from 45-50% and that H1 margin gains were partly driven by FD interest income.

financial_highlights.value: INR78 crores (H1 INR19 crores, H2 INR59 crores)

segments.name: Test, measurement and simulation systems (TMS)
segments.commentary: Core business, described as the heart of operations; 36 projects executed in H1 FY27 valued at around INR33.18 crores. Customers include PSUs and DRDO agencies. Management expects TMS to keep growing at 20-30% a year.

segments.name: Abhedya Systems (wholly owned subsidiary, R&D)
segments.commentary: New experts hired for R&D; commercial production expected in H2 FY29 if plans hold. Management did not disclose financials.

segments.name: Project Udaan (new facility, build-to-print and build-to-spec)
segments.commentary: Civil construction is ongoing, with first-floor roof concrete complete; completion targeted by March 2027 and operations by end-2027. Management expects certification around Q1 2028 and commercialisation in about two years, with contribution starting FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth guidance of 25-30%, which management said it expects to meet; CFO said the company expects to touch its guidance number.
EBITDA and PAT growth guidance of 30-35%. The CFO said the 40-45% figure in the earlier outlook included FD interest income, and core growth stays at 30-35%.
Management said the current margins are sustainable, with no guidance to expand or contract.
Order book of INR20 crores and pipeline of INR54 crores targeted for billing by mid-February 2027.
Project Udaan: civil construction completion by March 2027, internal testing by December 2027, inspection and certification in Q1 2028, and about three months to get the certificate.
High Precision GIMBAL System and custom single-board computer products expected to be marketable around mid-2027, adding an estimated INR3-4 crores a year initially, with break-even thereafter.
Ongoing internal SOP and technology upgrade expected to finish between December 2026 and March 2027.
capex_capacity: Project Udaan is a new facility whose civil construction is in progress. Management expects operations from end-2027 and certification around Q1 2028.
Abhedya Systems (wholly owned subsidiary) is expected to start commercial production in H2 FY29.
Management said the Udaan facility will cover both build-to-spec (in-house design) and build-to-print (production of designs supplied by clients), with build-to-print expected to contribute first.
Inventory rose in H1 because of work-in-progress and pre-ordered long-lead items for orders due by mid-February 2027. Management said this stock will be consumed by March.
demand_pricing: Management said the order book is INR20 crores and the pipeline INR54 crores, with about 60% of the pipeline being repeat orders. Total of around INR74 crores is described as converted from the INR110 crores tender pipeline cited in May 2026.
All INR22 crores of order spillover from the prior period was billed in H1 FY27, according to management.
Management said it could not share the split of the INR54 crores between technical evaluation, commercial negotiation and pending purchase orders. Government procurement timelines vary.
Competitive moat: management said customised boards, signal processing and software go through R&QA certification by government agencies, which it says takes 2-3 years to replicate.
Analysts asked for a segment split. The CFO said the H1 segment data was not readily available and would be shared later.
The company said it has no export sales; all revenue is domestic.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the EBITDA guidance reduced from 45-50% to 30-35%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said core growth is 30-35%; the earlier 40-45% figure included FD interest income. He said the core growth guidance is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Was the INR22 crore spillover from the last call completed in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: MD said all spillover orders were billed in H1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H1 margin improvement driven by, including software value-add?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the margin gains are driven by FD interest income, with fixed costs steady. He said the gains are across the board and not from software or revenue mix, and that segment-level analysis had not been done for the limited review.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 revenue reach the guidance (INR100 crore-plus implied H2 of about INR65 crores)?
qa_highlights.answer: MD said the 25-30% target is supported by the INR20 crore order book and the INR54 crore pipeline; he called anything above it a bonus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and role of the new Udaan facility, and what does it add to revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: MD said Udaan will start contributing in FY28 and that TMS will continue to grow alongside it. Management declined to quantify the Udaan revenue contribution.

qa_highlights.question: How do defense program delays (QRSAM, P-75I, NGC) affect the order intake?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said Digilogic is part of about 10 programmes, of which 3-4 have moved into production, so TMS has not been impacted by the delays.

H2 must deliver about INR65 crores of revenue to reach FY27 guidance (implied by analyst math), which is heavily dependent on billing by mid-February 2027.
Project Udaan has schedule risk: civil completion by March 2027, certification in Q1 2028, then about 3 months for certification. Management did not quantify Udaan revenue.

Government procurement delays; sales cycles depend on tender stages and purchase orders.
Segment revenue split and export data were requested but not provided on the call; the company said it would follow up.

544685|2026-03.headline: Shadowfax Q4 FY26 revenue about INR 1,237 crores (+74% YoY) with record 4.5% PAT margin; FY26 PAT INR 112 crores.
544685|2026-03.overview: Management reported record Q4 FY26 growth and profitability: revenue about INR 1,237 crores (+74% YoY, +6.7% QoQ), adjusted EBITDA about INR 58 crores (4.7% margin vs 4.3% in Q3 and 0.7% a year ago) and PAT INR 56 crores (4.5% margin). For FY26, revenue exceeded INR 4,200 crores (+69%), adjusted EBITDA was about INR 159 crores (roughly 3x FY25) and PAT was INR 112 crores vs INR 6 crores. Management guided to 27-30% overall growth, 100-120 bps adjusted EBITDA margin improvement through FY28, and FY27 capex of INR 180-190 crores, while investing in real estate, dark stores and large-shipment coverage.

financial_highlights.change: vs 4.3% in Q3 FY26 and 0.7% in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Express parcel
segments.commentary: About 75% of revenue; management says it is gaining share via new client wins, deeper engagement and value-added services such as same-day, next-day and reverse logistics. Top 2-3 customer concentration unchanged QoQ.

segments.name: Hyperlocal
segments.commentary: Grew more than 50% YoY and 16% QoQ in Q4; quick commerce volumes picked up and operations with Amazon Now commenced. Management guides 45-50% growth for this segment in the next year.

segments.name: Other logistics services
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR 80 crores of the INR 1,200-plus crores quarterly revenue; wind-down of experimental services is largely complete as of Q4 FY26, with reshaping towards critical logistics.

guidance_outlook: Overall business growth guidance maintained at 27-30%; hyperlocal expected at 45-50% YoY.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expansion of 100-120 bps over the next couple of years through FY28; 200-250 bps per year after FY28 until steady-state EBITDA.
Steady-state adjusted EBITDA margin viewed as sustainable at early double digits.
FY27 capex guided at INR 180-190 crores, flat in absolute terms vs FY26; dark stores to be less than 10% of capex.
Pin code coverage to rise from 15,600 (of 19,300) to about 17,000 by end FY27 and full country coverage by FY28; large-shipment pin codes from about 6,000 to 10,000 in FY27.
Plans to set up about 100 dark stores in FY27 for vertical quick commerce (about 15 today).
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guided at INR 180-190 crores, flat in absolute terms vs FY26; dark stores less than 10% of capex.
Real estate footprint up 35% between September 2025 and March 2026 (leased last-mile and middle-mile sortation centres).
Touch points rose from 4,200 to 4,700 in about six months; opening about 120-150 pin codes per month.
OneNCR, one of the largest sorting centres, went live a few months back after about six months of dual costs; new last-mile hubs take six to eight months to reach efficiency.
Over the last three years more than 60% of capex went to sorting centres and about 85% to sorting centres plus last-mile hubs; strategy is to run a dual manual/automated setup.
demand_pricing: 3PL market share estimated at about 28-29% for Q4, up from about 17-18% a year earlier; growth split roughly 50-55% market growth and 40-45% share gains.

Quick commerce: management says it maintains pricing as largest 3PL in the segment; works with six to seven QC platforms.

qa_highlights.question: Where is market share gain coming from, and will it stabilise by FY28?

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY26 margin expansion look better as capex normalises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said significant operating leverage is yet to come, with opex from investments returning in FY27-FY28, and that H2 capex was made in advance for FY27 capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Dark store unit economics and ROIC?
qa_highlights.answer: Top dark stores run at about 20%+ gross margin; breakeven in three to four months; average revenue INR 8-15 lakh per store per month; ROIC too early to quantify with 15 pilot stores.

qa_highlights.question: Margin guidance basis and service EBITDA?

qa_highlights.question: Lost shipment cost and white goods impact?
qa_highlights.answer: About half of the roughly 6% is quality-check debits from reverse logistics and half pure losses; management cited image-recognition upgrades and fixes in large-parcel damages in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Amazon Shipping and competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said captive arms deprioritise external customers at peak, so they do not see such models working in India; D2C/SME is a meaningful double-digit share of revenue, not disclosed exactly.

risks_watch: Geopolitical and crude price volatility; fuel is under 10% of costs and contracts carry fuel surcharges, but customer demand for logistics could slow if fuel rises sharply.
Lost shipments and QC debits at about 6.1% of revenue, well above the 4-5% long-term goal; white goods expansion could add to losses.
Dual-cost drag from new sorting centres and last-mile hubs (six to eight months ramp) could weigh on near-term margins.
Hyperlocal YoY growth slowed in Q4 due to a strong prior-year Q4 base; competition in quick commerce crowdsourcing from platforms like LoadShare.
Dark store ROIC not yet proven at scale; 100-store target in FY27 is a new vertical.
Lower average shipment volume (volumetric weight) reduced realisation QoQ, per analyst question on yield dip.

EBITDA margin widened to 39.49% from 36.55%, driven by the rental mix and utilisation. Management said MS scaffolding capacity has reached about 6,285 tonnes via temporary rented-premise facilities, ahead of IPO timelines, and entered aluminium formwork. Guidance calls for ~50% CAGR, with the mix shifting toward lower-margin sales, rising capex (~Rs 130 crore) and rising debt.

rows.why: Four of nine aluminium machines already running with five pending and installation by Sept 2026; capacity is at about 40% of target peak, and the Mathura 90 kg augmentation is under construction with civil works started.

544698|2026-03.headline: H2 FY26 total income rose 28% YoY to INR12,656.59 lakh and net profit rose 158% to INR432.20 lakh; FY26 PAT was INR750.29 lakh.
544698|2026-03.overview: PAN HR Solution's first earnings call, held 12 June 2026 after its February 2026 BSE SME listing, covered H2 and full-year FY26 results. Management reported H2 total income of INR12,656.59 lakh (+28% YoY) and H2 net profit of INR432.20 lakh (+158% YoY), against a prior-year H2 that was smaller. Full-year PAT of INR750.29 lakh looked moderate because FY25 included a one-time INR6.5 crore prior-period income. The company ended FY26 with net worth of INR3,751 lakh, cash of INR2,434 lakh and no debt, and set out a plan to reach INR1,000 crore revenue by FY29.

financial_highlights.change: Full-year YoY comparison not stated; FY25 base included INR6.5 crore one-time exceptional prior-period income

segments.name: Manpower outsourcing / workforce deployment
segments.commentary: Deployed workforce grew from about 10,000 at IPO to over 11,000 on payroll as of the call. Clients are concentrated in e-commerce, quick commerce, logistics, warehousing and manufacturing; management cited more than 17 clients.

segments.name: Emerging services (3PL, payroll, compliance, HR outsourcing, white-collar hiring)
segments.commentary: Management said these are new or being scaled: 3PL and B2B models were not previously done, and white-collar one-time staffing has started. No revenue figures were given for these lines.

guidance_outlook: Target to grow FY27 turnover by approximately 40%.
Target revenue of INR1,000 crore by FY29 (within three years), with the 3PL model named as the first growth lever.
Priorities for FY27: deploy IPO proceeds into working capital, move toward pay-and-collect contracts, expand into new geographies and sectors, and grow payroll, compliance and HR services.
Management expects a higher-margin mix over time, but said some contracts carry lower margins while creating operating leverage.
capex_capacity: Workforce deployment rose from about 10,000 at IPO to more than 11,000 on payroll; the company said it now operates in the South and West as well as North and East.
Management said internal infrastructure is underused and that new services can run on existing infrastructure without major new investment.
IPO proceeds are to go mainly to working capital expansion, and acquisitions are under consideration; no specific acquisition target or deal size was named.
demand_pricing: Revenue in FY26 was affected by contract repricing and billing-cycle changes, as stated by management.

Management said it had turned away pay-and-collect clients in the prior year because of fund constraints and can now pursue them; pay-and-collect has started at one or two locations with existing clients.
Competitive positioning rests on compliance credibility (operating since 2015), balance-sheet strength, and an integrated single-window model covering salary, compliance and workforce management.
Management did not quantify pricing or margin changes.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors read moderate full-year growth versus strong H2 numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 shows strong growth; the full-year PAT gap reflects a FY25 base that included INR6.5 crore one-time prior-period income. It attributed the revenue slowdown to not taking pay-and-collect clients in FY25 for lack of funds.

qa_highlights.question: How will the IPO capital be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: First priority is business expansion and working capital; the company is also watching acquisition opportunities. No amount or timeline was given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the acquisition targets and why acquire?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets are workforce management, staffing and payroll companies with strong client bases; the rationale is to gain client databases and avoid duplicating infrastructure. No named targets or valuation were disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the INR1,000 crore FY29 revenue goal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the 3PL business with existing clients (not previously pursued due to funds), new areas, stronger existing-client relationships and acquisitions, targeting completion within three years.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins come under pressure with growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some contracts carry lower margins but generate operating leverage; the focus is on profitable growth and improving return ratios.

qa_highlights.question: What are the return-ratio expectations (ROE, ROCE)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said return ratios are a priority; temporary dips are possible while capital is deployed for growth. No ROE or ROCE figures were given.

risks_watch: Full-year PAT comparison is distorted by the FY25 one-time INR6.5 crore income; the underlying base needs confirming.
Revenue was hit by contract repricing and billing-cycle changes in FY26; watch whether these persist in FY27.

The 40% FY27 turnover target and INR1,000 crore FY29 goal depend on working-capital deployment, pay-and-collect contracts (which raise working-capital needs) and acquisitions with no named targets yet.
Margin dilution from lower-margin contracts and the new 3PL, white-collar and pay-and-collect mix.
Client concentration: management cited more than 17 clients, which is a small base for the stated scale-up.
The company said it has no debt, but no quarterly or segment breakdown was given.
544698|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and the balance sheet, but vague on specifics: acquisition targets, segment revenue, margins and return ratios were given only in general terms. Answers on the FY26 full-year profit gap were more defensive, and several answers repeated the strategy without numbers.
key_quotes: Our H2 revenue for FY 2025 increased from INR98.85 crores to INR126.57 crores this year, which shows a 28% year-on-year growth.
Investors should look at financial year 2026 as a stronger and clearer reflection of the company's actual business performance and earnings quality.

Today we are a debt-free company, we don't have any liability, nor was there any before, and even now we don't have any liability.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.why: 3PL and B2B models were not done before and white-collar one-time staffing has started; pay-and-collect has begun at one or two locations, and 3PL is named as the first growth lever for the INR1,000 crore FY29 goal, though no revenue was given for these lines.

rows.why: IPO proceeds are partly earmarked for acquisitions and management is watching targets with strong client bases, but no named target, valuation or deal size was disclosed.

rows.label: Virtually debt-free with INR2,434 lakh cash at FY26 end
rows.why: Net worth was INR3,751 lakh with cash of INR2,434 lakh and no debt, which gives funding room for working capital and acquisitions without borrowing.

tone.note: Management was confident on H2 growth, the balance sheet and the INR1,000 crore FY29 goal, but gave no numbers on acquisitions, segment revenue, margins or return ratios; questions on the FY26 full-year profit gap and the margin trade-off got more defensive answers.

544699|2026-03.headline: Aye Finance Q4 FY26 profit rose 100% QoQ to INR86 crore, with credit cost down to 4.3% and FY27 guidance of 25-30% AUM growth.
544699|2026-03.overview: Aye Finance closed FY26 with AUM of INR7,044 crore (up 27% YoY, 6% QoQ) and Q4 disbursements of INR1,655 crore (up 26% QoQ). Q4 profit was INR86 crore, up 110% YoY and 100% QoQ, with FY26 profit up 13% to INR194 crore. Asset quality improved for a fifth straight quarter, with credit cost at 4.3%, PAR X at 6.9% and GNPA at 4.77%. Management guided FY27 to 25-30% AUM growth, 3.5-4% credit cost, 8.25-8.75% opex ratio and 4-4.5% ROA, with borrowing costs expected to fall 25-35 bps.

segments.name: Mortgage loans
segments.commentary: Mortgage is 23% of portfolio vs 12% in FY24; PAR 90 at about 2.7% (up vs December quarter), PAR X at about 4.1%, with a target PAR 90 of 2-2.5%. Book is about INR1,500-1,600 crore per management, versus INR1,300-1,400 crore in an analyst's figure.

segments.name: Hypothecation loans
segments.commentary: Secured hypothecation is about 40-47% of book (figures differed in the call) and unsecured hypothecation about 37%. Unsecured HL is said to behave like the secured book; management sees yields stable.

segments.name: CGFMU-covered book
segments.commentary: Roughly INR500 crore of hypothecation book is covered under CGFMU as of March 2026; the company has not used CGTMSE.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth guided at 25-30%; opex growth of about 15% is expected to support this.
FY27 credit cost guided at 3.5-4%, with Q4 FY27 expected at 3-3.25%; three-year asset quality target 3.25-3.75%.
Opex ratio to fall to 8.25-8.75% in FY27 from 9.6% in FY26; three-year opex guidance about 7-7.5% per analyst's reading.
ROA target of 4-4.5% with leverage of 4-4.5x (total assets to borrowings) and ROE in the high teens; management says this is reachable within FY27.

Borrowing cost expected to fall 25-35 bps from the FY26 level (management later clarified from the Q4 blended 10.87%), driven by replacing high-cost debt, a possible rating upgrade from A stable and partly offset by rising rates.
PAR X to fall to 5.5-6% over FY27 (about 100-150 bps), with about 30 bps in H1. Profit split expected at 35-40% in H1 and 60-65% in H2.
capex_capacity: Presence in 18 states and 3 union territories with 571 branches, 6.40 lakh+ active borrowers, and 70+ business clusters; branches are mainly Tier 2 and Tier 3 towns.
FY26 staffing rose 17-18%; mortgage manpower rose about 30% and collections team about 70%. FY27 manpower growth is expected to normalise to about 10%, mostly in branch sales and collections.
Collections capacity is to be redeployed to clean up NPA and write-off portfolio.
Management plans at least one new product launch in FY27 (gold loan, solar-based business lending or others), with market research due by end of Q1.
Mortgage share targeted at 30-35% of the portfolio over the next two to three years.
demand_pricing: Management says the micro-MSME segment is recovering, with rural consumption and formalisation supporting working-capital demand; April collections are not materially different from Q4 and April disbursements are seasonally lower.
Yield on hypothecation loans is stable; the blended yield falls as mortgage share rises, offset by lower cost of borrowing.
Management says it is not seeing a West Asia impact in March data, and the customer base is not linked to organised supply chains.
Collection efficiency: non-OD CE improved from 99.1% in Oct-25 to 99.5% in Mar-26; Bucket 1 CE rose from 51.8% to 62.5%. Stage 2 (30+60 DPD) is 1.12% of the portfolio.
Competition was not discussed in depth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the product mix changing, and what is the target secured/unsecured split?
qa_highlights.answer: Mortgage is 23% of book, target 30-35% in 2-3 years. Balance is hypothecation, with about 40% secured and about 30% unsecured. Management says 96% of customers own residential or commercial property.

qa_highlights.question: Why is NIM flat in FY27 guidance despite the equity raise and lower cost of funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says mortgage mix lowers yield, offset by replacing old debt at 10.13% incremental cost, worth 30-35 bps. Q3 NIM was 14.2% and Q4 16.4%, mostly from lower borrowing costs and less borrowing after the IPO. NIM is guided to stay level.

qa_highlights.question: Why has credit cost fallen only gradually despite collection efficiency recovering?
qa_highlights.answer: The NPA pool still bulges from early crisis slippages; more than 70% is provided in the hypothecation NPA book. Credit cost should decline from Q2-Q3 FY27, reaching 3-3.25% by Q4 FY27. Stage 3 PCR is to stay above 60%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in non-interest income in Q4 and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: The rise came from fair value gains on mutual funds and a cross-currency swap impact. The net effect is about INR10-11 crore. The company plans to move these fair value items to OCI from April 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What are the mortgage PAR 90 and sustainable GNPA levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Mortgage PAR 90 is about 2.7%, up from December, with PAR X at 4.1%. Target PAR 90 is 2-2.5% and credit cost below 2% on the mortgage book.

qa_highlights.question: What is the borrowing maturity profile?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR2,400 crore of borrowings fall due in the next 12 months, at an average cost of about 10.95%, which management describes as relatively expensive debt.

risks_watch: Credit cost path depends on collection efficiency holding and on resolution of the NPA pool; FY27 credit cost guidance of 3.5-4% depends on this.
Rising market interest rates could offset the 25-35 bps borrowing-cost decline; management says priority-sector status limits the impact.
Mortgage PAR 90 rose QoQ to about 2.7%; the mortgage book is new and its credit cost is still elevated.
The opex ratio must fall from 9.6% to 8.25-8.75% while AUM grows 25-30%.
Possible rating review from A stable could lower borrowing costs, but timing is not specified.
Management did not give a timeline for a new product launch beyond end-Q1 market research.
544699|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and constructive on asset quality, profitability and FY27 targets, with the company citing the guidance as conservative. Less precise on some numbers, with corrections made on the cost of borrowing base and secured/unsecured splits.
key_quotes: Our expectation is that for the guidance would be that for FY26, we will target a growth in the range of 25% to 30%.
we expect to be guided in our workings on a 3.5% to 4% credit cost, supported by better portfolio quality and sustained collection efficiencies.
So we strongly believe that the opex can be brought down to the 8.25% to 8.75%
Our PAR X or PAR 1 plus, whatever you want to call it, stood at 6.9%, improving from 7.6% in quarter 3 of FY26.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 AUM growth guided at 25-30% (midpoint 27.5%) vs 27% YoY in FY26, backed by Q4 disbursements of INR1,655 crore (+26% QoQ) and manpower growth of about 10%.

rows.why: Management plans at least one launch in FY27 (gold loan, solar-based business lending or others), but market research is due only by end-Q1 and no size or date is given.

rows.label: Borrowing cost cut of 25-35 bps in FY27
rows.why: About INR2,400 crore of borrowings due in 12 months at ~10.95% average cost are being replaced, and the Q4 incremental cost of 10.13% is below the blended 10.87%, so a ~30 bps decline is guided.

rows.label: PAR X falls to 5.5-6% over FY27
rows.when: H1 FY27 for ~30 bps, full year by Q4 FY27
rows.why: PAR X fell from 7.6% in Q3 to 6.9% in Q4 (down 70 bps QoQ) and is guided to drop a further 100-150 bps, with about 30 bps in H1.

rows.why: Mortgage is 23% of the book, up from 12% in FY24, and management targets 30-35%; the mortgage book is still new with PAR 90 at about 2.7%.

tone.note: Management was confident on asset quality, the credit cost path to 3-3.25% by Q4 FY27 and FY27 AUM growth of 25-30%, but was cautious on the mortgage PAR 90 rise and the NPA pool; analysts pushed on the NIM flat guidance, the borrowing cost base and inconsistent secured/unsecured splits.

544699|2026-06.headline: Aye Finance Q1 FY27: AUM up 28% YoY to INR7,324 crores, PAT up 144% to INR75 crores, credit cost eased to 4.01%.
544699|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 disbursements rose 22% YoY to INR1,219 crores, the strongest first quarter on record, and AUM grew 28% YoY to INR7,324 crores. Gross NPA fell 28 bps QoQ to 4.49% and credit cost fell 29 bps QoQ to 4.01%, which management says is already at the top of the 3.5%-4% guidance band. Net total income rose 38% YoY to INR322 crores and NIM improved 20 bps QoQ to 15.9%. Fee income dropped QoQ on lower direct assignment volumes and a one-off FX gain last quarter, and management kept the FY27 guidance unchanged while signalling possible refinement at H1.

segments.name: Hypothecation loans
segments.commentary: Core product, ~24-month tenor, average ticket ~INR1.5 lakh, ~78% of portfolio; portfolio ROI ~27.5%-28%; PAR X ~7.5%, PAR 30 ~6.6%, PAR 90 ~5.35%.

segments.name: Mortgage / Micro LAP
segments.commentary: ~22% of portfolio; portfolio ROI ~23.5%; PAR X ~5%, PAR 30 ~5%, PAR 90 ~3%; LTV ~35%-40%. Management expects only marginal mix increase in FY27, with a longer-term target of ~30%-35%.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guided at 25%-30% for FY27; Q1 AUM growth was 28% YoY.
Credit cost guided at 3.5%-4% for FY27; management says Q1 at top of band and expects improvement, with narrower guidance possible by end of H1. Long term, ~3%-3.5% once mortgage share reaches ~30%.
NIM guided flat at 14.25%-14.75%, with management flagging possible upside given Q1 NIM of 15.9%.
Opex-to-assets guided at 8.25%-8.75%; Q1 at 8.9%, with Q1-Q2 likely above band and Q3-Q4 expected inside it.

Borrowing cost expected to fall a further 10-15 bps after the India Ratings upgrade (IND A to A+, stable; CP to IND A1+). Lower cost on incremental borrowings is 20-25 bps over the year per the earlier statement.
Plan to add ~40-50 branches in FY27 (~10% of branch base, counting large branches). Team to grow ~10%. Medium-term opex target of 7%-7.5% over 3 years.

Medium term: vision of INR24,000 crores AUM within 5 years (~27%-28% CAGR). Product mix target over 3 years: 60%-70% hypothecation, ~30% Micro LAP, ~10% other secured products such as gold loans and solar loans.
Leverage at 3.15x; fresh equity needed at 4x-4.5x, which management says gives 2-2.5 years of growth runway (book to ~INR14,000 crores). Targeted ROA 4.5%-5% post-tax at 3.5%-4% credit cost.
capex_capacity: 571 branches across 18 states and 3 union territories as of June 2026; plan to add ~40-50 branches in FY27, with additions and splits visible between Q2 and Q3.
Branch strategy: ~10% annual growth in large-branch equivalents plus splits of mature branches (~44 splits last year, reported profitable from day one).
Team growth ~10% (13%-15% manpower increase mentioned for new branches), against a base of ~11,000 employees.
AUM per employee up 12% YoY.
demand_pricing: Credit policy tightened: approval share fell from ~55% to ~45% of logged cases, while customer additions still rose 38% YoY.

Management says the micro-enterprise market is under-penetrated (Aye has penetrated ~2%-3% of it); digital fintech and UPI lenders are seen as a limited overlap, with 7%-8% of fresh sourcing from digital channels.
Seasonality: Q1 typically ~20%-22% of annual disbursements; H1 ~40%, H2 ~60%. April was seasonally weak but May-June collection efficiency was ~99.3%.
Non-OD collection efficiency 99.2%; Bucket 1 collection 54.5%. Post-PAR 90 collection ~29%-30%, per management.
Pre-closure rate ~3%-3.5% annualised for hypothecation and ~5%-5.5% blended. Direct assignment target kept at 5%-7% of AUM (about 5% today).

financial_highlights.change: +28% YoY, +4% QoQ from INR7,044 crores in March 2026
-28 bps QoQ from 4.77%; vs 4.6% a year ago
-29 bps QoQ; includes ~INR6 crores management overlay
vs 9.5% at end of FY26; guidance 8.25%-8.75%
DA income ~INR20 crores absent; ~INR12 crores FX gain moved to OCI

qa_highlights.question: Why is the 3.5%-4% credit cost guidance well above peers despite tighter underwriting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said hypothecation (~24-month tenor, ~INR1.5 lakh ticket) differs from peers' Micro LAP book; terminal losses are ~5.5%-6% for both products, translating to ~3.5% annual credit cost, with ~3% possible in a good year. Q1 is already at the top of the band; guidance could narrow by end-H1.

qa_highlights.question: Fee and other income fell QoQ: what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed ~INR32-33 crores of decline to no direct assignment in Q1 (DA ~INR20 crores last quarter) and ~INR12 crores FX gain last quarter now moved to OCI, plus lower cross-sell on lower disbursements. Cross-sell insurance income was INR9 crores in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Can NIM exceed the upper end of 14.25%-14.75% guidance, and how do yield and cost of funds move?
qa_highlights.answer: Weighted cost of borrowing fell to 10.78% from 10.87%; incremental borrowing cost ~10.20%, ~60 bps lower. Further 10-15 bps drop expected from the India Ratings upgrade. Portfolio yield 22.4% expected to drift slightly lower as mortgage grows, but NIM guidance held flat.

qa_highlights.question: How much management overlay is in the credit cost and on the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Around INR6 crores of overlay was created within the Q1 4.01% credit cost; total overlay on balance sheet is INR11 crores, in Stage 2 and Stage 3. Target overlay is about 0.5% of book, used to smooth cross-cycle credit cost within 3.5%-4%.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term: how achievable is INR24,000 crores AUM in 5 years, and what is the product mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a 2%-3% market penetration and branch-led origination; target mix over 3 years is 60%-70% hypothecation, ~30% Micro LAP and ~10% other secured products such as gold and solar loans. About 55,000 declined customers are seen seeking gold loans, with 20%-plus doing so.

qa_highlights.question: Will PAR X at ~7% be sufficient to deliver the 3.5%-4% credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes: at ~7% PAR X, credit cost of 3.5%-4% and post-tax ROA of 4.5%-5% are achievable. Management also guided sustainable PAR X at about 6%-6.5% and expects Q3-Q4 PAR to moderate from 7.01%.

risks_watch: Opex-to-assets at 8.9% in Q1 is above the 8.25%-8.75% guidance band; management expects Q1-Q2 above band and Q3-Q4 inside it.
PAR X at 7.01% and PAR 90 for mortgage (~3%) vs hypothecation (~5.35%); management has limited deep-bucket collection capacity in mortgage and says improvement depends on it.
Monsoon below normal (IMD ~92% of LPA) with stress possible in central India and southern peninsula; management says large states are not expected to be affected.
Credit cost guidance and NIM guidance may be refined at end-H1; management flagged possible upside on both.
Fee income is lower with no DA in Q1; DA target kept at 5%-7% of AUM, currently about 5%.
Q1 disbursements are seasonal (about 20%-22% of annual); Q2 and Q3 branch additions are back-loaded and the 40-50 branch plan needs to show up in those quarters.
Capital adequacy and leverage: leverage 3.15x, with fresh equity needed at 4x-4.5x (about 2-2.5 years of runway); ROE currently low due to IPO capital.
key_quotes: Quarter 1 has definitely been encouraging where we are already at the top of that band that we are talking of, and as we move into the subsequent quarters, we do feel that this number should improve further.

So, answer to your question is that yes, 7% is good enough. It will deliver to us the credit cost that we're talking of, 3.5% to 4%, and it will deliver the ROA which we are targeting, which is probably 4.5% to 5%.
So, I think right now, 8.9% versus the highest 8.75%, I think we are very much there.
We are targeting an AUM growth, as we had said in the guidance, between 25% to 30% for this year.
544699|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, asset quality and funding, with management stating that Q1 credit cost and opex are already close to guided bands. 544699|2026-09.headline: Aye Finance Q2 FY27: PAT more than doubled to INR87 crore (+151% YoY) as credit cost fell to 3.82% and NIM hit 15.6%, above the 14.25-14.75% guidance.
544699|2026-09.overview: AUM rose 26% YoY to INR7,597 crore (+4% QoQ) and Q2 disbursements were INR1,403 crore (+10% YoY, +15% QoQ), with repeat loans down 3% YoY. Credit cost fell for a seventh straight quarter to 3.82%, now inside the 3.5-4% guidance, and GNPA eased to 4.20%. Opex ratio fell to 8.6% from 8.9% QoQ, and management says NIM is running ahead of guidance partly because a rating upgrade to IND A+ was not factored in. Management reiterated FY27 guidance and flagged that the second half, which carries about 60% of disbursements, is where delivery will be tested.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR65 crore in H1 FY26 (+148%)

segments.name: Hypothecation loans (core)
segments.commentary: Management describes itself as the dominant player with no meaningful competition in this segment. Productivity per loan officer reached 4.85 files per month in Q2, against about 4.2 in FY26 and a FY27 budget of about 5.

segments.name: Micro-LAP / mortgage
segments.commentary: Mortgage PAR X rose about 1 percentage point over the last quarter to around 6%, still below hypothecation. Management tightened policy and disbursements are being slowed, mainly in parts of MP and Gujarat. Mortgage foreclosures are rising to about 22-23% of the portfolio.

segments.name: Cattle / dairy
segments.commentary: Cattle book is held at roughly 25-28% of AUM, underwritten with a minimum of four to six high-yielding cattle, and static-pool data is described as marginally better than the market. Management does not plan to grow it aggressively.

segments.name: Gold loans (planned)
segments.commentary: Under evaluation as a pilot, with new branch setups in cities where existing branches sit. Around 20% of micro-enterprise customers already hold gold loans. Management expects to update on the plan later in the year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth guidance of 25-30% reiterated; management says it is in the range and 30% is possible but not committed. Three-year vision of 28-33% AUM CAGR and 4-4.5% ROA was shared in July.
FY27 credit cost guided at 3.5-4%, with management expecting to average around 3.5% plus or minus a few bps and exit the year lower.
NIM guidance of 14.25-14.75% maintained for now; management may revisit it in Q3 if the upside persists.
FY27 opex ratio guided at 8.25-8.75%; management expects it to move into range in H2 and to be around 8.5% for FY27.
FY27 ROA guided at 4-4.5%, with ROA expected to move into range as H2 volumes build.

Next year (FY28) levers cited: about 50 bps opex-ratio benefit, 10-25 bps lower credit cost, and about 25 bps lower interest cost, with ROA guidance said to be unaffected by insurance commission changes.
PAR X targeted below 7% by H1 and below 6.5% by year-end. Non-OD collection efficiency expected in the 99.2-99.3% range.
No fresh equity needed for about 2 years at current capital; management sees leverage moving to 4-4.5x, implying ROE in the high teens to low 20s over time.
capex_capacity: Branches held at 571 at the end of H1 FY27. More than 30 new branches are to become operational in Q3 FY27, and about 80 branches (35-40 new plus about 40 splits) are planned for the year.
Existing branch infrastructure is said to support about INR4,000-4,500 crore of additional AUM over the near term.
AUM per branch was INR13.3 crore in Q2 (INR12.8 crore in Q1). AUM per employee was INR0.67 crore vs INR0.57 crore a year ago.
Employee count budgeted to grow 12-15% in FY27. Headcount is expected to rise 5-7% in H2, mostly in Q3, for distribution and collections.
Pilot gold loan branches are planned for this year and are not expected to strain the opex budget.
demand_pricing: Repeat loans fell 3% YoY in Q2 (up 10% QoQ). Management attributes this to festive timing shifting into Q3 and expects a stronger Q3.
Management says it is not using average ticket size to grow the book; growth is coming from productivity.

Drought has been declared in parts of Maharashtra, Karnataka and Madhya Pradesh, which account for about 18% of AUM. Disbursements are being consciously slowed there, with branch-level calls in MP and Gujarat.

Bucket 1 collection efficiency was 52.8%, dipping over the last three to four months (UP included). Management attributes this to pre-festive cash-flow tightness and expects improvement after November.
Non-OD collection efficiency was 99.2%. Bihar, UP and Rajasthan, the largest states, were largely unaffected by the monsoon.
Borrowing rose to about INR1,100 crore in Q1 and about INR1,200 crore in Q2. The bank share of borrowings rose to 35% from 32%, with no tightening seen from banks.
About 8-9% of primary borrowers overlap with MFI loans (about 30-32% at household level), and FOIR includes MFI obligations.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management of reaching the top end of FY27 AUM growth (30%) given the H2 weighting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the H2 is about 60% of disbursements and that it is in the 25-30% range. Reaching the higher end is possible, depending on H2 execution, with repeat loans, gold loans and new branches as levers.

qa_highlights.question: Target ROE and dilution risk over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: ROA of about 4.5% combined with 4-4.5x leverage implies ROE in the high teens to low 20s, built up gradually as debt is added. Management does not expect dilution over the next two financial years, given net worth of about INR2,600 crore plus.

qa_highlights.question: Asset quality and credit cost outlook for H2, and cattle portfolio behaviour in inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost is expected to fall toward 3.5% with a lower exit rate. Cattle underwriting requires four to six high-yielding cattle and avoids marginal dairy farmers; static-pool data is marginally better than peers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ECL provisions change, and what was the write-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management overlays were added to Stage 2 and Stage 3 this quarter (Stage 2 moved from INR42 crore to INR48 crore). Write-offs rose modestly to about INR95 crore, including about INR45 crore already fully provided, so credit cost was flat.

qa_highlights.question: Fundraising conditions given rising rates and liquidity tightening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reported no difficulty. Borrowings were about INR1,100 crore in Q1 and about INR1,200 crore in Q2, the bank share rose to 35%, and the incremental cost was 10.04%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the insurance commission impact can be offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 50 bps of opex-ratio benefit, 25 bps of lower interest cost even after a 25 bps rate rise, and 10-25 bps of lower credit cost next year, which together should absorb the impact without repricing. A 50 bps rate hike is estimated at 7 bps ROA impact in FY27 and 15 bps in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why is NIM guidance kept at 14.25-14.75% when Q2 is 15.6%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited expected yield pressure from the growing ML book and slow repeat business, plus higher borrowing costs. It will revisit guidance in Q3 if the upside holds.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company insured against drought or natural catastrophe?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said insuring the full book would not be ROA-accretive given low loss rates. CGFMU cover is used selectively, at about INR200-300 crore of the book. Credit life insurance would not help in a drought.

risks_watch: H2 execution: about 60% of disbursements fall in H2, and management says the top end of the 25-30% AUM growth guidance depends on how H2 plays out. Repeat loans (down 3% YoY in Q2) and new branches (30+ operational in Q3) are the levers.

key_quotes: So, this solid first half has significantly enhanced our conviction to deliver on our stated FY27 guidance.
Whether we will be in the closer to 30%, I wouldn't like to commit now. But is it possible? Yes, it is definitely on our hindsight.
The primary reason is that our guidance had factored in more aggressive increase in repo rates.
I think our guidance for ROA should stay untouched.

qa_highlights.question: Is TMT a low-margin vertical?

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue is output-based, and what growth is expected?

544709|2026-06.headline: Gaudium IVF Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9.1% YoY to ₹19.4 crore, while reported EBITDA margin fell to 12.5% from 29% on expansion and marketing costs.

Management reiterated FY27 targets of about 30% revenue growth and 10 new hubs, but the quarter's growth rate is far below that target.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly 400-500 bps EBITDA margin expansion to 17-18%, and is it sustainable?

qa_highlights.question: How is the shift to Tier 2/3 cities affecting store-level margins?

qa_highlights.question: How will the IPO proceeds (about ₹46 crore) be deployed and what revenue will follow?

qa_highlights.question: Store sizes, unit economics and capex for new stores; revenue and EBITDA targets for FY27-28?

qa_highlights.question: What share of same-store growth came from volume versus pricing, and why is ASP up while bill value is flat?

qa_highlights.question: What is the MBO/LFS margin profile and working capital cycle, and what is the Nine99 payback?

qa_highlights.question: How does the FY30 revenue CAGR of 35% reconcile with FY26 growth of 11.2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plan includes about 100 more stores beyond 250 by 2030, online growth, and 600-1,000 LFS counters by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Online versus EBO revenue split for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Online is about 1-2% of revenue today and expected to reach about 10-12% over the next couple of years; no split for FY27 was given.

544717|2026-03.headline: CleanMax FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 28% to INR1,295 crore and PAT to INR86 crore; contracted capacity 5.7 GW with at least 1.5 GW addition guided for FY27.
544717|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue and EBITDA each grew about 28%, with EBITDA at INR1,295 crore against INR1,015 crore, and consolidated PAT rose to about INR86 crore from about INR19 crore. Operational capacity reached 3.1 GW after adding about 1,400 MW, and contracted capacity stood at 5.7 GW including 2.6 GW yet to be executed. Management guided to at least 1,500 MW of RE power sales additions in FY27 but gave no financial guidance. Key new risks raised were Rajasthan CTU curtailment (Bikaner 2 substation at about 30%) and the proposed deviation settlement mechanism (DSM) rules, which management has not yet quantified.

segments.name: RE Power Sales (C&I PPAs)
segments.commentary: Operational capacity 3.1 GW plus 2.6 GW contracted and under execution, total 5.7 GW; about 90% of EBITDA, with EBITDA margin 83.5% and gross margin around 92-93%. Average PPA tenor 23.17 years.

segments.name: RE Services (build-own-transfer style)
segments.commentary: Operational capacity 555 MW with another 215 MW under construction; EBITDA margin rose to 19.6% from 14.4%. Revenue growth about 28-30% across both segments.

guidance_outlook: Minimum 1,500 MW of RE Power Sales capacity addition in FY27; management said it is very confident of achieving this.
No financial guidance given; management reiterated reported EBITDA has historically been about 1.1x run-rate EBITDA, described as a past pattern rather than a forecast.
Storage/BESS response to DSM and curtailment to be announced in about three to four months.
Management expects EBITDA margin on RE Power Sales to reach nearly 86% in 3-4 years from about 83% today.
Grid forecast for end of Bikaner 2 backdown is September 2026, which management urged investors to treat conservatively.
Net debt to EBITDA target range of 5 to 5.5x; asset-level net debt to EBITDA cited at about 4.3x.
capex_capacity: Added about 1,400-1,471 MW of capacity in FY26 (RE Power Sales plus RE Services) versus less than 500 MW in FY25; operational capacity rose from about 1,700 MW to 3,100 MW in RE Power Sales.
Contracted pipeline of 2.6 GW yet to be executed at start of FY27; management said 100% of capacity expected in FY27 is already contracted.
A 530 MW CTU project at Koppal in Karnataka (450 MW wind, 80 MW solar) is being added in FY27; a 525 MW CTU project in Rajasthan is about 13% of run-rate EBITDA.
Approximately 1 GW of the FY27 additions expected in STU projects.
Solar commissioning planned to be light in July-September 2026 quarter; module deliveries for solar to resume from September or October 2026.
Under construction in Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh and Uttarakhand, adding new states; currently dispatching power in more than seven states.
demand_pricing: Data and AI customers are 42% of contracted capacity (about 2,400 MW), up from 14% (about 260 MW) on 1 April 2024; named clients include Princeton Digital Group, Iron Mountain, STT Data, and global big tech (Apple, Meta, Google, Amazon per management).
Repeat business was 74% of new volumes contracted in FY26; 82% of volumes are with AA/AAA or MNC clients, 96% with A-rated and above; 588 customers.
Contracted tariff on 2.6 GW under execution averages about INR3.85/unit (about 70% solar, 30% wind, negligible storage).
About 1,600-1,700 MW of the 5.7 GW is contract-for-difference (VPPA/I-REC type) with firm price exposure; management said there is no merchant price exposure on these.
Average PPA tenor 23.17 FY26 (22.73 FY25, 21.54 FY24); average lock-in about 18 years; no client disputes across more than 1,100 contracts.

Management expects module-cost increases from ALMM to pass through to tariffs; customer savings fall from about 30-35% to about 22-25%, with demand still robust; buying accelerated ahead of the June 2026 transition.
Reported grid uptime 99.24% in FY26; wind PLF rose from 32% to 35%, while solar PLF was slightly lower on weaker radiation.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Iran war and supply constraints on capex, module costs and interest rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not seen material adverse movement in equipment availability or capital costs attributable to the Iran war, while acknowledging a volatile situation.

qa_highlights.question: Share of under-construction CTU capacity, curtailment exposure and PPA protection?
qa_highlights.answer: The 530 MW Koppal CTU project is mostly wind in South India where curtailment is seen as minimal; PPAs give no protection if the grid curtails, since corporate customers do not pay for performance.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the new deviation settlement mechanism (DSM) on revenues?
qa_highlights.answer: No final decision and no internal impact estimate yet; the rules are sub-judice and the government is in talks. Storage is being evaluated to limit DSM downside, with an update in three to four months.

qa_highlights.question: Nature of INR414 crore pre-tax cash flow hedge gain and negative minority interest?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedge is a balance-sheet fair-value entry on VPPA/I-REC contracts with zero P&L impact given fixed tariffs; minority interest is negative because young SPVs (asset age under two years) carry interest and depreciation before profits.

qa_highlights.question: BESS in the contracted portfolio and tariffs?
qa_highlights.answer: Only about 5-7 MW of BESS within the 2,600 MW under execution; management would not separate tariffs for storage.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of rising module prices on IRRs?
qa_highlights.answer: Tariffs are expected to adjust to module costs; management said it prices to a constant target IRR, with no expected impact on margins or volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA margin lower than utility peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Scale and higher SG&A from business development, multi-state offices and 13 MW average PPA size; margin expected to rise to about 86% in 3-4 years, with the 2-3 point gap offset by higher tariffs.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost outlook and Bikaner curtailment timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Refinancing may lower costs, but management would not make bold bets given macro risk. Bikaner 2 substation curtailment is about 30%; grid expects end by September 2026 but management urged more conservatism.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 pipeline mix and data-centre share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no reason for the wind/solar mix or the Data and AI share (42% at both start and end of FY26) to change, and says FY27 additions are already fully contracted.

qa_highlights.question: Is run-rate EBITDA adjusted for curtailment, and EBITDA per MW?
qa_highlights.answer: Run-rate EBITDA is not adjusted for curtailment and assumes about 1-1.5% grid downtime; management says per-MW EBITDA is 30-35% higher on a DC basis versus peers using AC.

risks_watch: Rajasthan CTU curtailment: Bikaner 2 at about 30%; management sized impact at about 2.5% of run-rate EBITDA for six months at 40% backdown and about 6.5% for a full year at 50%.
DSM rules: impact not yet quantified; rules are sub-judice, and forecasting improvements are needed industry-wide.
Module cost step-up from ALMM rules from June 2026 and possible timing slippage; solar contracting paused pending government decision.
Rising interest rate environment could offset refinancing benefits; 40% of debt is fixed rate.
Ramp-up of new assets: revenue stabilisation takes three to six months after COD, and the asset-level net debt build-up depends on this.

544717|2026-06.headline: Clean Max Q1 FY27 PAT rose to INR55 crore on revenue more than doubling to INR832 crore; FY28 EBITDA guided at minimum INR3,000 crore.
544717|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose 107% YoY to INR832 crore, with RE power sales up 47% to INR528 crore and RE services jumping to INR300 crore from INR41 crore. Reported EBITDA rose 68% to INR462 crore (adjusted INR494 crore, up about 74% on a cash basis), and PAT reached INR55 crore. Management added about 500 MW of capacity in the quarter and issued its first FY28 EBITDA guidance of a minimum INR3,000 crore, with steady-state net debt of about INR16,000 crore. Near-term headwinds include a roughly 70% curtailment at the Bikaner CTU project, which management expects to persist through FY27.

segments.name: RE services (C&I EPC and O&M)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR300 crore vs INR41 crore a year earlier; EBITDA margin 11.2%. Order book of 147 MW contracted and under execution, with management saying order-to-execution is within 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the deferral of ALMM List-II (cells) and whether the company can benefit.
qa_highlights.answer: Projects commissioned before 31 December can use domestic modules with imported cells, saving about INR60 lakh per MW; company is pulling forward some Maharashtra and Karnataka brownfield STU builds, and no module contract is signed yet.

qa_highlights.question: Can capacity by BESS bay for the Koppal CTU project be broken out, and is the March 2027 second bay a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the split on hand; said BESS have spare evacuation capacity and fungibility across the two bays, so a slight delay in the second bay should not break the 1.5 GW target.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debenture holders get a security cover change from 0.7x to 1x?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the trust deed allowed a range of 0.7x to 1.25x; the company fixed it at 1x for consistency with the planned corporate bond, not an increase.

qa_highlights.question: Battery storage: how it plays into business and whether new PPAs include batteries.
qa_highlights.answer: Company has greenlit a first BESS STU project in Rajasthan, signed MOUs with three clients in the last month, and sees three C&I use cases; BESS-as-a-Service tariff uplift estimated at INR3-4/unit excluding generation cost.

qa_highlights.question: Curtailment impact on EBITDA and quarterly generation/PLF detail.
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates the Bikaner CTU project is 13% of run-rate EBITDA; at 70% curtailment that is about INR170 crore on a full-year basis; EBITDA would be about 8-9% higher without it. PLF given on trailing 12 months basis only.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive threat from Adani, Reliance and NTPC entering C&I, and why hyperscalers keep choosing CleanMax.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites 15 years of C&I focus, 600+ customers with 80% of new volume from repeat clients, multi-state wind-plus-solar footprint, and a fragmented market where it holds about 14% share.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 3,000 crore FY28 EBITDA guidance corporate-level, and what is the peak debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is corporate-level, including RE services; steady-state net debt corresponding to INR3,000 crore EBITDA is about INR16,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainability of growth: can the company repeat contracted capacity growth of about 4,000 MW over the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can meet or exceed about 4,000 MW of contracted additions over two years, but tripling is not feasible given execution limits; organisational gaps in five to six areas were reviewed with the board.
