544718|2026-03.headline: PNGS Reva FY26 revenue rose 70% to INR439 crore and Q4 revenue rose 139% to INR138 crore, though FY26 PAT grew only 9% to INR65 crore.
544718|2026-03.overview: PNGS Reva reported its first full standalone year (FY26) as a separate entity, with revenue from operations of INR439 crore (up 70% on restated FY25) and EBITDA of INR95 crore at a 22% margin. Q4 FY26 revenue was INR138 crore (up 139% YoY), with EBITDA of INR31 crore (22% margin) and PAT of INR21 crore (16% margin). Management attributed the margin dilution versus the earlier divisional period to standalone costs such as rent, inventory and logistics, and CEO/CFO/compliance functions. Management guided to 25-30% SSG and top-line growth in FY27-28, with 15 new stores over 24 months funded from IPO proceeds. Around INR55-60 crore of FY26 revenue was surplus gold received as consideration, per management.

financial_highlights.change: +70% YoY vs restated FY25 INR258 crore

segments.name: SIS (Shop-in-Shop, within P.N. Gadgil stores)
segments.commentary: 34 SIS stores at year-end (30 at start of FY26); the 30 pre-existing SIS generated about INR313 crore in FY26, and SIS-level SSG was about 40% in FY26. Management says SIS represent roughly INR350 crore of top-line and about INR330 crore of inventory; commission is 4% of sales on a blended basis, with no commission on gold.

segments.name: EBO (company-operated exclusive outlets)
segments.commentary: 2 COCO stores currently (one added post-IPO). Management's target per EBO is about INR9 crore revenue at 0.75x stock turn, about INR1.5 crore EBITDA initially, rising to INR3-3.5 crore in 3-4 years. Capex about INR20-25 crore per EBO; rent-based, asset-light.

guidance_outlook: SSG guided at 25-30% a year for FY27 and beyond, not below 25%, assuming stable gold prices; a sharp gold rally could repeat the ~40% SSG seen in FY26.
Top-line growth guided at around 25-30% for the next two years, led mainly by the SIS base and new stores.
15 new stores over a 24-month period (one already open): 6-7 in FY27 and the remainder in FY28; split about 60% Maharashtra and 40% outside, with 2 out-of-state stores in FY27.
Inventory turn expected to hold around 1.31x as new EBOs at 0.75x are offset by SSG; EBO breakeven 8-12 months in Maharashtra and 18-24 months outside.

Brand spend of 3-4% of top-line annually, plus about INR2 crore per EBO spread over 12-18 months. Gross margin may gain as brand value is loaded into diamond pricing over time, though percentage margin may fall as gold share rises.
No equity dilution expected; growth funded by internal accruals and a sanctioned debt headroom of roughly INR150-200 crore, with borrowing expansion after 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Store economics for SIS and EBOs: revenue per store and footfalls?
qa_highlights.answer: SIS commission is about 4% of sales blended, none on gold; FY26 SSG about 40%. EBO target is about INR9 crore revenue at 0.75x turn (about 2.5-3 customers a day at INR1.2 lakh bill), about INR1.5 crore EBITDA initially, rising to INR3-3.5 crore in 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from around 30-32% to 22%?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone costs such as separate premises rent, inventory and logistics department, and CEO, CFO and compliance functions were not borne by the division earlier. Management says these costs now load the P&L and sustain a lower EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: Is 28% gross margin and 22% EBITDA margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin can rise as brand value is loaded into diamond pricing; currently no brand premium is charged, and the industry runs 30-35% or up to 40-42% gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: How will gold price rises affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin percentage may contract as gold share rises, but management expects rupee gross profit to be maintained or grow.

qa_highlights.question: What happens to surplus gold received in exchanges?
qa_highlights.answer: It is received as consideration and sold in the open market or B2B to avoid working capital being stuck; inventory is valued at average purchase price, so no inventory gain is booked.

qa_highlights.question: Will inventory turn fall as 6-7 new EBOs open in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 1.31x to be maintained because new EBOs at about 0.75x are offset by SIS SSG; it says a fall would be limited to between 1.25x and 1.35x.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue outlook for FY27-28 and SSG?
qa_highlights.answer: SSG 25-30% and top-line growth 25-30% a year, mainly from SIS and new stores; SSG could again be around 40% if gold prices spike as in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How will growth capex be funded post-IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal accruals (about INR64 crore FY26 earnings retained), with INR150-200 crore of unused sanctioned debt; no equity dilution expected, and borrowing expansion planned after 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Will store breakevens and inventory differ by region?
qa_highlights.answer: Maharashtra EBOs are expected to reach 0.75x turn and about INR1.5 crore EBITDA in 8-12 months; outside Maharashtra in 18-24 months. Early-stage turn could be 0.25-0.5x in the first 4-5 months.

Inventory turn dilution from 6-7 new EBOs in FY27 at about 0.75x turn and slow early-stage ramp; EBO breakeven 8-12 months in Maharashtra and 18-24 months outside.

Related-party and governance questions: sister company Gargi Fashion Jewellery sells similar product at 14k gold; management shared bandwidth across two entities, and Gargi lacks a CEO.
Lab-grown diamond competition and changes in import duty or GST; management says price effects are statutory and uniform across brands.
Buyer count and disaggregated customer data were not disclosed; management offered to share by email, so customer-growth metrics remain open.
key_quotes: Our inventory turn are at 1.31 times in FY26 as our store network continues to mature.
SSG, I am expecting around 25% to 30%, it will not be less than 25% to 30%.

So in value term that it is there, but if gold prices remain stable, I am expecting 25% to 30%, but if gold prices shoot up just like last year, it again can match with the previous year's SSG growth.

544718|2026-06.headline: PNGS Reva Q1 FY27 revenue rose 119.5% YoY to INR118 crore, with PAT of INR27.21 crore (23.06% margin) and EBITDA margin of 28.76%.
544718|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached INR118 crore, up 119.5% YoY, driven mainly by diamond caratage volumes, which management said rose more than 50% in quarter. Gross profit was INR41.83 crore (35.46% margin), EBITDA INR33.92 crore (28.76%), and PAT INR27.21 crore (23.06%). Management attributed margin strength to scale and better caratage-based diamond realisations, while flagging that marketing spend, deliberately deferred to Q2-Q4, will dent PAT by 1-2% per quarter for the rest of the year. Network reached 37 stores (3 COCO, 34 SIS) after a Pune COCO opening on 7 July 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Are EBITDA and PAT margins sustainable, and what drove them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited scale (turnover roughly doubled) and better caratage-based diamond realisation. Full-year EBITDA expected at 25-27% and PAT at 22-23% after marketing dent.

qa_highlights.question: Volume growth in June/July and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Diamond caratage volume up more than 50% in Q1; July not closed, so no figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Hedging approach for gold inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: No MCX hedging; relies on natural hedge from periodic gold buying and selling. Gold loan limit available but unused as gold share of inventory is small.

qa_highlights.question: SSSG split between COCO and SIS?

rows.why: Capacity is tight beyond Q2 FY27 with existing capacity covering only FY27 to early FY28, the company is already building two Chhapara facilities, and Ahmedabad land is acquired for growth beyond FY28-29, so further capex is likely to be guided, though the utilisation level is not disclosed.

544720|2026-06.headline: Omnitech Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 61.5% YoY to INR166.6 crore and PAT rose 468.7% to INR29.73 crore, with management guiding 35–40% YoY growth.
544720|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 61.5% YoY to INR166.6 crore, EBITDA rose 90.8% to INR50.62 crore, and PAT reached INR29.73 crore. Net working capital days fell to 233 from 294 at FY26-end, driven mainly by lower inventory and receivable days. Management reiterated an order book above INR3,000 crore and a two-facility capex programme of about INR250 crore at Chhapara. Net debt to equity rose to 0.41x from 0.34x, and cash fell to INR133.75 crore from INR163 crore.

segments.name: Energy
segments.commentary: About 49% of Q1 revenue, down from about 52.7% in Q4 FY26. Pure oil and gas is below 40% of revenue per management.

segments.name: Motion control and automation
segments.commentary: About 24% of Q1 revenue.

segments.name: Industrial equipment systems
segments.commentary: About 19% of Q1 revenue.

segments.name: Others / diversified industrial applications
segments.commentary: About 6.9% of Q1 revenue, which management linked to early revenue from defence and aerospace first articles.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guided at about 35–40% YoY for FY28 (management said FY27/FY28 framing was on a YoY basis).
EBITDA margin guided at 30% and above.
Gross margin currently around 70%; management estimates a range of 68% to 71%.
Net working capital days target: a further 10–20% improvement, with historical levels below 200–220 days cited as the reference.
Two new facilities at Chhapara to be operationalised within about 14 months; the new Chhapara facility is expected to start commercial operations in FY28.
Depreciation moved from written-down value to straight-line method, expected to continue in coming quarters.
Defence and aerospace revenue expected over 1–3 years; some revenue expected in FY27 and more in FY28.
capex_capacity: Annualised machine-hour capacity is about 31–32 lakh hours across three plants: Metoda about 11 lakh, existing Chhapara about 19.5 lakh, Padavala about 1.37 lakh (as stated).
Capex of about INR250 crore for two new facilities at Chhapara: about INR100 crore buildings and INR150 crore plant and machinery, of which about INR25 crore is for existing Chhapara capacity.
Post-capex capacity is estimated at 42–43 lakh machine hours; capacity to be added in stages as machines are installed.
Some spillover of capex into FY28 is expected because of rain, with projects running about 1–1.5 months behind schedule.
Land acquired in Ahmedabad and Hyderabad; no capex plan yet for these sites. Management said debt of INR390 crore remains after INR50 crore of IPO-funded repayment.
A 1.2 MW solar plant funded from IPO capex has started generating power.
demand_pricing: Order book is above INR3,000 crore as of 31 July 2026, including a multi-year Weatherford order exceeding USD100 million. About INR2,000 crore relates to two large orders with 3–5 year execution, and about INR1,000 crore is short- to moderate-cycle (6–18 months).

Geographic mix in Q1: North America 52%, Asia 27%, India 17%, Europe/UK 3%; exports about 78% of revenue. Management expects North America at 55–60% of the order book, with Middle East and Europe growing.

Management said raw-material cost changes are passed to customers through pass-through mechanisms and quarterly business reviews, with a lag of about 2–3 months; it also cited forex pass-through. It said 100% pass-through.
Existing facilities can generate about INR800–900 crore of annual revenue, per management.
Asset turnover of about 2–2.5x and ROCE above 20% expected over time, per management.
Nadcap accreditation is in progress and defence/aerospace first articles are underway; approvals may take 6–15 months.

qa_highlights.question: What are machine-hour capacities by site, and what is the capex split?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity is about 31–32 lakh hours; the INR250 crore capex (INR100 crore building, INR150 crore plant) takes this to 42–43 lakh hours, with about INR25 crore of the machinery for existing Chhapara.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size and timing of the large-order execution from the two anchor orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said execution has started, with an expected run-rate of about INR50 crore and more, ramping over years one to five; short-cycle industrial orders of about 3–4 months are also being executed.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins be assessed for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management projected 35–40% growth and EBITDA margin of 30% and above, and said margins are capability-driven with product-level variation of 1–2%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did raw material cost rise sequentially and what is the pass-through lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed changes to product mix in a low-volume, high-mix business and to a 2–3 month lag tied to quarterly reviews; it said pass-through is 100%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scalable revenue potential from the new capex and what ROCE should be assumed?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing plants can do about INR800–900 crore a year. New capacity will be added in stages; management expects asset turnover of 2–2.5x and ROCE above 20% at peak, though this takes years.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be further working capital improvement, and what is the order-book geographic mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets a further 10–20% improvement, citing minimum MOQ needs for new vertical first articles. North America is 55–60% of the order book, with Middle East and Europe making up 10–20%.

risks_watch: Capex spillover into FY28 and about 1–1.5 months of schedule delay due to rain.
Working capital remains elevated at 233 days, and management said MOQ needs for new FAs may keep inventory high.
Net debt to equity rose to 0.41x and cash fell by about INR29 crore quarter-end to quarter-end (from INR163 crore to INR133.75 crore).
Sequential raw-material cost increase (transcript cites 20%, 24%, then 28%) and the 2–3 month pass-through lag.
Defence and aerospace approvals (Nadcap, FA) are not complete and timing is uncertain.
Revenue concentration: energy is 49% of revenue and 78% of revenue is exports; North America is 52%.

vs 0.34x at FY26 year-end (transcript says 2.41 times 0.41)

But we are right on track as far as the FA approvals are concerned and also the process which are in line for us to get approved.
So, it is not a segment-specific, but of course, sometimes in a some product we may have a some 2%, 3%, 4% lesser margin, and some product have a little bit more margin.
So, it takes around 2 to 3 months to pass through that.
544720|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth, order book and capacity, with a bullish 35–40% YoY outlook and 30%+ EBITDA margin framing. Cautious and evasive on specifics: margins are described as capability-driven with no segment detail, FA/defence timing is hedged on approvals, and the net debt ratio and raw-material pass-through lag were addressed only loosely.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin guided at 30%+ with gross margin ~70% (range 68-71%), but Q1 raw-material costs rose sequentially (20%, 24%, 28% cited) with a 2-3 month pass-through lag, and management was evasive on margin drivers.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: INR250 cr Chhapara capex (INR100 cr buildings, INR150 cr plant) lifts machine-hour capacity from 31-32 lakh to 42-43 lakh, staged as machines are installed; new facility starts commercial operations in FY28 and is running 1-1.5 months late.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 35-40% YoY revenue growth, backed by execution of two anchor orders at about INR50 cr run-rate ramping over years one to five, and about INR1,000 cr of short-cycle (6-18 months) orders within the INR3,000 cr+ book.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: The INR250 cr two-facility programme is already committed, so a fresh announcement is not needed; utilisation is about flat at 31-32 lakh hours, not clearly at 80%+ stress, and land in Ahmedabad and Hyderabad has no capex plan yet.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Order book above INR3,000 cr as of 31 July 2026 (incl. multi-year Weatherford order above USD100 mn) and Q1 revenue +61.5% YoY, but guidance is a 35-40% YoY range for FY28, with no near-term raise signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Capex running 1-1.5 months behind schedule because of rain, working capital still at 233 days, net debt/equity up to 0.41x from 0.34x, and defence/aerospace approvals (Nadcap, FA) may take 6-15 months.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Defence and aerospace first articles are underway with some revenue expected in FY27 and more in FY28, though Nadcap approval timing is uncertain (6-15 months); Others segment was 6.9% of Q1 revenue.

rows.label: Anchor orders ramp (INR2,000 cr over 3-5 years)
rows.why: About INR2,000 cr relates to two large orders with 3-5 year execution, execution has started with an expected run-rate of about INR50 cr and more, and about INR1,000 cr is short-cycle (6-18 months).

rows.label: Further working-capital release
rows.why: NWC days fell from 294 to 233 (target a further 10-20% improvement, reference below 200-220 days), but management said MOQ needs for new FAs may keep inventory high (inventory days 182 vs 225 at FY26-end).

rows.label: Raw-material pass-through lag
rows.why: Management claims 100% pass-through with a 2-3 month lag, but raw-material cost rose sequentially (cited 20%, 24%, then 28%), so near-term gross margin could compress before pass-through catches up.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, the INR3,000 cr+ order book and Chhapara capacity, but cautious and evasive on margin drivers, the raw-material lag, FA/defence approval timing and the rise in net debt to equity to 0.41x.

544726|2026-03.headline: Kotyark FY26 revenue Rs 314.9 crore, EBITDA Rs 48 crore, PAT Rs 19.4 crore, at only 7-8% capacity utilisation after Rajasthan expansion to 1,500 KLPD.
544726|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of Rs 314.9 crore, EBITDA of Rs 48 crore and PAT of Rs 19.4 crore while running at roughly 7-8% capacity utilisation. The Rajasthan biodiesel plant was expanded from 500 KLPD to 1,500 KLPD, taking cumulative annual capacity to about 4,80,000 KL. Management cited an executable order book of about Rs 80 crore and a pipeline of about Rs 215 crore, and announced two new 200 KLPD plants at Jhajjar and Kanpur due by December 2026. Management guided utilisation to rise towards 60-70% over several years, with near-term growth of 15-20% stated. Several answers were vague or inconsistent, and the call did not provide quarterly figures or a specific capex amount.

segments.name: Biodiesel (OMC and industrial)
segments.commentary: Rajasthan (Sirohi) capacity raised from 500 to 1,500 KLPD; cumulative capacity about 4,80,000 KL per year. Management says industrial sales are rising after ARAI certifications, and the company has three plants: two in Padgol, Gujarat and one in Sirohi, Rajasthan.

segments.name: Glycerin and byproducts
segments.commentary: Management cited glycerin as a byproduct monetised across pharma, food, cosmetics, personal care and paint; no volume or revenue figures were given.

segments.name: FMCG
segments.commentary: Analyst asked about recently launched FMCG products; management said they are doing well across all markets, with no figures given.

guidance_outlook: Utilisation to improve gradually towards 60-70% over the next few years, per management.
Near-term growth of 15-20%, possibly up to 30%, with at least 15% expected; management said revenue and utilisation growth would be roughly in line.
Management said margins would improve a little as utilisation rises, but gave no quantified margin target.

Two new 200 KLPD plants at Jhajjar (Haryana) and Kanpur (Uttar Pradesh) expected to be commissioned by December 2026, adding 400 KLPD (about 75% increase in capacity per management), funded from internal accruals.
Management targets 60-80% growth over the next four to five years.

Biodiesel exports: management said an export licence would take four to six months, with a Padgol or Sirohi unit converted to an EOU and ISCC certification pending; the call gave conflicting timelines and export revenue was said to arrive 'this year'.
risks_watch: Margin compression: the analyst cited a drop from about 15% to 8-10% operating margin; management did not reconcile the two figures.
Utilisation at 7-8% against a 1,500 KLPD plant and the 400 KLPD expansion; growth depends on OMC tenders and industrial demand.
Policy risk: an isobutanol blending plan was mentioned by the minister; management called it unviable on price and said the government favours ethanol.
Legal matters: the promoter's seized-raw-material case (next hearing next month) and the Supreme Court penalty matter with no timeline; a Rajasthan registration renewal is pending.
Export timing is unclear: management gave a 4-6 month licence timeline and also said revenue would arrive 'this year' and in Q1; ISCC certification is still pending.

Governance and disclosure: management declined a factory visit and some answers were evasive or unclear (asset turnover, employee plans); promoter share sales were described as being used to reduce debt towards zero-debt.
Feedstock: management said it uses 10-15 non-edible feedstocks and does not use used cooking oil (UCO).
544726|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and capacity, but vague and sometimes inconsistent on specifics such as margins, export timelines, utilisation and asset turnover, which management deferred. Management was defensive on policy questions and declined to comment on the isobutanol plan.
key_quotes: We are also setting two new biodiesel manufacturing facility at Jhajjar in Haryana and Kanpur in Uttar Pradesh, each with a capacity of 200 KLPD.
Management remains confident of improving utilization level gradually over the next few years towards 60 to 70%.
Kotyark Industries achieves a yield of more than 99%, and that is also one of our strengths.
No, I am reducing debt. I am taking the company towards a zero-debt position.

Execution expected over next three months

financial_highlights.change: Figure raised by analyst; not confirmed by management

qa_highlights.question: Why are OMCs not increasing biodiesel tender quantity and blending despite higher crude prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it depends on government policy and OMC requirements and blending will keep rising gradually.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current operating margin given the move in OMC rates, and why did it fall from about 15% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said current margins are 8-10%, that raw material cost moves with OMC rates so the margin is unchanged, and that it manages costs so PAT is not significantly affected; it did not reconcile the 15% figure.

qa_highlights.question: Will revenue and utilisation grow by 15-20%, and will margins hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue and utilisation growth would be roughly in line at 15-20%, possibly up to 30%, with at least 15% expected; margins would improve a little as utilisation rises.

qa_highlights.question: When can exports start and will revenue come in FY27 or FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the export licence takes four to six months, one of the Padgol or Sirohi units would be converted to an EOU, and ISCC certification is pending; it said export revenue would come 'this year itself'.

qa_highlights.question: What is the asset turnover expected at the Sirohi plant at normal utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give an asset turnover figure; it gave Rs 3,500-4,000 crore as the revenue at optimum utilisation and said it would explain asset turnover later.

qa_highlights.question: Is the promoter share sale being used to fund the new plants, and what is the debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the proceeds stayed in Kotyark, it took nothing personally, and the sale was to reduce debt, with the aim of a zero-debt position.

capex_capacity: Rajasthan (Sirohi) biodiesel capacity raised from 500 to 1,500 KLPD in FY26; cumulative annual capacity about 4,80,000 KL; management expects utilisation to rise gradually to 60-70% over next few years from current 7-8%.

Two new 200 KLPD biodiesel plants at Jhajjar (Haryana) and Kanpur (Uttar Pradesh), total 400 KLPD, expected commissioning by December 2026; management said this is about a 75% capacity increase; funded from internal accruals.

No capex amount disclosed for the Jhajjar and Kanpur plants; management said plant cost is about one-fourth of peers' Rs 250-300 crore investment for 300-350 KLPD plants, but gave no figure for the new projects.
Existing storage judged sufficient; no additional storage or depot plans; company uses own vehicles for finished goods delivery.
Management declined a factory plant visit, offering an office visit instead.
demand_pricing: Demand driver cited: OMC blending tenders; analyst said an earlier tender ran at about 5 crore litres per month and a current tender for 15 crore litres over three months has been issued, and asked why OMCs are not raising blending; management said it follows government policy and OMC requirements and will increase gradually.
OMC tender allocation has moved from location-based to total-quantity-based; management said the company only needs to fulfil quantity, and previously it bid in locations where it was not L1.

Pricing: management said raw material cost moves with OMC rates, so a lower rate leaves margin unchanged; at current rates operating margin is 8-10% (analyst had cited about 15% in FY26; management said margins have improved in industrial sales without disclosing price).

Industrial demand: management said industrial sales are rising after ARAI certifications for mining and generator operators; industrial diesel reportedly around Rs 140 per litre per analyst, price not disclosed by management.
Customers named by management: sells biodiesel to Modern Insulators and semi-finished biodiesel to E-Diesel Biofuels; management said it can supply raw or semi-finished material to competitors.

Exports: management said biodiesel export is currently banned and a licence is being obtained; the company needs one of its Padgol or Sirohi plants converted to an EOU and ISCC certification, which is in process.

Glycerin: management cited monetisation across pharmaceuticals, foods, cosmetics, personal care and paint; no volume or revenue numbers given. Vera carbon certification with over 57,000 carbon credits generated.
Order book: executable order book of about Rs 80 crore from OMCs and other customers, expected to execute over the next three months; pipeline of about Rs 215 crore.
Feedstock: management said it uses 10-15 non-edible oils and does not make biodiesel from used cooking oil, citing higher cost and lower yield.
Geography: current focus is North India; management said it may later expand to Maharashtra; no plans for southern expansion stated.

rows.why: Two 200 KLPD plants at Jhajjar and Kanpur (400 KLPD, about 75% of current capacity) are under construction with commissioning guided for December 2026, funded from internal accruals.

544733|2026-06.headline: GSP Crop Science Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR386 crore (from INR377 crore) and PAT grew about 16% to INR26.4 crore, helped by a one-off land sale gain.
544733|2026-06.overview: Revenue was broadly stable at INR386 crore versus INR377 crore in the prior-year quarter, with strong domestic momentum partly offset by raw material constraints in international business. Gross margin improved on a richer mix of specialty and patented products, and EBITDA was stated at around 11%. PAT rose almost 16% to INR26.4 crore, but management said about INR5.7 crore of other income came from a land sale, which is a one-off. ICRA upgraded the long-term rating from A to A+ stable, citing IPO-funded debt repayment and performance.

segments.name: Domestic B2C (branded)
segments.commentary: About 45% of Q1 revenue. Patented products are about 20-22% of B2C sales; management aims to roughly double this over 3 years. Recent launches PCT 410 and Fighter are gaining volume.

segments.name: Domestic B2B
segments.commentary: About 45% of Q1 revenue. Co-marketing of patented products with B2B partners showed good growth. Management targets B2B at 30-35% of revenue over the next 3 years.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: About 10% of Q1 revenue, seasonally weighted to H2 (Latin America, mainly Brazil). Q1 hit by raw material constraints, order slippage to China, and Brazil credit and liquidity concerns. Expected to be about 20% of mix over 3 years.

guidance_outlook: Management expects around 15% growth rate, with EBITDA growing 13-14% over the next 2-3 years (earlier in the call, EBITDA margin guidance of 12-13% was given).

Management expects the Q2 season to track anticipated growth; PAT in Q2 is expected to be a similar share of full-year PAT as last year (Q2 FY26 was about 60% of full-year PAT), with the absolute number higher.
Management expects Brazil demand to recover from September for H2 ahead of the October season.
Management targets a domestic market share rise from about 3-3.5% to 7-8%.

Management says patented product share of the portfolio will double in 2-3 years, with about 12 products launched in the last 3 years and two to three new patented formulations and one or two technicals a year.
capex_capacity: Technical capacity utilisation is about 70-75%, with room to grow and scope to swap high-value, low-volume products in multi-product plants.
Formulation plant utilisation is about 25-30%; management says formulations are sized for peak season and are not a bottleneck.
Backward-integration technical plant at Dahej and Saykha was capitalised after the prior quarter, raising depreciation.
Technical plant can run 12 months to supply H2 export demand from Latin America.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices were volatile in Q1 due to geopolitical events and petrochemical-linked inputs. Rupee depreciation of about 10-11% also raised input costs. Management said B2B prices can be passed on, while B2C has a lag covered by inventory.
Demand was held back by price volatility, with farmers, channel partners and formulators delaying purchases. Management cited El Nino forecasts and crude volatility.
Monsoon rains from July were good; cotton and soybean acreage is up and chillies are increasing. Management expects insecticide and fungicide demand to benefit.

Brazil demand is weak with customer liquidity and credit issues, and some orders moved to China on logistics. Management is cautious and is focusing on established B2B partners and second-tier distributors in Argentina and Uruguay.
Management says farmers are moving to specialty molecules and preventive spraying. It cited West Bengal as an example.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mix between technicals, formulations and branded patented products?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel mix is about 45% B2C, 45% B2B and 10% export. Formulations are about 75% and technicals about 25%. Patented products are about 20-22% of B2C, with a target to double over 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of IPO fund utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: The loan repayment object has been fully met during the quarter. A small residual amount remains pending bank settlement of brokerage, which may take 2-3 months, before the IPO account can be closed.

qa_highlights.question: How are raw material costs affecting margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin expansion is mainly from product mix. Rupee depreciation of 10-11% and petrochemical-linked price volatility raised input costs. B2B passes costs through, and B2C is covered by inventory for now.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Q1 export business faring and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Brazil orders were delayed by pricing volatility and some shifted to China. Management expects destocking, with demand returning from September for the October season. It is pursuing Argentina and Uruguay via second-tier distributors and new registrations.

qa_highlights.question: How is Kharif progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: July rains were good and key kharif acreage is up. Management said South India (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka) is still a wait-and-watch situation based on monsoon. No material shortage is seen currently.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Technical utilisation is about 70-75% with scope to add high-value products. Formulation utilisation is about 25-30%, which management says is by design for peak-season capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R&D pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: The company plans one or two new technicals a year, with data generation taking 4-5 years, and two to three new patented formulations a year, with a pipeline covering the next 4-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-off nature of other income and the outlook for it?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR5.7 crore of the INR8.3 crore other income is the land-sale gain. No further other income is planned for the remaining quarters. Management said the land sale is a one-off.

risks_watch: Other income of about INR5.7 crore from a one-off land sale inflated Q1 PAT. Excluding it, management's PAT growth looks much lower, and the analyst cited roughly flat PBT.
Raw material volatility and rupee depreciation of 10-11% could compress B2C margins if pass-through lags.

544754|2026-03.headline: Kissht (OnEMI) FY26 AUM rose 73% YoY to ₹7,066 crore; GNPA fell to 2.12% and FY26 PAT grew 75% to ₹281 crore.

Asset quality improved, with GNPA down 77 bps YoY to 2.12% and Stage-3 ECL coverage at 86.2%. Management deliberately reduced yields to target higher-quality borrowers, which compressed the Q3-to-Q4 margin, and guided to FY27 AUM growth above 40%, ROA of 4.5-5% and ROE of 19-21%.

segments.name: Loan Against Property (LAP)
segments.commentary: AUM about ₹518 crore across 98 branches in 8 states, or 7.3% of AUM. LTV is about 48% and expected to stay range-bound. LAP is not yet at breakeven and is about 1-2 years from steady-state ROA.

No disbursement guidance for FY27; guidance is on AUM growth.

New wholly-owned subsidiary created to distribute mutual funds and wealth products.
demand_pricing: Margin compression is deliberate: yields reduced to win higher-quality, lower-risk borrowers, with benefits from operating leverage and lower funding costs partly passed to customers.
Repeat customers: 11.76 million unique customers to date, about 3.5 million active; repeat share supports growth.
Acquisition: digital marketing under 50% of acquisition, partner channels (merchants, e-commerce, aggregators) about 55%, organic about 30%.
Competition cited as Bajaj and Chola; management points to credit performance and repeat-customer base as edge.
Borrowing cost on-book ranged 11.5%-14.25% across 45+ lenders.

qa_highlights.question: Rating upgrade outlook and impact on borrowing cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Crisil rated A- in Feb 2026 and India Ratings A- in Nov 2025. About 200 bps lower marginal cost of borrowing already seen since the Crisil upgrade. Another upgrade is possible in FY27 (discussion over next 6-8 months), worth a further 100-150 bps in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why is GNPA so much higher than two years ago (0.79% to 2.89%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a technical change: the write-off period was extended from 120 to 150 days after discussion with auditors. GNPA has been stable on the 150-day basis for two years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 OPEX rise and other income fall?
qa_highlights.answer: LAP not yet at breakeven and branch additions; plus a one-time Q4 investment in field collections staff for FY27 recoveries. Other income fell sequentially with a small margin compression.

qa_highlights.question: What is the portfolio yield and where does it settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 portfolio yield about 30-31%, 50-75 bps below Q3. Management expects a similar downward trend for four to six quarters. Yield minus cost of borrowing is about 18-19% near term.

qa_highlights.question: Is FLDG capped at 5% and can lenders push IRR above it?
qa_highlights.answer: Contractual risk is capped at 5% FLDG. Lenders may negotiate on hurdle rates, but the exposure does not extend beyond the FLDG.

qa_highlights.question: How is AUM growth changing the ROA and secured-mix outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall AUM growth above 40%. The 4.5% ROA guidance covers the whole book, with secured lending at lower ROA. Management expects secured to reach roughly 19-21% ROE over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did LAP and AUM growth accelerate QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Targeting higher-quality customers at lower rates, plus repeat customers from the 3.5 million active base. Management says April-May momentum continues.

risks_watch: Yield compression is guided to continue for four to six quarters; ROA of 4.5-5% depends on funding-cost and opex offsets.
LAP is loss-making at the margin and needs 1-2 years to reach steady-state ROA; 80 new branches add opex.
Stage-3 and gross NPA trends depend on the 150-day write-off policy; a change in policy would shift the reported number.
Off-book book depends on FLDG partner appetite and on negotiated lender hurdle rates.
Rating upgrade and resulting funding-cost cuts are not assured; timing depends on FY27 rating reviews.

544754|2026-06.headline: Kissht Q1 FY27: PAT rose 59% YoY to INR 95 crore and AUM 61% YoY to INR 8,001 crore, with credit cost down to 6.80% of average AUM.
544754|2026-06.overview: Management reported AUM of INR 8,001 crore (+61% YoY, +13% QoQ) and PAT of INR 95 crore (+59% YoY, +16% QoQ), with ROAA at 5.05% and ROAE at 21.20%. Credit cost fell to 6.80% of average AUM from 7.02% in Q4 FY26 and 8.85% in Q1 FY26. Total income as a share of average AUM fell 249 bps QoQ, which management attributed to deliberate pricing for higher-quality customers and a rise in off-book share from 49.7% to 53.6%. Management reiterated FY27 guidance (AUM growth of 40%+, 15% credit cost reduction, ROA of 5%+ and ROE of 20%+) and said it is on track.

qa_highlights.answer: Ranvir Singh said 13% QoQ growth already in Q1 means the company expects to over-deliver on the 40%+ 12-month AUM growth guidance.

Management cited credit cost falling to 6.80% from 7.02% and said Q1 bounce seasonality should reverse in July-September, with July collections better than June.

544785|2026-03.headline: Hexagon Nutrition FY26 revenue rose 17.8% to INR382.63 crores, EBITDA margin expanded to 13.83% and PAT grew 56.1% to INR37.94 crores.

544799|2026-06.headline: Turtlemint's first post-listing call: FY26 revenue up 57% to INR 1,098 crores, Q4 first adjusted-EBITDA breakeven quarter (INR 60 crores service EBITDA).
544799|2026-06.overview: Management reported FY26 platform premium of INR 3,868 crores (up 31% YoY) and operating revenue of INR 1,098 crores (up 57%). Service EBITDA rose 70% to INR 142 crores (about 13% of revenue), and Q4 revenue of INR 357 crores (up 42%) delivered the company's first breakeven quarter at adjusted EBITDA on a consolidated basis. Corporate overheads fell to 23% of revenue in FY26 from 38% in FY25, and PAT before exceptional items was INR 129 crores. Management declined formal guidance but said FY27 should be profitable on a full-year consolidated basis and that losses or profitability gaps would improve by more than 40%.

segments.commentary: About 97% of FY26 revenue is commission from the broking subsidiary; PoSP premium grew more than 40% in FY26. General insurance is more than 90% of platform premium (revenue split is 90% GI, 10% non-GI per management); health grew more than 60%.

segments.name: Turtlefin (enterprise)
segments.commentary: Enterprise partners (banks, NBFCs, fintechs) contribute about 20% of platform premium, roughly INR 770 crores by the analyst's arithmetic. Take rate is low, transaction-based, and management called it high margin with no direct variable cost.

segments.name: Adjacencies (mutual funds, loans)
segments.commentary: Mutual fund AUM about INR 1,400 crores through the subsidiary; loan disbursement run rate about INR 300 crores annualised, recently launched. Non-insurance businesses are about 3% of FY26 revenue.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance; board decided not to give future guidance, but management gave directional color.
FY27: management expects to reduce losses or improve profitability by more than 40% and to be profitable on a full-year consolidated basis; each quarter expected to exceed the prior one.
FY27 corporate overheads expected to grow with inflation rather than volumes; no exceptional items expected in FY27.

Medium term (about five years / FY30): service EBITDA expected to rise from 13-14% to about 24-25% of revenue, corporate overheads to fall to sub 5-6% of revenue, giving EBITDA/PBT/PAT of about 18-20% of revenue.
Long-run growth framed as continuing the historical 40%-plus CAGR in revenue and key KPIs; dividend policy possible after one to two years of sustained profitability.
capex_capacity: Balance sheet has few fixed assets (IT equipment, offices); no costs are capitalised, all expensed.
Digital partner base: 93,000+ P3M active at 31 March 2026 (51% CAGR over seven years); about 6.5 lakh verified DPs; 46 insurers (45+ partners per Q&A); coverage across 19,000+ PIN codes.
Turtlemint Academy averages 52,000+ monthly active users and 6,500+ training hours per month; certifies over 5,000 new sellers per month.
Insurance Hub gives paperless policy issuance across 40+ insurers; 8 lakh+ quotes generated daily.
Agentic AI and LLM automation under development for support tickets, renewal calling, claims and activation; more updates promised.
demand_pricing: Growth drivers: recruitment of new DPs (about 80% non-insurance background, mostly under 35) plus productivity gains in existing cohorts (frontline premium productivity up 20%+ YoY).

Health insurance growth above 60-75% helped by affordability tailwinds and GST cuts; commissions were cut in Oct-Dec quarter and management says the platform passed these through without slowing volume.
Renewal rates in Q4 were significantly higher than in the same quarter of the prior year; management says renewal rates are above industry averages.
Insurer concentration is low: top 3 insurers about 22% of business; top 100 DPs generated 4.62% of platform premium.
Claims desk settled over INR 85 crores of delayed or rejected claims in Q4.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited DP recruitment and productivity, the renewal book, and health tailwinds; H1 growth was flattered by base effects, Q4 growth (about 42%) is closer to steady state, and management expects historical 40%-plus growth to continue.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the asset-light model incurs costs only after a transaction, so commission changes are passed down, as shown in the Oct-Dec GST period. It could not say how the regulator will classify PoSPs as agents or brokers.

qa_highlights.answer: About 80% of DPs come from non-insurance backgrounds with 60-65 profiles; onboarding is digital plus a pan-India branch network. Management did not quantify TAM.

qa_highlights.answer: Enterprise premium is about 20% of platform premium (about INR 770 crores by the analyst's arithmetic). The take rate is low but volume-based and high margin, since tech is already built and licensed; enterprise growth should accelerate as new accounts go live.

qa_highlights.answer: Renewal service EBITDA margin is about 2.5-3x the new business margin. Renewal revenue is INR 225 crores; management declined to disclose renewal premium.

qa_highlights.answer: Non-insurance is about 3% of FY26 revenue. Mutual fund AUM is about INR 1,400 crores and loan disbursement run rate about INR 300 crores annualised; the incremental revenue drops straight to service EBITDA.

544829|2026-06.headline: SBI Funds Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 15% YoY to ₹1,149 crore and PAT reached ₹873 crore, up 37% QoQ.
544829|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first earnings call after the company's IPO listing. Mutual fund QAAUM reached ₹12.6 trillion (up 11% YoY) with a 15.1% overall market share, while operating revenue of ₹1,149 crore and operating profit of ₹907 crore grew 15% and 17% YoY. Management attributed margin gains mainly to asset-mix shift from passive funds toward equity, hybrid, arbitrage and gold/silver ETFs, and said the TER cut was passed on to distributors with a net neutral-to-positive effect. Management declined to give guidance, citing the silent period.

segments.name: Alternates (PMS, advisory, international, AIF)
segments.commentary: Together about 8% of operating revenue. Management said AIF and PMS are more attractive than equity on margin, and the company plans one more AIF product this quarter.

segments.name: Passive
segments.commentary: Passive QAAUM ₹4 trillion, up 12% YoY; management said low-yield passive concentration has declined, adding about 2 bps to overall margin.

guidance_outlook: No quantitative guidance given; management cited the silent period for QAAUM, opex and ESOP details.

544833|2026-06.headline: Caliber Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR657 crore (vs INR393 crore), but reported EBITDA margin fell to 16.8%, or 20.02% adjusted, on diesel costs.
544833|2026-06.overview: Revenue for Q1 FY27 was INR657 crore against INR393 crore a year earlier, with coal mining services contributing about 91% (INR597 crore). Reported EBITDA was INR110 crore, a 16.8% margin, which management says was 20.02% after adding back INR10.57 crore of diesel escalation recovered from Coal India. Cash profit rose to INR68.54 crore from INR55.37 crore, though PAT margin was lower because of higher depreciation and interest from Q1 capex. Management attributed the margin dip to the Iran-war diesel spike and guided FY27 revenue growth of 45-50%, EBITDA growth of 35%+ and PAT growth of 35%+.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 margin compression one-off or will it continue through the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the dip to the Iran-war diesel spike, pointing to 20.02% adjusted EBITDA and a normalised ~23% margin once fuel eases; it called the diesel event one-off and cyclical in nature, with Q2 trend described as stabilising.

qa_highlights.question: Does the coal mining business have full fuel escalation clauses, and why did power and fuel cost rise from ~30% of revenue in FY22 to ~47% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: All coal mining projects have fuel escalation, but timing mismatch means a small portion is absorbed. Management said the rise reflects the shift from logistics to mining, where fuel intensity is higher, and that mining was 86% of FY26 revenue versus 40-60% earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company planning MDO and iron ore, and how will the capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, MDO coal, MDO iron ore and iron ore mining are being explored, along with one critical mineral block in Maharashtra. Funding is from IPO proceeds of INR167 crore for equipment and cash flow from lower EMIs; no capex figure was given for MDO.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company give FY27 and FY28 revenue and margin guidance, and what is the 2-3 year capex?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 guidance was given in closing remarks: revenue growth 45-50%, EBITDA growth 35%+, PAT growth 35%+. No FY28 guidance was given; capex for the next 2-3 years was deferred to a later date.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gross debt, cost of debt and year-end debt expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Opening FY27 debt was INR1,024 crore, expected to fall to about INR750 crore at year-end without new tenders; average cost of debt 8.5-9%, expected to decline after the rating upgrade to A minus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bidding pipeline and win rate, and are bids outside coal being pursued?
qa_highlights.answer: 8-10 tenders in coal and overburden are pending results; the company is evaluating iron ore and MDO projects on margin and ROCE. No win rate was disclosed; a tender list would be shared on email request.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT margin fall while EBITDA grew, and is the depreciation policy different?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Nikhil Karwa said higher depreciation and interest in Q1 from the quarter's higher capex, with the new assets not yet contributing a full quarter of revenue, explained the lower PAT margin; no change in depreciation policy was indicated.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Adani Power Parsa suspension and is any amount outstanding?
qa_highlights.answer: Work stopped after land issues at the site; equipment was moved to the Jayant site in Singrauli, Madhya Pradesh, to avoid idle cost. Management says there was no loss, and work has not restarted at Parsa though it remains in touch with Adani.

544838|2026-06.headline: XtraNet Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to ~Rs 51 crore, but EBITDA rose 89% to ~Rs 10 crore (20.59% margin) on services mix.
544838|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 11% YoY to about Rs 51 crore in Q1 FY27, while operating EBITDA rose 89% to about Rs 10 crore, with margin up 855 bps to 20.59%. PAT was about Rs 6 crore (+77% YoY), a PAT margin of 11.88% (+444 bps). Management attributed the margin expansion to a higher services share, which was about 65-68% of revenue versus about 46% in Q1 FY26. Order book stood at about Rs 373 crore across 55 projects as of June 30, 2026, after fresh orders of about Rs 60 crore in the quarter.

segments.name: Proprietary platforms (Synergy, XtraTrust)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 14% of Q1 FY27 revenue; XtraTrust is a MeitY-approved certifying authority with about 850,000 subscribers onboarded.

segments.name: Digital services
segments.commentary: Contributed about 12% of Q1 FY27 revenue, covering banking support, cloud analytics, AI, IoT and blockchain.

Management expects 55-60% of the current order book to be executed in FY27 (the CFO said 55%).

Management is expanding data center capacity at XtraTrust to onboard more subscribers, targeted within the next quarter.

qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 35-40% annual growth in the segment, keeping it at about 50% of revenue, driven by DC modernization, new DR setups, NOC and cyber SOC.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue and margin guidance and its drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 target is Rs 500+ crore versus FY26 Rs 365 crore (about 35% growth), supported by the Rs 375 crore order book (55-60% executable in FY27) and new bids.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company compete in digital trust and PKI against peers such as eMudhra?
qa_highlights.answer: XtraTrust has about 850,000 subscribers on recurring models, 10,000+ partners, 30-minute issuance, and an in-house PKI engine; eMudhra is the main competitor.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital cycle for data center projects?
qa_highlights.answer: End-to-end cycle of 12-15 months; government billing realises in about 120-150 days, and O&M/services billing in 45-60 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split between services and products, and the margin difference?
qa_highlights.answer: Services were about 60% of FY26 revenue, now 65-68% in Q1; product EBITDA margin is about 6-8% versus 20-22% for services.

qa_highlights.question: How do CAPEX and OPEX models and recognition work?
qa_highlights.answer: Typically 50-60% of a project is CAPEX billed over 6-18 months; the rest is billed over 4-7 years as O&M. Revenue is recognised on billing with straight-line annuities and no step-ups.

qa_highlights.question: Is hardware price inflation passed through to clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Not a direct pass-through; prices are locked with OEMs per project after order, and price escalation clauses are now used in new bids and repeat orders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the typical bid-to-order conversion timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Government and PSU orders take about 60-90 days from proposal to order; large enterprise, aviation and BFSI take 30-60 days.

544870|2026-06.headline: Behari Lal Engineering Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18% YoY to INR151.7 crore, with EBITDA of INR29.7 crore (19.6% margin) and high-value share at 60.4%.

544880|2026-06.headline: Horizon Industrial Parks Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23% YoY to INR200 crores, with EBITDA of INR161 crores (80% margin) and a net loss of INR12 crores.

qa_highlights.question: How does the INR967 crore contracted run rate translate into reported EBITDA and timing?

544880|2026-09.headline: Horizon Industrial Parks Q2 FY27 revenue rose 30% YoY to INR213 crore, EBITDA INR173 crore at 81% margin, net debt cut to INR2,765 crore.

H1 leasing reached 4.4 million sq ft, about two-thirds of the 6.5 million sq ft FY27 target, and H1 development completions reached 2.7 million sq ft against a 6 million sq ft target. qa_highlights.question: Status of the CWC litigation and downside risk?
qa_highlights.answer: The matter remains sub judice, with no significant update since the Jan 2026 hearing. The court has said it will not stop development in the interim, and management continues construction.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 55% YoY growth is volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes were approximately the same YoY, so growth came from product mix and customer relationships. No quantification was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin, given EBITDA of about 14% in Q1 after 9.5% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins move quarter to quarter with product mix and that the company focuses on profit amount rather than percentage. It did not commit to a sustainable margin range.

qa_highlights.question: How is gold price risk hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: The company buys gold equal to what it sells on the same day at market price. Inventory is carried at a weighted-average cost that management says is below market, so no hedging is needed.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin expansion comes from product mix and how much from inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mix was one factor and gold-price gains add 1-3 percentage points YoY. Analysts disputed that Q1 had gold gains, and management gave no split.

qa_highlights.question: How is growth funded and what is the working-capital cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Profits are reinvested, and the bank lines are open. The IPO raised equity to about INR450 crore to fund working capital. Management said the business needs more working capital as it grows.

qa_highlights.question: Are customers moving karigar work in-house, and what is the moat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said handcrafted, co-created bridal designs and long-standing relationships protect the business. It gave no figures to show the moat.

qa_highlights.question: Why did job-worker count fall and employee cost drop QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prefers larger, organised contract manufacturers. Employee cost fell because Q4 included an ex-gratia payment to directors, which will not recur.

risks_watch: Margin sustainability: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin of about 14% vs 9.5% in Q4 FY26; management gave no sustainable range and said margins move with product mix. Track next quarter's gross and EBITDA margin against this base.

Unquantified growth drivers: 55% revenue growth attributed to mix and relationships with volumes described only as 'approximately same'; volume split and gold-price contribution (management cited 1-3 pp YoY) were not quantified. Watch for the promised Q2/Q3 volume data.

Working capital and funding: trade receivables of INR126 crore (about 22-23 days), inventory turnover about 8x, and management saying working capital needs keep growing; IPO proceeds (INR38 crore working-capital portion) are a key use to track against bank line usage.

Customer in-housing and moat: analysts questioned whether large customers such as Kalyan and P.N. Gadgil moving to in-house karigars threatens the outsourced model; management gave no share or retention figures.

Gold-price hedging and inventory accounting: hedging relies on a same-day buy-to-sell policy and weighted-average inventory valued below market; management did not show the inventory gain component, which analysts disputed for Q1.

544885|2026-06.headline: Gaja AMC Q1 FY27 PAT rose 35% YoY to INR27.2 crores; total income up 26% to INR51.8 crores.
544885|2026-06.overview: First quarterly call as a listed company. Total income rose 26% YoY to INR51.8 crores and PAT rose 35% to INR27.2 crores, with LTM PAT at INR89.1 crores (+38%). Performance income of INR29.7 crores (+17% YoY) drove most of the income, while management fee income of about INR16 crores grew 7%. Cost-to-income improved to 38.4% from 42.3%. Management repeatedly declined to give forward guidance on carry, fund deployment or fundraising timelines.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said performance income becomes more predictable as firms mature, and that fee income does not grow with NAV. Q1 split was about INR16 crores fee and INR30 crores performance; LTM is the right lens.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for Fund III carry given low gross IRR?

544886|2026-06.headline: Tempsens Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% to INR118 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 22% from 25.3% on higher employee cost.
544886|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 33% YoY to INR118 crores, led by Electrical Heating (+148.8% to INR25 crores) and Temperature Sensing (+42% to INR60 crores), while Specialized Cables fell 8.8% to INR32.5 crores on export order timing. EBITDA rose 15.7% to INR26.6 crores, but margin compressed about 330 bps to 22%, driven by a roughly 140 bps hit from employee cost (up 45% to INR20.4 crores) and a high prior-year gross margin base. Management guided FY27 revenue growth in line with the three-year blended growth rate and said margins should recover in H2 FY27. Four capacity projects with aggregate peak revenue potential of about INR500 crores are slated to commission between Q4 FY27 and Q3 FY28.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR25 crores, up 148.8% on oil and gas dispatches in India, Southeast Asia and Middle East; 5-year standard furnace supply contract signed with a life sciences OEM.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR32.5 crores, down 8.8% on export order timing; cable harness line launched with UL certification; Unit 8 greenfield under construction, completion by Q2 FY28.

qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated roughly 75-90% of revenue from critical applications, with 10-20% from regular, more competitive industries; vendor approvals can take 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify TAM; said new-age products could grow in the high 20s or 30s percent over 2-3 years. Newer products segment addressable market is about INR3,000 crores with less than 1% currently addressed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin recovery bridge and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost increase reflects headcount added for future projects; margin recovery expected to start in H2 FY27, not FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Middle East/Africa and political situation a risk to revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no negative impact seen in the next few quarters; electrification trend could be positive mid-term.

qa_highlights.question: When will the INR500 crore incremental capacity reach full utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity comes online from Q1 FY28 with construction largely done by Q3 FY28; full utilisation expected around FY29-FY30, with plants typically run at about 80% maximum.

544889|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 7% YoY to INR218 crores, while new-business opex drag of INR23 crores left consolidated EBITDA at INR45 crores.
544889|2026-06.overview: Symbiotec's first earnings call after its BSE/NSE listing reported Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue of INR218 crores (+7% YoY), with API revenue of INR215 crores (+6% YoY, volume-led) and API EBITDA of INR66 crores (+9% YoY). Consolidated EBITDA was INR45 crores and net profit about INR14 crores, which management said understates underlying profitability because of INR23 crores of new-business opex and INR11 crores of depreciation that were previously capitalised as pre-operative expenses. No CDMO or injectable revenue was booked in the quarter, versus about INR33 crores of milestone revenue in Q4 FY26. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of roughly 20% revenue growth and 25% EBITDA growth, with a plus/minus 5% band, and pinned new-business revenue to milestones in H2 FY27 and commercial CDMO revenue to the next 6 to 12 months.

544891|2026-06.headline: Hy-Tech Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR430 million, but EBITDA margin fell to 19.6% from 21.5%, which management blames on price-revision timing.
544891|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 13% YoY to INR430 million and PAT rose 11% to INR46 million, while EBITDA was flat at INR84 million and margin contracted about 190 bps. Management attributed the margin dip to input-cost increases from the Feb–April period whose OEM price revisions, effective 1 April, are expected to be recognised only in Q2, and a cut-off sales shift into the next quarter. This was the company's first earnings call after its 1 September listing on NSE and BSE. Management guided to ~20% revenue growth, 25–30% PAT growth and a 24–25% EBITDA margin for FY27, with capacity expansion and new-customer wins as the main drivers.

rows.label: US subsidiary and export mix
rows.why: US is about 25% of revenue and a US subsidiary is being set up; the 50% export target in five years depends on Europe, Australia, New Zealand and Dubai growth, and tariffs are a risk.

tone.note: Management was confident on 20% revenue, 25-30% PAT and 24-25% margin recovery, but was evasive on the 6.5-acre plant cost (not until November), customer names and the order book, and leaned on Q2 price-revision catch-up for the Q1 margin drop; analysts probed the margin, PPE discrepancy and capex.

544898|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 7.28% YoY to INR 133.66 crore and PAT grew 14% to INR 29.28 crore, while growth depends on GPU capacity going live from Q3.
544898|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 133.66 crore, up 7.28% YoY but down 20.20% QoQ, which management attributed to design services booked in a subsidiary (SPOCHUB) in Q4 FY26. PAT rose about 14% to INR 29.28 crore and EBITDA was INR 559 million at a stated 42% margin. Management said the step-up depends on the Sharon AI GPU deal (8,200 B300 GPUs in Sydney), now expected to bill from Q3 FY27 after a delay from the earlier mid-September target. Management declined to give any forward revenue or profit guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Sharon AI go-live delayed from mid-September, and when will revenue start?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the date slipped by about 1.5 months, with billing starting now. It targets early Q3 or mid-Q3, and later said November first week go-live, with billing from Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the quarterly revenue growth (7-8%) inconsistent with a 30-40% order book growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited seasonality with Q3 and Q4 stronger historically; Q1 growth of about 8% was called appropriate given domestic deliverables. Growth is expected QoQ from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GPU pricing locked for the Sharon deal and can its rate be fixed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the Sharon GPU purchase cost and the customer revenue are both locked at pre-decided rates, with a 7-year contract.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 1,500 GPUs be deployed by Q4 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the target as correct, with deployment by January-February 2027 (mid-to-end Q4).

qa_highlights.question: Are there capex subsidies (PLI) or any client concentration risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not eligible for capex subsidies such as PLI. On concentration, management said advance-funded contracts reduce risk, and it did not name the clients or confirm any China exposure.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be any deal-related guidance for FY27 or FY28?

GPU supply constraints: management cited OEM delivery delays of 4 to 9 months, and said it relies on partner relationships to expedite deliveries.
Revenue concentration and counterparty risk: the Sharon AI deal is a single 7-year lease, and the European banking client was not named; management did not address China exposure directly.

Revenue quality: FY26 SPOCHUB design services and the Managed Services jump were described as one-time, so underlying growth (Q1 +7.28% YoY) needs to be tracked against the 30-40% domestic order book CAGR claim.
Capex funding mix (customer advances, IPO proceeds, partial debt) and the INR 1,500 crore plus INR 1,500 crore FY27 capex plan, where management did not give the amount already deployed.

We are targeting PAT margins in the range of 15% to 20%. So, that's our target PAT margin. We will not work for anything lesser than that.
No. We cannot give any forward -looking numbers, so that is not yet, like, company has not planned to disclose anything like that.

544901|2026-06.headline: Purple Style Labs Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR119 crores (from INR106 crores), but EBITDA was negative INR11 crores vs negative INR4 crores a year earlier.
544901|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first full quarter with the four large-format experience centres opened in FY26 (Fort Mumbai, South Ex Delhi, Linking Road Bandra, Madison Avenue New York). GMV rose to INR193 crores from INR133 crores and AOV rose to INR86,000 from INR66,000. Revenue from operations was INR119 crores, gross margin held at 36%, and EBITDA and PAT losses were wider than a year earlier on the higher fixed cost base of the new stores. Inventory and net working capital fell year on year, but borrowings rose to INR436 crores at June 2026 from INR371 crores at FY26 end.

segments.name: Mumbai (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR50 crores from INR28 crores in the first three months of FY26. Mumbai was the largest market in FY26 GMV at INR205 crores.

segments.name: Delhi (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR39 crores from INR29 crores. Delhi FY26 GMV was INR166 crores.

segments.name: Hyderabad (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR16 crores from INR10 crores.

segments.name: USA (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR29 crores from INR20 crores. New York flagship opened in March 2026 and is the first US store; US was online-only before that.

guidance_outlook: No objective margin or profitability guidance given; management said it would refrain from it.
Q1 is the leanest quarter; management said the cost structure set in Q1 will carry into Q2 absent changes, and clearer trends are expected over the next two quarters.
No significant new experience centre expansion is planned near term; the first full year of the FY26 store investments is to be observed.

EBITDA break-even framing: on a P&L basis, gross profit of about INR55 crores would be needed for zero EBITDA, with lease-related costs of INR45 crores (lease interest plus ROU depreciation) included. On a cash basis, lease payments of INR29 crores imply a smaller gap.
Lease interest and ROU depreciation are expected to stay broadly flat unless stores change. Other finance cost should decline as operating profit reduces debt.
capex_capacity: Four large-format experience centres opened in FY26: Fort Mumbai and South Ex Delhi (operational since Q2 FY26), Linking Road Bandra (end-March 2026), and Madison Avenue New York (March 2026).
Store footprint is organised by geography, not by store, so same-store sales are not tracked. Mumbai now runs two large-format centres.
The New York lease is a June-end lease with a shorter tenure, so rent can be adjusted after 12-18 months of performance.
Inventory is expected to stay roughly flat at the current level absent further expansion. Management said inventory is around INR160 crores, with breadth-led singular-unit stock.
demand_pricing: AOV rose to INR86,000 in Q1 FY27, from INR76,000 in FY26 and INR46,000 in FY24. Store AOV is about 2.5x online AOV (India online about INR38,000 vs store about INR90,000 in FY26).
Active designer brands fell to 1,109 in FY26 from 1,910 in FY24. Top 100 designers were 67% of sales in FY24.
Average GMV per customer rose to INR108,000 in FY26 from INR67,000 in FY24. Top 50,000 customers contributed INR702 crores of FY26 GMV of INR722 crores.
Women's wear above INR1 lakh grew to INR312 crores GMV in FY26 from INR187 crores in FY24. Women's wear below INR35,000 fell to INR86 crores from INR162 crores.
Gross margin percentage is said to be broadly flat across price points. Management argued that absolute gross profit per piece rises with higher ticket size.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow still negative and borrowings rising despite lower inventory and working capital? When does the business become self-funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the lower inventory reflects better inventory management after the FY22-25 build-up, and higher customer advances (INR49 crores) helped working capital. Debt is funding interest costs, and Q1 is not operationally profitable. It asked investors to observe the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Does the higher-ticket strategy improve gross margin or only AOV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said percentage gross margin is similar across categories. The benefit is in absolute gross profit per piece (e.g., at 40% margin a INR2 lakh piece yields INR80,000 vs INR8,000 for a INR20,000 piece), plus lower supply and customer complexity from the long tail.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of outright purchase, consignment and backorder inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consignment split is business-sensitive and not disclosed. Outright purchase forms the inventory on the books. Backorder advances are about one month of revenue, and average delivery is 45-60 days, so backorder customer advances are not inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for finance costs in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Lease interest plus ROU depreciation (INR45 crores in the P&L) should stay at Q1 levels absent new store changes. Other finance cost should fall as operating profit reduces debt.

qa_highlights.question: What GMV scale, gross margin and operating leverage are needed for EBITDA positivity?
qa_highlights.answer: On an EBITDA basis, gross profit of about INR55 crores would be needed. Adding the lease costs of INR45 crores (P&L) or INR29 crores (cash) raises the required gross profit. Management referred to the detailed P&L on slide 20.

qa_highlights.question: What is the New York store's AOV and break-even, and what is the SSG for mature stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a New York store AOV of about INR1.25 lakh (about USD1,500), based on a 2.5x multiple to online AOV. It did not give a break-even GMV. Same-store growth is not tracked because the company reports by geography.

544903|2026-09.headline: Deepa Jewellers Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25% YoY to INR 626 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 7.24% on plain-gold mix and PAT rose 37% to INR 37 crore.
544903|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 25% YoY to INR 626 crore, with EBITDA of INR 45 crore (up 17% YoY, margin 7.24%) and PAT of INR 37 crore (up 37%, margin 5.96%). H1 FY27 revenue rose 30% to INR 1,057 crore, EBITDA rose 24% to INR 84 crore (7.95% margin) and PAT rose 32% to INR 64 crore. Management attributed the Q2 growth moderation to festive demand shifting into H2, and said lower gross margin came from a plain-gold-heavy sales mix, with PAT supported by other income and a lower tax rate. The company also commenced its in-house Hyderabad manufacturing facility in September 2026 and guided to 40-45% revenue CAGR for FY27-FY29.

segments.name: Job work
segments.commentary: Volume of 318 kg in Q2 (+44% YoY) and 544 kg in H1 (+51% YoY). Realisation per gram fell to about INR 178-180 from about INR 200 a year earlier, which management attributed to plain-gold mix rather than pricing changes.

segments.name: Jewellery manufacturing (invoice/own gold)
segments.commentary: Volume of 491 kg in Q2 (broadly stable) and 783 kg in H1 (-5% YoY). Own-processing realisation fell to about INR 12,600/g from INR 14,500/g, attributed to lower gold prices, plain-gold mix and higher 18-karat sales.

segments.name: Studded vs plain gold mix
segments.commentary: Studded share was 57% of H1 FY27 sales, against 65% in FY26, with plain gold at 43%. Management targets studded share of 75% over the next three to four quarters.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR of 40-45% guided for FY27, FY28 and FY29, with FY27 growth of 40-45% compared with FY26 (March 2026) base; the 40-45% figure was also described as a 40-50% revenue CAGR for two years at a constant 24-karat gold rate of INR 50,000.
EBITDA margin expected to expand 80-120 bps over the next 4-6 quarters, driven by the Hyderabad facility, Tier-2/3 expansion, studded mix and standalone store sales.
Gross margin pressure from plain-gold mix expected to normalise in upcoming quarters.
Hedging to rise from 94% toward close to 100% of gold holdings over the next two to three quarters.
Working capital cycle (inventory days plus receivable days) expected in the 55-65 day range; inventory and receivables expected to normalise from Q3.
Internal accruals, IPO proceeds and existing debt expected to fund growth through FY29.
Effective tax rate guided at the standard 25.168%; Q2 benefit came from deferred tax on IPO expenses, with the tax shield reversing in later years.
capex_capacity: In-house manufacturing facility in Hyderabad, about 6,700 sq ft, commenced operations in September 2026.
Facility capacity of about 1.5 tonnes a year on single shift and about 2.5 tonnes a year on double shift.
Facility processed 65 kg (13% of volume) in Q1 FY27 and 167 kg (21%) in Q2 FY27; management expects about 40% in Q3 and about 50% in Q4.
Second sales office in Chennai planned for December 2026; Bangalore office planned for April-May 2027, following Vijayawada office.
Long-run target mix of 65% in-house and 35% outsourced manufacturing; outsourced work to shift in-house from Q4 FY27.
demand_pricing: Revenue concentrated in South India (Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala); client base about 373 customers including 47 jewellery retail chains such as Joyalukkas, Kalyan, Lalitha and Bhima.
Q2 growth moderated as festive demand shifted into H2; H1 typically contributes about 40% of annual revenue.
Retail customers shifting from cash purchases to old-gold exchange after a gold price spike, moving sales from invoice basis to job work; management said total volume shifted rather than fell.

Job work conversion margin is about 75% and invoice-basis about 8%, with a similar ROCE/ROE in both models; job work is priced at about 1% lower wastage (4% vs 5%) because it needs no working capital.
Gold price assumption for guidance: constant 24-karat rate of INR 50,000 per 10 g; average selling gold price rose from about INR 8,000/g in FY25 to INR 11,950/g in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin and grammage realisation decline in Q2, and why did job work realisation drop about 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the change was a shift toward plain gold jewellery (lower margin than studded), not a strategic or operational change, and expects normalisation. Job work realisation fell to about INR 178 from INR 202 a year earlier (about 11%), attributed to the same SKU mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory and receivable days rise versus March 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said March is not a like-for-like base because year-end corporate purchases stop; higher inventory came from stock built for the new Vijayawada sales office in September after IPO proceeds. Management expects normalisation from Q3 and a combined inventory plus receivable cycle of 55-65 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue outlook for the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth to come from new geographies (Vijayawada, Chennai, Bangalore offices), SKU expansion into studded casting, Nakshi and Tapa jewellery (16 SKUs launched in Q1), and client store expansion including franchise models. Guidance is 40-45% CAGR for FY27-FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin impact of the new facility, and what EBITDA margin should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation and karigar costs weighed on Q1 and Q2 margins; benefit expected from Q3 as more volume shifts in-house. Management guided to an 80-120 bps EBITDA margin expansion over 4-6 quarters, with a note that studded mix and standalone store sales also contribute.

qa_highlights.question: How is gold price exposure hedged, and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: 94% of gold holdings were hedged as of 30 September through gold metal loans (3.25% p.a.), MCX short futures and back-to-back unfixed purchases from bullion suppliers. Target is close to 100% within two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the effective tax rate fall to about 15%, and will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the standard rate is 25.168%; the lower Q2 rate reflects deferred tax on IPO expenses, which Companies Act treats against securities premium while Income Tax allows over five years. The effect is expected to even out in later years.

qa_highlights.question: Will promoters draw salary, and how will they be compensated?
qa_highlights.answer: Both Ashish Agarwal and Dev Agarwal will not draw salary from 1 October 2026, and Dev Agarwal said no salary is planned for at least 10 quarters, after which the board will decide.

risks_watch: Gross margin and realisation pressure from plain-gold mix and lower gold prices; management quantified a 50% gold price fall at about 60 bps gross margin impact.
Working capital intensity: inventory and receivable days rose versus September FY26, and growth of 40-45% needs funding from accruals, IPO proceeds and debt.
Execution risk on new Hyderabad plant ramp-up (targeted about 40% of volume in Q3 and 50% in Q4) and on Chennai and Bangalore office launches.
Shift of retail customers toward old-gold exchange could keep invoice-basis sales subdued and raise job work share.
Customer concentration in South India and in a few large jewellery chains.
Tax rate normalisation from Q2 deferred benefit back to 25.168%.
Hedging coverage to rise to close to 100%; monitor in next quarter.
